- Defining material-change policy for every comment, JSDoc form, generic instantiation, or source move beyond recording evidence useful to those later decisions.
- Persisting production snapshots, caches, source-bearing receipts, or auxiliary source stores.
- Revisiting parked Phase F, configuration, consent, host-integration, or Wayfinder work.

## Further Notes

- The product remains unnamed. Jev is the external review backend, not the product.
- The declaration-extraction feasibility brief is the agreed scope. The declaration-extraction research report is advisory evidence and must not be treated as runtime proof.
- The experiment can complete successfully by disproving the candidate composition, provided the fixture corpus, reproducible evidence, and limitations are recorded.
- Discuss the evidence before adopting a production contract, starting classification experiments, or resuming broader host integration.

title: Phase F: enable and revoke repository review consent
body:
## Parent

https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/3

## What to build

A user explicitly enables review for a repository and actual review destination, can revoke it, and gets a non-prompting, zero-egress outcome without approval. Approved edits continue through the existing synchronous advisory review path.

This is an approved implementation slice of #3, which remains the normative specification. Preserve its architectural decisions, strict TypeScript and exact matched Effect 4 RC cohort (currently 4.0.0-rc.116), Decision.probability/DecisionModel/ai-typesafe integration, synchronous advisory behavior, and scope exclusions. Full post-edit file plus repository-relative path is provisional milestone context, not a permanent product boundary. No extraction, shell-write detection, directory consent, new hosts, release packaging, or formal-tool integration is added. Include user documentation, relevant real JSON subprocess acceptance tests, strict type/dependency checks and regression coverage in this slice; ordinary tests stay deterministic/offline. Research remains advisory.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Enable identifies the canonical Git working-tree root, Jev backend, actual destination, and repository-wide eligible-source scope before recording approval in user-owned state. Installation/project policy cannot grant approval.
- [ ] Consent is keyed by canonical root/backend/destination; approved combinations are reusable, while different checkouts, moved roots, worktrees, or destinations do not inherit unrelated approval. Outside a discoverable working tree there is no egress.
- [ ] Disable revokes future dispatch; consent is checked at dispatch, without claiming to recall already transmitted source. Hooks never prompt and preserve completed edits.
- [ ] Credential inspection exposes only environment-variable name/presence, defaulting to TYPESAFE_API_KEY. Never automatically source environment files or store credential values in shared configuration.
- [ ] Use bounded structured outcomes for missing consent/credentials and review availability, distinct from exclusions and reviewed-with-no-findings; leave interactive notification delivery to its own slice.
- [ ] Real JSON subprocess tests cover grant reuse, revocation, repository/backend/destination combinations, attempted project authorization, and zero source egress without approval.
- [ ] Actual Effect TypeSafe provider tests with fake HTTP assert destination, authentication channel, and exact allowed payload fields, including intentional source/questions/criteria. Synthetic sentinels detect unrelated files, transcripts/tasks, absolute local paths, environment dumps, or credentials leaking into payload/logs. These tests make no paid calls and assert no server-retention guarantee.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

title: Compare diff, whole-file, and declaration review inputs
body:
## Problem Statement

Issues #5–#8 conditionally accepted the TypeScript 7 source-parser plus native-LSP composition as a declaration-extraction feasibility result. That experiment established recoverability and bounded degradation; it did not establish that declaration-oriented input improves Jev's semantic judgments enough to justify a production extractor.

Phase F issues #9–#15 intentionally continue with the provisional full post-edit file plus repository-relative path contract. In particular, #15 evaluates rule meaning and batch interactions under that contract. A separate experiment is required to vary the input contract without conflating input effects with rule-batch effects or silently broadening Phase F.

## Decision this issue informs

Determine whether declaration plus bounded referenced context produces a material semantic improvement over diff, whole-file, or declaration-only input while preserving negative controls, bounded latency, explicit incompleteness, and the authorized paid-call budget.

A passing result authorizes production-extractor architecture work; it does not select an extractor, expand production consent, or integrate extraction into Phase F. A failing result is valid evidence to reject or narrow declaration-oriented review. An unavailable or under-covered run is inconclusive, not a pass.

## Input modes

Render the same underlying edited fixture through four versioned input contracts:

1. textual before/after diff plus repository-relative path;
2. full post-edit file plus repository-relative path;
3. edited declaration alone plus repository-relative path;
4. edited declaration plus bounded outbound referenced context, completeness, and omission metadata.

Record the exact input-contract version, renderer identity/digest, fixture/content identity, rule-definition identity, extraction profile, source-character count, and request byte count. Filename and any explicitly supplied domain text remain identical across modes. Do not add task transcript or unrelated repository context.

## Corpus and expectations

- Use at least 24 human-authored synthetic edited fixtures: at least six each for TypeScript interfaces, type aliases, Zod schemas, and Effect Schema definitions.
- Pre-register at least 12 context-required cases, six diff-sufficient controls, and six whole-file-dilution cases. Categories may overlap only when the rationale explains why.
- Include positive violations, valid negative controls, superficially similar negatives, and explicit ambiguous/unchecked cases. Rule 2 is the genesis focus; include other existing rules only where the fixture rationale makes them applicable.
- Every checked fixture/rule pair has a rationale and an expected probability band established before live execution. Use the existing clear band `p < 0.3` and violation band `p > 0.7` unless a different finite interval is justified in advance. Missing labels mean unchecked, never clear.
- Backend output must never create or revise ground-truth labels.

## Completeness policy

Each fixture declares the referenced evidence required for its checked expectations. Extraction classifies the rendered input as:

- `complete`: all required evidence is present;
- `incomplete-irrelevant`: omissions exist but none affect the checked expectation;
- `incomplete-required`: required evidence is missing, ambiguous, unsupported, or capped.

`incomplete-required` never becomes a clear/no-finding result. It produces an explicit incomplete observation and is excluded from semantic pass-rate denominators. Exercise incomplete-required behavior deterministically offline; a paid diagnostic call is allowed only if separately enumerated and counted before the run. Unknown completeness is incomplete.

## Pre-registered semantic gates

Use three repetitions for every live fixture/input-mode scenario and the same production rule definition, fixed rule batch, and DecisionModel path. Rule-batch variation belongs to #15 and is held constant here. For a checked fixture/rule/mode, the mode satisfies its expectation when at least two of three available repetitions land in the pre-registered band.

The declaration-plus-context candidate passes semantic comparison only when all apply:

- At least 10 of the 12 context-required cases satisfy their expected bands, and it exceeds both diff and declaration-only by at least three cases on that subset.
- At least five of six whole-file-dilution cases satisfy their expected bands, and it exceeds whole-file by at least two cases on that subset.
- At least five of six diff-sufficient controls satisfy their expected bands; it is no more than one case worse than the best baseline mode on that subset.
- Across pre-registered clear negative controls, no more than one declaration-plus-context case crosses out of the clear band, and it is no more than one case worse than the best baseline.
- Every checked comparison has three available repetitions after bounded retries. Any missing checked observation makes the milestone inconclusive until rerun within budget; transport failure is not a semantic negative.

Ambiguous/unchecked cases are reported but cannot make a gate pass or fail.

## Latency, size, and paid-call gates

- Separate extraction, rendering, backend, and end-to-end timing. Report cold and warm extraction separately.
- Warm declaration-plus-context extraction p95 must be at most 250 ms on the declared milestone environment, and end-to-end p95 must remain within the configured 1,000 ms per-file deadline. These are milestone gates, not universal SLOs.
- Declaration-plus-context median rendered request bytes must not exceed whole-file median bytes over the checked corpus. Every request must remain within its declared extraction/source-character caps; no cap is promoted to a production default by this experiment.
- The planned matrix is 24 fixtures × 4 input modes × 3 repetitions = 288 logical paid calls when all applicable rules are batched once per input. With at most two transient retries, the absolute maximum is 864 transport attempts.
- Before execution, reconcile calls already spent against the cumulative authorized 1,000-call project budget. Do not start unless the remaining ledger covers the declared maximum. If it does not, respec the matrix or retry policy before any live call; do not silently weaken semantic gates mid-run.
- Record aggregate timing, usage, availability, and request-size evidence only. Do not commit credentials, synthetic source-bearing paid responses, or individual probabilities.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fixture manifest records human-authored expectations/rationales, category membership, required evidence, and stable content identities before live execution.
- [ ] Four versioned renderers produce the defined modes from the same fixture/edit without changing path or domain context.
- [ ] Deterministic offline tests cover rendering, identity/digests, completeness classification, comparison math, retry/call-budget enforcement, missing expectations, and inconclusive outcomes.
- [ ] Declaration-plus-context uses the #5–#8 experiment seam or a separately identified successor without presenting disposable record internals as a production contract.
- [ ] The pre-run plan records exact backend/provider, DecisionModel, rule definitions, renderer versions, repetitions, extraction caps, environment, expected 288 logical calls, absolute retry maximum, and verified remaining authorization.
- [ ] Live execution is an explicit credential-gated milestone and ordinary tests make zero paid calls.
- [ ] The report separates deterministic conformance, transport availability, semantic gates, the held-constant rule-batch identity, incomplete cases, latency, request size/usage, and corpus coverage.
- [ ] The report produces one of `advance-to-production-architecture`, `reject-or-narrow`, or `inconclusive`, with every failed or unmet gate visible.
- [ ] Any later production adoption receives a separate architecture decision plus consent/egress and evaluation-fixture updates.

## Relationship to other work

- Depends on the completed feasibility evidence in #5–#8.
- Reuses the shared fixture/expectation/scenario/observation/comparison/run model in `PRODUCT-RULE-EVALUATION-MODEL.md`.
- Runs alongside Phase F #9–#14 and does not block their current full-file implementation.
- Does not replace #15. Issue #15 evaluates rules and batching under the Phase F full-file contract; this issue isolates input-contract effects.

## Out of scope

- Selecting or integrating a production extractor.
- Expanding repository consent or transmitting new production context.
- Re-reviewing unchanged dependents.
- Other language frontends.
- Choosing permanent context budgets or universal SLOs.
- Treating probabilities as calibrated truth or retroactively changing labels after observing results.

title: Specify the direct-event review pipeline
body:
## Destination

Produce an implementation-ready, normative, host-neutral specification for the product pipeline from a trusted dedicated direct-edit event through stable snapshot capture, semantic extraction, individual Jev evaluation, bounded scheduling, and coherent host advice delivery.

The design remains host-neutral, with Codex and Claude Code as product targets. The initial validation baseline is Codex CLI 0.155.1 on Linux arm64 in headless operation; interactive/headful Codex testing is also planned. These test surfaces do not permanently restrict the architecture. Supported claims must follow actual conformance evidence. The specification must cover:

- dedicated direct-edit events with explicit recipient and canonical-root evidence;
- stable capture of the named current filesystem snapshot;
- one individual Jev request per semantic review unit;
- bounded work/result/advice handling with coherent host delivery;
- truthful failure, staleness, restart, and unsupported-event behavior; and
- a disposable one-off prototype that validates the contract.

The prototype validates the contract and is not production implementation.

## Notes

This is a decision map, not an implementation authorization.

- Use the `grilling` and `domain-modeling` skills for decisions and terminology.
- Use the `prototype` skill for the disposable prototype.
- Use `to-spec` only after the decisions are resolved.
- The prototype runs in a separate worktree from `master`; ordinary validation uses a deterministic fake backend. The later accepted [prototype resolution](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/25#issuecomment-5769310014) superseded the original paid-call prohibition with explicitly bounded paid milestones and sanitized evidence.
- Otherwise-unaccounted shell, unknown-tool, external-process, or human changes are intentionally deferred to [Decide checkpoint reconciliation coverage and mechanism](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/38).
- Broad worker-lifecycle, shell-write, attribution, and declaration-extraction research is retained as advisory evidence and must not be duplicated.
- Direct review work may hold source transiently for extraction and a Jev request. Queues, successful-result reuse, and advice are resident-memory only with accepted crash loss.
- Do not assign, claim, or resolve child tickets while charting.

## Constraints already established

- A dedicated direct-edit event is the fast path and must supply intended-recipient and canonical-root evidence. The product separately captures current eligible source; when available evidence cannot associate the captured review unit and complete logical review input with that recipient, it must not claim attributable review. Root co-location, matching reads, or the latest caller is not attribution.
- Host payloads are supported only through versioned conformance evidence. A tool name, path, or patch is not silently generalized into universal filesystem coverage.
- Stable capture and semantic extraction precede review admission. Incomplete or stale capture is not evidence of a clean review.
- Each semantic review unit gets an individual Jev request; several semantic items are not combined into one request.
- Equivalent queued/running work joins; bounded retained successful results may be reused by complete logical request identity. Failures do not satisfy successful-review identity.
- Queue output is also a queue: warning/advice results are collected and delivered coherently rather than emitted as serial warning chatter.
- Delivery is fire-and-forget unless a host supplies reliable acknowledgement; no model-visible delivery claim is invented.
- Dynamic backend switching, durable replay, exactly-once processing, and production scaling topology are postponed.

## Decisions so far

- [Name the semantic review unit and pipeline vocabulary](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/19): Adopted `Artifact`, `ReviewUnit`, finite recursive reference, `ChangeSet`, `ObservationResult`, `ReviewWorkItem`, `ReviewInput`, `ReviewResult`, and `AdviceBatch` vocabulary with transient source.
- [Research worker lifetime across agent hosts and concurrent sessions](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/32): Source-inspected fresh workers plus file continuity; OpenCode adds a resident map; concurrent isolation and teardown gaps remain advisory inputs.
- [Prototype resident MCP-hook lifecycle on pinned Codex](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/30): Resident MCP memory across edit/Bash/Stop demonstrated; readiness, restart, and shutdown limits retained.
- [Research hook dispatch, worker lifetime, and feedback delivery](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/33): Per-event workers need explicit shared-worker routing; host feedback checkpoints and remaining conformance probes identified.
- [Choose the product process lifetime and hook transport](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/31#issuecomment-5755947269): Command-hook clients idempotently ensure one singleton resident reviewer when simplest; internal state is isolated by explicit recipient and canonical root, with accepted crash loss.
- [Define the unified review-ingress and exact-snapshot deduplication contract](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/20#issuecomment-5755947635): Direct events use shared semantic admission and complete logical-request equality for joining/reuse; checkpoint-specific conclusions moved to the follow-up effort.
- [Define observation origins and host checkpoint triggers](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/21#issuecomment-5755947406): Dedicated direct edits remain the current origin; checkpoint trigger and catch-up conclusions moved to the follow-up effort.
- [Define review scheduling and batched host-delivery semantics](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/23#issuecomment-5755947732): Finite cycles feed recipient/root-partitioned advice; delivery is fire-and-forget, and pending advice may expire by measured relevance age.
- [Research attribution and tenancy patterns across hosts](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/37#issuecomment-5755889943): Borrow detection patterns but reject session-only ownership and unsafe same-root fan-out.
- [Prototype change attribution across concurrent agents and subagents](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/36#issuecomment-5755946932): Direct events can target a captured agent/root; preserve subagent identity and never treat a root as a recipient.
- [Define direct-event completeness, recovery, and concurrency semantics](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/24#issuecomment-5768044770): Direct-event MVP reads only event paths, does not create worktrees, drops unestablished agent-specific advice, and uses bounded recipient/root-partitioned scheduling with truthful lossy recovery.

- [Define Git-ignore-aware file selection and directory exclusions](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/35#issuecomment-5768609945): Direct named paths default to declarative inclusion; repository/nested Git ignores and narrow safety gates exclude before reads, while analyzer applicability—not extension policy—controls semantic review.

- [Prototype the direct-event review pipeline](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/25#issuecomment-5769310014): Validated the bounded direct-event pipeline for the controlled-writer TypeScript/Codex envelope, including two-call live Jev seam and resident-pipeline milestones plus truthful attempted/unacknowledged host delivery.

- [Set the initial supported envelope from prototype evidence](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/26#issuecomment-5769768281): Selected the narrow Codex 0.155.1/Linux arm64/headless controlled-writer TypeScript envelope, provisional tested limits, and rate-limited truthful operational notices.

- [Publish the direct-event review specification](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/27#issuecomment-5769913273): Published [Direct-event review specification v1](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/42) with `ready-for-agent`; final requirements, testing seams, versioned envelope, and evidence limits are ready for implementation handoff.

## Not yet specified

None remaining for this destination. The normative specification is published; implementation and checkpoint reconciliation are subsequent efforts.

## Out of scope

- [Define source-free checkpoint and artifact-index state](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/22): closed without resolution after the user narrowed this destination to direct events; its research and prototype evidence moved to [Decide checkpoint reconciliation coverage and mechanism](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/38).
- Checkpoint reconciliation and claims about otherwise-unaccounted shell, unknown-tool, external-process, or human changes; these are owned by the follow-up effort.
- Agent-addressed advice for unattributed changes in a concurrently shared working root.
- Production implementation.
- Choosing parallel versus durable queues or another production scaling topology.
- Choosing truncation, overflow, or another huge-change strategy.
- Claiming support for host/environment surfaces without conformance evidence.
- Universal interception or mid-command interception.
- Deletion review semantics.
- Source-bearing persistent queues or state.
- Treating a full file as the permanent review unit.
- Dynamic agent/backend switching and mutation-history reconstruction.
- [Specify optional after-tool reconciliation beyond the MVP](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/34): early reconciliation remains a future checkpoint concern.

title: Name the semantic review unit and pipeline vocabulary
body:
## Question

What canonical domain terms and boundaries should the product use from a stable filesystem change through semantic extraction, review scheduling, backend evaluation, and host delivery?

Resolve whether the tentative `TypeShapeReviewUnit` accurately names one root type-shape artifact plus its bounded outbound reference closure, completeness, and snapshot/projection identities. Distinguish at least the stable change set, eligible review-unit set, review work item, rendered review input, backend request, review outcome, advice delivery item, and host advice batch.

Use the existing glossary and declaration-extraction/input-contract evidence. The input-contract comparison ended `reject-or-narrow`; do not silently authorize declaration-oriented production input while naming the seam.

title: Define the unified review-ingress and exact-snapshot deduplication contract
body:
## Question

What host-neutral contract lets dedicated direct-edit observations and checkpoint-reconciled changes converge through one review ingress without losing changes or reviewing the same semantic snapshot twice?

Decide the ingress identity and idempotency rules. Deduplication must consider exact snapshot and review-projection identity rather than suppressing work solely by path, tool name, origin, or event ID. A later distinct snapshot at a path already touched by an edit tool must remain eligible.

title: Define observation origins and host checkpoint triggers
body:
## Question

Which canonical host-neutral observation origins and checkpoint trigger classes does the product specify, and how does the initial Codex adapter map its lifecycle events to them?

Cover the fast dedicated-edit boundary, optional early reconciliation after potentially mutating or unknown tool events, and an authoritative Stop catch-up boundary. Host events say when to reconcile, not which paths changed. Preserve the bounded Codex 0.155.1 evidence and state unsupported gaps explicitly.

title: Define source-free checkpoint and artifact-index state
body:
## Question

What source-free persisted checkpoint metadata is sufficient to compare complete stable file snapshots across host-hook invocations without becoming a durable review-work log?

Decide worktree/session/policy identity, checkpoint and manifest identities, optional per-artifact identities and projection fingerprints used for comparison, baseline/reset behavior, atomic retention, and validation. Persist hashes, identities, omissions, statuses, and bounded metadata only. This state records completed observations; it does not persist queues, requests, results, advice, or pending work, and it does not regenerate reviews lost on restart. Never copy source into checkpoint state; source may exist transiently for extraction and a backend request.

title: Define review scheduling and batched host-delivery semantics
body:
## Question

What logical work-queue and result/advice-queue contract preserves prompt single-item review while preventing serial backend-call/agent-warning chatter during bursts?

Each semantic review unit must remain an individual Jev request. A single due item must not wait for a quota. Decide throttling and dispatch-cycle semantics, when completed results flush to the host, how queue quiescence and host deadlines interact, and how the current globally budgeted single Codex response is preserved or versioned. Do not choose parallelism, truncation, or a huge-change scaling strategy in this ticket.

## Established constraints

- Both the review-work queue and result/advice queue are in-memory and nonpersistent.
- Queue capacities are hardcoded, not user-configurable.
- Capacity must be bounded by both item count and retained bytes; a bounded item count alone does not bound transient source memory.
- Queue-full behavior is explicit; work is never silently dropped, allowed to grow without bound, or spilled into source-bearing persistent storage.
- Crash/recovery restart may lose queued, running, cached, or completed-but-undelivered review work. Source-free reconciliation state does not regenerate it. Routine idle cleanup, client timeout, or ordinary shutdown must not silently discard suggestions.

## Process-boundary follow-through

Apply [Choose the product process lifetime and hook transport](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/31). Specify admission ownership, collecting advice through subsequent command-hook replies, and bounded Stop collection. Resolve how pending work/advice survives ordinary pauses and how final delivery works at normal host shutdown when the Stop deadline expires. A quiet host is not necessarily gone. Do not equate returning bytes over IPC with proven model-visible delivery. Keep this compatible with in-memory queues and accepted crash loss.

## Evaluation-reuse follow-through

Apply [Define the unified review-ingress and exact-snapshot deduplication contract](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/20#issuecomment-5754603126). Specify bounded successful-result cache retention and how joined or cached evaluations feed advice delivery, including a restored earlier snapshot whose advice was already delivered versus advice still pending. Evaluation reuse does not itself authorize repeated advice or dropping pending advice; cache eviction must not silently discard pending advice.

title: Define direct-event completeness, recovery, and concurrency semantics
body:
## Question

What minimal state machine and externally visible guidance keep attributable direct-event capture, semantic extraction, review scheduling, and host advice truthful under unstable reads, concurrent writers, duplicate or out-of-order events, process interruption, reviewer restart, backend failure, stale snapshots, relevance expiry, and bounded-resource rejection?

Specify the truth boundaries for captured, incomplete, pending, reviewed, stale, expired, skipped, unavailable, rejected, and delivered-or-unacknowledged outcomes. These are advisory meanings, not a mandatory closed enum or TypeScript representation. No unstable or stale evidence may be reported as clean or delivered as current advice.

## Process and tenancy follow-through

Apply [Choose the product process lifetime and hook transport](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/31#issuecomment-5755947269) and [Prototype change attribution across concurrent agents and subagents](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/36#issuecomment-5755946932): command-hook clients idempotently ensure one singleton resident reviewer when simplest; many concurrent starts produce one process. Partition bounded work, results, and advice by explicit recipient and canonical working root. Preserve subagent identity when supplied and never infer ownership from the latest caller.

A direct event is eligible for agent-addressed advice only when host evidence identifies the intended recipient/root for the exact current snapshot. Define stable capture, duplicate/out-of-order handling, late-result applicability checks, crash-loss/reset behavior, and bounded admission without introducing durable replay or an exactly-once system.

## Scheduling and cleanup follow-through

Apply [Define review scheduling and batched host-delivery semantics](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/23#issuecomment-5755947732). Use fire-and-forget host delivery. Pending advice may expire after an evidence-selected relevance age even while a host is quiet; expiry does not prove delivery or closure. Exact-snapshot staleness retires advice immediately. Keep failure recovery simple: bounded attempts followed by an explicit unavailable outcome; rerunning and losing advice are acceptable.

Inactive singleton tenant state may be removed after all work, advice, and resources are gone, subject to bounded cleanup. Do not require post-exit collection, guaranteed final drain, or proof of model-visible delivery.

Checkpoint reconciliation and claims about otherwise-unaccounted filesystem changes are owned by [Decide checkpoint reconciliation coverage and mechanism](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/38), not this ticket.

title: Prototype the direct-event review pipeline
body:
## Question

Does a disposable end-to-end prototype validate the resolved attributable direct-event capture, semantic extraction, individual Jev-request, singleton-tenancy, bounded scheduling, applicability revalidation, and coherent host-delivery contracts within a candidate supported envelope?

Build and run a one-off deterministic prototype in a dedicated development worktree from `master`, using a fake backend and no paid Jev calls. The development worktree isolates this disposable experiment; creating or requiring worktrees is not product behavior. This is a HITL prototype, not production implementation.

## Direct-event boundary and capture cases

Exercise the versioned Codex direct-event candidate: a successful `PostToolUse` event for native `apply_patch` on the pinned validation surface. Treat the event's Add/Update path headers as candidate-path and attribution evidence, not as authoritative post-image bytes or a universal changed-line set. A declared deletion is skipped/out of scope; recreated paths are not treated as deleted output. Pure rename/move syntax, metadata-only changes, Bash/shell writes, external writes, and checkpoint catch-up are unsupported by this direct-event contract.

Read only eligible event-named paths, subject to [Define Git-ignore-aware file selection and directory exclusions](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/35). Validate stable repeated capture, one- and multi-file events, malformed or nonregular paths, missing and recreated paths, repeated and out-of-order events, concurrent writers, and interruption. Multi-file paths have independent capture/extraction outcomes; independently valid units may proceed without claiming the whole observation was complete.

Explicitly exercise the same-artifact race: if another writer replaces the artifact before first capture and the available evidence cannot establish that the captured unit belongs to the event's recipient, do not reinterpret the current bytes as that recipient's review. Report it as unsupported, unavailable, or skipped rather than clean. Matching reads establish stable observed bytes, not writer identity.

## Semantic identity and publication cases

Extract independently identifiable `ReviewUnit`s with their finite supporting evidence. Each unit receives one logical Jev evaluation. Use the complete canonical logical `ReviewInput`—including rule content and input-contract context—as pending-work and successful-result-reuse identity. Source and projection fingerprints are equality evidence, not substitutes for the complete identity. A distinct file snapshot may still render the same logical request and join/reuse it; failures never satisfy successful-review identity.

Before publication, re-read and re-extract the relevant path/unit and revalidate the complete logical `ReviewInput`, including applicable rules and input-contract evidence. Do not use whole-file equality as the normative freshness rule, and do not publish when semantic identity or supporting evidence cannot be established. Confirm that an unrelated sibling-artifact edit need not stale an otherwise identical review input, while a relevant artifact/evidence change retires the old result.

## Singleton reviewer, attribution, and host conformance

Validate command-hook clients idempotently ensuring one singleton resident reviewer per operating-system user/machine when that is the simplest implementation. A large concurrent ensure-running stress case must converge on one owner. Internally isolate admission, work, successful-result reuse, pending advice, and cleanup by explicit advice recipient and canonical working root; apply both global and per-partition bounds. Preserve subagent identity when supplied. Root co-location and the latest caller never substitute for a recipient.

Exercise simultaneous startup, missing initialization, stale endpoints, obsolete-lifetime messages, concurrent clients, bounded readiness/retries, uncertain IPC, client timeout without cancellation of accepted work, real reviewer restart with accepted crash loss, safe cleanup only after work/advice/resources are gone, and lazy restart. Exact lock and IPC mechanisms belong to the prototype.

Keep Codex CLI 0.155.1/Linux arm64/headless as the initial live baseline and add interactive/headful evidence if available. Exercise separate existing worktrees as distinct canonical roots without implying that the product creates worktrees. Claude Code remains a design target requiring a named version and independent conformance evidence.

## Scheduling, capacity, and advice cases

Validate immediate single-item dispatch, finite dispatch cycles, a fixed backend worker bound, independent per-unit backend requests, queued/running joining protected from cache eviction, bounded successful-result reuse, and deterministic selection of one count-and-byte-bounded combined advice response per host interaction.

Capacity accounting must cover global and per-recipient/root item and retained-byte limits across capture, extraction, queued/running inputs, duplicate bookkeeping, promised outcome reservations, successful-result reuse, and pending advice. Admission failure is explicit. Accepted fresh outcomes are not arbitrarily evicted; formatter overflow remains pending subject to the established bounds.

Validate applicability retirement, evidence-selected pending-advice relevance expiry (including a candidate near ten minutes), bounded backend attempts followed by explicit unavailable outcomes, fire-and-forget host submission, and truthful attempted/unacknowledged delivery. A hook timeout is not reviewer death. Do not build durable replay, exactly-once processing, acknowledgement requirements, hidden retries, final-drain guarantees, or a status-history system.

## Evidence boundary

Keep deterministic fake-backend tests separate from actual host-visible conformance evidence. Measure startup/readiness, capture stability, extraction and evaluation latency, capacity, response bounds, expiry candidates, and delivery observations needed by [Set the initial supported envelope from prototype evidence](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/26). Preserve reproducible fixtures and sanitized evidence without credentials, source-bearing paid responses, or unsupported model-visible-delivery claims.

The earlier observation-baseline/checkpoint test handoff in this issue's comments is historical and superseded for this direct-event prototype. Checkpoint scanning, baselines, otherwise-unaccounted changes, and shell/external catch-up are owned by [Decide checkpoint reconciliation coverage and mechanism](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/38) and must not be smuggled into this prototype.



## File-selection and analyzer-applicability follow-through

Apply [Define Git-ignore-aware file selection and directory exclusions](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/35#issuecomment-5768609945). The direct event supplies candidate paths, so the declarative default includes named paths unless excluded; it does not walk directories or use a global language/extension allowlist. Exercise repository and nested `.gitignore`, tracked matching files, `.env`/`.env.*`, permanent `node_modules` exclusion (better safe than sorry), containment/regular-file/symlink gates, explicit product globs, and allowed `build`/`dist`/`generated`/`vendor` names. Prove excluded content has zero source reads and zero backend calls.

Keep analyzer applicability after bounded stable capture. Exercise unrelated extensions, obvious binary input, no applicable analyzer, and contained parser/probe failure. These cases must not crash, enqueue backend work, emit agent-visible advice, or consume advice tokens; bounded local diagnostics may record them, and independent files continue. Do not turn this direct-event test into checkpoint traversal; filesystem discovery is owned by the checkpoint-reconciliation map.

title: Set the initial supported envelope from prototype evidence
body:
## Question

Given the completed decisions, research, and disposable direct-event prototype evidence, what exact versioned host/environment/workload/attribution envelope may the specification call supported, and how must unsupported or out-of-envelope work be reported?

Set claims only for surfaces actually exercised. At minimum, decide and record:

- agent host, exact version, operating system/architecture, and headless versus interactive/headful mode;
- the native direct-event and payload forms accepted by the adapter, including proven Add/Update and multi-file behavior and explicit deletion, rename/move, shell/external-write, metadata-only, malformed, and missing-path boundaries;
- file-selection policy from [Define Git-ignore-aware file selection and directory exclusions](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/35), supported file kinds/sizes, semantic artifact shapes, evidence-closure bounds, and input-contract/rule identity;
- stable-capture and same-artifact concurrent-writer limits, including cases where matching reads cannot establish that the observed bytes belong to the event's recipient;
- recipient, subagent, canonical-root, same-root concurrency, and separate-existing-worktree evidence without treating a root as a recipient or claiming that the product creates worktrees;
- singleton startup/readiness, client timeout, restart/crash-loss, obsolete-lifetime rejection, cleanup, global and per-partition capacity, concurrency, latency, cache, pending-advice, response, and relevance-expiry bounds; and
- what host submission was observed, distinguishing fire-and-forget attempted/unacknowledged delivery from any model-visible-delivery claim.

Support claims must use the domain contract's actual truth boundary. A direct event supplies candidate paths and recipient/root evidence; the product separately captures and extracts the current eligible source. If available evidence cannot associate the captured `ReviewUnit` and complete logical `ReviewInput` with that recipient, do not claim attributable review. Do not use path, whole-file equality, tool name, event ID, source fingerprint, or projection fingerprint alone as complete review identity.

Name incomplete, skipped, rejected, unavailable, stale, expired, attempted/unacknowledged, and unsupported outcomes honestly. Do not claim universal interception, exact writer attribution under an unobservable overwrite race, model-visible delivery without evidence, or clean review after partial/unstable capture.

## Scope clarification

The validated envelope is a conformance claim, not a permanent architectural restriction. The design remains host-neutral with Claude Code and Codex targets. Start with Codex CLI 0.155.1/Linux arm64/headless evidence, add planned interactive/headful testing when available, and name every untested host or mode explicitly. Claude Code requires its own named version and independent evidence; architectural intent is not support.

Checkpoint reconciliation, observation baselines, Stop/shell/external catch-up, and otherwise-unaccounted-change support claims belong to [Decide checkpoint reconciliation coverage and mechanism](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/38).



## File-selection and analyzer-applicability evidence

The supported envelope must apply [Define Git-ignore-aware file selection and directory exclusions](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/35#issuecomment-5768609945) and distinguish named-path selection from semantic analyzer applicability. Do not state a global extension allowlist. Record evidence for nested `.gitignore`, tracked matching paths, permanent protected gates, configured narrowing globs, unrelated extensions, obvious binary input, no applicable analyzer, and contained malformed-input/analyzer failure. Unsupported or failed applicability remains quiet to the agent and produces no backend request; diagnostics may expose the reason without consuming advice tokens.

title: Publish the direct-event review specification
body:
## Question

Publish the resolved direct-event map as an implementation-ready normative specification using `to-spec`, including the accepted testing seams, disposable prototype evidence, and versioned supported envelope.

The specification must clearly separate:

- the host-neutral direct-event domain contract and invariants;
- versioned host-adapter mappings and their conformance evidence;
- measured/evidence-selected supported-envelope parameters versus configurable policy;
- normative requirements versus non-normative implementation guidance; and
- deterministic fake-backend verification from live host-visible evidence.

Carry forward the final decision vocabulary and supersessions. In particular, specify event-named eligible-path capture rather than repository-wide scanning; recipient/root evidence without treating the root as a recipient; unsupported same-artifact attribution races; one `ReviewUnit` per individual Jev request; complete canonical logical `ReviewInput` identity for joining/reuse; relevant-unit and complete-input publication revalidation without a whole-file fallback; globally and per-partition bounded in-memory scheduling/advice; fire-and-forget attempted/unacknowledged delivery; and truthful lossy restart, rejection, staleness, expiry, and unsupported-event behavior.

Use the pinned mutually compatible Effect 4 RC cohort and the provider-neutral `Decision` / `DecisionModel` API with `@effect/ai-typesafe` as implementation constraints. The vendored historical client is evidence only, not a production dependency. Apply `ready-for-agent` to the published specification.

Do not implement production support in this task. Do not include checkpoint reconciliation, observation baselines, Stop/shell/external catch-up, source-bearing persistence, dynamic backend switching, universal interception, or other requirements owned by [Decide checkpoint reconciliation coverage and mechanism](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/38) or later efforts.



## File-selection contract to publish

The specification must incorporate [Define Git-ignore-aware file selection and directory exclusions](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/35#issuecomment-5768609945): permissive declarative named-path selection for direct events, repository/nested `.gitignore`, the accepted narrow safety floor, no global extension allowlist, and quiet analyzer-owned applicability/failure. It must keep checkpoint traversal semantics in the separate checkpoint-reconciliation effort.

title: Define review-unit pipeline vocabulary
body:

- define the canonical artifact, observation, review-unit, work-item, input, result, and advice-batch vocabulary

Supports #19.

title: Prototype resident MCP-hook lifecycle on pinned Codex
body:
## Question

Can Codex CLI 0.155.1 on the declared Linux arm64/headless surface deliver multiple lifecycle events through `mcp_tool` hooks to one already-connected, resident product-style MCP server process?

Build a disposable one-off conformance probe in a separate worktree from `master`. Record sanitized process identity, event order, connection/server lifetime, startup readiness, synchronous response delivery, timeout/failure behavior, and session-end behavior across at least direct edit, Bash, and Stop events. Compare only against the already-proven fresh-child command-hook behavior. Make no paid Jev calls, retain no source/transcript/credentials, and do not implement the production integration.

The prototype answers host/process facts only; it does not select the product architecture.

title: Choose the product process lifetime and hook transport
body:
## Question

What product process lifetime and Codex hook transport should the initial supported integration use so the lifetime of queues, caches, in-flight work, and checkpoint comparison state is explicit?

Choose among the proven one-shot command-hook CLI, a one-shot hook client connected to a resident product daemon, a resident MCP server reached through `mcp_tool` hooks, or an app-server-adjacent integration. Decide who starts and stops the product process, its session/worktree scope, how synchronous advice returns to the host, and what a process failure loses.

Use [Research: Codex hook and product process lifetime](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/blob/master/RESEARCH-CODEX-HOOK-PROCESS-LIFETIME-2026-09-20.md) and the pinned-version MCP lifecycle prototype. Do not choose checkpoint persistence or durable work semantics before this process boundary is selected.

## Resume context

Start with the [current discussion handoff](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/31#issuecomment-5754366916): settled feedback/crash-loss constraints, completed evidence, remaining process ownership and transport choices, proposed probe, and workspace pointers. Earlier durable-queue recommendations are not accepted architecture.

title: Research Abide lifetime across agent hosts and concurrent sessions
body:
## Question

How does Abide manage process and state lifetime across Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode, including separate or concurrent agents/sessions, restart, and cleanup? Which narrow lifetime patterns can inform the product process-boundary decision?

This is the user-requested expansion of the previous Abide research: reuse the existing competitor report and investigate lifetime and multi-agent behavior only. Use Luna Max research, primary source citations, the repository research methodology, and separate source class from verification state. Findings are advisory and do not choose the product architecture. No paid Jev calls.

title: Research hook dispatch, worker lifetime, and feedback delivery
body:
## Question

For pinned Codex CLI 0.155.1 and an explicitly identified Claude Code documentation/version surface, how do sequential and parallel edit/tool calls become hook invocations, how long may those workers live, and when can their feedback reach the agent?

Distinguish multiple matching handlers, multiple tool calls, and one multi-file tool call. Establish synchronous/async waiting, timeout/cancellation/session shutdown, existing-worker routing, and feedback delivery while active or idle. Investigate whether a worker may drain shared pending work, and what coordination is product-owned. Examine session initialization plus lazy ensure-running on any hook as a resident-worker option without assuming built-in singleton management.

Use primary-source research with source class separate from verification state. Reuse existing Abide lifetime and pinned MCP evidence. No paid Jev calls. This resolves host facts, not architecture, queue durability, or SQLite choice. Capture unknowns and the smallest conformance probe needed.

## Task scope and prior planning

## Question

For a version after the MVP, should supported host hooks trigger early checkpoint reconciliation after potentially mutating or unknown tool completions, including failed tools that may already have written files?

Specify which host events qualify, evidence required for each adapter, scan frequency/coalescing and cost, and how checks reuse the existing file-selection policy and unified review ingress. Keep host events as timing signals, not changed-path authority. Do not introduce another review queue merely for this trigger.

## Context

Deferred explicitly by the user while resolving [Define observation origins and host checkpoint triggers](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/21). The MVP uses dedicated-edit hooks and a host-neutral turn-completion catch-up checkpoint. This is a future specification task, outside the current map; it does not authorize implementation.

title: Define Git-ignore-aware file selection and directory exclusions
body:
## Question

Should the product honor Git ignore rules by default when selecting files named by dedicated direct-edit observations, and how should that interact with explicit product includes/excludes and protected safety gates?

The user explicitly rejected universal hard exclusions based only on directory names such as `build`, `coverage`, `dist`, `generated`, `target`, or `vendor`: users may legitimately place source there and own the cost of an overly broad policy. The exact mandatory safety floor for `.git`, `node_modules`, sensitive paths, nonregular files, and repository boundaries remains to be decided rather than inferred here.

Resolve repository and nested `.gitignore` files, tracked files matching ignore patterns, repository-local/global Git excludes, explicit opt-in for ignored source, behavior outside Git, user responsibility for expensive selections, and safe directory pruning. Excluded content must not be read or submitted for review.

Update the direct-event specification and prototype expectations after this decision is accepted. Checkpoint-specific policy consistency is owned by [Decide checkpoint reconciliation coverage and mechanism](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/38). This ticket does not authorize production implementation.

title: Prototype change attribution across concurrent agents and subagents
body:
## Question

Can the product attribute dedicated edits and checkpoint-discovered otherwise-unaccounted changes to the correct agent process or subagent when concurrent agents share a working root, so advice is delivered only to the intended recipient?

Use a disposable prototype in a separate worktree with a deterministic fake backend and real agent-host runs. Exercise a parent agent plus subagent and concurrent agents producing distinct changes X and Y in one working root. Record the identity fields and event boundaries available for direct edits, shell or external writes, and checkpoint reconciliation; determine whether X, Y, or X+Y can be attributed and safely delivered. Compare same-root and separate-worktree cases. No paid Jev calls.

Also provide a single self-contained logic-prototype HTML file that exposes the observed attribution states and lets a human drive ambiguous and attributable scenarios. The answer must state the safe MVP boundary, including whether unattributed reconciliation must be postponed or restricted.

title: Research Abide attribution and tenancy patterns across hosts
body:
## Question

What technical patterns does Abide use across its Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode integrations to attribute direct edits, shell or checkpoint-discovered changes, state, and feedback to the correct session, agent or subagent, repository/worktree, and advice recipient under concurrent activity?

Inspect pinned and current primary source, tests, and official host contracts. Determine whether Abide has a reusable solution for singleton or per-worker tenancy, concurrent agents sharing one working root, unattributed filesystem changes, queue/result ownership, ambiguity handling, and recipient selection. Classify each relevant pattern as BORROW, DEPEND ON, OPTIONAL INTEGRATION, or REJECT. Keep documentation/source claims separate from runtime evidence, avoid repeating the broad competitor review, and name the exact prototype gaps.

title: Decide checkpoint reconciliation coverage and mechanism
body:

Incomplete checkpoint decision map. #39 owns human review of the retained prototype; #40 owns the coverage promise, followed by #41 selection/traversal. #34 is the separately deferred optional after-tool trigger. Produce an implementation-ready, host-neutral decision and specification for whether and how the product discovers otherwise-unaccounted working-tree changes beyond trusted direct-edit events. Decide exact versus explicitly best-effort catch-up, validate the chosen authority, and state truthful coverage, restart, and degradation boundaries.

## Decisions so far

<!-- Empty until a child decision is resolved. -->
