title: Direct-event review specification v1
body:
## Problem Statement

Coding agents need useful review of the semantic units they edit without waiting for every backend evaluation. Current direct-edit evidence names candidate paths and an intended recipient; it does not supply authoritative final source or prove authorship under concurrent overwrites. The product needs an implementation-ready contract that provides bounded, attributable, current advice and reports uncertainty honestly.

This is the normative **Direct-event review specification v1**, published from [Publish the direct-event review specification](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/27) and the resolved map [Specify the direct-event review pipeline](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/18). “Must” and “must not” are requirements. The initial supported profile below is versioned separately from the host-neutral contract. Prototype evidence establishes feasibility within its recorded limits; it does not establish that production support already exists.

## Solution

Short-lived agent-host command-hook clients idempotently reach a resident reviewer. A trusted direct-edit observation supplies named paths and explicit recipient/root evidence. The reviewer selects eligible paths, captures stable current bytes, extracts independently reviewable semantic units, evaluates each unit through Jev, and retains bounded advice for the earliest supported host reply. Before handoff it revalidates the relevant unit, rules, and complete review input. Ordinary editing continues after bounded admission.

Jev is TypeSafe's external backend. The product is the host-neutral review integration; agent hosts own their tool loops. Codex and Claude Code are design targets. Only the specific Codex profile below has accepted conformance evidence. Model-provider metadata does not define the adapter set.

## User Stories

1. As an agent user, I want ordinary edits to continue promptly, so that review latency does not block my workflow.
2. As an agent, I want one coherent bounded response, so that review feedback does not arrive as repetitive warning chatter.
3. As an agent user, I want each changed semantic unit evaluated independently, so that unrelated declarations are not combined into a single judgment.
4. As a repository owner, I want only event-named candidate paths captured, so that direct review does not scan my repository.
5. As a repository owner, I want repository and nested Git ignores honored, so that ignored untracked content stays out of review.
6. As a repository owner, I want tracked matching files to follow Git's tracked-file semantics, so that ignore patterns do not unexpectedly disable their review.
7. As a user, I want my exclusions preserved across configuration layers, so that project configuration cannot weaken them.
8. As a user, I want sensitive, administrative, dependency, symlink, and outside-root paths excluded before source reads, so that selection enforces the agreed safety floor.
9. As a user, I want language applicability owned by analyzers, so that file selection does not impose a global extension allowlist.
10. As an agent, I want unrelated or unparseable input to be quiet, so that it consumes no advice tokens or backend calls.
11. As a user, I want unstable capture reported truthfully, so that partial bytes are never mistaken for a clean review.
12. As a user editing several files, I want independent valid paths to proceed, so that one failed path does not suppress them.
13. As an agent, I want advice addressed to my explicit identity and working root, so that another agent's results do not leak into my context.
14. As a subagent user, I want child identity preserved, so that sharing a root does not redirect advice to a parent.
15. As a concurrent user, I want unsupported attribution races acknowledged, so that matching reads are not presented as proof of authorship.
16. As a user, I want equivalent pending work to join, so that duplicate events do not multiply evaluations or pending advice.
17. As a user, I want bounded reuse of successful complete inputs, so that restoring a previously reviewed unit can avoid another paid call.
18. As an agent, I want relevant changes to invalidate old advice while unrelated sibling changes preserve it, so that feedback stays applicable.
19. As an operator, I want global and per-recipient/root count and byte limits, so that bursts cannot create unbounded logical state.
20. As an agent, I want capacity rejection and backend failure distinguished from a clean result, so that missing review is visible when appropriate.
21. As an agent, I want repeated operational notices rate-limited, so that persistent failures do not flood my context.
22. As an agent, I want excess fresh advice retained for later replies, so that formatting limits do not silently discard it.
23. As a user, I want stale and expired advice suppressed, so that old recommendations are not delivered as current.
24. As an operator, I want simultaneous hook clients to converge on one resident owner, so that startup races do not duplicate reviewers.
25. As a user, I want accepted resident work to survive a hook-client timeout, so that client lifetime does not cancel owned work.
26. As a user, I accept losing suggestions on actual reviewer restart, so that the product can keep work and advice in memory.
27. As an operator, I want obsolete-lifetime messages rejected and reservations released, so that restart and failure cannot mix old state with new work.
28. As an agent user, I want delivery described as attempted/unacknowledged when that is all the host proves, so that submission is not confused with model visibility.
29. As a repository owner, I want source egress to retain explicit repository/backend consent, so that a new pipeline cannot bypass my existing approval boundary.
30. As an implementer, I want deterministic offline tests and separately recorded live evidence, so that ordinary validation is reproducible and support claims remain traceable.
31. As an operator, I want exact host versions and operating limits stated, so that architectural intent is not confused with tested support.

## Implementation Decisions

### Domain contract and ownership

- An `Artifact` is an independently identifiable semantic subject; the initial kind is `typeShape`. A `ReviewUnit` contains one root artifact and its finite recursive supporting evidence. Reference states are expanded, included, or omitted; the root is not its own reference, and a back-edge to it is included. Missing required evidence is incomplete.
- A `ChangeObservation` is raw change evidence. A `Snapshot` is transient captured source. A complete `ChangeSet` exists only after complete stable observation; empty complete sets are valid. Partial multi-file success must remain independent path/unit outcomes within an incomplete `ObservationResult`, never a complete parent `ChangeSet`.
- A `ReviewWorkItem` freezes a unit with its available observation, rule-set, and input-contract context. Independent path success does not require inventing a complete parent change set. Queue position and mutable runtime state are separate from this value.
- `ReviewInput` is the complete canonical logical input to evaluation. `ReviewResult` describes an actual evaluated work item; backend transport responses remain internal. Results may contribute to an `AdviceBatch`, which is a bounded host handoff attempt.
- Source and projection fingerprints are equality evidence. Neither alone substitutes for the complete logical input. No universal status enum, permanent per-event record, or new domain wrapper is required simply to name an implementation stage.
- The host adapter translates native events into the canonical observation. Core capture/extraction/scheduling must not parse Codex patch syntax. Recipient identity includes host/session/agent dimensions as needed, preserving a supplied subagent identity. Internal work, joins, successful reuse, advice, and notice state are isolated by explicit recipient and canonical Git working root. A root is never a recipient; missing identity never inherits the latest caller.

### Selection, capture, and attribution

- Direct observations supply candidate paths. Capture must read only eligible named source paths and relevant supporting evidence on revalidation; it must not walk or recursively expand candidate directories. Reading applicable ignore/configuration metadata does not authorize source discovery. Existing worktrees have distinct canonical roots; the product does not create them or require their use.
- The declarative default includes named paths unless excluded. User/project includes may narrow selection; the highest-precedence include list replaces inherited lists, while exclusions accumulate and always win. Negated product re-inclusion cannot undo exclusions.
- Apply repository and nested `.gitignore` with Git pattern/nesting and tracked-file semantics. Tracked matching files remain eligible; ignored untracked files are skipped. Do not load `.git/info/exclude` or global `core.excludesFile` for this profile. Ordinary includes cannot opt ignored source back in. Non-Git roots are unsupported.
- Before source reads, enforce regular nonsymlink files within the canonical root, reject symlink traversal and Git administrative paths, exclude `.env` and `.env.*` basenames, and exclude every path under a `node_modules` segment. Includes cannot override these gates. `build`, `coverage`, `dist`, `generated`, `target`, and `vendor` names have no universal exclusion. Excluded content must have zero source reads and zero backend calls.
- Use conservative Effect-scoped bounded capture with repeated content/hash and metadata agreement. Mid-capture mutation, deletion/recreation, missing/nonregular paths, cancellation, and unstable capture must not create mixed or partial review evidence. Each candidate has an independent outcome. Declared deletion stays unsupported even if its path has since been recreated; unsupported move syntax must not cause capture of the wrong path.
- The text boundary supports bounded UTF-8, including a UTF-8 BOM, and rejects NUL/obvious binary input. Analyzers own further probing and parsing and must contain failures on arbitrary bounded input. No applicable analyzer or contained applicability/parse failure creates no backend work, agent advice, or advice-token consumption. Bounded local diagnostics are optional.
- Stable matching reads establish observed bytes, not the writer. The supported profile requires an explicit controlled-writer condition. If the captured unit and complete input cannot be associated with the intended recipient, no recipient-specific recommendation may be produced. Invisible same-artifact overwrites are outside the claimed envelope; a later attributable direct event can create its own work. There is no hidden retry or whole-file fallback for uncertain semantic identity.

### Evaluation, identity, and publication

- One independently selected `ReviewUnit` receives one individual Jev request, containing its root and bounded required evidence. Multiple roots must not be combined into a single request; a request may evaluate the applicable Noul rules for that one unit.
- Canonical equality covers the unit and supporting evidence, relevant path/domain payload, completeness and versioned input-contract context, immutable rule content, and evaluation interpretation used by the contract. Transport/event IDs and queue bookkeeping do not create distinct evaluations. The retained prototype's same-file named-type contract and live renderer are the baseline evidence; adopting another rendering/extraction contract requires a distinct identity and new conformance evidence.
- Within a recipient/root partition, check queued/running equality before reserving another evaluation. Equivalent requests join; duplicate bookkeeping itself stays bounded. Pending joins must remain valid regardless of successful-cache eviction. Different whole-file snapshots may render the same complete input and join/reuse; matching path or unchanged root text alone is insufficient.
- Retain successful evaluations in a bounded memory-only cache, including successful clear results. Failures, malformed responses, rejection, and incomplete work are never successful reuse entries. Cache eviction permits later reevaluation but must not evict independent pending advice. No unbounded delivered-history registry is required.
- For A → B → A, retire A advice when B makes it inapplicable; a retained successful A evaluation may be reused when complete input A returns, making advice eligible again even if previously submitted. A missing cache entry permits reevaluation. Joined observations of the same currently pending input must not multiply advice.
- Immediately before publication/handoff, recheck selection and re-read/re-extract the relevant path/unit and supporting evidence; revalidate current rules and complete canonical input. Unrelated sibling/comment edits may preserve applicability. Relevant unit/evidence/rule/contract changes retire the old result. Unknown semantic identity is unavailable/skipped, with no whole-file equality fallback. Late superseded results must not become current advice. Revalidation cannot guarantee freshness after handoff.
- Use TypeScript with exact compatible Effect `4.0.0-rc.116` pins for `effect` and companion packages, including testing/provider packages. Integrate through provider-neutral `Decision` / `DecisionModel`, `Decision.probability` for the initial Noul rules, and `@effect/ai-typesafe`. The vendored historical client remains evidence only. Validate expected decision keys and finite in-range probabilities before accepting a result. A clear result requires successful evaluation with adequate evidence; it emits no empty advice.
- Preserve repository/backend source-egress consent from the existing ADR: user-owned consent for the canonical repository and fixed Jev destination, never self-granted by project configuration. The existing digest-confirmed enable flow and dispatch-time grant recheck remain required. Do not bypass revocation when moving evaluation into a resident process. Dynamic backend switching is excluded.

### Scheduling, capacity, advice, and lifecycle

- Use short-lived command-hook clients and an idempotently ensured singleton reviewer per operating-system user/machine when simplest. Initialization may eagerly start it; subsequent hooks must also ensure it. Concurrent starters converge on one owner. Owner election and local IPC are cross-process responsibilities; Effect coordination alone does not supply them.
- Bound startup/readiness and genuinely transient retries. Stale endpoints must not displace a live owner. An IPC timeout is not proof of reviewer death. Accepted work belongs to the resident lifetime, independently of the client request; a timeout or client exit alone does not cancel it.
- Maintain bounded keyed FIFO work and recipient/root advice state. An idle lone item dispatches promptly. Select finite dispatch cycles; later arrivals belong to a later cycle and cannot extend the existing cycle indefinitely. Enforce the fixed backend concurrency bound.
- Apply both global and per-partition item/retained-byte accounting across ingress, capture/extraction reservations, queued/running input, duplicate bookkeeping, success reuse, promised outcomes, notices, and pending advice. Reserve enforceably bounded outcome space before admission; unknown backend output cannot be assumed to fit. Reject explicitly when admission would exceed a bound. Release reservations and joins on every terminal path. Bound transport frames/connections separately before recipient decoding.
- Accepted fresh outcomes must not be arbitrarily evicted for normal capacity pressure. Stale retirement, relevance expiry, explicit cancellation/failure, actual host closure, and reviewer restart are allowed loss boundaries. This contract bounds logical retained payload, not JavaScript/native-parser RSS. Prototype pre-decode buffers do not establish complete per-recipient accounting.
- Ordinary collection becomes eligible when its finite cycle completes or the oldest pending result in that dispatch cycle reaches the maximum advice-wait age, whichever is first. New arrivals do not reset that age. Eligibility does not manufacture a host reply opportunity. Return one deterministic, globally budgeted batch at the earliest supported reply; let older eligible advice progress. Count and encoded-response bytes include operational notices. Excess eligible advice remains pending subject to prior admission bounds. A zero finding budget is not successful delivery.
- The Codex successor adapter supports asynchronous resident admission and later collection. A supported Bash hook may collect already pending advice; Bash never supplies direct-review paths. Bounded ready-only turn-end collection, where mapped, must not wait for queue quiescence or deny/extend turn completion. It adds no Stop-based observation or catch-up requirement. Final drain is not guaranteed.
- Handoff is fire-and-forget, `attempted-unacknowledged` without reliable acknowledgement. Failed/uncertain IPC is not delivered; response bytes are not proof the model saw or acted on advice. No delivery retry or exactly-once protocol is required. Optional reliable acknowledgement must not broaden evidence claims for this profile.
- Advice expires at age greater than or equal to the profile relevance age since its result became pending. Expiry is independent of host closure and never implies delivery. Stale and expired advice must not be handed off.
- A real reviewer restart may lose queued/running work, successful cache entries, results, notices/cooldowns, and advice. Start with empty state and reject obsolete-lifetime messages; do not reconstruct lost work. Actual agent-application closure may discard its remaining work/advice. A pause or missing callback alone is not closure. Cleanup must not discard owned live work or pending advice and is allowed after work/advice/resources are gone; later hooks may lazily restart.

### Truthful outcomes and operational notices

Observation, evaluation, applicability, and delivery outcomes may be represented orthogonally. Excluded, unsupported, incomplete, rejected, unavailable, stale, and expired never mean reviewed-clear. A partial multi-file observation cannot be published as a complete change set. Never publish mixed bytes, mixed recipients, invalid results, or known-stale advice.

Exclusions, unsupported operations, no analyzer, and contained applicability failures stay quiet to the agent. Capacity rejection and Jev unavailability may produce a short attributable operational notice under this exact eligibility policy:

1. The first failure is immediately eligible.
2. Repeated failures of the same kind for the same recipient/root are suppressed for 60 seconds.
3. The first later failure at or after the boundary is eligible again and may include the suppressed count. A timer alone does not generate a notice.
4. Capacity rejection and Jev unavailability have separate keys. Key/counter state is bounded and lost on restart.
5. Retention and delivery are best effort within existing response/state bounds. Notice retention failure cannot recursively generate another capacity notice or displace accepted fresh findings. Unknown recipients receive no addressed notice.

### Versioned adapter and supported profile

The initial profile is **direct-event v1 / Codex CLI 0.155.1 / Linux arm64 / headless command hooks / controlled writer**. Node 24.20.0 is recorded prototype runtime metadata, not evidence for other runtime versions. Other host versions, platforms, or modes require their own conformance evidence.

The adapter accepts successful native `PostToolUse(apply_patch)` with `hook_event_name`, `tool_name`, `session_id`, `turn_id`, `tool_use_id`, optional preserved `agent_id`, `cwd` resolving to a canonical Git root, and the bounded native patch in `tool_input.command`. Host identity belongs to the versioned adapter context. `Edit` and `Write` are matcher aliases, not proof of different observed native tools. Add selects applicable named units. Update selection requires a nonempty added line, compared after trimming whitespace, to occur in the selected root declaration and no other candidate root declaration. Ambiguity must not generalize into arbitrary hunk mapping. One to sixteen named candidates are supported, each with independent outcomes.

Delete, move/rename, metadata-only changes, shell/external writes, malformed events, missing required identity, and checkpoint discovery have no supported direct-review mapping. A missing path is not a successful capture. The final live host run covered Add; Update and multi-file support derives from native-payload plus deterministic pipeline evidence and must be described separately.

The analyzer profile covers UTF-8 `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mts`, and `.cts`, uniquely named interfaces/type declarations, and bounded finite same-file references. These suffixes constrain analyzer applicability, never global file selection. Schema extraction, declaration merging, cross-file/imported or unresolved evidence, arbitrary hunk mapping, and language-server extraction are unsupported. Real child-specific delivery remains unvalidated even though identity preservation and partition isolation are required/tested deterministically.

| Parameter | Initial profile value | Classification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native patch command | 64 KiB maximum | Tested envelope ceiling |
| Named candidate paths | 1–16 | Tested envelope ceiling |
| Source capture | 32 KiB per file | Tested envelope ceiling |
| Declarations | 64 per captured file | Tested analyzer ceiling |
| Same-file reference closure | 16 referenced names per unit | Selected ceiling; exact-boundary evidence gap below |
| Global logical capacity | 64 items / 8 MiB | Selected tested bound |
| Recipient/root logical capacity | 16 items / 2 MiB | Selected tested bound |
| Successful-result cache | 8 entries / 128 KiB, also charged to capacity | Selected tested bound |
| Backend concurrency | 2 requests | Selected tested bound |
| Combined advice response | 5 items / 2 KiB | Selected tested bound |
| Singleton readiness | 10 seconds | Selected operating bound |
| Client request deadline | 1.5 seconds | Selected operating bound; does not cancel owned work |
| Jev request deadline / retries | 15 seconds / zero automatic retries | Provisional selected policy |
| Normal advice collection window | 50 ms | Selected tested policy |
| Pending-advice relevance age | 600,000 ms, expiry at equality | Provisional selected policy |
| Operational-notice cooldown | 60,000 ms per failure kind/recipient/root | Accepted policy; new deterministic acceptance cases required |

KiB and MiB mean 1,024 and 1,048,576 bytes. Measured prototype timing is evidence, not a latency service level. Deadline, retry, relevance, and notice values are policy choices; tests establish mechanics, not optimal values. User configuration remains responsible for declarative path narrowing and applicable rule policy under the existing configuration contract. The table does not promise a new configuration key for every bound, nor let configuration silently broaden supported host/extraction surfaces. Changes to supported limits or semantics require a revised profile and corresponding validation.

One evidence discrepancy must remain explicit: the accepted envelope states 16 referenced names per unit, but the prototype's visited-name counter includes the root, allowing at most 15 additional names. This specification preserves the accepted 16-reference requirement; production conformance must test that exact boundary. The prototype alone does not establish it.

## Testing Decisions

The accepted testing seams are carried forward from the resolved prototype and envelope decisions. Prefer the highest product boundary: direct-event admission through collection with a controlled Effect `DecisionModel`, real temporary Git/filesystem fixtures, and deterministic clock/concurrency gates. Retain focused snapshot, backend-response, configuration/consent, and adapter tests where they isolate an external boundary; do not test private maps, fiber counts, or chosen lock APIs as product requirements.

Existing prior art includes the repository's runtime review tests, injectable `SnapshotReader` and `ReviewBackend`, controlled decision-model layer, Codex adapter tests, configuration/consent tests, and the disposable direct-event experiment. The current synchronous runtime and snapshot reader are reusable seams, not proof they already satisfy stable capture, resident scheduling, or the new profile.

Required acceptance coverage:

1. Adapt successful Add, narrowly corroborated Update, and multi-file native payloads; reject malformed/oversized commands and unsupported operations without wrong-path capture. Preserve required identity/root evidence. Separately test delivery-only hooks with zero new capture/backend work from shell activity.
2. Prove zero source reads/calls for exclusions: nested Git patterns/negation, tracked matching files, ignored untracked files, accumulated globs, `.env`/`.env.*`, `node_modules`, administrative paths, containment and symlink traversal. Prove ordinary generated/vendor/build names remain selectable. Do not add filesystem traversal tests as direct-review requirements.
3. Exercise stable repeated capture, in-capture mutation, deletion/recreation, malformed/nonregular/missing paths, cancellation, byte limits, valid UTF-8 BOM, binary/NUL input, unrelated suffixes, and contained parser failure. Independent valid paths continue without claiming a complete parent observation.
4. Exercise unique named units, finite recursive same-file evidence, exact declaration/reference ceilings, unresolved references, ambiguity, unsupported schema/merging/imports, and one request per unit. Clear units emit no empty advice.
5. Prove complete-input pending joins, bounded duplicate storms, cache-independent joining, successful reuse, failure/malformed-output non-reuse, cache eviction, A → B → A restoration, and partition isolation. Mutating rule content or input-contract context must change identity even when source is unchanged.
6. Before publication, test unchanged input across unrelated comment/sibling edits, changed relevant declaration/reference/rules/contract, unavailable semantic identity, and late old completion. No test may authorize a whole-file freshness fallback. Explicitly demonstrate that matching reads cannot prove writer identity; uncertain attribution emits no addressed advice.
7. With deterministic time and explicit gates, prove prompt lone-item dispatch, finite cycles under continuous arrivals, two-call concurrency, cycle-completion/50 ms collection, oldest-result aging, deterministic five-item/2 KiB combined response, retained overflow, and expiry just before/at/after 600,000 ms. No sleeps as concurrency or timing oracles.
8. Exercise global and per-partition count/byte pressure at ingress, capture/extraction, queued/running work, cache, outcome reservations, pending advice, duplicates, and notices. Prove explicit rejection, no arbitrary eviction of accepted fresh outcomes, bounded transport before decoding, and reservation cleanup on every terminal path. Do not claim hard RSS from a logical ledger test.
9. Test notice eligibility on first failure, suppression before 60,000 ms, eligibility at equality, no timer-only emission, separate failure kinds/recipients/roots, optional suppressed counts, bounded cooldown state and restart reset, no recursive rejection notice, and no displacement of accepted findings. State pressure must not bypass an active key's suppression guarantee. This policy was accepted after the 21-group prototype suite; it is required future coverage, not existing runtime evidence.
10. Test concurrent ensure-running, missing initialization, stale endpoint/live owner, bounded readiness, uncertain/disconnected IPC, timeout without accepted-work cancellation, actual process kill/restart, obsolete-lifetime messages, cleanup refusal with pending work/advice, lazy restart, and distinct existing worktrees. Retain the prototype's 100 concurrent starters/eight separate client processes as prior evidence.
11. Test existing consent preview/digest confirmation and dispatch-time revocation under resident execution. No project configuration may grant egress; no omitted test consent may make a paid call.
12. Test zero automatic retries and the selected 15-second Jev deadline using the fake backend. Older offline prototype defaults of five seconds/one retry and gated 60-second fixtures do not override this specification.

Model-based/property tests may use a small direct-event reference model and a constrained valid TypeScript module generator with known mutations; retain shrink/replay information and hand-written unsupported-shape fixtures. Do not inherit the superseded checkpoint baseline/scan/property plan.

Keep three evidence levels distinct:

- **Offline deterministic behavior:** ordinary tests make no paid Jev calls. The retained prototype passed 21 scenario groups. New implementation must pass the full acceptance contract above, including later policy and migration requirements absent from that prototype.
- **Pinned live host conformance:** record hook entry, adaptation, submission, and any independently observed model visibility separately. The final recorded headless run admitted Add, returned no immediate advice, then submitted one item on a subsequent Bash hook. Exact model repetition was absent. Earlier successful repetition and ambiguous missing-handler runs do not establish universal emission or reliable model visibility. Interactive/headful attempts established no support.
- **Bounded paid milestones:** authorized milestone runs must declare call ceilings, retry policy, source limits, deadlines, and sanitized retained output. The provider seam used two calls; the initial resident attempt used one valid call and rejected an unresolved-reference fixture; the corrected resident run used two calls. Five calls total, zero retries. Record fixture IDs, bands, contract outcomes, and timing only; retain no credentials, source-bearing responses, raw advice/transcripts, individual probabilities, or provider usage. Further paid runs are unnecessary for publishing this spec.

## Out of Scope

- Production implementation as part of this publication task; this issue is the specification for a later implementation effort.
- Checkpoint reconciliation, observation baselines/artifact indexes, repository-wide discovery, Stop/shell/external catch-up, and otherwise-unaccounted changes; these belong to [Decide checkpoint reconciliation coverage and mechanism](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/38).
- Universal interception/emission, mid-command interception, authoritative post-image or exact writer attribution under invisible overwrites, and agent-addressed unattributed changes.
- Unsupported host versions, interactive/headful Codex, Claude Code or other hosts without independent versioned conformance, and claims of real child-specific delivery.
- Delete/move review semantics; schema/cross-file/language-server extraction; arbitrary hunk mapping; huge-change truncation or overflow strategies beyond explicit bounds.
- Source-bearing persistence, durable replay, reconstruction of lost work, mutation history, exactly-once behavior, delivery retry systems, guaranteed final drain, and model-visible-delivery guarantees.
- Dynamic backend switching, production scaling topology, process RSS guarantees, mandatory status/history endpoints, or a universal status enum.

## Further Notes

### Authority and supersessions

The final decisions below are normative inputs adopted by this specification. Research reports remain advisory. Earlier one-shot/synchronous-only delivery, per-session process counts, whole-file fallback, projection-only identity, checkpoint convergence, restart reconstruction, and mandatory final-drain wording are superseded by their later amendments. The supported-envelope decision selects policy; older prototype constants are not competing requirements.

- [Name the semantic review unit and pipeline vocabulary](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/19)
- [Define the unified review-ingress and exact-snapshot deduplication contract](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/20), with its direct-event scope correction
- [Choose the product process lifetime and hook transport — singleton correction](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/31#issuecomment-5755947269)
- [Define review scheduling and batched host-delivery semantics](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/23), including delivery/expiry correction
- [Define direct-event completeness, recovery, and concurrency semantics — audited amendment](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/24#issuecomment-5768044770)
- [Define Git-ignore-aware file selection and directory exclusions](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/35#issuecomment-5768609945)
- [Prototype the direct-event review pipeline — accepted resolution](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/25#issuecomment-5769310014)
- [Set the initial supported envelope from prototype evidence](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/26#issuecomment-5769768281)
- [Repository/backend consent ADR](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/blob/a3c72f1/docs/adr/0001-repository-scoped-backend-consent.md) and [accumulated-exclusion ADR](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/blob/a3c72f1/docs/adr/0002-accumulate-file-exclusions.md)

### Evidence assets

The disposable prototype is pinned to `76b6139`; it remains separate from production:

- [Verdict and limitations](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/blob/76b6139/experiments/direct-event-pipeline/VERDICT.md) and [reproduction guide](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/blob/76b6139/experiments/direct-event-pipeline/README.md)
- [Offline evidence](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/blob/76b6139/experiments/direct-event-pipeline/evidence/offline.json)
- [Paid provider-seam evidence](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/blob/76b6139/experiments/direct-event-pipeline/evidence/live-jev.json)
- [Paid resident-pipeline evidence](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/blob/76b6139/experiments/direct-event-pipeline/evidence/live-pipeline.json) and [initial rejected-fixture attempt](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/blob/76b6139/experiments/direct-event-pipeline/evidence/live-pipeline-initial-rejected.json)
- [Final pinned host run](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/blob/76b6139/experiments/direct-event-pipeline/evidence/host-run-1790035254066.json)

### Non-normative implementation guidance

Existing Effect services/layers, scoped fibers/finalizers, atomic state, bounded queues, controlled `DecisionModel`, and clock injection are useful seams. A keyed atomic ledger is needed beyond queue count bounds. The notice research suggests `Clock.currentTimeMillis` with atomic `Ref.modify` over a bounded keyed map; it does not require a particular map, cache, schedule, or rate-limiter implementation. Linux `flock`, Unix sockets, and descriptor-relative capture are prototype mechanisms, not host-neutral architectural requirements. A production implementation must satisfy the observable contract regardless of these choices.

## Parent

## What to build

A supported Codex Add event produces attributable advice for one independently reviewable type declaration, using stable current source and the existing Effect/Jev integration. Establish the smallest complete direct-event path through admission, selection, capture, evaluation, and revalidated host output.

The normative contract is #42. Preserve product/Jev/agent-host terminology; research and prototype mechanisms are advisory, and earlier synchronous/checkpoint behavior does not override that specification. Each slice includes its own verification; the final conformance ticket is not a substitute for tests in earlier slices.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Adapt successful Codex CLI 0.155.1 Add payloads in the adapter, preserving explicit host/session/agent identity and canonical Git working root; reject missing identity and unsupported operations quietly. Core review code does not parse native patch syntax.
- [ ] Read only eligible event-named regular nonsymlink source files. Honor nested repository Git ignores and tracked-file semantics, accumulated exclusions and replacement includes; exclude administrative paths, symlink traversal, outside-root paths, .env/.env.* and node_modules before source reads. Do not load global Git excludes or .git/info/exclude, walk directories, or universally exclude build/generated/vendor names.
- [ ] Capture at most 32 KiB per file with bounded repeated byte/hash and metadata agreement. Contain mutation, deletion/recreation, missing/nonregular files, cancellation, malformed UTF-8 and binary/NUL input; accept UTF-8 BOM. Unsupported analyzer input is quiet with no backend call.
- [ ] Extract one unique named TypeScript interface or type declaration without required references, freeze its complete ReviewInput and rules, and evaluate it individually through Decision.probability / DecisionModel and @effect/ai-typesafe at the exact 4.0.0-rc.116 cohort. Validate decision keys and finite in-range probabilities; successful clear emits no empty advice.
- [ ] Preserve digest-confirmed repository/backend consent and dispatch-time revocation. Enforce the selected 15-second Jev deadline and zero automatic retries using a controlled backend.
- [ ] Require the controlled-writer condition and explicit recipient association; matching reads never prove authorship. Revalidate selection, semantic input and rules before handoff, without a whole-file freshness fallback; report submission only as attempted-unacknowledged.
- [ ] Demonstrate the complete path with deterministic offline tests, a controlled DecisionModel and real temporary Git/filesystem fixtures. Keep this narrow initial path distinct from full profile conformance.

None (can start immediately).

title: Continue review across short-lived hook clients
body:
## Parent

https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/42

## What to build

Short-lived hooks ensure a resident reviewer, admit attributable work promptly and collect its advice on later supported replies. Ordinary editing proceeds while accepted evaluation belongs to the resident lifetime.

The normative contract is #42. Preserve product/Jev/agent-host terminology; research and prototype mechanisms are advisory, and earlier synchronous/checkpoint behavior does not override that specification. Each slice includes its own verification; the final conformance ticket is not a substitute for tests in earlier slices.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Provide cross-process idempotent ensure-running with one resident owner per operating-system user/machine, bounded startup/readiness of 10 seconds, and a 1.5-second client request deadline. Hooks ensure the reviewer even when initialization was omitted.
- [ ] Bound transport frames/connections before decoding recipients and retain explicit recipient/canonical-root isolation, including supplied child identity and distinct existing worktrees.
- [ ] Show accepted work completing after client timeout, disconnect or exit; do not interpret an IPC timeout as reviewer death or cancel resident-owned work with the requesting client.
- [ ] Adapt direct edits to admission and supported later replies to collection. Bash supplies no capture paths or backend work; any mapped turn-end hook is bounded ready-only collection and never waits for queue quiescence or extends completion.
- [ ] Preserve current configuration and user-owned consent at dispatch, including revocation after admission. Use the selected Jev deadline/retry policy in resident execution.
- [ ] Revalidate advice before handoff. Uncertain/failed IPC is not delivered; successful submission is attempted-unacknowledged and does not claim model visibility or guaranteed final drain.
- [ ] Exercise admission-to-later-collection and timeout independence with deterministic backend/concurrency gates and separate process integration tests. Retained state remains bounded even before the full burst-accounting slice.

- https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/43

title: Handle concurrent bursts within the full operating bounds
body:
## Parent

https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/42

## What to build

Concurrent direct edits are processed promptly through finite dispatch cycles while explicit admission bounds protect accepted outcomes and keep retained logical state bounded.

The normative contract is #42. Preserve product/Jev/agent-host terminology; research and prototype mechanisms are advisory, and earlier synchronous/checkpoint behavior does not override that specification. Each slice includes its own verification; the final conformance ticket is not a substitute for tests in earlier slices.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dispatch an idle lone item promptly, select finite keyed FIFO cycles and assign later arrivals to later cycles; continuous arrivals cannot indefinitely extend a cycle. Run at most two backend requests.
- [ ] Enforce global 64-item/8 MiB and recipient/root 16-item/2 MiB logical limits across ingress, capture/extraction reservations, queued/running inputs, duplicate bookkeeping, cache, promised outcomes, notices and pending advice as those features are enabled.
- [ ] Reserve enforceably bounded outcome space before accepting work; unknown backend output cannot be assumed to fit. Explicitly reject work that would exceed count or byte limits without evicting accepted fresh outcomes.
- [ ] Bound transport independently before recipient decoding and release reservations/joins on every success, failure, cancellation, rejection and lifecycle terminal path.
- [ ] Test count and byte boundaries, malformed/oversized backend output, independent partition pressure and sustained arrivals using deterministic clocks and explicit gates. Logical accounting evidence makes no hard RSS guarantee.

title: Join duplicate work and reuse successful evaluations
body:
## Parent

https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/42

## What to build

Equivalent observations share queued/running evaluation and reuse bounded successful complete inputs, reducing repeated paid work without duplicating pending advice or crossing recipient boundaries.

The normative contract is #42. Preserve product/Jev/agent-host terminology; research and prototype mechanisms are advisory, and earlier synchronous/checkpoint behavior does not override that specification. ## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Canonical equality includes root/evidence, relevant path/domain payload, completeness, versioned input contract, immutable rule content and evaluation interpretation. Event IDs, queue bookkeeping, path equality and source fingerprints alone do not define evaluation identity.
- [ ] Check queued/running equality before another reservation. Duplicate storms retain bounded bookkeeping and joins remain valid independently of successful-cache eviction.
- [ ] Cache successful evaluated results, including clear results, at no more than eight entries/128 KiB charged to the logical ledger. Failures, malformed responses, incomplete inputs and rejections are never successful reuse entries.
- [ ] Isolate joins, cache entries and advice by explicit recipient and canonical root; equivalent currently pending observations cannot multiply advice.
- [ ] Demonstrate A → B → A: obsolete A advice retires, retained successful A may become eligible again on restoration even after earlier submission, and a cache miss permits reevaluation without unbounded delivered-history state.

title: Collect bounded batches without losing overflow
body:
## Parent

https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/42

## What to build

The earliest supported host reply receives a coherent bounded batch of eligible current advice, while overflow remains available for later replies until it becomes stale or expires.

The normative contract is #42. Preserve product/Jev/agent-host terminology; research and prototype mechanisms are advisory, and earlier synchronous/checkpoint behavior does not override that specification. Each slice includes its own verification; the final conformance ticket is not a substitute for tests in earlier slices.

- [ ] Make ordinary collection eligible when its finite cycle completes or its oldest pending result reaches 50 ms, whichever occurs first; new arrivals do not reset aging and eligibility does not manufacture a host reply.
- [ ] Select one deterministic combined response with at most five items and 2 KiB encoded bytes, including operational notices when present. Allow older eligible advice to progress.
- [ ] Keep excess fresh eligible advice pending within admission reservations; capacity pressure and a zero finding budget cannot silently discard it or count as successful delivery.
- [ ] Expire pending advice at age greater than or equal to 600,000 ms since becoming pending, independently of host closure. Revalidate freshness immediately before every handoff.
- [ ] Keep mapped turn-end collection ready-only and bounded, without final-drain guarantees. Failed/uncertain IPC never becomes delivered; submission remains attempted-unacknowledged.

title: Make process-boundary tests robust under shared CPU contention
body:
## Problem

The canonical offline suite can report false failures when the shared development host is CPU-saturated. On final master at `c906851ac0c38329b2538ca4ccb559d7313fdfd6`, five unrelated process-heavy tests hit Vitest’s exact 5-second default timeout while another workspace process continuously consumed about 97% CPU. There were no assertion failures.

The same complete suite, with only `testTimeout` raised to 60 seconds, passed 302 tests with the two credential-gated live tests skipped. Focused direct-event conformance also passed 185/185 with its canonical command.

One genuinely oversized cooldown test was separately made deterministic in #54. The remaining failures span configuration subprocess, diagnostics process, evaluation process, and resident saturation/cache cases, indicating a shared scheduling-budget problem rather than one product behavior. The final landing record is documented on #53.

## Goal

Keep genuine hangs bounded and visible while preventing normal CPU contention from turning otherwise-correct process-boundary tests into false negatives. This must not relax product deadlines or hide assertion failures.

## Scope

- Inventory tests that spawn real Node processes or perform intentionally large bounded resident scenarios.
- Introduce one documented test-harness policy or helper for those tests instead of scattered arbitrary timeout increases.
- Keep ordinary unit tests on the tighter default where practical.
- Preserve explicit child-process deadlines, cleanup, and failure diagnostics.
- Do not use sleeps as correctness or concurrency oracles.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The canonical `npm test` command passes under normal load and under a reproducible bounded CPU-contention fixture.
2. A deliberately hung child still fails within a documented finite bound and is terminated/cleaned up.
3. Product runtime deadlines, retry policy, and supported-profile limits are unchanged.
4. Timeout failures identify the child/test phase rather than reporting only a generic Vitest timeout.
5. Typecheck, the full offline suite, and `npm run conformance:direct-event` pass.
6. Documentation explains the distinction between product deadlines and test-harness scheduling allowance.

## Evidence

- Main landing and final audit: #53
- Deterministic cooldown-test follow-up: #54
- Final master: https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/commit/c906851ac0c38329b2538ca4ccb559d7313fdfd6

title: Specify convenient Codex onboarding
body:
## Destination

Produce an implementation-ready specification for convenient Codex onboarding on Linux and macOS, for interactive and headless use: acquire and install the product, enter a Jev API key once, activate a repository, verify useful review, and update or remove the integration while preserving other tools.

## Notes

This is a decision map, not production implementation or release-publication authorization. The product remains unnamed; Jev is its external review backend.

Standing decisions from the user:
- Codex first; design the installation boundary for additional agent hosts later.
- Both interactive and headless Codex, on Linux and macOS, are required. Current runtime evidence is narrower and must not be promoted into broader support.
- Enter the API key once with secure local storage. Environment-variable injection remains available for automation; environment-only onboarding is insufficient.
- Overlapping writes to the same reviewed content are considered rare and deferred. Do not make concurrency handling an onboarding blocker or introduce a new single-writer setup requirement. Preserve the documented current limitation and existing safeguards; do not claim new attribution guarantees.

The user delegated routine defaults; ask only material scope, authority or user-experience questions. Continue to the next available action without asking whether to proceed.

Use `grilling` and `domain-modeling` for decisions; `prototype` for the disposable setup experience; `research` for bounded unresolved external facts. Use repository PRODUCT-RESEARCH-METHODOLOGY.md for comparative evidence. Research is advisory, and no untested host/platform support may be advertised.

Existing working-copy inputs in /workspace/typescript/jev:
- PRODUCT-ONBOARDING-SPEC-DRAFT.md — audit, proposed flow, acceptance gates, and accepted user decisions.
- PRODUCT-RESEARCH-ADVISORY-2026-09-22-ONBOARDING.md — existing source comparison; do not repeat broad comparative research.
- RESEARCH-HOOK-ATTRIBUTION-2026-09-22.md — distinguishes available hook/child identity from later disk-snapshot ownership.
- evidence/direct-event-v1/MVP-EXPERIENCE.md — completed real headless Codex/real Jev review-and-repair demonstration; not normal installation or macOS evidence.

These are currently local working-copy artifacts, not published branch links. Existing normative constraints include [Direct-event review specification v1](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/42) and [Phase F configuration](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/3), amended only where this effort explicitly decides.

## Decisions so far

<!-- Resolution detail belongs in closed child tickets; append named context pointers here. -->

- [Research secure credential storage for Linux and macOS](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/58): Native-vault mechanisms identified; persistent store selection, prompt control, deadlines, and real-host access remain explicit adoption gates.

- [Choose the Codex installation and activation path](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/57#issuecomment-5777870642): Terminal-first agent-callable CLI; install once for the user, enable per repository; explicit updates with optional simple update notices.

- [Define the saved credential lifecycle](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/59): One saved Jev key, environment override, logout preserves repository enablement; native-store recovery and credential invalidation defaults recorded.

- [Walk through the complete Codex onboarding experience](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/60#issuecomment-5778212047): Captured interaction model adopted under delegated defaults; user waived mandatory walkthrough review, no usability validation claimed.

- [Set onboarding acceptance and compatibility boundaries](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/61#issuecomment-5778213225): Installed-product testing seam and release gates settled; native-vault and platform mechanisms require implementation evidence.

## Not yet specified

None blocking specification handoff. Native-store and macOS mechanism probes are explicit implementation/release gates, not assumed compatibility. Material failures must return for a scope decision rather than silently weakening the requirement.

Final specification: [Implement convenient Codex onboarding](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/62), published with `ready-for-agent`. The user authorized finalization using routine defaults without mandatory walkthrough review. No production implementation or new validation is claimed.

## Out of scope

- Production implementation, publishing packages, marketing identity, or installing into the user's real host configuration.
- Additional agent-host implementations, Windows support, enterprise fleet management, and remote rule distribution.
- Checkpoint reconciliation, shell/Stop discovery, overlapping-writer coordination, and stronger concurrent-write attribution guarantees.
- Changes to rule meaning or source-input contracts solely to simplify onboarding.

The `to-spec` handoff is complete: accepted requirements and delegated testing defaults are consolidated in the linked implementation specification.

title: Choose the Codex installation and activation path
body:
## Question

Which user-facing distribution and activation path should the first Codex onboarding release provide: an installed CLI with native hook configuration, a Codex plugin wrapping the runtime, or a deliberately defined combination?

Decide the default installation scope, durable executable ownership, ordinary host trust flow, version/update responsibility, and preservation/removal contract. Consider interactive and headless Codex on Linux and macOS. Do not require registry/cache resolution on every edit. Detection is not support, installation is not trust, and installation does not grant repository source-egress consent.

Use the existing onboarding research and draft; new broad comparative research is unnecessary. Resolve a product decision, not an installer implementation. The output must state which runtime/host/platform facts remain acceptance gates rather than pretending they have been tested.

title: Research secure credential storage for Linux and macOS
body:
## Question

Which secure local credential-store mechanisms can support enter-once Jev credentials on Linux and macOS, with bounded noninteractive retrieval from Codex hooks and a resident reviewer?

Use primary OS/service documentation and narrowly relevant maintained integration sources. Establish locked/absent-store behavior, user-session/headless availability, prompting controls, replacement/deletion semantics, packaging constraints, and what is possible to validate in the available environment. Distinguish a headless agent in a logged-in user session from a server without a session vault. Keep environment injection as an automation alternative; do not silently turn secure storage into a plaintext file.

The user chose the experience, not a specific vault API/library. Return a source-pinned advisory recommendation with unresolved runtime checks; do not claim macOS execution from Linux. No paid calls, real credentials, keychain changes, or host installation. Capture the report on a throwaway research branch and link its immutable commit in the resolution.

title: Define the saved credential lifecycle
body:
## Question

What exact credential lifecycle will make enter-once secure storage reliable for interactive and headless Codex on Linux and macOS?

After the focused vault research, decide storage selection, masked entry, environment precedence, inaccessible/locked-store recovery, cross-process lookup, replacement, logout, queued work and resident credential invalidation. Preserve repository/backend/destination consent as a separate authority. Decide how an installation reports stored-but-unusable credentials without prompting from hooks or silently falling back to plaintext. Resolve the product contract and required validation boundaries, not implementation.

title: Walk through the complete Codex onboarding experience
body:
## Question

Does the proposed setup, first-review verification, diagnosis, update and removal experience feel convenient and truthful to a new Codex user?

Using the chosen distribution/activation path and credential lifecycle, produce a disposable walkthrough covering first install, repeated setup, an existing unrelated hook, missing/locked credentials, native hook trust, repository consent, a first useful review, and removal. Keep configuration, trust, readiness, actual completed review, and model visibility distinct. Review with the user and record the accepted experience and recovery language. Do not install into the user's real host or implement the product. Overlapping-write handling is explicitly outside this effort and must not become a setup question.

Include an agent-initiated CLI setup path using noninteractive structured outcomes, with a usable handoff for any user-only key entry, vault unlock, host trust or unresolved consent. Do not route secrets through chat. Updates are explicit; update-available notices are optional only if simple. See the resolved [installation and activation decision](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/57#issuecomment-5777870642).

title: Set onboarding acceptance and compatibility boundaries
body:
## Question

What observable acceptance gates and compatibility promises make the onboarding specification ready for implementation?

After the setup walkthrough, settle the minimum Linux/macOS and interactive/headless Codex matrix, package-versus-source-checkout testing, host-native trust, other-hook coexistence, credential-vault lifecycle, resident activity reporting, first real review-and-repair evidence, update rollback and scoped uninstall. Prefer a small set of high-level installed-product/real-host seams with deterministic offline checks underneath. Distinguish already demonstrated behavior from new release gates. Identify any prerequisite mechanism probe and ensure no known unsupported behavior is labeled ready. This decision supplies the testing-boundary input for the subsequent to-spec handoff; it does not authorize implementation or paid executions automatically.

title: Implement convenient Codex onboarding
body:
# Convenient Codex onboarding — implementation specification

## Problem Statement

The product has demonstrated a real Codex edit → Jev finding → model repair loop,
but users still lack a supported way to install, activate, diagnose, update and
remove it. A source-checkout demo does not establish a convenient installed
experience. Users should enter a key once, preserve their other tools, and know
whether review actually happened. Coding agents need to invoke the same setup
operations without asking for secrets in chat or hanging on interactive prompts.

## Solution

Provide a terminal-first, resumable installed CLI. Start with Codex on Linux and
macOS, in interactive and headless operation, while keeping host-specific
installation behind an adapter boundary. Install once into the selected user's
host configuration; enable review separately for each canonical repository and
Jev destination. Store one default Jev key in persistent native credential storage,
with an explicit environment option for automation.

Setup checks compatibility, previews owned changes, installs the integration,
connects credentials, offers repository enablement, guides native host trust,
and reports readiness. Trust may occur earlier if the adapter requires it. Users
can stop with the integration installed and repository review disabled. Repeated
setup resumes incomplete steps without duplicating or damaging working ones.
The supported happy path requires no manual configuration or source-code edits.

This is an implementation contract, not a claim that onboarding or the expanded
platform matrix already works. Product, package and executable names remain
undecided; `review-tool` is only a command placeholder.

## User Stories

1. As a new user, I want to install a released package without cloning the repository, so that setup does not depend on a development environment.
2. As a Codex user, I want compatibility checked before configuration changes, so that unsupported environments receive a useful explanation.
3. As a user with multiple agent profiles, I want to choose the host configuration home, so that installation affects the intended profile.
4. As a user, I want to preview installation changes, so that I understand what will run in my agent.
5. As a user of other hooks, I want their configuration preserved, so that adding review does not break my workflow.
6. As a returning user, I want repeated setup to resume safely, so that interruptions do not require starting over.
7. As a user with malformed or modified configuration, I want a precise conflict and recovery action, so that setup does not overwrite my work.
8. As a user, I want to enter my Jev key once through a masked prompt, so that later sessions can reuse it securely.
9. As a user, I want the key kept out of project files, command arguments and logs, so that ordinary collaboration does not disclose it.
10. As a user with a locked credential store, I want explicit login to guide recovery, so that background hooks never unexpectedly ask for passwords.
11. As an automation operator, I want an explicit environment credential option, so that headless execution can work without a user-session vault.
12. As a user with both saved and environment credentials, I want the selected source identified without its value, so that account selection is predictable.
13. As a user replacing a key, I want cancellation or storage failure to preserve the old key, so that unsuccessful login does not destroy working access.
14. As a user logging out, I want the saved key removed and future queued use invalidated, so that later calls cannot reuse it.
15. As a user logging out with an environment override, I want to know that override remains active, so that I can disable review if that is my intent.
16. As a repository owner, I want to approve the canonical root, destination and eligible-source scope, so that installation alone cannot authorize source transmission.
17. As a returning user, I want valid prior repository approval reused, so that routine setup does not repeatedly ask the same question.
18. As a user, I want host trust handled by Codex, so that installation respects the host's security and managed policy.
19. As a coding agent, I want noninteractive commands and structured outcomes, so that I can install, diagnose and perform requested updates reliably.
20. As a coding agent, I want actionable user handoffs for unavailable authorization or credentials, so that setup does not hang or solicit secrets in conversation.
21. As a user, I want offline doctor to distinguish installation, trust, credentials and enablement, so that I can fix the actual missing step.
22. As a user, I want activity to distinguish pending, clear, finding and unavailable states, so that silence is not mistaken for successful review.
23. As a user, I want finding submission distinguished from observed model reaction, so that status does not exaggerate delivery evidence.
24. As a new user, I want an optional explicitly paid synthetic demo, so that I can observe useful review without sending my current project.
25. As a user, I want ordinary supported edits to establish review activity, so that a demo is not mandatory.
26. As a user, I want explicit updates with clear failure recovery, so that version changes do not silently disrupt my integration.
27. As a user, I want changed hooks to report required trust or restart steps, so that an update cannot claim readiness prematurely.
28. As a user, I want repository disable to prevent future dispatch regardless of credential source, so that I can stop review without uninstalling shared components.
29. As a user, I want scoped uninstall to preserve other hooks, rules, credentials and grants, so that removing one integration does not damage reusable state.
30. As a Linux or macOS user, I want exact tested compatibility stated, so that I can distinguish supported execution from an unverified configuration.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Scope and baseline.** Retain the existing asynchronous direct-event review contract, bundled Noul rules, source eligibility/extraction limits, session/child identity and existing runtime safeguards. Do not add scanning or alter rule meaning for onboarding. Use TypeScript and the matched exact Effect `4.0.0-rc.116` cohort with Decision/DecisionModel and the ai-typesafe provider; the historical vendored SDK is not a production dependency.
- **Installed runtime.** Package a durable executable, resident entry point, parser artifacts and runtime dependencies that work without development dependencies or a source checkout. Declare and validate runtime, OS and architecture requirements. No transient package download on each hook invocation. Do not promise a standalone binary before native packaging works. Package coordinates are release details, not an authorization to publish.
- **Command surface.** Support setup, install, login/logout, enable/disable, doctor, status, optional live demo, explicit update and scoped uninstall. These share operation contracts for humans and agents. Doctor is read-only and offline; install/login/enable do not implicitly call Jev. Updates may download packages but do not transmit project source.
- **Automation contract.** Provide explicit host/scope inputs, noninteractive operation, stable exit outcomes and versioned JSON results with completed/pending steps and actionable errors. Missing secret entry, vault unlock, host trust or consent yields bounded `needs-user-action`; no unattended terminal wait. Existing concrete user authorization can be reused. Project instructions cannot grant source-egress consent. Secret handoff is a masked user terminal prompt or explicitly selected automation stdin channel, never chat or an argument value.
- **Ownership and preservation.** Maintain source-free, secret-free versioned user-owned installation records identifying host, scope, configuration location, exact owned entries, runtime version and fingerprints. Parse actual host configuration; preserve unrelated settings, matcher groups and meaningful order. Reject unreadable/malformed configuration instead of treating it as empty. Detect duplicate representations and locally modified owned entries. Reconcile explicitly rather than overwrite. Honor custom configuration homes and managed policy; never modify trust records or enable globally disabled hooks to evade policy.
- **Mutation recovery.** Preview owned changes. Use bounded configuration locking or concurrent-change detection and atomic writes per file. Journal multi-file progress and expose partial completion/recovery; do not claim cross-file atomicity. Do not restore stale whole-file backups over another tool's changes. Quote executable and argument paths correctly. This protects installer configuration, not concurrent source-writer attribution.
- **Credential storage.** Keep one saved default Jev credential per user, shared across enabled repositories and future adapters. Select persistent native storage scoped to product/backend/destination/profile; repositories cannot choose arbitrary vault entries. Linux Secret Service and macOS Keychain are mechanism candidates. Choose a binding only after real-context probes prove persistence and bounded nonprompting lookup. No plaintext, colocated-key encryption or volatile-store fallback presented as saved secure storage.
- **Credential selection.** An explicitly configured credential environment variable is environment-only: absence or invalidity is an error, with no saved-key fallback. Otherwise a nonempty default `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` overrides the saved default. Report source and accessibility, never values. A rejected credential must not trigger a retry with another account. Do not automatically source environment files or edit shell startup files.
- **Credential lifecycle.** Only explicit login/setup credential actions may unlock storage. Hooks, residents and offline doctor never initiate prompts; lookup must be bounded within responsiveness requirements. Preserve the old key if replacement fails or is cancelled; successful replacement invalidates its old generation. Logout deletes only the owned saved item and invalidates queued/cached generations before new dispatch. Report deletion failure honestly and suspend saved-key use pending recovery. Logout preserves repository grants and cannot remove the caller's environment key. Already dispatched requests cannot be recalled; do not claim guaranteed zeroization of JavaScript strings.
- **Consent and trust.** Reuse preview plus matching-digest confirmation for canonical working root, Jev backend/destination and repository-wide eligible-source scope. Store grants in user-owned state and recheck at dispatch. Installation, saved credentials and host trust are separate from enablement. No automatic grant for another or moved root. Respect normal host trust and required reload/restart behavior without bypass flags. Users can install without enabling any repository.
- **Readiness and activity.** Report installed/compatible runtime, configured integration, trusted/required/unknown host trust, credential accessibility in the execution context and repository enablement independently. Source-free observed activity distinguishes no observation, skipped, pending, completed-clear, findings, submitted, unavailable, incomplete and restart/lost state. Hook output proves submission, not model visibility. Report model reaction only with separate observed evidence. Missing instrumentation must be reported as unavailable, never clear.
- **First-value experience.** Offer ordinary supported edits or a separate opt-in live demo in a disposable synthetic repository with its own consent and declared source/call/time limits. Use the installed release, actual host, normal trust and production provider. Disclose the intentionally flawed input without prescribing the model's repair. Keep only sanitized stage outcomes, versions, timestamps and bounded counts. Record stochastic failures/inconclusive outcomes honestly; never lower thresholds or silently substitute a fake backend to force success.
- **Updates.** Require a user-requested update operation; omit update-available notices unless simple. No automatic upgrades or polling subsystem. Preview executable/hook changes, preserve still-applicable grants and credentials, report new trust/restart requirements, and respect resident protocol compatibility and in-flight work. Retain the previous working installation on failure where possible; otherwise report precise partial state and a recovery command.
- **Disable and uninstall.** Disable prevents future provider dispatch for the selected repository regardless of credential source. Uninstall removes only selected owned host integration and its installation record, preserving unrelated hooks, user rules, saved keys and grants. Explain remaining reusable state and use separate logout/disable operations for removal or revocation. Do not kill another active installation's work or imply already sent requests can be recalled.
- **Advisory adoption.** Borrow convenient staged setup, explicit ownership, preservation and actionable diagnosis patterns from the comparative research. Do not adopt an external installer dependency, substring ownership heuristic, destructive default rewrite, or checkout/cache-dependent runtime. Native plugin distribution is deferred; it is not required to ship this CLI contract.

## Testing Decisions

The primary acceptance boundary is the **installed product**: invoke the packaged
CLI in isolated user homes and repositories and run its generated integration
through real Codex. Assert observable outcomes and preserved user state, not
internal call sequences. Reuse existing direct-event, resident, consent and host
conformance fixtures for deterministic checks beneath that boundary. Test the
installer, credential resolver, consent integration and status behavior through
their public operations; do not build a separate test-only review implementation.

| Gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Clean package | Packed release without source checkout or development dependencies executes CLI, parser, resident and hook; declare exact runtime/OS/architecture versions. |
| Preservation and recovery | Install/repeat/update/uninstall preserve an independent hook and unrelated settings; cover malformed/unreadable config, duplicates, modified owned entries, concurrent configuration edits, partial writes and quoted paths. |
| Authorization | Install performs zero provider calls; unapproved or moved roots remain disabled; disable is checked before later dispatch; normal native trust applies. |
| Credential lifecycle | Saved key survives new sessions; real hook/resident access is bounded and nonprompting; test locked/absent storage, explicit/default environment precedence, cancellation, replacement, deletion failure and queued-generation invalidation without value leakage. |
| Platform and mode | Linux and macOS each demonstrate interactive and headless Codex. Publish exact tested profiles; an untested cell stays a release gap. Environment-only server tests complement but do not replace saved-key validation. |
| Honest activity | Distinguish readiness from actual invocation/completion/submission; cover no observation, skipped, pending, clear, findings, unavailable and lost state. Observe the independent hook in the real host rather than assuming handler order. |
| Lifecycle | Reject unsupported profiles before configuration writes; diagnose missing parser/runtime/resident facilities; exercise update failure, trust/restart requirements and scoped removal without disrupting unrelated work. |
| Live first value | At a declared budgeted milestone, the installed release with real Codex and Jev yields a finding, observed model reaction, independently validated repair and follow-up completion. A failed or inconclusive run is recorded as such. |
| Privacy and convenience | No paid calls in ordinary tests/doctor; sanitized evidence only; no manual host-config or implementation edits in the supported happy path. Record setup actions and time separately from review latency. |

Ordinary tests use controlled offline responses. Real native-vault and host tests
are explicitly separated from portable deterministic suites. Existing real-host
conformance and the recorded MVP review-and-repair demonstration provide prior art,
but the latter bypassed ordinary trust and packaging and proves only the documented
Linux arm64 headless profile. It is not macOS, interactive or install-to-first-review
evidence. Unit tests and successful installer exit alone cannot satisfy acceptance.

Before committing to a vault binding or advertising compatibility, probe native
prompt suppression, actual lookup deadlines, persistence, macOS capture/resident
portability and installed parser loading. These are implementation prerequisites,
not unanswered product preferences. If they fail, resolve the mechanism or raise
a material scope decision; do not silently reduce Linux/macOS scope.

## Out of Scope

- Additional host implementations, Windows, enterprise deployment and remote rule distribution.
- Native plugin packaging, automatic upgrades and update-notification infrastructure.
- Checkpoint reconciliation, shell/Stop discovery, changed rule meaning or broader source extraction.
- Overlapping-writer coordination and stronger concurrent-write attribution. Preserve current limitations and safeguards without a new single-writer confirmation or exclusive-worktree setup requirement.
- Multiple saved credential profiles and arbitrary project-selected vault identities.
- Public product naming, registry publication and changing the user's real host installation as part of this specification task.

## Further Notes

The user selected the major scope choices, delegated routine defaults and explicitly
chose to proceed without a mandatory walkthrough review. The prototype captures
the chosen interaction model; it has not received human usability validation.
Testing defaults are settled under that delegation. No new paid validation or
production implementation was performed while finalizing this specification.

This specification fills the onboarding deferral in Phase F and adds saved native
credentials while preserving explicit environment selection, consent semantics and
the direct-event review contract. Research remains advisory; only requirements
stated here are adopted. The earlier onboarding draft is historical design input.

- [Onboarding decision map](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/56)
- [Installation and activation decision](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/57)
- [Credential research and adoption gates](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/58)
- [Saved credential lifecycle](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/59)
- [Disposable walkthrough](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/blob/525888c/experiments/onboarding-walkthrough/README.md)
