- [Phase F configuration](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/3)

title: Run direct-event review from a clean Linux package
body:
## Parent

[Implement convenient Codex onboarding](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/62)

## What to build

Acquire a locally packed release in a clean Linux environment and execute the existing direct-event review path without a development checkout. This establishes the installed-product seam for later onboarding. No registry publication or public naming is required.

The parent specification governs shared scope and constraints.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The packed artifact contains a durable CLI, parser and resident entry point; runtime execution succeeds without development dependencies or checkout paths.
- [ ] An isolated real Codex fixture invokes the packaged hook and completes a controlled offline review using existing consent and environment credentials; preserve the current supported profile and review semantics.
- [ ] Existing conformance remains green; any packaging prefactor preserves behavior and lands before dependent installation work. Keep Effect dependencies exactly matched to the specified cohort.
- [ ] Declare tested runtime/OS/architecture and diagnose missing runtime/parser/resident prerequisites. No transient package download occurs per edit.
- [ ] Retain sanitized package/host evidence and a repeatable clean-install fixture; do not change the user’s real host or transmit paid requests in ordinary tests.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

title: Run the packaged direct-event review path on macOS
body:
## Parent

[Implement convenient Codex onboarding](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/62)

## What to build

Run the same packed CLI, parser, capture and resident review path on macOS, removing Linux-only assumptions where required. This is an actual installed review slice, not a portability-only refactor.

The parent specification governs shared scope and constraints.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The clean package executes a real Codex hook through capture, resident dispatch and controlled offline completion on a declared macOS/runtime/architecture profile.
- [ ] Validate or replace Linux-specific process locking, descriptor/capture and launch assumptions without weakening existing capture or review-input guarantees.
- [ ] Reuse the installed-product fixture from the Linux package slice; Linux remains green and missing facilities produce actionable errors.
- [ ] Retain sanitized evidence; mark untested modes or architectures unverified. A missing macOS runner is a validation blocker, not a pass.
- [ ] No additional source-writer coordination, rule changes or paid calls are introduced.

title: Install, enable and remove an owned Codex integration
body:
## Parent

[Implement convenient Codex onboarding](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/62)

## What to build

Use the shipped CLI to install into an isolated selected Codex home, explicitly enable a repository, observe a controlled review using environment credentials, disable it and remove the integration safely. Login and guided setup follow separately.

The parent specification governs shared scope and constraints.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Preview compatibility and exact owned changes before mutation; install an adapter-backed user-scope integration with versioned ownership records and a durable packaged executable.
- [ ] Repeat installation is idempotent. Preserve unrelated settings/order/hooks; handle custom homes, quoted paths, malformed or unreadable config, duplicate scopes and locally modified owned entries without destructive overwrites.
- [ ] Bound configuration locking/concurrent-change detection, write atomically per file and expose journaled partial completion/recovery for multi-file failures; never restore stale whole-file backups over other tools.
- [ ] Enable uses canonical root/backend/destination preview and matching-digest approval; install grants no source egress. Disable prevents later provider dispatch; moved/unapproved roots remain disabled.
- [ ] Guide native trust without editing trust records, bypass flags or evading managed policy. Real Codex invokes the integration and an unrelated hook remains effective.
- [ ] Scoped uninstall removes only owned integration state and preserves user rules, credentials, grants and unrelated work; clearly explain remaining state and no recall of sent requests.
- [ ] Provide noninteractive operation and versioned structured results for these commands; exercise public CLI behavior with controlled offline responses.

## Blocked by

- [Run direct-event review from a clean Linux package](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/63)

title: Save, replace and revoke the review credential on Linux
body:
## Parent

[Implement convenient Codex onboarding](https://github.com/dearlordylord/jevs/issues/62)

## What to build

Enter a key once using the installed CLI, then use it from a new Codex/resident session on Linux. Deliver the full credential lifecycle, including replacement and logout before future dispatch, rather than a storage-only API.

The parent specification governs shared scope and constraints.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Probe persistent Secret Service storage and actual bounded nonprompting host/resident retrieval before selecting a binding; no plaintext or volatile fallback presented as durable secure storage.
- [ ] Masked login or explicitly requested stdin stores one owned default credential without a paid verification call; new sessions reuse it. No values enter arguments, repository files, ordinary logs or source-bearing evidence.
- [ ] Explicit credentialEnvVar selection is environment-only; otherwise the nonempty default environment key overrides saved storage. Missing/invalid selected credentials never fall back to another account.

- [ ] Logout preserves grants, reports a surviving environment override and cannot recall sent requests. Deletion failure is honest and suspends saved-key use pending recovery.

title: Generate configuration documentation and JSON Schemas from Effect Schema
body:
## Problem Statement

Users need to discover what the review integration can configure without reading a large README. They also need a complete, accurate configuration guide. Maintainers currently repeat configuration definitions across Effect Schema, manually maintained JSON Schemas, and prose. These copies can drift, leaving editor assistance and documentation inconsistent with the product.

## Solution

Use Effect Schema as the source of structural field definitions. Generate a short README introduction and a full configuration reference through one generator module. Generate the product's configuration and rule-pack JSON Schemas from their Effect Schema definitions as well.

The README introduction must demonstrate that configuration is available, summarize useful capabilities, show a small valid example, and link to the full guide while using little space. The full guide must describe all configuration fields and retain reviewed explanations of behavior that field schemas cannot express. A deterministic verification command must detect stale generated output.

## User Stories

1. As a new user, I want the README to show that the review integration is configurable, so that I can discover this capability quickly.
2. As a new user, I want a compact overview of what I can configure, so that I can assess whether the product meets my needs.
3. As a user, I want a small valid configuration example, so that I can start configuring the product.
4. As a user, I want a direct link to the full guide, so that I can find details without enlarging the README.
5. As a user, I want the full reference to describe every configuration field, so that I do not need to inspect implementation code.
6. As a user, I want field types, accepted values, bounds, and requiredness documented accurately, so that I can write valid configuration.
7. As a user, I want omission, inheritance, empty values, and defaults distinguished, so that I understand the result of leaving a field out.
8. As a user, I want configuration precedence and accumulated exclusions explained, so that I can predict file selection.
9. As a user, I want repository enablement explained separately from configuration, so that I do not mistake a configuration field for permission to send source to a review backend.
10. As a user, I want the guide to distinguish accepted settings from settings used by the current runtime path, so that I do not expect unsupported behavior.
11. As a user, I want unsupported authorization fields rejected, so that configuration cannot be mistaken for repository approval.
12. As a user, I want editor assistance to use the same field definitions as the product, so that its suggestions remain useful.
13. As a rule-pack author, I want the rule-pack JSON Schema generated from the corresponding Effect Schema, so that its field definitions do not need a separate manual update.
14. As a maintainer, I want to change structural field definitions once, so that documentation and JSON Schema outputs stay consistent.
15. As a maintainer, I want the short-version selection logic in the generator module, so that the README does not become another manually maintained reference.
16. As a maintainer, I want one update command for generated outputs, so that regeneration is repeatable.
17. As a maintainer, I want a read-only stale-output check, so that automated validation detects missing regeneration.
18. As a documentation author, I want authored explanations preserved during generation, so that accurate behavioral context is not overwritten.

## Implementation Decisions

- Use the existing TypeScript and pinned Effect 4 RC cohort. No dependency upgrade is required by this feature.
- Effect Schema owns field names, structural types, requiredness, representable constraints, and field descriptions through annotations. Do not maintain a parallel handwritten field catalog or JSON Schema definition.
- Generate both existing product-owned JSON Schema artifacts from the single canonical Effect-defined wire format. The existing hand-written artifacts are prototype outputs, not a compatibility baseline; assess generated output against the specified wire format semantically, not solely as text changes. Vendored historical evidence is excluded.
- A single generator module produces both documentation versions. Its explicit selection and presentation logic makes the short version; it must not simply truncate the full reference.
- The short version includes a capability summary, a small valid example, and a link to the full guide. Avoid an exhaustive field table in the README.
- The full version covers the complete configuration structure, including nested rule overrides, runtime settings, and rule-pack references. A new comprehensive rule-pack authoring manual is not required.
- Keep generated material within clear boundaries so regeneration preserves authored surrounding prose. Shared descriptions and behavioral explanations must have one maintained source wherever reused across outputs. Generated repetition is acceptable; separately maintained copies are not.
- Read defaults and other reusable values from their existing authoritative definitions rather than copying constants into the generator. Optionality does not imply that a field has a local default: omission can mean inheritance.
- Preserve reviewed behavioral explanations for precedence, protected exclusions, repository enablement, credential selection, and the fixed Jev destination. Follow the existing decisions on repository-scoped approval and exclusion accumulation.
- Verify current runtime behavior before publishing claims about settings. In particular, accepted configuration fields must not be presented as effective controls for a runtime path that ignores them.
- Explain the limits of JSON Schema: it does not replace JSONC parsing, semantic checks, explicit conversion into internal types, or repository policy. Effect Schema owns the accepted structural wire format; remove parallel manual structural validation. Configuration uses a ruleOverrides map only and rejects array shorthand and inert consent/enabled fields. Rule packs use schemaVersion, id, contentVersion, threshold, message, and string-valued criteria.false/criteria.true; reject packId, packVersion, version aliases, defaultThreshold, defaultMessage, and object-form criteria. There are no users relying on these prototype alternatives. Code-native Noul question structures remain separate and are explicitly rendered to the Effect Decision string contract.
- Provide deterministic update and read-only check modes. Check mode reports stale or missing generated artifacts and returns a failure status without rewriting files. Connect it to the repository's applicable automated validation.
- Borrow the sibling project's marked-section generation and verification pattern, adapting it to configuration constraints rather than treating its extractor as a drop-in implementation.

## Testing Decisions

- Proposed primary seam: exercise the generator's public update/check boundary in temporary fixtures. Assert externally visible artifacts, exit status, and preservation of authored content, rather than helper structure or schema traversal internals.
- Verify that generation emits both documentation versions and both JSON Schemas, is deterministic and idempotent, and that check mode succeeds for current output and fails without modifying stale or missing output.
- Verify representative public field contracts: nested fields, unions, optionality, numeric bounds, descriptions, and reusable definitions. Demonstrate that changing an authoritative schema definition updates the relevant generated artifacts without editing a second field catalog.
- Validate generated examples using the existing configuration decoding boundary. Use the existing configuration and rule-pack test suites for focused regressions as the canonical input boundary replaces prototype alternatives.
- Prior art: existing Vitest configuration decoding tests and subprocess tests already exercise public configuration behavior and temporary-directory workflows. The sibling project's reference generator supplies prior art for stale-output verification.
- Keep tests deterministic and offline. No credentials, paid Jev calls, or agent-host sessions are needed.
- The user confirmed this test approach: generated outputs, the update/check commands, and example validation through the existing configuration decoder.

## Out of Scope

- New configuration capabilities, precedence rules, repository enablement rules, host adapters, or model-provider targets.
- Making currently inactive runtime settings effective.
- A broad decoder rewrite beyond removing duplicate structural checks and unsupported prototype input forms, or a general runtime bug-fixing project.
- A separate schema definition language or documentation framework.
- Generating or rewriting vendored historical artifacts.
- A full rule-pack authoring manual, a hosted schema service, or release-distribution changes.

## Further Notes

The user explicitly requested no independently maintained duplicate definitions, both short and full documentation versions, short-version logic in the generator module, and generation of product JSON Schemas from Effect Schema.

Inspection found an existing discrepancy to resolve before using fractional threshold examples as acceptance evidence: the Effect Schema permits fractional rule-override thresholds, while a manual decoder helper appears to require integers. Treat this as a bounded contract prerequisite or linked bug; do not silently change the documented contract to match an accidental restriction.

The rule-override map is the sole accepted configuration form. Remove array shorthand and the other prototype alternatives named above from decoding, generated schemas, tests, and documentation. Conversion from the accepted wire format into internal data types must be explicit.

Existing unrelated working-tree changes must be preserved. This issue specifies future implementation; preparing it does not implement the feature.

title: Prepare Jevs 0.1.0 npm release
body:
Prepares the public `@jevs/jevs@0.1.0` release for #87. The package exposes `jevs` and its helper commands, retains the pilot hook ownership, consent, and credential identities for migration, and ships a host-side command that checks the reviewed commit and exact archive SHA-256 before publishing directly to npm `latest`. The source repository remains private, so the release record uses commit and archive checksum evidence rather than npm provenance attestation.

Linux arm64 validation passed the offline suite (426 tests; one provenance assertion updated and its four-test file rerun), typecheck, native verification, scoped tarball audit, production-only packed conformance, and a scripts-disabled user-prefix installation under shell Node 22.22.2 selecting packaged Node 24.20.0. An isolated pilot-to-scoped-package update preview/apply passed across separate npm prefixes. Two local packs matched SHA-256 `7f8acec0adc1c24aa57255207e499dd10ada7182666fe172d462ef96bb3de874`; the 105-file archive and seven native artifacts audited against clean commit `acaf0d75fd37d2bb6f8511480ed71b26b7324fda`.

The release guide makes CI optional evidence, not a publish gate. Publication still requires the reviewed change on clean `master` and the maintainer's logged-in npm host. After publication, the registry archive must match the checksum and pass isolated package and supervised live review-and-repair checks on each advertised profile. The record leaves those cells pending until measured; no registry release is claimed yet.

title: Simplify pinned npm release command
body:
Stores the reviewed source commit and archive SHA-256 in `scripts/npm-release-pin.json`, so the maintainer can run `git pull --ff-only origin master && npm run release:local` without copying long hashes. The release script still requires clean `master` equal to `origin/master`, verifies the pinned commit is in its history, compares the built archive with the pinned checksum, and verifies the registry artifact and `latest` tag. The release archive contents and digest remain unchanged because the pin and release record are outside the package allowlist.

This removes only duplicated command-line values; CI remains optional evidence and does not gate publication.

title: Select pinned Node for host release
body:
The host publish command failed on Node 25.6.1 because release assembly is pinned to Node 24.20.0 to reproduce the reviewed archive checksum. This follows the host-runtime selection used by Huly: the publishing guide runs `mise exec node@24.20.0 -- npm run release:local`, so `mise` selects Node for npm and the release script even when a newer Node is active. A direct invocation under the wrong runtime now prints the exact remediation command.

This changes release guidance and its preflight error only; it does not change the package archive or release pin. CI is not a publication gate.

title: Install host dependencies before release build
body:
The macOS release attempt used Node 24.20.0 successfully but failed because the checkout's `node_modules` lacked TypeScript 7.0.2's locked Darwin arm64 optional compiler package, likely because dependencies had been installed on Linux. Huly's production release script restores dependencies from its frozen lockfile before building. Jevs now does the same with its pinned Bun 1.3.14 via mise, using `--frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts`, before running the release build. The host flow therefore repairs cross-platform `node_modules` while keeping its one-command deployment path.

The guide documents this step, and the release script verifies the package manager pin. This does not change packaged files or the archive SHA. CI is not a gate.

title: Specify diff-selected type and function review branches
body:
## Current disposition — 2026-10-04

Complete for the specification scope. The accepted [direct-edit type/function contract](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/docs/type-function-review-proposal.md) resolves root selection, supported declarations, bounded cross-file evidence, rule capabilities, identity, freshness and quiet skip behavior. The owner's 2026-09-29 adoption decision superseded the earlier future-prototype-only gate; implementation is reconciled in #138. Comparative quality evaluation remains #150, with no superiority claim from adoption.

[PR #149](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/pull/149) merged on 2026-09-30 at `07ecd4e4654ca4193c4d834b03f1db385d309b7d`; that commit is an ancestor of the audited checkout. The earlier “draft/unmerged” handoff is superseded.

## Original task scope

## Goal

Specify a proposed Hapsland review-input flow for a directly observed edit. The diff selects changed semantic roots; it is not automatically sent to Jev as the review input.

For each selected root, classify the artifact as a type declaration or a function declaration. Define a bounded expansion appropriate to that artifact kind, then select configurable rules whose required evidence is available. The type and function branches may have different review-unit and review-input contracts.

This is a specification task for later product decision, not authorization to implement either branch or to add raw-diff review.

## Questions the specification must resolve

- How does a direct-edit diff identify roots in Add and Update events? What happens when one edit changes several roots, or when attribution is uncertain?
- Which type declarations and function declarations are in scope? How does each branch expand references or other supporting evidence, and where do depth, count, byte, time, and source-egress limits apply?
- How are rule packs/configuration associated with artifact kind, input contract, and evidence requirements? Can a rule apply to both branches?
- What is the exact review unit, completeness state, snapshot/projection identity, Jev payload, and stale-result policy for each branch?
- When analysis is inapplicable or required evidence is missing, how does Hapsland skip review quietly? Keep agent-facing advice free of non-actionable errors; retain only bounded, source-free coverage/status reasons for human inspection. No raw-diff fallback is implied.
- How will synthetic positive/negative fixtures and bounded live evaluation test semantic value, false advice, latency, and egress before production adoption?

## Handoff

Produce a normative proposal that separates accepted requirements from open choices, names the versioned contracts and supported host events, and gives acceptance checks for a later prototype. Reconcile it with the current same-file named-type direct-event profile and the result of #16. Keep checkpoint reconciliation, shell/Stop discovery, and re-review of unchanged dependents outside this task unless explicitly re-scoped.

Related: #96 (user-contract readiness), #16 (input comparison), #19 (review-unit vocabulary), and the current direct-event supported profile in `docs/direct-event-v1-supported-profile.md`.

title: Complete OpenCode lifecycle integration and native support acceptance
body:
## Current status — 2026-10-04, reconciled after #116

Incomplete: **OpenCode implementation and exact native support acceptance remain**, not merely a final live validation. The current OpenCode adapter is intentionally quiet; install/update return unsupported and doctor reports the missing pre-edit permit lifecycle. Owned uninstall remains available. See the [current OpenCode boundary](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/docs/opencode-installation.md) and [installer](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/src/onboarding/opencode-installation.ts). The older after-hook candidate is not a currently enabled review path.

Claude implementation and selected native Linux observations are delivered through #145 and later [native-language evidence](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/evidence/native-languages/index.json), including selected live Jev finding/repair/clear observations. These supersede the older blanket “no live Jev” comment but do not establish arbitrary modes, versions, reaction rates or the current registry artifact. Do not redo that delivered work under this task.

Remaining sequence:

- [ ] Select the exact OpenCode version/mode/platform and decide whether to resume this integration.
- [ ] Establish a blocking pre-edit permit hook, correlated after-edit identity, retirement of failed/unused permits and a finish boundary supporting bounded advice wait. Available API fields alone do not establish these runtime guarantees.
- [ ] Implement the accepted lifecycle through the shared canonical boundary, then exercise installer coexistence/removal and stale/failure cases.
- [ ] Observe finding submission, native model visibility, subsequent action and follow-up separately in bounded authenticated runs before declaring support.

Keep additional Claude support cells explicit; macOS remains #172 and registry artifact checks remain the publishing workflow. Current contract/evidence owners are the testing matrix, advice contract and installed compatibility record. Removed `docs/issue-94-*` snapshot links in historical comments are not current owners. No new native run, provider call or support claim was made during this reconciliation.

## Task scope and prior planning

## Goal

Extend Hapsland beyond its current Codex CLI adapter to Claude Code and OpenCode. Keep the product-owned review unit, rule policy, consent, Jev integration, and source limits independent of the agent host. Declare support only for exact host versions and modes that pass real-host checks.

## Work

- Inspect each host's official lifecycle and payload contract. Identify direct successful edit events, available attribution to the exact current snapshot and advice recipient, feedback channels, trust/installation steps, headless behavior, and failure behavior. Record gaps explicitly.
- Implement a host adapter for each supported edit path. Preserve the current direct-event review-input contract and quiet skip behavior when an event cannot establish a supported semantic root. Do not claim shell-write or checkpoint coverage from hook installation alone.
- Add preview/install/update/uninstall and doctor behavior that preserves unrelated hooks or plugins and keeps repository enablement and source-egress consent separate from installation and host trust.
- Test asynchronous advice handoff: measure edit-to-submission and edit-to-agent-visible advice on representative findings, including no later event, stale result, restart, timeout, and host failure. Do not promise a fixed delivery time without evidence.
- Use deterministic offline fixtures for ordinary tests and isolated real-host runs for host-owned behavior. Record sanitized, source-free version/mode/platform evidence; no credentials or source-bearing responses in records.

## Acceptance

- A compatibility card and tested adapter path exist for Claude Code and OpenCode separately. Unsupported event/mode cells remain explicit.
- Findings reach the intended agent context in a real run, with observed reaction distinguished from writing output to a hook or plugin.
- No accepted review result is delivered after its snapshot or recipient authority is stale; failures leave the completed edit intact and do not spam the agent with non-actionable errors.
- Installation, coexistence with another tool, disablement, and removal are exercised without taking ownership of unrelated host configuration.

Use the Codex delivery baseline from #97 when choosing each host's handoff strategy.

This issue does not include checkpoint reconciliation, turn-end discovery, or shell-write catch-up. Those remain separate decisions.

title: Evaluate Hapsland with a multi-file interface and parser task
body:
## Current status — 2026-10-04

Incomplete evaluation; the previous Stage 2 protocol was stopped by owner decision. [The existing stop comment](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/95#issuecomment-5827251402) remains authoritative for its missing runtime record, absent valid pair and prohibition on retries under that protocol. #150 asks a distinct input-context comparison question.

Next decision: whether to resume the broader agent-output evaluation under a newly accepted fixture and separately preregistered bounded protocol. No pilot retry, paid backend call or evidence of output improvement is implied by this cleanup. Historical stop-report snapshot links may be retrieved at their provenance commits; their absence at current `master` is not a new experiment result.

## Task scope and prior planning

## Goal

Design and run a comparative evaluation of Hapsland's effect on an agent's code quality and task performance. The first deliverable is a prompt and resulting code tree for owner review. Do not start the comparative runs until the owner accepts that prompt and tree.

## Stage 1: choose a task

- Draft a realistic prompt that asks an agent to build a substantial, multi-file interface/type and parser tree. State normal functional requirements and tests. Do not hint that the agent should create mistakes, mention the review rules, or steer it toward a known failure.
- Pilot candidate prompts with a declared agent host/model, such as Codex with Luna; max reasoning is optional, without Hapsland. Check that the result is a useful tree and that an independent review finds genuine errors relevant to Hapsland's supported rules. A prompt that produces no such errors is not the evaluation fixture; record that selection process rather than hiding it.
- Save the selected prompt, agent/host version, environment, seed or repeat settings where available, and the generated tree or a reviewable private artifact. The owner reviews the tree and explicitly accepts or rejects this fixture before Stage 2.

## Stage 2: paired runs after owner acceptance

- Freeze the accepted prompt and predeclare the quality rubric, unit of comparison, sample count, cost/time ceilings, and stopping rule.
- Compare matched runs of (A) agent self-review plus Hapsland and (B) agent self-review alone. Use the same tested-agent host/model/reasoning effort, task, tools, time budget, and evaluation method. The developers may use any model. Vary only Hapsland availability; record exposure, findings, agent-visible advice, attempted repair, and final artifact separately.
- Assess final correctness with tests and independent review of the interface/parser design. Measure elapsed time, Jev requests/cost, agent tokens/cost where available, false or missed findings, and repair cycles. Separate host submission from demonstrated agent visibility. Measure the fraction of eligible findings visible before the originating turn ends, visible only on a later turn, and never visible before expiry or resident loss. Report variance and limitations; do not infer causality from one lucky pair.
- Keep ordinary harness tests offline. Any live Jev runs need an explicit bounded call plan, available credentials, and sanitized evidence. Do not print or commit credentials or source-bearing live responses.

## Handoff

Stage 1 ends with a concrete prompt and tree for owner review. Stage 2 begins only after that review accepts the fixture. This issue is evaluation design and execution work, not a claim that the current product improves agent output.

title: Prepare user contracts for future review branches and rule forms

title: Prototype Codex turn-end review delivery
body:
## Question

For Hapsland's supported Codex direct-edit path, how often does review remain in flight when the originating turn ends? Would a bounded turn-end wait let the intended agent see and act on more findings without an unacceptable delay or feedback loop?

This is an isolated measurement and prototype task using Codex with Luna as the tested agent model. It does not authorize a production Stop hook, a change to normal edit latency, checkpoint reconciliation, or an unbounded wait.

## Baseline measurement

- Reconcile #23 and #24 with the implemented adapter. Check the exact tested Codex versions for synchronous Stop, background-hook completion, model-visible output, and session-end behavior; current host documentation alone is not conformance evidence.
- In isolated sessions, record source-free timestamps for edit hook entry/return, review admission, backend completion, turn completion, host submission, and independently observed model reaction. Use synthetic source and a controlled offline backend first.
- Report denominators separately: eligible direct edits, admitted reviews, completed reviews with findings, findings still in flight at turn end, findings visible in the originating turn, visible later, and never visible before expiry/session end. Keep clear/unavailable reviews separate from findings. A selected fixture set is not a population rate.

## Prototype alternatives

Compare the current subsequent-hook collection against at least a bounded Stop-hook wait for the **current repository and advice recipient's** admitted work, not the global queue. For this prototype, the Stop hook should wait at most 5 seconds from hook entry for the recipient-scoped queue, collect ready advice, and allow normal turn completion when no actionable finding is ready. Include IPC and response writing inside that 5-second budget. If a current finding is ready, test Codex's supported continuation/feedback path and cap repeated continuations so the hook cannot loop forever. A queue that cannot drain before the ceiling must not hold the turn indefinitely.

Also check whether a Codex background hook can deliver completed review output at the next safe point on the exact supported host version. Treat it as a separate candidate rather than assuming it works or combining several changes into one result.

Use controlled backend delays before and after turn end, plus multi-unit and failure cases. Measure added edit latency, added turn-end latency, same-turn agent visibility, reaction/repair, stale-result suppression, recipient isolation, and results after timeout. Run the tested Codex agent with Luna; select and record its reasoning effort before the experiment. The developers may use any model. Record exact host/model/version/mode. If useful, perform a separately budgeted live Jev sample with available credentials and retain only sanitized aggregate evidence.

## Handoff

Produce a comparison and recommendation: keep the current policy, specify a bounded turn-end collection path, investigate background hooks further, or choose another approach. Include the observed frequency and latency distribution with sample limits, and assess whether the provisional 5-second ceiling is useful before recommending any production value. Production adoption needs its own compatibility and acceptance gate.

Related: #95 evaluates whether visible advice improves task output. This issue determines the Codex delivery path independently of that task fixture. Checkpoint reconciliation and shell-write discovery remain out of scope.

title: Resident dispatch sends prepared source after completed exclusion update
body:
## Confirmed defect

On the unfixed direct-event resident route, a prepared `type.ts` unit reached `DecisionModel.decide` after a completed `.review.jsonc` update excluded that path. This violated existing conformance obligation 11b, which requires current configuration to be rechecked before resident backend dispatch. Later publication revalidation could suppress advice, but only after the provider attempt.

The original synthetic reproduction was observed on development revision `b4af0533ba3fdf2689fdc15b2b745134e16c9caf` (Linux arm64, Node 24, Effect RC.116): allowed control 1 attempt, initially excluded control 0, prepare → exclude → dispatch 1. The observer was the provider-neutral model boundary, not the serialized HTTP body. [Retained evidence](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/fix/security-queued-dispatch-debug/docs/research/queued-exclusion-reproduction.md) records the scheduling barrier and scope.

## Fix and regression

[PR #102](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/pull/102) reloads current file policy after credential resolution and applies the shared path selection predicate to the prepared unit before provider evaluation. It also rechecks consent/root and credential authority at that boundary.

Run `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=1 src/resident/security-queued.test.ts`. The four cases cover an allowed positive control, an initially excluded path, a completed exclusion update after preparation, and an exclusion completed during the credential-to-dispatch wait. All four pass on the fix; queued excluded work makes zero provider attempts. The cases are included in direct-event conformance obligation 11b.

After `npm run build`, run `node scripts/security-prototype/installed-queued-witness.mjs`. The fresh installed archive produced attempt counts `1/0/0` on the fix. The same witness on an isolated unfixed checkout exited 1 with `1/0/1`. These are offline synthetic tests; the complete resident HTTP body remains a separate formal-gate witness.

title: Resident debug logging emits source-bearing unexpected exceptions
body:
## Confirmed defect

On an unfixed resident at revision `a6799312fcc6d2cccdcd66c318f98b62cffd1808` (Linux arm64, Node 24.20.0), an unexpected source-bearing `Error` injected after real preparation was printed verbatim to process stderr with `REVIEW_RESIDENT_DEBUG=1`. The `ResidentServer.afterPrepare` test hook supplied a synthetic marker also present in the fixture source. This proves the catch/output behavior for an injected unexpected cause; it does not prove that a naturally occurring production exception currently contains source.

The two resident catches used `console.error(cause)`. The normal launcher redirects resident stderr to a startup diagnostic file, but that exact launcher-file path was not exercised with the injected cause. Existing diagnostic requirements in #3 and #13 call for bounded, source-free output.

## Fix and regression

[PR #102](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/pull/102) replaces those arbitrary exception logs with fixed preparation/evaluation categories. Run `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=1 src/resident/security-sinks.test.ts`; the injected-error case requires the bounded preparation category and rejects the synthetic source marker in actual child stderr. Its other case checks an ordinary controlled backend failure against resident IPC, output, and isolated stores.

After `npm run build`, run `node scripts/security-prototype/installed-debug-witness.mjs`. The fresh installed resident module emitted the fixed category and no marker. The same witness on an isolated unfixed checkout exited 1 because the marker reached stderr. These tests cover the catch-to-stderr boundary. Observing the normal launcher's diagnostic file and arbitrary attempted writes remains separate formal-gate work, recorded in the [prototype results](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/fix/security-queued-dispatch-debug/docs/research/formal-security-prototype/RESULTS.md).

title: Validate concurrent build/replay after atomic native artifact publication
body:
