Incomplete: the artifact-publication fix is merged; the original concurrent security replay acceptance remains untested. [Commit bd1f251a](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/commit/bd1f251ae0af6779aa2e16010f4dc8d420d9f93d) stages native builds/copies and atomically renames onto a new inode. The current retained gate passed all three [native-artifact tests](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/scripts/native-artifact.test.mts). The [bounded scratch parser probe](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/evidence/effect4-migration/native-publication-probe.json) reproduces overwrite crashes and observes atomic publication completing on Linux arm64 / Node 24.20.0. It explicitly does not attribute every historical crash.

Remaining acceptance: reproduce the original bounded **concurrent helper build plus security replay**, observing both process exits and the authorized/denied wire outcomes. The scratch-parser probe and inode tests do not replace that boundary. Preserve synthetic/offline execution and finite deadlines.

Original reproduction paths belong to the historical comparison branch, not the current `master` documentation tree.

## Task scope and prior planning

## Affected revision and profile

Comparison branch `52a90f3` (`research/formal-security-tool-comparison`), Linux arm64, Node 24.20.0. This is a development/build reliability defect; no source egress or production security bypass was observed.

## Reproduction

From that checkout, with the connector prototype installed as documented in `docs/research/formal-security-prototype/connector/README.md`, start `npm run build` concurrently with `node --experimental-strip-types security-run.mjs strict 424242 11` from `docs/research/formal-security-prototype/connector`. The replay uses only synthetic repository fixtures and an offline Jev transport. In three bounded paired trials, the build completed and the replay exited by SIGSEGV with no stderr. In a separate control, delayed `node scripts/build-capture-helper.mjs` overlapped the replay and produced SIGSEGV in three of three trials. Eight replay-only concurrent runs passed. Full sanitized timing and controls: `docs/research/formal-security-reliability.md` on the comparison branch.

## Expected versus observed

An active resident/replay should not crash when a local build refreshes native artifacts. The native helper currently copies Tree-sitter `.node` bindings directly into `native/prebuilt` using `copyFileSync` (`scripts/build-capture-helper.mjs`); the replay's analyzer loads/uses those bindings. The experiments localize the trigger to helper overlap, but do not identify which binding copy or native instruction faults.

## Acceptance check

Use an isolated or atomic artifact replacement strategy so a build cannot replace a binding in place while an active process uses it. Add a bounded synthetic concurrent build/replay check: both processes must complete without SIGSEGV, and the replay must still report its authorized and denied wire scenarios. Keep normal security checks serial until that acceptance is met; a process crash must never count as a security counterexample or a passing gate.

title: Deliver and validate reusable background and Stop review delivery
body:
**Completed on 2026-09-27 within the owner-accepted Linux scope.** PR #108 merged at `29d5d72`. The owner explicitly accepted timing review and Linux adoption and authorized closure. The [closure workflow](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/actions/runs/36297644979) passed and created/linked #113 for deferred macOS validation. See the [completion report](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/105#issuecomment-5853044119) and [evidence/dispositions](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/master/evidence/advicing-linux/finish-decision-linux.md). The planning text below is retained as history; unproven native observations remain explicitly limited by the accepted scope, not asserted as passing.

## Context

Background delivery was part of the original intended product behavior. The current production Codex path admits reviews asynchronously but collects ready advice through subsequent mapped edit hooks; asynchronous review execution alone does not provide background host delivery.

Issue #97 completed selected delivery measurements and disposable prototypes. Native Codex background-hook output reached the model when it arrived before a subsequent model request; later output missed the opportunity before session end. Bounded Stop collection provided another delivery opportunity, including through the production resident on the supported Linux profile. Neither background delivery nor a production Stop collection hook was adopted by that measurement.

This issue owns composed background and bounded Stop delivery for Codex and Claude Code on Linux. Both hosts must use one reusable resident-owned delivery lifecycle and ownership protocol, partitioned by advicee, including when their collectors race. The current production delivery policies remain unchanged until the combined contracts are accepted and their gates pass. The observable product outcome is a suggestion that the agent previously missed reaching the agent and being acted on: first in headless Codex, then in headless Claude Code.

Related decisions:
- #24 defines explicit advicee/root partitioning for work, results, and advice, freshness, and delivery truthfulness.
- #36 establishes the attribution boundary: preserve supplied agent identity; shared-root checkpoint-only changes have unknown origin and no agent advicee.
- #64 completed the broader packaged macOS Codex host integration. It does not validate this combined delivery path.
- #87 tracks the supported installed-release profiles.

**Stop terminology:** `Stop`/`SubagentStop` is the agent runtime hook when an agent tries to finish. Hapsland may wait inside that hook. A Stop block response carries ordinary review advice and asks the runtime to continue the same Hapsland round; a Stop allow response closes Hapsland's round. There is no Jev Stop API call.

## Goal

Deliver and validate background review delivery together with bounded Stop collection as one reusable runtime-neutral delivery architecture for Codex and Claude Code on Linux. Background delivery should make completed advice available at supported host safe points without requiring another edit. Stop collection should provide a final bounded opportunity for eligible advice, including a bounded reoffer of background-submitted advice when agent consumption is unknown. Show a matched before/after Linux case in which a review suggestion previously missed the agent, then reaches the agent and causes an independently verified repair: first in headless Codex, then in headless Claude Code. Decide the exact waiting and continuation policy and establish the host and resident evidence required before production adoption.

## Current evidence and open gates (2026-09-26)

- **Matched Linux before/after outcome passed three consecutive runs after correction `bc50725`:** [round 1](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/feat/issue-105-composed-delivery/evidence/advicing-linux/linux-repeatability-final-1.json), [round 2](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/feat/issue-105-composed-delivery/evidence/advicing-linux/linux-repeatability-final-2.json), [round 3](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/feat/issue-105-composed-delivery/evidence/advicing-linux/linux-repeatability-final-3.json). Codex 0.155.1 ran first, followed by Claude 2.1.218, on Linux arm64 / Node 24.20.0 with the production resident and controlled offline Effect backend. Every before completed review with no finding handoff or repair; every after handed off advice through a Stop block response, observed a repair edit, checked the repaired file, and completed a clear follow-up. The resident was ready before runtime launch. Background was registered but delayed, so these do not prove simultaneous collector behavior.
- **Native background outcome passed on both runtimes:** [background record](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/feat/issue-105-composed-delivery/evidence/advicing-linux/linux-background-final.json) records background finding submission, repair, repaired file, and clear follow-up without a Stop block. This is a selected available delivery opportunity, not proof of all final-response/after-end timing boundaries.
- **Nonpassing baseline attempts retained:** the [cold miss](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/feat/issue-105-composed-delivery/evidence/advicing-linux/linux-repeatability-round-cold-miss.json) had no Claude baseline backend completion; the [fast-baseline miss](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/feat/issue-105-composed-delivery/evidence/advicing-linux/linux-repeatability-round-fast-baseline-miss.json) delivered advice and repaired in the baseline itself. Neither is a valid missed-advice before case. Passing selected attempts do not establish a population success rate or cold-start reliability.
- **Candidate code and checks:** `b36b879` implements resident round ownership and policy. Full suite: **535 passed, 2 skipped**; build passed. Direct-event conformance passed **231/231**, and clean package conformance passed after Codex edit-hook correction `bc50725`. The source-free resident-contract harness passed **14/14** on candidate `44d3992`, recorded in `a67be55`. After merging current master in `98298a4`, the final full suite passed **535 tests / 2 skipped**. Build, direct-event **231/231**, clean package, setup package, and pinned installed-host conformance all passed. These checks are separate from native agent visibility and repair evidence.
- **Selected final-candidate command timing passed:** [ptrace record](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/feat/issue-105-composed-delivery/evidence/advicing-linux/linux-final-command-timing.json) measures native child creation through exit. Codex edit commands took 303.289 / 315.180 ms and Stop commands 343.550 / 2,260.624 ms; Claude edit commands took 320.371 / 339.752 ms and Stop commands 2,783.928 / 3,808.083 ms. All four measured Stop commands stayed below five seconds. Tracing adds overhead. Deliberately delayed background commands were cancelled at teardown, so their lifetimes do not measure background delivery latency. PreToolUse launch windows are absent from that earlier tracer record; the later timing evidence below supplies nine such windows. Broader timing distributions remain unestablished.
- **Deterministic resident-contract gates passed 14/14:** [results](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/feat/issue-105-composed-delivery/evidence/advicing-linux/linux-round-contract.json), [scope](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/feat/issue-105-composed-delivery/evidence/advicing-linux/round-contract-linux.md). Seven cases for each Codex/Claude adapter identity use the real resident, local IPC, real Stop CLI, and controlled offline Effect backend. They cover deadline cancellation and queued-resource cleanup with zero retained review bytes/advice/cache/current-work records; unavailable notice/closure; stale removal; multi-unit collection; background lease competition; acknowledged and uncertain background reoffer once without a new evaluation; four fixture repair continuations, fifth-finding discard, and fresh-round count renewal. Old tokens cannot regain ownership. Runtime events, edits, and acknowledgements are fixtures; this harness contains no native agent or live Jev and does not establish visibility or actual agent repair.
- **Native Stop isolation passed the observed subset (`407b003`):** [record](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/feat/issue-105-composed-delivery/evidence/advicing-linux/linux-native-isolation.json), [scope](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/feat/issue-105-composed-delivery/evidence/advicing-linux/native-isolation-linux.md). Concurrent Codex and Claude sessions in distinct physical worktrees used one shared resident and received only their own finding. Two supplied Claude child IDs each received their own SubagentStop finding; parent Stop received neither. Codex's child invocation exposed no available subagent route and made no edit, so Codex child isolation remains unobserved. These are Hapsland native Stop-output checks, not background delivery, model visibility, repair, or proof of simultaneous backend evaluation.
- **Review artifact and worktree index:** [draft PR #108](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/pull/108) contains the candidate implementation, evidence, and independent Foldkit package. The single active #105 worktree is `/workspace/typescript/jev-worktrees/issue-105-composed` on `feat/issue-105-composed-delivery`. [PR #110](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/pull/110) and the older sidecar PR #109 are closed as superseded; their branch history remains available. No separate #105 sidecar worktree is needed. Draft status does not establish production adoption.
- **Latest native timing, contention, and routing evidence (`dc5ff9e`):** [scope and retained attempts](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/feat/issue-105-composed-delivery/evidence/advicing-linux/native-background-timing-linux.md). Codex background submission occurred inside a native tool call and repair followed without Stop block; the delayed follow-up review did not clear before cleanup. Claude background submission occurred inside a streamed final-message interval, followed by Stop reoffer and repair; earlier consumption is unknown. Codex Stop won the only finding lease during overlapping collection; Claude background won first and Stop later received a distinct reoffer lease. Concurrent Codex background sessions each received only their own advice. Nine instrumented PreToolUse commands took 294.16–356.35 ms including wrapper/observer overhead. After-end observations cover two seconds only.

- **Claude recovery rerun (`5135735`):** [report and retained records](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/feat/issue-105-composed-delivery/evidence/advicing-linux/claude-reset-rerun-linux.md). Minimal settings-excluded control exited 0 in 3.818 s. Concurrent background routing passed on the first pair: distinct native sessions/worktrees, shared resident, only own background finding and Stop reoffer, zero foreign deliveries, no hook failures. The actionable foreground-tool interval remains unproven after three attempts despite native repair in all three. Attempt 2 observed clear-review completion inside foreground Bash but initiated SIGTERM at 100 s and returned after pipe/process closure at 106.201 s; it is a nonpassing timeout. Attempts 1/3 exited successfully but made no Bash call and had no clear follow-up before cleanup. No fourth attempt ran. Earlier runtime failures' cause remains unknown.

### Owner support decision and remaining acceptance work

The owner **accepts the narrower Linux support boundary on the condition that the bottom of the Foldkit demo contains the timing diagram described below**. This is a recorded scope decision, not a claim that unobserved probes passed. The owner delegated representation choices after Astra pre-research. The Foldkit package is now inside draft PR #108 in the single #105 worktree; production Hapsland does not import it.

| Area | Accepted evidence/disposition | Remaining acceptance work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before → after repair | Three final matched Linux runs, plus separate native background repair and clear follow-up on Codex and Claude | Preserve required product case labels and evidence scope in demo |
| Round ownership and Stop rules | Resident contract 14/14; native lease overlap and reoffer; four requests per round, each new round gets four; restart resets count | Show reducer coverage and limits; no count carry across restart, now or planned (#107 closed not planned) |
| Routing | Concurrent native worktree Stop/background routing passed on both runtimes; two supplied Claude child IDs isolated | Show observed scope; do not imply native Codex child coverage |
| Runtime timing and visibility | Narrower boundary **conditionally accepted**: actionable Claude foreground-tool interval unproven; Codex in-progress final/model-request and child behavior unobserved; after-end evidence bounded to two seconds; submitted output does not prove consumption | Display these limits and successful/missed scenarios in bottom timing diagram; no automatic additional probe requirement solely to fill accepted unknowns |
| Missed exploratory attempts | Claude three tool-window attempts retained; all repaired, none passed target interval; attempt 2 timed out despite later clear review inside Bash | Label exploratory targets separately from required product outcomes; retain timeout and missed-interval distinctions |
| Candidate checks | Full suite 535 passed / 2 skipped, build, direct-event 231/231, clean/setup packages and pinned installed-host conformance passed | Keep separate from native behavior and reducer guarantees |
| Foldkit timing-diagram condition | **Implementation fulfilled** in the Foldkit package of draft PR #108 (`fa1277c`); build and browser render passed. The page has a top jump link to bottom timelines, observable agent stages, required/exploratory and observed/unproven labels, visible unknown spans, and explicit partial reducer coverage | **Open:** owner visual review and adoption. Grey spans mean missing evidence, not measured runtime stages; typed event identity and reducer replay do not prove native timing/visibility |
| Final review/adoption and closure | Narrowed boundary accepted subject to diagram condition; not an unconditional completion declaration | **Open:** visually review implemented diagram, record final review/adoption outcome; keep #105 open; closure must create/link macOS follow-up |

## Acceptance criteria

### Conditional Linux boundary and Foldkit timing diagram

- [x] Record owner acceptance of the narrower Linux support boundary **conditioned on the diagram requirement below**. Previously unobserved timing/child/visibility cases remain stated support limits, not passing observations. This disposition governs the detailed timing and runtime-coverage criteria below.
- [x] **Implementation fulfilled in the Foldkit package of PR #108 (`fa1277c`), subject to owner visual review/adoption:** add a timing diagram at the **bottom of the Foldkit demo** with a top jump link. Show observable agent/runtime stages versus unknown internal stages; successful and missed scenarios; required product cases versus exploratory probes; and exactly what the sidecar reducer statically checks and cannot establish. A completed write, fixture repair, or unknown model timing must not be shown as proven native agent consumption. Use the recorded evidence and preserve timeout/missed-interval outcomes.
- [ ] Review the diagram and evidence labels against #105, record the final adoption/review outcome, and complete the closure-triggered macOS follow-up requirement. Do not close #105 or merge merely because the narrower boundary is conditionally accepted.

### Single installed behavior and user decision

- [x] **Candidate installer implementation verified:** composed background + bounded Stop is the only behavior generated for supported Codex and Claude installations. The former runtime gate is absent. Both installers unconditionally register PreToolUse admission, composed PostToolUse admission plus async background, Stop/SubagentStop, and prompt hooks; no installed legacy/composed selector exists. The synchronous composed edit path returns after admission for both runtimes. Legacy CLI behavior remains callable for before-case probes but is not installed as an alternate mode. This checks candidate implementation; shipping/adoption still requires the separate owner decision and remaining gates below.
- [ ] Before closing #105, review the repeatability evidence, host limitations, and rollout/support impact **with the owner**. Record the owner’s explicit decision in this issue. The owner has directed that the accepted implementation have one behavior, but final adoption still depends on the evidence gates below; do not infer sign-off on unresolved failures from that design direction.


### Observable before → after outcome on Linux

- [ ] Establish a reproducible **before** case for each host with the current delivery policy: one attributable direct edit creates a controlled, actionable finding; the agent finishes without another mapped edit; no suggestion reaches an agent-visible host response before that finish; and the target defect remains. Record review completion and absence of handoff separately. A merely delayed or failed backend result is not a valid before case.
- [ ] Establish the matching **after** case on the same fixture with the candidate delivery path: the finding is current, a bounded hook response hands its suggestion to the intended host advicee, a subsequent model action independently demonstrates follow-through, the resulting file satisfies the requested repair, and a follow-up review is clear. A completed stdout write, acknowledgement, final message claiming repair, or elapsed wait alone is insufficient. Retain sanitized event order and exact before/after outcomes; do not infer a population success rate from selected runs.
- [ ] Pass the before/after gate **first with headless Codex on Linux**, then **with headless Claude Code on Linux**. Use the exact installed host and Node versions declared for each run, the production Hapsland resident, and a controlled offline Effect `DecisionModel`; state which host hook mechanism produces the after result. For **each host**, the after case must use background + bounded Stop composition through the same reusable resident delivery module, with host-specific hook output semantics. Existing Claude block-only behavior is prior evidence, not a passing #105 after case. A submitted suggestion without independently observed repair does not pass.

### Priority: accepted round and delivery behavior (2026-09-26)

- [ ] **P1 — Hapsland round ownership and cleanup:** A Hapsland round stays active when Hapsland asks the agent to continue at Stop. It closes when Hapsland finishes Stop handling and allows completion, without claiming that every other hook also allowed the agent to finish. Atomically close admission and cancel or discard all live work and data owned by that round, including pre-edit permits, already submitted advice and delivery records. Fence late results and duplicate events; retain only a source-free closed-round marker and truthful incomplete/discarded counts. A fresh attributed edit after another hook's continuation may start a new Hapsland round, even with the same native `turn_id`; repeated Stop, poll, retry, or old callback must not. Closing one agent's round must not affect another's.
- [ ] **P1 — Four Stop continuation requests:** Allow at most four Hapsland `decision: "block"` requests per Hapsland round. Count a reserved request before output; an uncertain write uses that reservation. Background output, repair edits, native turn changes, and repeated hooks do not reset the count. On the next Stop after exhaustion, allow completion without waiting for advice Hapsland cannot present, close the round, and classify remaining work as incomplete/discarded. Native runtime limits or other hooks may end work earlier; four is Hapsland's maximum, not four guaranteed resumptions. Preserve this per-round limit across duplicate Stop events and expiry while the resident process remains running; each new Hapsland round gets its own four requests. The owner explicitly rejected carrying a round’s count across resident restarts, including as future work. A restart mid-round forgets that count and may permit four more requests for the same unfinished agent work. Unbounded repeated restarts can yield unbounded aggregate continuation requests; reset on restart is accepted product behavior.
- [ ] **P1 — Same-round background-to-Stop reoffer:** If current advice was submitted through background output before Stop began or while Stop waits, but agent consumption remains unproven, Stop may offer that advice once within the active Hapsland round. Revalidate eligibility and coordinate the same resident-owned lease/submission state. Do not rerun Jev for reoffer. Discard the advice when the round closes; cross-round reoffer of submitted advice is not the owner decision.

The candidate round implementation is now pushed as `b36b879`: shared admission permits, round-owned review resources, four Stop requests per round, cleanup/fencing, and same-round reoffer. This is candidate code, not production adoption or proof that every acceptance criterion passes. The completed specification below governs the remaining conformance work.

### Completed specification rules (2026-09-26)

- **Round binding and fresh events:** Every admitted observation, preparation job, review unit, Jev request, advice item, lease, waiter, and output permit carries an opaque Hapsland round ID and resident lifetime. Native turn changes and prompts do not reset an active round. Install synchronous `PreToolUse` admission for eligible edit tools: before execution, obtain a source-free permit bound to advicee, native tool-use ID, round, and resident lifetime. `PostToolUse` must consume the matching permit before capture or review, including in the first round. No source capture, review queue, or Jev request occurs at PreToolUse. Duplicate IDs cannot renew consumed permits or repeat review. Closing a round invalidates all its permits. Reopening requires a pre-edit invocation that provably began after the monotonic closure boundary, still within its original deadline; the resident checks this atomically. Late IPC arrival, retries, delayed child-process launch, and missing timing must not create fresh authority. Installed wrappers must preserve a conservative invocation-start bound and deadlines through startup; expired/orphaned invocations fail incomplete. Preserve supplied child identity on both hooks; a parent permit cannot authorize a child's edit. Native transcript availability is not required. Validate the paired hooks and timeout/closure races on both pinned Linux runtimes before claiming conformance.
- **Ordering evidence and limits:** Process-start time is not the runtime event's queued time. The pre-edit permit proof also requires the runtime's synchronous barrier and cancellation of timed-out hook commands; a direct-exec wrapper alone does not prove arbitrary native scheduling. On 2026-09-26 pinned Codex 0.155.1 and Claude 2.1.218 headless/no-persistence main-agent probes delayed PreToolUse 6.5 seconds under a two-second timeout. Matching PostToolUse occurred after 2,019 ms and 2,046 ms respectively, so edits can proceed after hook timeout. Neither hook recorded its delayed completion through seven seconds after runtime exit. The same Claude child probe observed matching child PostToolUse after 2,040 ms and no delayed completion. Missing permits must therefore reject PostToolUse. These bounded observations do not establish arbitrary delayed launch, every descendant process, or all concurrent tool schedules; retain these validation limits explicitly.
- **Stop output ownership:** One collector owns an active Stop attempt. Reserve a continuation slot and per-advice Stop handoff before authorizing output. A repeated notification or permit cannot authorize replay. Uncertain output, partial writes, process death after authorization, and lost acknowledgement consume the reservation. A later continuation may present distinct late or overflow advice from earlier work without a new edit; repeated presentation of the same advice through Stop cannot spend another slot. Background submissions and native turn changes neither spend nor restore Stop slots.
- **Reoffer window:** Current background-submitted or uncertain advice from before Stop or during its wait is eligible for one Stop reoffer within that round. Coordinate lease ownership and final eligibility; do not steal an already authorized background write or rerun Jev. Uncertain Stop output consumes the one reoffer. No advice is carried across closure. Pending overflow can remain only while that round stays active.
- **Cleanup order:** Mark closed and fence admission/collection/output authorization first; resolve waiters and revoke unreleased permits/leases; remove queued work and cancel owned preparation/Jev/network operations; then release captured source, artifacts, advice, notices, and delivery records. Every late callback checks the round fence before publishing or enqueueing. Another round's resources remain unaffected. Record source-free closure reason, reservation count, and stage-specific discarded/incomplete counts. Cleanup may finish after the hook exits only after the fence is effective and within resource bounds.
- **External write limitation:** Bytes already written cannot be recalled. An output permit released to another process can race closure despite a final fence check; classify unresolved output as uncertain. Guarantee no new output authorization after closure and no late review publication, without claiming atomic recall of external stdout or exactly-once delivery.
- **Expiry and restart:** Advice expiry never resets the active round's count. Retain a source-free session denial marker if event-history capacity is exhausted; do not reopen through eviction. Resident restart discards in-memory work and fences old-lifetime IPC, but may reset the unfinished round’s continuation count and event history under the owner's explicit scope decision. Carrying the count across restart is not planned; reset on restart is accepted behavior.
- **Three artifacts:** Production default-branch behavior, #105 candidate behavior, and the Foldkit reducer/diagram prototype must be reported separately. The prototype can check round transitions and ownership; it cannot establish native hook delivery or Jev cancellation. Validate the completed candidate before claiming the revised policy passes Linux.

### Owner architecture decisions (2026-09-25)

- [ ] **Reoffer at Stop:** Apply the P1 same-round background-to-Stop rule above. Recheck advicee, freshness, authority, deadline, and lease ownership before handoff. A repeated host presentation is acceptable here; it must not enqueue another review or rerun Jev. Preserve distinct evidence for review completion, host submission, agent visibility, and repair. Record and validate the background/Stop race on both Linux hosts.
- [ ] **Cohesive shared delivery API:** Keep the existing resident work queue and pending-advice store authoritative. Put collection policy, leases, submission/uncertain state, and Stop reoffer decisions behind one runtime-neutral resident-facing delivery API. Codex and Claude hook adapters provide host identity and native output only. Do not create host-specific review queues or move the review backend pipeline merely to make one class own everything. Maintain an architecture/data-flow diagram that distinguishes work, advice, delivery attempts, and the unknown host-visibility boundary.

These are owner design decisions, not final production adoption. The acceptance-status table above records passed observations and the conditionally accepted support limits for the detailed criteria below; owner visual review/adoption remains open.

### Combined architecture and contract

- [ ] Implement one reusable runtime-neutral delivery module backed by the production resident. It owns bounded waiting, advicee-scoped collection, leases, host-submission/uncertain state, stale revalidation, batching, expiry, failure outcomes, and Stop continuation policy. Codex and Claude adapters may differ only where their hook input, registration, output, or host lifecycle semantics require it; they must not fork the work/advice queue or duplicate the delivery state machine. Run shared contract tests against both adapters.
- [ ] Document how each host's edit adapter, production resident, background hook, and Stop hook compose through that shared module. Keep one authoritative resident-owned work/advice lifecycle; delivery triggers must not create separate review queues or repeat backend evaluation merely to deliver a result. Explain how existing subsequent-edit collection participates in the same ownership protocol.
- [ ] Specify the advicee tuple, including canonical working root and host/session/supplied agent identity. Use the same advicee scoping and current-advice eligibility rules on every collection path.
- [ ] Specify each host's background-hook registration, bounded waiting/resource use, completion output, and cancellation/session-end behavior. Distinguish review completion, resident collection, host submission, and independently observed model visibility. Background completion must not be assumed to interrupt an in-flight model request or start a new turn.
- [ ] Specify shared collection/lease/acknowledgement behavior when background, Stop, and subsequent-edit collectors overlap. Prevent competing collectors from concurrently handing off the same advice; define ownership transfer, lease expiry, and recovery after failed or uncertain output. Address the case where background output is submitted but the model has not yet consumed it when Stop fires. Do not equate a successful output write with model visibility or promise exactly-once delivery.
- [ ] Specify stale-result revalidation at handoff, bounded batching and explicit overflow disposition, and unavailable/backend-failure behavior consistently across delivery paths. Unknown or failed outcomes must not be reported as clean.
- [ ] Specify each agent runtime's Stop waiting policy and total bounded Stop deadline, including startup, IPC, collection, response writing, and exit. Treat the five-second ceiling from #97 as a tested candidate, not an established production default. Apply the accepted P1 four-request limit and Hapsland round-close rule; validate repeated Stop calls, repair edits, late Jev responses, bounded-batch overflow, resumed subagents, expiry, and restart.
- [ ] **Round-close resource contract:** Dispose of every round-owned state item: pre-edit admission permits, admitted edit observations, queued ingress and review-unit jobs, running Jev evaluations, captured artifacts and current-work references, pending advice and operational notices, leases, background waiters, submitted/uncertain handoff records, and Stop state. Fence late admissions and completions so they cannot recreate work after closure. Cancel owned work where possible; discard late results as incomplete, never clean. Keep other agents and later rounds unaffected. Record the closure and race properties for later formal verification. The closure boundary is Hapsland's allow response, not proof of the runtime's all-hooks decision.

### Host and resident validation

- [ ] Run background and Stop paths and their composition through the production resident on both exact headless Linux profiles: Linux arm64 / Codex CLI 0.155.1 / Node.js 24.20.0, followed by Linux arm64 / Claude Code 2.1.218 / Node.js 24.20.0. Establish actual hook registration, async delivery timing, Stop continuation behavior, and teardown semantics separately for each host. macOS is a post-closure manual follow-up, not a closure gate for #105.
- [ ] Demonstrate background delivery without another edit when a subsequent model request is available. Cover completion while a model request or tool call is active, completion during the final model response, and completion after turn/session end. Record actual delivery opportunities and limitations rather than assuming elapsed time guarantees visibility.
- [ ] Cover ready findings, completion during the Stop wait, deadline expiry followed by explicit round-close cleanup, unavailable/backend failure, stale revalidation, and multi-unit delivery through the production resident.
- [ ] Exercise the composition races: background collection overlapping Stop; background output submitted just before Stop but not yet known to be consumed; subsequent-edit collection overlapping either path; collector failure/cancellation or acknowledgement loss; and new findings generated by a repair continuation. Verify the specified ownership, bounded continuation, and retention behavior without claiming model visibility from acknowledgement alone.
- [ ] Run two concurrent host advicees with distinct controlled findings across both delivery paths and verify that each host response contains only advice for its own advicee. Cover isolated worktrees and the shared-root boundary; preserve subagent identity where the host supplies it. Unknown-origin checkpoint changes must not be delivered to an arbitrary advicee.
- [ ] Measure host commands from actual launch through response and exit on each tested profile. Distinguish edit-path latency, background completion-to-host-submission/model-visibility timing where observable, and added Stop latency. Record the selected deadline and limitations. Do not infer a population latency or repair rate from fixture runs.
- [ ] Retain sanitized evidence and update the product/release support statement for the tested Linux behavior. Do not enable a proposed production path if any required composition, isolation, or failure gate is unresolved; record a rejection or an explicitly revised support boundary instead. Keep the Codex and Claude support decisions separate.

Use a controlled offline backend first. Any live Jev validation requires its separately authorized milestone and sanitized evidence. This issue adds delivery opportunities for already attributable review work; it does not expand checkpoint discovery or change the accepted attribution boundary.

### Closure-triggered macOS follow-up

- [ ] Install a repository workflow scoped to the closure of **this issue (#105)**. When #105 closes, it must create and cross-link a new issue for manual testing on the owner's macOS machine with real Codex and real Claude Code. Make the creation safe to retry without producing duplicate follow-up issues. The new issue must request a before/after observation for each host, exact host/Node/macOS versions, suggestion handoff and independently observed follow-through, final repaired state and clear follow-up review, timing and failure notes, and sanitized evidence. No macOS result is claimed by closing #105.
- [ ] Close #105 only after the before/after outcome passes for both Linux hosts and both hosts' contract/race/isolation/failure gates have evidence-backed dispositions. A rejection of production adoption by itself does not satisfy the new outcome gate. Verify that the closure workflow created and linked the macOS follow-up; if creation fails, restore an open tracking state until the follow-up exists.


### Finish-decision policy and sidecar diagrams (owner decision, 2026-09-26)

- [x] **Vocabulary:** The runtime invokes its API hook named `Stop` or `SubagentStop` for a **finish attempt**. Hapsland may hold that hook call open for a **finish-decision wait**. Its later response is either **continue with advice** (`block` in the runtime API) or **allow finish** (`allow`). These are separate events; neither a response command nor a completed write proves model visibility or the actual end of the agent's round. [Product glossary](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/feat/issue-105-composed-delivery/CONTEXT.md) and [candidate design](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/feat/issue-105-composed-delivery/docs/advicing-target-contract.md) use these terms.
- [x] **Accepted policy for the model:** During one open finish-attempt hook call, wait for the virtual round's unfinished source/review work and any active background output until it all settles or Hapsland reaches its safe hook deadline, whichever happens first. At that boundary, classify all available Jev results together with pending advice. Select all actionable findings as one abstract batch if a continuation slot remains; otherwise choose allow finish. Discard queued work and request cancellation of in-flight source reading and Jev requests admitted before the decision. A continue-with-advice decision keeps the virtual round active for fresh repair edits; allow finish closes it. Fence old callbacks. The four-request count is per virtual round and survives a continue-with-advice decision.
- [x] **Sidecar implementation:** Commit [`5f5bdf1`](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/commit/5f5bdf1) adds distinct edit, review, and Jev-result queues; separate settable source and Jev capacities; automatic work-conserving starts; a reducer-derived policy view of unfinished work and results; both finish triggers; typed batch/discard/cancellation effects; and a separate Foldkit finish-decision diagram. The main graph derives routes from accepted reducer changes and distinguishes a requested response command from an observed background hook write. The sidecar build projects nine guided traces and eight timing companions. This is a one-agent, multiple-item design model, not production authority.
- [x] **Production and acceptance gap — resolved by PR #108 and owner acceptance (historical description follows):** The installed #105 candidate does not yet implement this new all-work-settled/deadline batch-and-cancel policy. The sidecar has no clock or external write/cancellation execution; its deadline is an input event and its output is a command. Map the accepted policy to the shared resident implementation, preserve round fencing and uncertain-write semantics, validate on both pinned Linux runtimes, and obtain the owner's visual review before treating this addendum as a passing production acceptance criterion. Keep #105 open.

title: Preserve Stop continuation limit across resident restarts
body:
## Context

Issue #105 accepts at most four Hapsland Stop continuation requests for one agent's Hapsland round **within one resident lifetime**. The resident keeps its round and continuation state in memory. Restart loses that state; repeated restarts can therefore allow more than four requests during work the agent runtime continues. The owner explicitly accepts this limitation for #105. This follow-up is low priority and does not block #105 implementation or closure.

## Goal

Decide whether Hapsland should enforce the Stop continuation limit across resident restarts. If so, implement a source-free durable record or a conservative recovery rule that cannot restore spent requests for an active round.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Specify what identifies the same Hapsland round before and after a resident restart, including main agents and subagents, without treating a native runtime `turn_id` as the round ID.
- [ ] Select and document durable recovery or fail-closed recovery. State the behavior for missing, corrupt, stale, and partially written state.
- [ ] Keep the counter scoped to the identified agent and round. A restart, duplicate Stop, uncertain output write, or repeated hook must not grant extra requests for that same round.
- [ ] Keep persisted records source-free, bounded, and removable when no longer needed. Preserve round-close cleanup and isolation of other agents.
- [ ] Verify restart and repeated-restart cases on supported Linux agent runtimes with sanitized evidence before claiming a cross-restart guarantee.

Until this follow-up is done, documentation and status output must describe four as a per-resident-lifetime maximum, not a durable maximum across arbitrary restarts.

Related: #105.

title: Implement shared resident delivery and all-work finish decisions
body:
Implements Hapsland's shared resident delivery for Codex CLI and Claude Code. Previously, the finish hook could return on the first finding while other admitted work remained unfinished. It now waits for all admitted work or its safe deadline, selects a bounded advice batch, cancels unfinished pre-decision work, and fences late results. Completed overflow advice and the four-continuation budget survive a block in the same virtual round. Atomic advice reservations and single-use output permits handle abandoned collectors and uncertain writes.

The owner accepted the timing diagrams and Linux result on 2026-09-27 and authorized merge and closure of #105. macOS validation is deferred to the separate task created and linked by the closure workflow after this PR reaches master. This PR references #105 without automatic closure so the workflow is installed before the issue is closed.

Validation:
- Full offline suite: 542 passed, 2 skipped; root build and typecheck passed.
- Real CLI/IPC resident contracts: 18/18 passed across both adapter identities.
- Explicit cooperative-review native probes: five selected cases passed on Linux arm64, Node 24.20.0, Codex CLI 0.155.1 and Claude Code 2.1.218. Both matched pairs repaired and cleared; Claude background repaired and cleared without a Stop block. The optional follow-up read is a declared fixture condition. Earlier misses remain recorded.
- Independent standards/spec reviews: zero remaining implementation findings.
- Foldkit build and browser rendering passed; its model and the small Bend proof are independent of production authority.
- Packaged setup: seven journeys passed. Installed-release replay stopped on pre-existing historical ancestry; clean-package replay stopped on an absent publishing guide. Neither is claimed passing; publishing remains #87.

Evidence and limitations: [finish-decision validation](evidence/advicing-linux/finish-decision-linux.md), [Linux index](evidence/advicing-linux/README.md), and [target contract](docs/advicing-target-contract.md). Hook submission does not prove model receipt or compliance. Tests explicitly instruct agents to act on findings; real users control that policy. Native Codex child routing, the actionable Claude foreground-tool window, and direct in-progress model-request timing remain unproven within the accepted boundary. These selected observations are not reliability estimates or a new pinned release support declaration.

title: Add Foldkit agent-flow sidecar for #105

The package shows where edit observations, resident work, Jev outcomes, pending advice, collection leases, and agent-runtime output flow. It labels the visibility boundary as unknown unless an agent action is observed. The reducer statically checks the visualization model, and guided traces exercise the round/Stop decisions.

This draft is for architecture review alongside #108. The production candidate is in #108; the sidecar is not presented as proof of native hook behavior.

title: Add standalone Foldkit agent-flow sidecar for #105
body:
Standalone Foldkit sidecar for #105. Production Hapsland does not import this package.

The first diagram and guided traces show an edit observation moving through the resident work scheduler, controlled review, pending advice, collection lease, and runtime hook output. The new **bottom timing view** shows seven selectable Linux scenarios: matched before/after Stop repair, background delivery, Stop reoffer/cleanup, observed Codex tool and Claude streamed-message intervals, three unproven Claude foreground-tool attempts, and bounded post-exit observation. The matched Codex/Claude before/after case is the default.

Each native panel uses a seconds axis for its own recorded run. Lanes distinguish observable agent-runtime hooks, Hapsland review, advice writes/Stop, and observed repair. Grey spans explicitly mean missing evidence, not measured model stages or proof of advice consumption. The page separately labels **required product behavior** versus **exploratory timing probe**, and **observed** versus **unproven**. It links to sanitized evidence pinned at production candidate `987674e`.

The companion paths use typed `EventId` values and labels from `TRANSITIONS`; `stepFlow` replays their abstract order when the page loads. This is partial reducer coverage. TypeScript checks event identity and data-flavor routes, while reducer replay checks the shown abstract sequence. Native timestamps, tool/message intervals, repair checks, hidden runtime processing, and concurrent agents are outside that reducer.

`npm run build` passed (TypeScript and Vite). This remains a draft for owner visual review alongside production draft #108; it is not native-host proof or production adoption.

title: Recheck background advice during an active tool call and formalize its delivery condition
body:
## Current status — 2026-10-04

Incomplete, low-priority native regression follow-up. #116 authority reconciliation does not replace the requested actual foreground-tool interval observation. The #105 record remains historical evidence; no new probe or repair-and-clear result is claimed. The retired sidecar is no longer a law owner: any formal condition belongs to the current canonical Bend model and must be checked for existing coverage before adding it.

## Purpose

Preserve #105's observed Codex behavior as a future regression check and candidate Law. This follow-up is low priority and is not a closure gate for #105.

## Recorded observation

Pinned Codex CLI 0.155.1 on Linux, using Hapsland's production resident and a controlled Effect reviewer:

| Observation | Time since runtime launch |
| --- | ---: |
| Bash PreToolUse | 9.081 s |
| Finding review completed | 17.169 s |
| Background response submitted | 17.223 s |
| Bash PostToolUse | 34.143 s |
| Repair edit hook returned | 37.621 s |

A native repair followed without a Stop block. The delayed follow-up review did not clear before round cleanup, so this was not a complete repair-and-clear acceptance run. [Retained native record](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/dc5ff9e/evidence/delivery-105/linux-native-background-timing-final-tools.json), [scope and limitations](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/dc5ff9e/evidence/delivery-105/native-background-timing-linux.md).

## Candidate Law

> Within an active Hapsland round, current eligible advice may be submitted through an authorized background collector without requiring the active tool to finish, another edit, or a Stop event.

Formalize this as a condition on Hapsland's permitted transitions, respecting freshness, lease ownership, collector budget, and round closure. This does not guarantee that the runtime schedules the collector or that the agent receives or follows its output. Any stronger eventual-delivery claim needs explicit scheduling and fairness assumptions.

## Recheck acceptance

- [ ] Run a bounded native Codex Linux probe; record exact runtime, Node, and candidate versions.
- [ ] Observe an actual foreground tool interval; do not infer it from the requested prompt.
- [ ] Establish actionable review completion and background submission inside that interval, without an intervening edit or Stop.
- [ ] Record later repair and clear-review outcomes separately; preserve misses and timeouts.
- [ ] Keep submission distinct from runtime receipt, model visibility, and action.
- [ ] Add or verify the conditional Law in the current canonical Bend model, including its assumptions and closure/ownership exclusions; the retired TypeScript sidecar is not an implementation target.
- [ ] Retain sanitized evidence and compare with the #105 observation.

title: Investigate functional architecture for the resident runtime
body:
## Goal

Investigate whether Hapsland's resident runtime should move away from class-based state ownership toward functional modules, explicit state transitions, and Effect 4 services. This is an architecture investigation, not authorization for a broad refactor.

## Scope

- Review `ResidentServer`, `ComposedDelivery`, `CapacityLedger`, `EvaluationReuse`, `DispatchCycles`, and `BendWorkTracker`, plus any other product code where class-owned mutable state makes behavior harder to understand or verify.
- Distinguish runtime state and effects from pure flow policy. Generated Bend decisions must remain authoritative; Jev evaluation remains on the Effect 4 provider-neutral `Decision` path.
- Compare the current design with at least one concrete functional design, including state ownership, event/command boundaries, lifetime and cancellation handling, IPC concurrency, and test seams.
- Treat Effect `Context.Service` and tagged error classes on their own merits; do not assume every `class` declaration should be removed.
- Assess migration cost, performance, risk of changing resident behavior, and whether an incremental refactor is worthwhile.

## Deliverable

A short architecture proposal with a current-to-proposed module map, one representative code-shape example, an incremental migration sequence, verification plan, and a recommendation to proceed or retain the current structure. Preserve the existing offline and package conformance contracts in any proposed path.

title: Sunset the TypeScript sidecar engine while preserving Bend scope and regression evidence
body:
## Problem Statement

Hapsland's visualization still lets a TypeScript sidecar reducer decide which actions are accepted and what history is replayed. The Bend pane follows that history, so the page can suggest that Bend drives the interaction when it does not. The sidecar reducer also supplies independent differential regression evidence and dynamic state assertions. Removing it from the page without accounting for those roles would lose useful assurance.

The shared sidecar/`Flow.bend` scenario is a deliberately simplified model. Production uses other generated Bend policies and ledgers through the resident, with TypeScript orchestrating effects and state. A Bend-only sidecar page would still **not** visualize the complete production lifecycle. The page must say what it actually depicts.

## Solution

Separate the sidecar's reference logic from the visualization. Make compiled Bend flow the authority for actions and history in the visualization, use TypeScript only for UI presentation and browser integration, and remove the TypeScript sidecar comparison from the page. Preserve the existing independent reference data until its role is assessed. Verify the page, then make a distinct commit at that checkpoint.

After that commit, audit the TypeScript oracle, state invariants, and regression checks. Move any necessary general properties into Bend or another independent contract check, retain fixed scenario expectations where they add value, and remove obsolete oracle or regression machinery only when replacement or redundancy is demonstrated. Report findings and the resulting decision to the user. A production-lifecycle visualization is a separate follow-up decision, not something this UI migration implicitly delivers.

## User Stories

1. As a viewer, I want the visualization to identify the model that drives it, so that I can interpret its diagrams accurately.
2. As a viewer, I want accepted actions to come from compiled Bend flow, so that the displayed state follows the stated authority.
3. As a viewer, I want rejected actions and their reasons to come from compiled Bend flow, so that invalid paths are explained consistently.
4. As a viewer, I want guided scenarios to continue working, so that I can learn the abstract flow step by step.
5. As a viewer, I want manual actions to continue working, so that I can explore behavior outside the guided path.
6. As a viewer, I want capacity and finish behavior displayed correctly, so that I can see the meaningful constraints of the abstract model.
7. As a viewer, I want rewind and replay to reconstruct the same Bend state and change history, so that I can inspect earlier decisions reliably.
8. As a viewer, I want the diagrams and timeline to stay synchronized with accepted Bend history, so that I can trust what I see.
9. As a viewer, I want the TypeScript-versus-Bend comparison removed once the page uses Bend, so that it does not imply two active UI authorities.
10. As a viewer, I want a clear scope note that `Flow.bend` is narrower than production, so that I do not mistake this page for a complete resident trace.
11. As a maintainer, I want UI rendering separated from the old reference reducer, so that retiring the reducer does not require removing the page.
12. As a maintainer, I want deterministic scenario expectations retained during migration, so that known accepted and rejected paths can still be checked.
13. As a maintainer, I want a separate commit after the UI migration, so that the later assurance decisions can be reviewed independently.
14. As a maintainer, I want the current oracle's distinct value documented, so that its removal is an evidence-based choice.
15. As a maintainer, I want the existing dynamic state invariants inventoried, so that none disappear silently.
16. As a maintainer, I want any necessary invariant expressed at an appropriate Bend or contract seam, so that it remains executable after the TypeScript reducer is retired.
17. As a maintainer, I want redundant regressions removed only after their coverage is accounted for, so that the test suite stays useful and lean.
18. As a maintainer, I want a final report with the oracle and invariant decisions, so that the sunset outcome is explicit.

## Implementation Decisions

- Treat the visualization UI, the simplified Bend flow, and the production resident as three distinct concerns. The production resident already uses richer generated Bend policies and ledgers; this task does not replace its orchestration.
- Isolate the legacy TypeScript reducer and reference scenarios from UI code first. A temporary reference package is acceptable if it makes dependencies clear; avoid a permanent package boundary unless it proves useful.
- Drive interactive action acceptance, rejection, state, and history from compiled Bend flow. Keep TypeScript for DOM, layout, routing, and other presentation work.
- Remove the sidecar comparison and TypeScript-driven projections from the UI. Do not delete independent reference fixtures or oracle inputs at this checkpoint merely because the UI no longer uses them.
- Preserve the scope distinction in page copy: the Bend-driven page depicts the simplified one-item virtual-round flow, while production also has permits, fan-out, final Stop cutoff, finding collection, leases, ticket outcomes, revision/reuse/cache behavior, notices, retention, and native effects.
- Make a discrete commit once the Bend-driven page is verified. The next phase is an audit, followed by any justified oracle, invariant, or regression changes and a report to the user.
- For the audit, distinguish executable general invariants from example laws and finite trace parity. Retain or replace checks according to the behavior they uniquely protect; remove an oracle or regression only if its value has been superseded or an independent contract covers it.
- Keep the visualization work deterministic and offline; no live Jev requests are needed.

## Testing Decisions

- The primary behavior seam is the visualization as a user interacts with it: guided and manual actions, accepted and rejected decisions, state and diagram updates, capacity and finish cases, and rewind/replay. Assert visible behavior and Bend-produced outcomes, not private UI helpers.
- Reuse the visualization package's build and projection check as the first gate, with a focused browser interaction check for the changed control paths. Add only the smallest new test seam needed to observe those paths.
- Keep the Bend package's existing law, proof, lifecycle, and sidecar-parity checks passing through the first commit. Its current differential runner covers 113 traces and 5,048 accepted generated steps; that finite comparison is prior art, not proof of full production equivalence.
- During the later audit, list each TypeScript structural assertion and regression family, identify its protected behavior, and verify any replacement at the broadest practical public contract seam. General properties may belong in Bend laws/proofs; independent fixed expected traces or resident-event contracts may be better for cross-language regression evidence.
- Do not delete a check merely because the new UI passes, and do not duplicate implementation logic in tests.

## Out of Scope

- Claiming that `Flow.bend` models the complete production lifecycle.
- Building a complete production-lifecycle visualization in this task; discuss that separately with the user after the handoff.
- Refactoring resident orchestration away from classes or changing production Bend decision boundaries.
- Live Jev validation, deployment, or unrelated runtime integrations.
- Immediate deletion of all scenario traces or the TypeScript oracle before the audit.

## Further Notes

- Research: [sidecar sunset assessment](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/feat/bend-full-flow/docs/sidecar-sunset-research.md).
- Architecture: [Bend and production touch-point diagrams](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/feat/bend-full-flow/docs/bend-production-backbone-diagrams.md).
- Previous estimates, with substantial uncertainty: split logic/UI 2–4 hours; Bend-driven UI 6–12 hours; UI cleanup and first commit 2–4 hours; oracle/invariant/regression audit 4–8 hours, plus 4–16 hours if replacement coverage is needed.
- The intended final checkpoint is a report to the user after the oracle/invariant audit, before treating the simplified page as evidence of production-lifecycle completeness.


Parent epic: [#116 — one authoritative Bend transition system](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/116). This issue is the first bounded cleanup step; its `Flow.bend` UI is transitional and does not become the production backbone.

title: Epic: one authoritative Bend transition system for Hapsland decisions
body:
## Completed — 2026-10-04

Final authority accounting and #136 lifecycle cleanup completed at the owner's request. Production uses the checked `Canonical.step` boundary; the earlier `Lifecycle.apply` proposal is historical. All current decision families and justified native exceptions are accounted for in `docs/typescript-decision-boundary-ledger.md`. The completion comment records acceptance criteria, current checks and evidence limits.

The #136 temporary plan/report have been consolidated into an immutable JSON evidence index with exact Git provenance for the original declarations; obsolete Markdown snapshots and their current inbound links were removed. These documentation/evidence edits are local, uncommitted and unpushed at closure. #147 remains separate visual design acceptance, #176 remains simulator expansion, and #172 remains native macOS validation. Closing this epic makes no release or universal host-support claim.

## Historical task scope and prior planning

## Current status (2026-09-28)

The Bend full-flow work is merged into `master` at [`ec605d1`](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/commit/ec605d1). #117–#137 and #141 are closed with scoped completion evidence. The [#137 final authority report](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/137#issuecomment-5873005822) describes the running same-file boundary: production and the dashboard use the checked `Canonical.step` adapter. The original `Lifecycle.apply` migration proposal below is historical; `Lifecycle.apply` remains model-only.

The epic stays open. #145 needs focused current-tip Claude delivery verification. #148 owns the remaining explicit Jev-request command and old direct-review retirement; #147 owns restoration of the production-flow graph. The accepted cross-file target is separate #138 work. #139, #140, #142, #143, and #146 track later backpressure, sizing, graph-limit, process-lifetime, and configurability decisions. These follow-ups do not turn the completed #117–#137 checkpoints into installed cross-file support or exhaustive host-race evidence.

The original problem, solution, and staged plan below record the migration proposal at issue creation. Use the current status and #137 report for implementation claims.

## Problem Statement

Hapsland does not yet have the single Bend flow authority originally targeted. The production resident calls many generated Bend policy functions, but TypeScript still composes their state and ordering. A simplified `Flow.step` drives the Bend side of the visualization, an older `Lifecycle.apply` aggregate remains model-only, and `Lifecycle` also contains newer finish functions used by production. The TypeScript sidecar is another simplified engine. Additional product decisions remain in TypeScript outside those five surfaces, including file and rule selection, finding derivation, scheduling, and configuration precedence.

These surfaces are not five complete independent implementations, and no specific runtime defect is established by their coexistence. They do make it hard to identify one authority for a decision, prove that the visualization depicts production, or remove obsolete paths safely. The previous single-reducer target was not delivered.

## Solution

Evolve the existing Bend `Lifecycle.apply` aggregate **in place** into the one authoritative transition boundary for included Hapsland product decisions. It receives events and measured facts, owns canonical policy state, and returns decisions and commands. Reuse the current production Bend modules as internal components. Route the resident through that boundary in verified vertical slices, deleting superseded TypeScript composition and direct policy-call paths as each slice lands. Ultimately the visualization replays the same canonical transition system, and the old abstract `Flow.step` and older finish aggregate paths are retired.

TypeScript continues to gather native facts and perform effects: filesystem and identity measurements, clocks, source capture, Jev requests, sockets/hooks/IPC, encoding, output, cancellation execution, and rendering. Jev classification is an external input. The epic's first design gate inventories every authored product decision and makes explicit any justified exception to Bend authority. This is one decision authority, not a requirement to put all code in one file.

## User Stories

1. As a maintainer, I want every production decision family mapped to its current owner, so that hidden authorities are visible before migration.
2. As a maintainer, I want static call sites distinguished from exercised runtime paths, so that the inventory does not overstate reachability.
3. As a maintainer, I want a clear distinction between product decisions, measured facts, effects, and display projections, so that the migration has a testable boundary.
4. As a maintainer, I want the existing sidecar cleanup completed as a separate checkpoint, so that one simplified duplicate can be retired without conflating it with production migration.
5. As a maintainer, I want one canonical Bend event and state model for admission, work, Stop, and delivery, so that those transitions cannot acquire competing owners.
6. As a maintainer, I want the current production Bend modules reused inside that aggregate, so that their validated rules are retained.
7. As a maintainer, I want the older and newer finish paths reconciled into one state and transition sequence, so that continuation and output authority are unambiguous.
8. As a maintainer, I want partition and global capacity updates coordinated by the same Bend authority, so that reservations and releases remain exact across advicees.
9. As a maintainer, I want asynchronous callbacks represented as events with lifetime, round, and operation identity, so that stale or duplicate completions cannot change current policy state.
10. As a maintainer, I want TypeScript to execute commands and return their observed outcomes, so that effects do not become a second policy engine.
11. As a maintainer, I want file eligibility, rule applicability, finding thresholds and ranking, configuration precedence, and work scheduling explicitly classified, so that the epic does not silently leave other product decisions in TypeScript.
12. As a maintainer, I want source-free expected traces independent of the Bend implementation, so that a single authority is still checked against a separate contract.
13. As a viewer, I want the eventual visualization to replay canonical production decisions, so that its steps correspond to the production model.
14. As a viewer, I want the diagram to mark native effects and Jev responses separately from Bend decisions, so that I can see the actual boundary.
15. As a maintainer, I want obsolete abstract engines and direct policy APIs removed when superseded, so that the end state has one production transition authority.
16. As a maintainer, I want structural checks on imports and state ownership, so that later code cannot quietly restore parallel flow engines.
17. As a maintainer, I want each migration slice independently reviewable and revertible, so that the consolidation can proceed step by step.
18. As the product owner, I want a final evidence-backed accounting of remaining exceptions and coverage, so that “one Bend source” has a precise, inspectable meaning.
19. As a maintainer, I want production and diagrams to call Bend through the same typed boundary, so that they cannot interpret the same transition differently.
20. As a maintainer, I want event encoding, numeric conversion, result decoding, and runtime validation shared, so that adapters do not repeat fragile integration logic.
21. As a maintainer, I want the TypeScript contract checked against compiled Bend output, so that declarations cannot silently drift from the runtime shapes.

## Implementation Decisions

- The first artifact is a source-linked authority map. Before migration, extend its open items to cover every generated export, production call, retained resident map, direct and legacy path, and mixed fact/decision branch. Record observed call sites separately from runtime reachability.
- Complete the existing sidecar issue as a bounded first cleanup. Its interim Bend-driven UI uses the simplified `Flow.step` model and must say so; it is not the final production visualization.
- Evolve `Lifecycle.apply` rather than adding a sixth permanent aggregate. Its current state/event/command structure is the starting point, not a drop-in final implementation. Replace its older finish state with the current production Round/Work semantics and fold the separately called production finish functions into the same transition authority.
- Keep Admission, Work, Round, Handoff, delivery, ticket, notice, reuse, cache, retention, and ledger rules as internal Bend modules where useful. Composition and policy state belong to the canonical aggregate; production adapters must not independently patch Bend state or choose follow-up transitions.
- Define explicit events for native observations and effect completions, and explicit commands for work and host effects. Preserve exact identity and stale-callback fencing. Do not store source or secrets in retained Bend state or evidence.
- Handle global accounting through canonical aggregate state or an explicitly subordinate ledger advanced only by that authority. Verify atomic replacement and release before locking in the state layout.
- Migrate coherent vertical slices: admission/round/work, then Stop/selection/delivery, then tickets, revision, reuse/cache, notices, retention, global accounting, and any included pre-review policy or scheduling. A slice removes its superseded decision owner when it becomes authoritative; temporary shadow comparison is read-only.
- Treat file/rule policy, finding derivation, configuration precedence, and scheduling as in-scope candidates for the inventory gate. An exception requires a stated reason, designated owner, and boundary test; parsing, physical observations, configured data, and Jev classification are distinct from Hapsland-authored decisions.
- After production migration, make the visualization a projection/simulator of canonical events and results. Retire the simplified `Flow.step` transition model and obsolete `Lifecycle` aggregate paths after independent evidence is retained. Shared primitives can move to neutral Bend modules.
- The end-state production adapter imports the canonical transition interface rather than individual policy transition exports. Internal Bend modules may remain; one authored decision authority does not mean one source file.
- Put the generated JavaScript behind one shared TypeScript boundary, as a module or package according to the dependency graph. It owns event encoding, numeric normalization, result decoding, and runtime validation. Both production and the final visualization call the same public transition interface; visualization-specific layout and display projection remain separate.
- Replace the present split between hand-maintained production declarations and the visualization's weaker `unknown`/`any` projection with one checked type contract. Prefer generated declarations if feasible; otherwise mechanically verify the declarations and decoders against the compiled Bend constructors. Do not rely on a source-hash check alone to establish TypeScript/Bend ABI compatibility.
- The shared boundary is introduced as existing direct calls are replaced, not as another independent decision implementation. The interim simplified UI in #115 may retain its current Flow adapter until the canonical visualization step.

## Testing Decisions

- The highest practical seam is a deterministic production-resident scenario with fake clock, source, Jev, and host effects. Assert externally observable acceptance, advice, cancellation, Stop response, and terminal outcomes, plus source-free command traces where those are contractually meaningful. Do not test private helper shapes.
- Reuse existing resident integration tests, Bend laws/proofs, generated-artifact verification, and the current sidecar parity suite through the first cleanup checkpoint. Finite parity establishes only the abstract overlap.
- Establish independent expected outcomes from accepted contracts and curated production traces before the aggregate switch. Never use the implementation's own output as its sole oracle.
- At each slice, test the affected end-to-end path and relevant callback orders: stale lifetime or round, duplicate callbacks, zero/many prepared units, exact capacity release, Stop with pending work, bounded continuations, uncertain writes, and final credential/source changes.
- Add structural checks after migration that production imports only the aggregate transition API, adapters do not mutate Bend policy state, and obsolete reducer entry points have no production or UI consumers.
- Exercise the shared public boundary against compiled Bend with representative and malformed tagged events/results, numeric limits, and every variant consumed by production or diagrams. Verify that type declarations, runtime decoders, and the generated artifact agree; reject unknown variants explicitly. Enforce that both consumers import the shared facade rather than generated JavaScript directly.
- Keep tests deterministic and offline. Do not print or commit credentials or source-bearing Jev responses. A new live Jev milestone needs a separate declared purpose and bounded request plan.

## Out of Scope

- One monolithic Bend file or moving physical I/O, filesystem reads, clocks, source contents, Jev inference, sockets, or UI rendering into Bend.
- Treating the existing `Flow.step` or `Lifecycle.apply` as production-ready by changing imports alone.
- Deleting independent expected traces merely because there is one implementation authority.
- Claiming complete runtime reachability or correctness from a static call map, finite parity run, or example laws.
- Refactoring TypeScript classes for its own sake; related functional-architecture work is tracked separately.

## Further Notes

### Staged work

- [x] Complete the [#117 authority audit](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/117) and settle explicit scope exceptions.
- [x] #115 — retire the TypeScript sidecar engine from the visualization and preserve independent regression evidence.
- [x] Specify canonical events, state, commands, global-capacity coordination, and independent trace expectations.
- [x] Build the shared typed Bend boundary and make compiled-output, declaration, and runtime-decoder checks part of its build gate.
- [x] Route admission, round, and work composition through `Canonical.step`; the earlier `Lifecycle.apply` plan was superseded.
- [x] Migrate Stop, selection, leases, delivery, and finish composition; retire the older production finish path.
- [x] Reconcile remaining policy families against the current authority ledger; migrated gates and justified native exceptions are accounted for in the 2026-10-04 completion report.
- [x] Drive the visualization from canonical events; retire `Flow.step` as an executable abstract engine. #147 tracks graph detail restoration.
- [x] Verify the final import/state boundary and publish the [#137 report](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/137#issuecomment-5873005822).

Evidence: [#117 audit and archived checkpoint](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/117#issuecomment-5881729536), [#118 reconciliation](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/118#issuecomment-5881729899), [#137 final authority report](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/137#issuecomment-5873005822), and [#115 sidecar sunset](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/115). [Issue #114](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/114) is related resident-architecture research, not a prerequisite or a replacement for this epic.
