## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Define initial global and advicee partition state ownership, event and command envelopes, lifetime/round/operation identities, stale or duplicate completion outcomes, and native fact/effect boundaries.
- [x] Decide ordered partial capacity replacement, exact release, and cross-advicee coordination; map the old and production finish paths into one eventual sequence without assuming that existing aggregate events are production-ready.
- [x] Specify tagged variants, numeric bounds, malformed input/output behavior, and how declared TypeScript shapes will be checked against compiled Bend constructors.
- [x] Run initial independent, source-free expected traces derived from accepted behavior, including competing advicees, zero/many prepared units, pending-work Stop, and uncertain output. Extend the trace set in each later slice rather than predesigning every event.

## Blocked by

- #117 — Audit Hapsland decision ownership and runtime reachability
- #118 — Reconcile Hapsland behavioral sources before the Bend migration

## Reader notes

The resident is Hapsland's local background process. Its review capacity ledger lives in that process's memory and records temporary reservations for review-related records. Each reservation uses one item and its measured bytes. The ledger checks item and byte limits for both the whole resident and the identified agent's review scope. These are four checks, not four kinds of work or a measure of Jev's own capacity.

This first Bend slice models temporary space while Hapsland prepares review units and space held for each accepted unit. Preparing units is part of review. Other installed resident records join the canonical model in later tasks. `FinishReady` means the Stop wait ended; later rules still choose advice or finish.

The first-slice model accepts up to 16 unit sizes in one preparation result and caps active rounds and reservations for compiler/adapter validation. These are temporary model bounds, not the installed capacity policy. A duplicate result and a result that arrives after its round ends both produce the current no-effect `StaleOperation` result. #122 can decide whether to give them separate diagnostics.

## Parent

## What to build

A selected advice batch receives one authorized host handoff and a truthful submitted, failed, or uncertain terminal outcome.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reconcile the older aggregate finish path with production Round/Work/output selection into one state and transition sequence; remove the superseded finish owner.
- [ ] Revalidate source, advicee, credential, expiry, and selected units at the final barrier; reserve one of four continuations before output authorization.
- [ ] Handle pre-authorization failure, partial or uncertain advice submissions, lost acknowledgements, exclusive submission ownership before Stop, and the one same-round Stop reoffer without a second Jev review.
- [ ] Verify the changed resident behavior offline with independent, source-free expected outcomes and fake clock, source, Jev, and host effects; cover relevant callback orders.
- [ ] Remove the superseded decision owner and direct policy calls for this slice; add a focused guard against their return. Keep source and secrets out of retained Bend state and evidence.

## Blocked by

- #124 — Route Stop waiting, cancellation, and round closure
- #125 — Route advice collection, background claims, and exclusive leases

## Reader wording

A background advice submission means Hapsland sends advice to the agent runtime after an edit, before the agent asks to finish. It does not edit a source file. A confirmed send does not prove the agent saw the advice; an unknown result proves even less. At Stop in the same Hapsland round, Hapsland may offer that same still-current advice once without another Jev review. After the Stop wait, Bend must choose whether to ask the agent to continue with advice or let it finish. `FinishReady` only says it is time to make that choice.

Terminology: call the act **background advice submission**, its terminal message an **advice-submission result**, and a second identical message a **duplicate result**. Call a message arriving after its round or resident lifetime a **late result**. Keep `OutputStarted`, `OutputTerminal`, and `StaleOperation` as code names and explain their meaning when shown to readers.

title: Integrate bounded cross-file evidence and resource budgets into the review spec
body:
## Current disposition — 2026-10-04

Complete for bounded cross-file integration and the owner's adopted production scope. [PR #149](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/pull/149) merged on 2026-09-30 at `07ecd4e4654ca4193c4d834b03f1db385d309b7d`; that commit is an ancestor of the audited checkout. The earlier “draft/unmerged” handoff is superseded.

Delivered: attributed type/function roots, bounded supporting-source traversal with path checks before reads, configured graph/source/evidence budgets, rule-specific evidence eligibility, complete review identity, pre-request and pre-advice freshness checks, and retirement of the same-file-only production input. Primary owners: [accepted review contract](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/docs/type-function-review-proposal.md), [current compatibility contract](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/docs/review-contract-compatibility.md), [pipeline](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/src/direct-event/pipeline.ts) and [graph resolver](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/src/direct-event/graph-resolver.ts). The current pre-release formats are version 1; older schema-2/v2 handoffs are superseded. The owner removed the separate total Jev-request byte ceiling on 2026-09-29; provider-specific native limits remain separately documented.

The retained gate includes the independent graph/resolver, review-wire, rule, pipeline and freshness tests. Advice-quality comparison is explicitly deferred to #150, not an unmet activation criterion. Platform/release validation remains separate.

## Original task scope

## Owner decision (2026-09-29)

Implement and enable bounded cross-file review for users now. A comparative Jev study is not a precondition for implementation or activation; that study may become a separate later task. This decision supersedes earlier adoption-gate language in this issue and the #93 proposal. Retire the same-file-only review path instead of retaining it as legacy support. The cross-file evidence path must also handle a declaration whose complete evidence is in one file.

Keep file selection before each source read, finite source and request limits, complete-evidence checks, revalidation before Jev and advice, and canonical Bend decision authority. Offline tests and source-scope accounting still verify these requirements. Do not describe adoption as empirical proof that Jev advice is better; that question is deferred.

## Current handoff (2026-09-28)

#117/#118 reconciliation and the #141 Bend-first import-graph model are complete. #120/#122 raised and migrated the current logical resident capacity, while #135–#137 documented the present canonical authority. This issue still owns native cross-file resolver/capture, supporting-path checks before read, complete-unit identity/revalidation, finite full-request gating, and production adoption. #142 owns later configurable graph limits; #140 owns provider-aware full-request sizing.

## Target review behavior

Hapsland selects a root declaration from an attributed edit. It may follow that root's references into other files. Those files supply evidence; they do not become new edited roots.

Before Hapsland reads each file, it applies file selection: containment, protected paths, Git ignore, and user include/exclude settings. The target has no separate repository grant. With no file settings, Hapsland selects all otherwise eligible files.

Example: A.ts uses B.ts; B.ts uses C.ts. A and B are allowed. C is excluded. Hapsland reads A and B, checks C's path, and never reads C's source. A's review unit lacks required evidence, so Hapsland sends no request for A to Jev. Other complete review units can continue.

## Size and later checks

- Up to **256 KiB per source file**.
- Up to **20 KiB for one encoded evidence tree**. The tree can contain evidence from several files. Stop following references and stop reading more supporting files when the tree limit is reached.
- Set finite total-file, total-read, and analysis-work limits before this path runs. [#140](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/140) owns later query/provider-aware sizing of the complete Jev request; the initial path still needs a finite full-request limit.
- Before sending a review unit to Jev, check that each contributing file is still allowed and matches the captured source. Check again before giving advice. Drop an old Jev result if the unit changed. Reuse a result only for the same complete evidence, rules, and Jev input.

## Integration with #116

- #117/#118: compare this target with running code and accepted requirements. #118 links the next task.
- [#141](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/141): after reconciliation, define the import graph in Bend first and show a separate dashboard state machine. Native code supplies syntax, path, and source facts.
- #120/#122: raise or rework resident byte limits with 256 KiB capture. Keep ordered partial admission and exact release. This is a supporting change, not the review goal itself.
- #132/#133: remove the old repository grant step and apply file selection before every source read.
- #127/#129/#134: check changed files and decide if an old Jev result is still valid; send only complete units.
- #135–#137: show the Bend ledger and graph decisions, then verify the running paths.

[#139](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/139) separately tracks later retry/backpressure for capacity refusal.

The current installed profile still has a 32 KiB source-capture cap and same-file analysis. #132 removed the separate repository grant: effective file settings now control selection. This issue states the cross-file target; it does not claim production reference traversal has landed.

title: Design bounded backpressure for capacity-unavailable review work
body:
## Current status — 2026-10-04

Incomplete future policy decision. Current resident-capacity refusal remains immediate. #160 owns a separate possible Jev-saturation queue and resident-wide freshness design; do not implement the same queue in both tasks or infer that a free request permit frees resident ledger capacity. The original dependencies name delivered canonical mechanisms, not current merge blockers. Implementation requires an accepted bounded retention/retry/fairness policy.

## Task scope and prior planning

## Purpose

Later product policy for capacity-unavailable review work. Current admission can reject an independent review unit immediately when the resident ledger cannot reserve it. The owner wants to explore bounded retention and retry/backpressure after the canonical capacity and scheduling migration, not implement it now.

## Decide before implementation

- Which capacity refusals are eligible for retry, and whether a refused unit remains associated with the original attributed observation and advicee.
- A finite item/byte bound, fairness among advicees, ordering, and behavior when new edits supersede retained work. Backpressure must expire even if capacity never returns; make its expiry a validated user setting with a finite default and ceiling, and define the exact expiry outcome.
- How retries interact with the canonical Bend ledger, FIFO dispatch cycles, Stop/round closure, cancellation, resident restart, and stale source or consent.
- Source-free status and dashboard representation; no retained source or secret and no duplicate Jev evaluation.

## Dependencies

#120 canonical cross-advicee capacity, #123 scheduling, #127 revision supersession, and #131 retention/lifetime cleanup. This issue does not change the current immediate capacity-unavailable outcome.

title: Make the complete Jev request-size gate query and provider aware

## Acceptance

- Reject or narrow before source-bearing egress when the complete request exceeds a finite declared limit. Do not treat a 256 KiB captured file or a 20 KiB evidence tree as the request size.
- Define how provider and query differences affect the limit, with deterministic offline boundary fixtures and source-free timing/size evidence.
- Preserve a finite conservative complete-request gate for the initial cross-file adoption; query/provider-aware refinement can follow later.

title: Specify Bend import-graph transitions and show a separate dashboard state machine
body:
## Purpose and timing

After the #117/#118 conversation and source/spec reconciliation, specify the cross-file import/reference exploration policy **in Bend first** and show it as a separate state-machine diagram in the dashboard. Use an Astra medium agent when the visualization work begins, as requested by the product owner.

## Boundary

Native TypeScript/host code observes syntax, resolves filesystem paths and import bindings, checks physical identities, and captures source. Bend receives source-free facts and owns the policy transition: pending/visited edges, permission-gate outcome, whether to request the next supporting file, finite budgets, cycle handling, and complete/incomplete unit outcomes. The canonical transition must not retain source or secrets. This separation keeps physical import resolution from masquerading as a Bend filesystem operation.

## Required scenario and checks

- A.ts → B.ts → C.ts, A and B allowed, C excluded: check C before any source read, stop that branch, mark A incomplete/no Jev, allow independent complete units.
- Model deterministic edge ordering, multiple imports, cycles, missing/ambiguous targets, excluded paths, and exhaustion of the 20 KiB canonical evidence-tree and total-read budgets.
- Produce independent source-free expected traces and a dashboard diagram that visibly distinguishes Bend decisions, native resolution/capture facts, and Jev outcomes. The diagram is separate from the final full-flow replay in #135 but uses the same checked transition adapter.

Related: #93, #117, #118, #119, #122, #133, #135, #138. No implementation starts until the current reconciliation checkpoint finishes.

title: Make Bend import-graph limits configurable and prove budget relations
body:
## Current disposition — 2026-10-04

Complete for configurable graph limits and the graph budget/termination proof scope. [PR #149](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/pull/149) merged on 2026-09-30 at `07ecd4e4654ca4193c4d834b03f1db385d309b7d`; that commit is an ancestor of the audited checkout. The earlier “draft/unmerged” handoff is superseded.

Delivered: validated immutable effective limits, Bend-owned admission/traversal accounting, generated graph adapter/projections, independently expected limit/cycle/omission traces, configured source capture, and [general budget and finite responsive-event termination proofs](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/packages/agent-flow-bend/import-graph-proof/PROOF.bend). The [previous acceptance evidence](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/142#issuecomment-5884627220) records the import-graph kernel `--verdict` passing; its distinct aggregate-proof kernel limitation is not upgraded here. The owner clarification about uniform source caps and removal of the separate total-request ceiling remains applicable.

Current owners: [configuration](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/docs/configuration.md), [ImportGraph](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/packages/agent-flow-bend/ImportGraph.bend) and [resolver tests](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/src/direct-event/graph-resolver.test.ts). The retained current gate passed 22 resolver tests and 4 graph-authority tests, plus the generated ABI and production authority checks. No new kernel-proof invocation or platform execution was performed in this reconciliation. Native measurements and stalled external effects remain outside the pure graph theorem's assumptions.

## Original task scope

## Goal

Make Hapsland's import/reference graph budgets configurable while keeping Bend authoritative for admission and traversal decisions. The current `ImportGraph.bend` embeds numeric limits for per-file source bytes, accepted evidence-tree bytes, total files/read bytes, outgoing edges, depth, and work steps. The dashboard also repeats some values for display.

## Work

- Define one validated, versioned effective-limits value for the graph transition. Decide which limits users may tune and which absolute safety ceilings remain fixed; reject zero, inconsistent, or unbounded settings. Carry one immutable snapshot through each review unit.
- Pass the effective limits to Bend as data. Bend must make every accept, skip, read, and terminal decision using those limits; host code may enforce an earlier physical read/transport guard but must not implement a competing policy. Keep the generated adapter, fixture replay, and dashboard projections derived from the same effective limits.
- Reconcile the pre-read full-file reservation with configurable per-file and total-read caps. Check the complete Jev request separately from the evidence-tree cap; #140 owns query/provider-aware request sizing.
- Add general Bend laws and proofs for the budget relations, beyond fixed examples: accepted tree bytes never exceed the configured cap; accepting a contribution of `n` changes total `t` to `t+n`; skipping a non-fitting contribution leaves `t` unchanged and preserves later pending branches; every accepted contribution has size at most the resulting accepted total. Strict `total > contribution` requires a positive previously accepted total. Prove analogous source-read accounting and boundary behavior where practical.
- Add deterministic boundary and configuration tests, including exact-limit values, invalid configurations, changed limits, and the branching A→B,C; B→D,E; C→F,G cumulative-overflow trace. Update configuration schema/docs and dashboard rules so labels and numeric limits reflect the effective Bend inputs.

## Boundary

Bend can prove relations over supplied byte counts. Native capture must still measure the canonical encoded contribution correctly and enforce physical read bounds. Coordinate with #93, #138, #141, and #140; this task does not claim production import resolution is already wired.

## Traversal termination proof

- Add a general Bend law/proof that traversal reaches `Complete` or `Incomplete` after a finite number of responsive graph events for every valid finite limits value, even if `node_bytes` is zero and the conceptual import graph is infinite. Use a decreasing work/fuel or equivalent well-founded measure; do not rely on positive node size.
- State the environment assumption precisely: each emitted `ResolveEdge`, `CheckPath`, or `ReadSource` command eventually receives its matching result, or the host delivers `DeadlineReached`. A stalled external command is outside Bend's unconditional liveness guarantee.
- Cover queue exhaustion, visited cycles, edge/work/depth/file/read limits, and rejected/invalid events. Distinguish reaching a terminal phase from the terminal phase's deliberate self-loop on later events.

title: Retire an idle Hapsland resident without losing review work
body:
## Current disposition — 2026-10-04

Complete for automatic safe resident retirement. [PR #149](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/pull/149) merged on 2026-09-30 at `07ecd4e4654ca4193c4d834b03f1db385d309b7d`; that commit is an ancestor of the audited checkout. The earlier “draft/unmerged” handoff is superseded.

The [resident](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/src/resident/server.ts) performs inactivity checks without a manual cleanup request; checked cleanup preserves open rounds, pending permits, connected clients and retained work/advice/output ownership. Current operational timing is **20 seconds** per inactivity check, as recorded in [TS-009a](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/docs/typescript-decision-boundary-ledger.md), replacing the earlier five-second observation. Quiet-round closure is a separate policy and does not equate one agent's exit with the end of shared work.

The [earlier acceptance record](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/143#issuecomment-5884627203) records the 100-caller convergence observation. The current maintained suite uses six requests across three clients rather than repeating that historical stress run; this change and its evidence limit are explicit in the [testing matrix](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/docs/testing-matrix.md). The current retained gate passed all 10 [resident subprocess tests](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/src/resident/subprocess.test.ts), including singleton ownership, contenders, automatic idle exit, preservation of live state, restart and termination. Historical five-second and 100-caller evidence is not a claim that those exact samples were rerun today.

## Original task scope

## Problem

The installed hook can start a detached Hapsland resident, but normal agent exit does not automatically request resident cleanup. `ResidentServer.cleanup()` exists and refuses to retire while work or advice is owned, yet production code does not call it as an idle policy. An empty resident can stay running after all agents leave. This is a live idle process, not an OS zombie, but it has the unwanted lifetime the owner reported.

This is a **process lifetime** task. #131 owns Bend transitions for retained state and exact release; do not merge its scope with this task. #51 established one owner per connection directory and safe explicit cleanup, but did not wire automatic retirement.

## What to decide and build

Choose a bounded, safe idle-retirement rule for the installed resident. The rule must not equate one agent's Stop or process exit with the end of every agent's work: several agents and worktrees can use one resident, and late review results or pending advice may remain useful.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] State which activity keeps the resident alive, when an idle timer starts, and when retirement occurs. Give a finite bound for a resident with no retained work and no active clients.
- [x] Trigger retirement in production without requiring a manual `cleanup` IPC request. Preserve pending work, advice, leases, notices, and valid resume opportunities under the chosen policy.
- [x] Keep one live owner per connection directory during concurrent hook starts, idle retirement, and immediate restart. A failed probe or disconnected client must not displace a live owner.
- [x] Verify with real subprocess tests: 100 concurrent callers reach one resident; losing launch contenders exit; an empty resident exits within the chosen bound; live work prevents premature exit; a later hook starts a new lifetime; no retired process remains running.
- [x] Record the process-lifetime decision and its limits in product docs using `resident` and `resident connection directory` from `CONTEXT.md`.

## Related

- #31 selected the process boundary.
- #51 tested failure/restart and explicit idle cleanup.
- #131 models retained-state cleanup in Bend.

title: Integrate Bend import graph and first canonical transition (#141, #119)

title: Unify resident admission and Claude delivery without losing synchronous feedback
body:
## Current disposition — 2026-10-04

Complete for unified Claude admission and delivery. [PR #149](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/pull/149) merged on 2026-09-30 at `07ecd4e4654ca4193c4d834b03f1db385d309b7d`; that commit is an ancestor of the audited checkout. The earlier “draft/unmerged” handoff is superseded.

The installed composed edit hook, background collection and Stop now share resident admission/provenance, currentness, response authority, lease/submission fences and one version-1 IPC contract. The separate retained-ticket route is retired. Final encoded Claude output is bounded at 10 KiB without a separate finding-count cap; mixed failed/finding work retains actionable advice while failures remain diagnostic. Primary owners: [advice contract](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/docs/advicing-target-contract.md), [Claude hook tests](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/src/direct-event/claude-cli.test.ts), [collection tests](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/src/resident/collection.test.ts) and [protocol tests](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/src/resident/protocol.test.ts).

The retained current gate includes hook/resident/protocol/collection coverage for ready/slow/clear/zero/mixed work, stale authority, concurrent collectors, malformed peers, failed output and bounded Stop behavior. #94 and #172 retain host/platform acceptance; deterministic output submission is not proof of model visibility or arbitrary-session compliance.

## Original task scope

## Problem Statement

When this issue was opened on `feat/bend-full-flow`, there is one Claude hook installation used in the owner's test environment. It registers a synchronous `PostToolUse` command, an asynchronous background command, and other lifecycle hooks. The installed synchronous command admits the edit and returns quietly; background and Stop collect advice. The same CLI also contains a separately invoked direct code path that can return current findings synchronously from `PostToolUse`, including user-authorized `block-current-findings`. These are code paths, not two installed Claude hook versions or two supported product modes. The product owner wants to retain that immediate opportunity because the observed Claude repair in the selected host trial followed a block, while advisory output did not produce an observed repair. Neither observation proves a general reaction rate. Internal CLI-to-resident IPC currently mixes version 2 admission with version 1 background/Stop collection. Ticket-wide outcome state can misrepresent mixed findings and failures.

## Solution

Make the branch's Claude test installation one resident-owned delivery flow with three possible output opportunities: synchronous `PostToolUse`, background, and Stop. Preserve the current user opt-in semantics for synchronous Claude block feedback and keep advisory as the default. Share admission, advice selection, currentness checks, bounded batching, leases, and output authorization across those opportunities. An advice item submitted by one surface must not be independently submitted by another while its existing lease or submission fence applies. Use one current, explicitly migrated local CLI-to-resident IPC contract. Retain only irreducible admission facts; each review unit identifies its admission. Derive collection summaries from work and delivery facts instead of retaining ticket-wide status as a second domain state.

## User Stories

1. As a Claude Code user, I want a current finding to reach the synchronous edit response when it is ready within that hook's safe budget, so that Claude has an immediate opportunity to act.
2. As a Claude Code user, I want advisory feedback to remain the default, so that stronger feedback requires my explicit choice.
3. As a Claude Code user, I want my `block-current-findings` opt-in respected for a current finding, so that the stronger response can prompt a repair.
4. As a Claude Code user, I want project policy to retain its ability to narrow my block opt-in to advisory, so that the established configuration authority is preserved.
5. As a Claude Code user, I want a revoked block opt-in checked at final handoff, so that an old choice cannot authorize a new block.
6. As an agent, I want feedback addressed to my exact session, working root, and subagent identity, so that another agent's findings never enter my context.
7. As an agent, I want findings from eligible review units across multiple admitted edits to be eligible for one bounded advice batch, so that admission boundaries do not fragment useful feedback.
8. As an agent, I want actionable findings to remain deliverable when the synchronous edit budget ends before review completes, so that background or Stop can provide a later opportunity.
9. As an agent, I want a finding already submitted by the edit hook to be fenced from concurrent background and Stop delivery, so that overlapping hooks do not immediately repeat it.
10. As an agent, I want an unavailable review unit to leave successfully reviewed findings deliverable, so that one failure does not hide useful advice from another unit.
11. As a user, I want failures and incomplete work to remain distinguishable from successful clear review, so that quiet hook output is not mistaken for a clean evaluation.
12. As a user, I want an edit that yields no review units to finish quietly without a stored ticket-wide `no-work` result, so that the resident tracks only useful facts.
13. As a user, I want my completed edit preserved when review, IPC, or hook output fails, so that feedback cannot undo the edit.
14. As a user, I want a Stop decision to account for all unfinished work in the Hapsland round, so that one finished admission does not close the round while another remains active.
15. As a maintainer, I want every review unit to identify its originating admission, so that shared or reused evaluations retain each edit's provenance.
16. As a maintainer, I want an admission record to contain only facts that cannot be derived from retained observations, units, and delivery state, so that it does not become a second view of system state.
17. As a maintainer, I want a single current local IPC contract for all installed collectors, so that protocol versions do not encode separate product behaviors.
18. As a maintainer, I want CLI and resident migration to be explicit and tested, so that mixed old and new binaries fail conservatively rather than misreporting success.
19. As a maintainer, I want diagnostic status to be computed from observed activity and work facts, so that user-facing status remains truthful without saving a redundant ticket outcome.
20. As a maintainer, I want the final Claude host response checked against the current 10 KiB encoded-output limit with no separate finding-count cap, so that wrapping a selected batch cannot exceed the host envelope.
21. As a maintainer, I want the installed configuration, accepted target contract, and support evidence to describe the same branch behavior, so that future work does not treat an obsolete direct path as the product contract.
22. As a maintainer, I want tests to distinguish host submission from model-visible reaction and repair, so that a completed write is not reported as agent compliance.

## Implementation Decisions

- Scope this work to the merged implementation and the owner's Claude test environment. This is candidate behavior, not a declaration of released Claude support.
- Keep one installed delivery behavior. The Claude synchronous edit, background, and Stop hooks use the same resident-owned work, advice, lease, currentness, notice, and Hapsland-round authority. Native hooks translate events and host output; they do not own another review queue.
- Preserve synchronous Claude `PostToolUse` collection and output within its existing safe hook deadline. If no eligible advice becomes ready in time, return quietly and leave later eligible advice to background or Stop. Retain the current default advisory mode, user-owned `block-current-findings` opt-in, project narrowing to advisory, and final authority recheck. This is a provisional product requirement based on limited host evidence; it is not a claim that every Claude run repairs.
- Bring the immediate feedback opportunity from the separately invoked direct CLI code path into the branch's single installed delivery flow. Once the shared flow supplies it, remove the separate collection code path. A collector's scope is the exact advicee and Hapsland round, with ordinary currentness and eligibility rules; an admission identifier is provenance and authority data, not an arbitrary output-batch boundary.
- Permit a bounded advice batch to contain eligible findings from several admissions in the same advicee scope. Preserve separate session, subagent, root, credential, and round fences. Reuse the shared selection and lease rules across synchronous, background, and Stop collectors.
- Preserve the difference between review completion, pending advice, lease, host submission, model visibility, and repair. An acknowledged host write establishes submission only. Concurrent or uncertain output follows the existing lease and reoffer rules; do not promise exactly-once model visibility.
- Each admitted observation may yield zero or many review units. Every review unit carries an admission reference. The admission exists before asynchronous source preparation; zero units need no persistent aggregate `no-work` claim. Keep only non-derivable facts needed for admission identity, authorization, lifetime, and preparation or output fencing; do not store a reverse unit list or status summary when it can be derived.
- Keep policy transition facts that govern unfinished work, valid findings, failures, and delivery. Compute any terminal or diagnostic view from those facts. Retire the ticket-wide `pending`, `clear`, `delivered`, `no-work`, and `unavailable` response taxonomy when its separate direct consumer is gone. A mixed finding and failed unit can yield advice while the failure remains observable; it must not be summarized as a single `unavailable` outcome that hides the finding. No terminal status is added to agent-facing hook output solely to replace that taxonomy.
- Use one versioned local JSON IPC contract between Hapsland CLI and resident. Migrate every installed caller, including Claude admission and all collection surfaces, as one explicit change with fixtures and documentation. Do not retain earlier IPC formats as parallel supported behavior. Mismatched peers must fail without claiming clear review or successful submission. These version numbers describe internal messages, not Claude hooks or formats supplied by Jev.
- Apply the current 10 KiB byte bound, with no separate finding-count cap, to the **final encoded Claude response** for each output surface, after host-specific wrapping. An oversized individual finding gets a bounded limitation outcome instead of repeated selection. Preserve final currentness and credential checks immediately before output authorization.
- Update the accepted delivery contract, configuration guidance, installer/support descriptions, and relevant historical-document lifecycle labels to reflect the decision. Distill durable explanations into current contract or code comments where useful; do not create a permanent migration diary. Record implementation completion and support claims separately from the product decision.

## Testing Decisions

- Use one primary deterministic delivery seam: invoke the Claude hooks configured by the branch's test installation through the real local CLI/resident IPC boundary, with controlled source, clock, and Jev decisions. This tests one integration with several hook events, not separate hook versions. Assert observable hook responses, preserved edits, advice submission, and Stop behavior. Test outcomes rather than private ticket containers or helper return shapes.
- At that seam, cover ready finding and clear results, slow work that moves from synchronous to later delivery, zero units, multiple units, two admissions in one eligible batch, one finding plus one failed unit, concurrent synchronous/background/Stop collectors, stale source, changed credential or feedback authority, resident restart, failed output write, and strict encoded Claude response limits.
- Reuse the existing Claude CLI, resident delivery, terminal collection, and composed Stop scenarios as prior art. Replace assertions about obsolete ticket statuses with assertions about agent output, resident work completion, activity diagnostics, and lease behavior. Keep independent expected outcomes rather than deriving test expectations from the implementation.
- At that same CLI/resident subprocess boundary, exercise the one IPC schema with valid, malformed, and mismatched-version requests and responses. These are protocol checks beneath the primary delivery scenario, not a second product delivery path. A failed migration must never be decoded as clear review or confirmed delivery.
- Keep ordinary tests deterministic and offline. Any authenticated Claude or live Jev validation is a separate declared milestone with bounded, sanitized evidence. If run, distinguish output written to Claude from model-visible advice, model-originated repair, and a follow-up clear evaluation.

## Out of Scope

- Replacing the existing collection timing mechanism with push delivery or waiting only for a latest monotonically increasing admission ID.
- New OpenCode host support, additional Claude versions or modes, and a general Claude support declaration.
- A promise that synchronous advice always arrives before the hook deadline or that Claude always follows advice.
- Persisting source, credentials, raw backend responses, or a durable replay log for admission status.
- Changing the accepted review-unit formation, file-selection, or Jev rule policy beyond the admission/provenance and delivery effects specified here.

## Further Notes

- The selected Claude host trial showed a model-originated repair after an opted-in block and no observed repair after an advisory submission. It supports preserving the immediate block opportunity for now, but does not establish a reaction rate or prove the background and Stop opportunities ineffective in every context.
- This work refines the accepted Hapsland advicing contract and intersects the Claude support and blocking-authority work in #94 and #112. It is a branch-level product decision for the Bend migration epic #116; completion and release support remain separately evidenced.
- The current branch's Claude test installation has a quiet synchronous edit hook despite the separately invoked immediate-feedback code path. The implementation must close that gap, then remove the separate path and old IPC formats. The exact final response-size check for Claude Stop is an identified migration acceptance gate.

title: Investigate configurable size and count limits
body:
## Question

Which of Hapsland's fixed size and count limits should users be able to configure? Current values include the resident's shared **512 items/64 MiB**, **16 items/2 MiB per partition**, **8 shared dispatch jobs**, and **4 Stop continuations per round**, plus capture, request, cache, transport, and output bounds. The **4-continuation Stop limit must become a validated user setting**; no higher default is accepted.

## Investigation

- Inventory the current limits, their owners, and which ones affect Bend decisions versus physical host safety.
- Recommend configurable values, defaults, hard ceilings, validation and precedence, and when an effective value is snapshotted for in-flight work. State how invalid or changed settings behave.
- For dispatch, distinguish preparation jobs from Jev calls; assess whether they need separate limits. For Stop, define a safe finite range for the user setting and explain how each value bounds extra agent turns and host behavior.
- Identify code, schema, docs, and dashboard changes needed without implementing them in this task. Coordinate graph budgets with #142, cross-file capture with #138, and full Jev request sizing with #140.

Deliver a concise recommendation in the issue. Keep all limits finite and preserve one authoritative decision path.

title: Restore the full production-flow graph from canonical Bend replay
body:
## Current status — 2026-10-04

Incomplete: the connected canonical diagram implementation is merged in [PR #149](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/pull/149), but the explicit owner visual acceptance remains open. The latest exact before/after cases are in the PR's “Review the visual change” section: guided step 25/35 (`collectionReady`, advice #10), step 24/35 (finding retention command), ninth request refusal step 29/34, and Stop wait step 4/7. Earlier draft/unmerged wording and older step numbers below are historical.

Next decision: inspect those named connected paths and accept or reject their design. The artifact did not change during this tracker cleanup; there is no new visual diff. Existing replay/browser results establish their stated code observations, not human design acceptance. This decision is explicitly separate from npm release and platform support.

## Task scope and prior planning

## Owner respec (2026-09-29)

The first #147 implementation is not visually accepted. Its separate boxes and route cards do not restore the connected node-and-flow diagram. Reopen the visual work in this issue and use the pre-#119 `packages/agent-flow-viz/src/diagram.ts` layout as the concrete presentation reference. The previous diagram's `Flow.step` reducer is retired and must not run. Reuse only visual ideas such as positioned nodes, drawn edges, movement, counts, and the finish view.

The production diagram is a full projection of the running canonical reducer. Every occupied node, active connection, item/count, branch, route, and command status must come from checked canonical state, events, commands, or explicit native facts. Presentation code may place, style, and label them. It may not derive a product decision or simulate a transition. If the canonical interface lacks a needed fact, extend its checked projection or show the boundary explicitly.

Acceptance requires inspecting actual connected arrows in the named guided cases, including a finding from Jev to pending advice, ninth Jev request refusal, and Stop wait/continuation. Compare each case with the current disconnected layout and identify the specific changed route or node. A static coverage inventory and passing projection checks do not substitute for the visible connected graph.

Cross-file evidence is being adopted in #138 by owner decision. Update any diagram labels that present cross-file traversal as merely future work when its production path is integrated. Do not attach this visual acceptance to an npm or other release decision.

## Problem Statement

The Hapsland dashboard once showed a navigable review-and-advice flow with distinct edit, source preparation, review queue, Jev, pending advice, and delivery stages. The #135 canonical migration replaced that full-flow graph with a five-box summary rail. The page now replays the production `Canonical.step` transition, but the main visual no longer exposes the state, routes, branches, and commands that make that replay useful. A viewer cannot readily see what moved, what is waiting, which decision Bend made, or which native effect follows. The separate import-graph diagram does not fill this gap in the production flow.

The prior `Flow.bend` diagram was a narrower one-agent teaching model, yet its presentation was richer. The current canonical model is the production decision authority. Its dashboard must explain more, while remaining a read-only projection of compiled Bend output. Hard-coded or outdated capacity descriptions would also mislead viewers. #148 separates the current shared eight-job dispatch ceiling into an eight-job preparation bound and an eight-request Jev in-flight bound; both remain distinct from review capacity ledger item and byte limits. This issue must display the integrated production model, not freeze either the old or new numbers into presentation code.

## Solution

Restore a full production-flow graph in the Hapsland dashboard, **at least as rich as the pre-#119 diagram**, driven throughout by the same checked `Canonical.step` adapter and compiled Bend transitions used by the resident. Guided and manual events, history navigation, state, commands, queue position, capacity, and highlighted routes must all derive from canonical replay. Source-free native facts may be scenario inputs. TypeScript may map Bend states and commands to labels, geometry, colors, and explanations; it must not calculate a product decision, advance a second flow model, or imply that a native effect happened merely because Bend made it eligible.

The overview must show the real review-and-advice topology: agent-runtime observation; admitted and queued preparation work; source preparation; admitted review units; the #148 ready-to-request event, Bend authorization command, Jev effect attempt and response; clear, finding, unavailable, and stale outcomes; pending advice; background and Stop collection; response authorization; observed output; and Hapsland-round closure or continuation. Distinguish Bend state/decisions, native TypeScript effects/facts, and external Jev responses. Show immediate unavailability when all eight Jev request places are occupied, without implying a Jev wait queue. Provide focused detail where the production model has additional branches such as capacity refusal, cancellation, revalidation, leases, uncertain output, and reoffer. Preserve the existing separate import-graph and native timing views, with their model-versus-production scope stated accurately.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- The main graph has at least the pre-#119 diagram's explanatory richness: distinct work locations, data and control routes, meaningful branch outcomes, active-step highlighting, item/operation identities where available, and an inspectable finish/delivery decision. A five-box linear rail alone does not pass.
- Every displayed Hapsland decision, state count, queue position, route activation, capacity result, and command outcome comes from the checked canonical replay of compiled Bend. Static layout and plain-language labels are presentation only. No `Flow.step`, parallel reducer, scenario-specific outcome table, or UI scheduler supplies business behavior.
- The graph follows guided and manual canonical events and remains correct through rewind, redo, history jumps, rejected events, and multi-item or multi-advicee examples. A rejection changes neither canonical state nor displayed item locations.
- The graph distinguishes “review work item ready,” “Bend authorized/commanded,” “native Jev effect attempted or observed,” “Jev response supplied,” and “host output submitted/uncertain.” It shows a command that was not sent, cancellation, late/stale response, and Jev-slot refusal according to canonical replay. It never treats an eligible unit or issued command as proof that a Jev request was sent, or a submitted message as proof that the agent used advice.
- Show preparation running slots, Jev in-flight request places, and review capacity ledger item/byte limits as three distinct quantities after #148 integration. Show Jev-slot refusal as immediate unavailability, not a queued position. Display current values only from checked Bend/adapter output or a generated inventory derived from it; do not copy a numeric limit into presentation code. If a runtime quantity is not exposed by the checked interface, add a checked projection rather than inventing it.
- The graph covers the canonical production transition families relevant to the full flow. A source-linked coverage inventory identifies which families have guided examples, which appear through manual replay, and which are native facts/effects outside Bend. Unmodeled or not-yet-integrated behavior is labeled as such, especially cross-file import traversal.
- The existing import exploration and native timing panels continue to work, without presenting their separate model/evidence as an executed production path.

## User Stories

1. As a product owner, I want a full production-flow graph, so that I can understand what Hapsland does after an edit.
2. As a dashboard viewer, I want to see distinct observation, preparation, review, Jev, advice, and delivery stages, so that I can locate work without reading raw command lists.
3. As a dashboard viewer, I want arrows for data movement and control signals, so that I can see how work and decisions travel through the system.
4. As a dashboard viewer, I want the current replay step highlighted, so that I can follow the effect of one event.
5. As a dashboard viewer, I want operation identities and counts on relevant stages, so that concurrent and queued work remains understandable.
6. As a dashboard viewer, I want pending, active, and running preparation work distinguished, so that its queue behavior is visible without inventing a Jev wait queue.
7. As a dashboard viewer, I want preparation concurrency, Jev request concurrency, and resident/advicee review capacity distinguished, so that I do not confuse execution slots with retained-record limits.
8. As a dashboard viewer, I want accepted and refused unit admissions shown in order, so that partial capacity decisions are clear.
9. As a dashboard viewer, I want a clear result distinguished from a finding, backend failure, and stale result, so that each terminal outcome means what it says.
10. As a dashboard viewer, I want Bend's Jev request command distinguished from an attempted or completed native effect, so that authorization is not mistaken for a sent request.
11. As a dashboard viewer, I want the Jev boundary and returned facts marked as external, so that Bend's authority is represented accurately.
12. As a dashboard viewer, I want pending advice, background submission, and Stop collection shown as distinct paths, so that delivery timing is understandable.
13. As a dashboard viewer, I want Stop waiting, continuation, allowance, cancellation, and closure displayed, so that I can follow the Hapsland round to its end.
14. As a dashboard viewer, I want authorized, failed, and uncertain host output distinguished, so that a write attempt is not confused with agent receipt or use.
15. As a dashboard viewer, I want revalidation, lease, expiry, and reoffer outcomes explained, so that advice does not seem to appear or disappear arbitrarily.
16. As a dashboard viewer, I want rejected events to leave the graph unchanged and show the reason, so that I can understand canonical guards.
17. As a dashboard viewer, I want rewind, redo, history jump, guided examples, and manual events to operate on the same graph, so that every navigation mode tells the same story.
18. As a maintainer, I want the dashboard to consume the resident's checked canonical adapter, so that visual behavior cannot drift into an independent decision engine.
19. As a maintainer, I want presentation mappings checked against canonical variants and example traces, so that a new Bend transition is not silently misrepresented.
20. As a maintainer, I want a coverage inventory for production transition families, so that a polished diagram does not hide missing or unshown paths.
21. As a maintainer, I want current preparation, Jev, and ledger limits displayed from Bend-derived values, so that changes do not leave stale UI claims.
22. As a product owner, I want the old graph's useful explanatory detail restored without reviving its retired reducer, so that the canonical migration improves both authority and understanding.
23. As a dashboard viewer, I want the separate import graph and native timing evidence clearly scoped, so that I can tell a modeled future path from current production behavior.
24. As a dashboard viewer, I want an eight-place Jev pool and immediate ninth-request refusal shown only when #148's canonical transition emits them, so that the graph does not invent a queue or imply that preparation consumes Jev places.

## Implementation Decisions

- Extend the existing dashboard and canonical replay rather than creating another simulator. The checked canonical adapter remains the single business-logic input for the production-flow view.
- Represent the topology with presentation-only nodes and routes keyed to canonical state, event, command, and projection variants. Static labels and geometry may be editorial; whether a route is active or a state is occupied must come from replay output.
- Keep native source capture, clock, Jev I/O, and host writes as labeled effect/fact boundaries. Source-free scenarios may supply their observed results as inputs; the dashboard may not infer those results from an earlier command.
- Follow #148's integrated dispatch truth: Bend retains preparation scheduling state and a separate Jev in-flight permit pool, while TypeScript retains native job handles and performs Jev effects. Show the eight-place Jev pool and immediate saturation outcome only through checked canonical output. Do not show a Jev wait queue; #139 merely considers one for future work.
- Keep the preparation-job bound, Jev request bound, and review capacity ledger limits separate. Obtain presented limits from compiled Bend output or a checked adapter projection, including changes made after the original dashboard was built.
- Preserve independent expected trace fixtures and the existing history semantics. Add guided examples where needed to demonstrate queue progression, multi-unit preparation, Jev outcome branches, advice delivery, and Stop behavior without scenario-specific result calculations in UI code.
- Do not reactivate the retired abstract flow reducer. If a desired production route has no canonical state, command, or fact boundary, mark the visual gap and link it to the relevant production-authority work; do not fill it with UI policy.
- Use the product glossary: Hapsland for the product, Jev for the external backend, agent runtime for the hook owner, Hapsland round for the review/advice period, review work item for a prepared unit, review dispatch cycle for a finite selected group, and review capacity ledger for retained item/byte accounting.

## Testing Decisions

- Use the existing dashboard browser interaction as the highest test seam. Step a source-free guided or manual event, inspect the rendered graph and accessible labels, then rewind or replay and verify the visible route, counts, branches, and outcome. Test what a viewer can observe rather than private layout helpers.
- Reuse the independent canonical trace fixtures and dashboard projection check to compare displayed states and commands with expected results. The displayed graph must not be its own oracle.
- Cover preparation queue admission and settlement, accepted/refused ledger capacity, Jev command versus actual attempt, eight concurrent Jev requests with a ninth ready item immediately unavailable, unsent/cancelled/stale requests, clear/finding/backend failure/timeout, Stop wait/cancel/continue/allow, background delivery and reoffer, uncertain output, rejection, and history navigation. Use only scenarios that the integrated canonical interface can express; label external facts honestly.
- Check that changed Bend-derived preparation, Jev, or ledger limits change the dashboard display without a second hard-coded UI value.
- Keep existing import-graph and native-timing browser checks. They verify those separate views without claiming production cross-file integration or live Jev execution.
- A visual comparison against the pre-#119 graph is an acceptance review for explanatory richness, not a source of business truth. Record the old graph's covered stages and interactions, then show their canonical equivalents or an explicit current boundary.

## Out of Scope

- Changing resident business rules, Jev request dispatch authority, backpressure policy, or capacity limits as part of a visual restoration.
- Integrating the separate import-graph model into production cross-file review.
- Live Jev calls from the dashboard or a claim that a source-free replay proves installed-host behavior.
- Reintroducing `Flow.step` or a TypeScript implementation of Bend decisions.

## Further Notes

The pre-#119 graph had 12 distinct process/storage/external/boundary nodes, event-numbered routes, active movement, item counts, and a separate finish-decision view. The current production page has five summary stages plus canonical replay controls and a capacity panel. The goal is functional parity or better in explanatory depth, not copying historical labels or asserting historical capacities.

At the time this issue was written, the canonical dispatcher allowed eight **combined** running preparation/review jobs. #148 replaces that meaning with an eight-job preparation bound and an eight-request Jev in-flight bound; a ninth ready Jev request settles immediately as unavailable. The resident's review capacity ledger separately limits retained items and bytes. The issue must not freeze any numeric limit into the UI; these values explain the required distinction and must be read from the integrated checked model.

Related work: #116 established one Bend decision authority; #135 replaced the full-flow view during canonical migration; #138 owns production cross-file evidence adoption; #139 owns future backpressure questions; #148 owns the Jev request command/result contract and separate Jev concurrency limit. Final acceptance of this graph's Jev boundary and capacity display follows #148 integration. Visual implementation may start earlier, but must label any not-yet-integrated route and cannot claim #148 behavior before production has it. This issue restores a truthful, rich visualization of the running canonical model and does not implement those separate product changes.

title: Make Jev requests explicit Bend commands and retire direct review
body:
## Current disposition — 2026-10-04

Complete for explicit canonical review-request authorization and retirement of direct stdin review. [PR #149](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/pull/149) merged on 2026-09-30 at `07ecd4e4654ca4193c4d834b03f1db385d309b7d`; that commit is an ancestor of the audited checkout. The earlier “draft/unmerged” handoff is superseded.

Delivered: source-free request authorization and issued/start/settled identities, separate bounded preparation and review-request pools, immediate saturation refusal without a Jev wait queue, late/duplicate outcome fencing, and permit release after physical settlement. The old whole-file JSON review command and Codex fallback are retired; semantic fixture evaluation remains. Current primary evidence: [independent request traces](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/conformance/canonical-jev-request-v1.json), [resident request tests](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/src/resident/jev-request.test.ts) and [authority ledger](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/docs/typescript-decision-boundary-ledger.md). The current retained gate passed all 10 resident request tests and the request/ABI/authority checks.

The [earlier acceptance record](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/148#issuecomment-5884627199) distinguishes its resident interruption coverage from the separate canonical physical-settlement barrier; this reconciliation makes no stronger native-finalizer claim. Future waiting/backpressure is owned by #160/#139 and does not block the current immediate-unavailable contract.

## Original task scope

# Make Jev requests explicit canonical commands and retire the old direct review command

## Problem Statement

Hapsland uses Bend as the authority for product decisions and TypeScript to execute physical effects. Today Bend records that a review work item has started, but the resident performs further checks and can call Jev without a distinct Bend command that authorizes that actual request. A `ReviewStarted` transition therefore does not say whether source code was sent to Jev. A skipped, cancelled, failed, or late effect cannot be traced as the measured outcome of one explicit request authorization. The current eight-slot dispatch limit covers preparation and review-evaluation jobs together, so it does not express the owner's intended limit of eight concurrent Jev requests.

Hapsland also retains an older whole-file JSON review command. It accepts a version-1 review request on standard input and can call Jev outside the resident review flow. The installed Codex, Claude Code, and OpenCode integrations use the resident path; the older command remains manually callable, has an old Codex fallback, and is referenced by active documentation, tests, and a historical benchmark. Leaving it in place obscures the intended single product review path.

## Solution

For an admitted review work item, TypeScript measures the native facts needed immediately before a Jev request and sends a source-free `JevRequestReady` event (provisional name) to the canonical Bend transition. This event is sent after preparation and final currentness, configuration, and credential measurements; the edit event and current `StartReview` event are too early to authorize egress. Bend checks the work identity and its eight-slot Jev request pool. If a slot is available, it reserves one and emits an explicit request command. If all eight are occupied, Bend immediately settles the work item as unavailable without sending or retaining it in a Jev wait queue. TypeScript executes an issued command with the actual source-bearing review input and reports the observed effect outcome to Bend as an event tied to the same work identity. Bend decides what to retain, cancel, ignore as stale, or offer as advice. Source text, credentials, and raw Jev responses never enter retained Bend state, command traces, or test evidence; the real Jev request still contains the source input required for review.

Remove the old whole-file JSON review command, its non-composed Codex fallback, and active code, tests, scripts, and documentation that exist solely for those routes. Keep the separate semantic evaluation command. It is a maintainer tool for checking Hapsland rules against fixtures and may later support user rule debugging; that later user-facing workflow is a separate task. Preserve shared Effect Jev infrastructure used by evaluation or the resident. Update the authority map so the old route is a decided retirement target, while keeping its historical audit facts accurate.

## User Stories

1. As a maintainer, I want Bend to authorize each production Jev review request explicitly, so that one transition authority governs review dispatch.
2. As a maintainer, I want the request command to identify its advicee partition, Hapsland round, review work item, and request operation, so that results cannot be applied to different work.
3. As an agent, I want Hapsland to avoid sending an ineligible or incomplete review unit to Jev, so that review only uses admissible evidence.
4. As a user, I want source code sent to Jev only for a Bend-authorized review work item, so that the product's review decision matches the executed effect.
5. As a maintainer, I want TypeScript to keep source and credentials outside Bend state and traces, so that policy state remains source-free.
6. As a maintainer, I want Bend to receive the observed outcome of each authorized command, so that command issuance is not mistaken for a completed request.
7. As a maintainer, I want Bend told when a request was never sent, so that pre-send invalidation, cancellation, or missing credentials do not appear as Jev outcomes.
8. As a maintainer, I want Bend told when TypeScript interrupted a running Effect, so that work state reflects the physical cancellation attempt.
9. As a maintainer, I want late or duplicate responses associated with their original work identity, so that Bend can reject effects on superseded work.
10. As an agent, I want a current Jev finding offered only under Bend's existing advice rules, so that an old finding does not become advice about a new source snapshot.
11. As a maintainer, I want clear, finding, backend failure, and timeout to remain distinct observed outcomes, so that operational failures do not become clear reviews.
12. As a maintainer, I want request counts and ordering observable in a deterministic resident scenario, so that the authorization boundary can be checked from outside its helpers.
13. As a maintainer, I want the old direct JSON review command and old Codex fallback retired, so that active review traffic follows the resident and canonical Bend path.
14. As a maintainer, I want the semantic evaluation command retained, so that fixture-based rule evaluation remains possible after old-path cleanup.
15. As a maintainer, I want active documentation and authority accounting to identify the surviving Jev routes correctly, so that future changes do not mistake historical paths for supported production paths.
16. As a dashboard viewer, I want the later flow graph to distinguish Bend authorization from an attempted or completed Jev effect, so that it depicts what actually happened.
17. As a user, I want at most eight Jev requests active at once across the resident, so that preparation work does not silently consume Jev request capacity.
18. As a maintainer, I want a ninth ready Jev review to settle immediately as unavailable, so that this task does not introduce a new waiting policy.
19. As a maintainer, I want preparation to retain its own finite eight-job bound, so that separating Jev capacity does not leave native file work unbounded.

## Implementation Decisions

- Keep the current canonical Bend transition as the product decision authority. Its existing dispatch queue, `StartReview` transition, and review result handling are starting points; do not treat `ReviewStarted` as proof that a Jev request was sent. Repurpose or split the existing dispatch behavior so preparation has its own finite eight-job bound and review evaluation no longer consumes those preparation slots. The precise internal scheduling shape can change, but it must not retain a shared eight-job cap that makes preparation compete with Jev requests.
- Inventory every path to Effect `DecisionModel.decide` before removal. Installed agent-runtime hooks use the resident; the manually callable whole-file JSON review path and old non-composed Codex fallback are to be retired. The semantic evaluation command remains an explicit, separate tool.
- Split native measurement from product choice at the final pre-request boundary. TypeScript may capture and render source, measure identity/currentness, read configuration and credentials, check physical availability, and report source-free facts in a dedicated ready-to-request event. Bend decides eligibility and emits an explicit request command for the identified review work item. TypeScript must not make a second Hapsland eligibility decision after that command; any physical inability to execute is reported back as an observed fact.
- Bend owns a resident-wide pool of eight concurrent Jev request permits, distinct from the preparation-job bound and the review capacity ledger's retained item/byte limits. Reserve a permit with the explicit request command and release it exactly once when TypeScript reports that the attempt did not start or the native effect has settled. Merely asking Effect to interrupt does not release a permit while the native call is still unsettled. When no permit is free, Bend immediately settles the ready work item as unavailable and releases its retained capacity; do not create a Jev wait queue in this task.
- The command and every corresponding observation carry enough identity to distinguish advicee partition, resident lifetime, Hapsland round, review work item, and the authorized request operation. Tie native handles and source-bearing input to opaque identities in TypeScript only.
- Report whether an authorized command was not sent, started and completed, failed, timed out, or was interrupted. An Effect interruption or cancellation is an observed event, not a silent removal. Bend advances or retires the work according to its canonical state and rejects stale or duplicate observations without changing current advice.
- TypeScript physically executes Jev requests and interruption. Jev's response is an external measurement; Hapsland's finding selection, relevance, and advice decisions remain Bend decisions. Keep raw response and credentials outside retained Bend state and source-free evidence.
- Do not introduce automatic retries in this task. A future Effect-level retry policy may be represented to Bend as one longer request, or future Bend policy may model individual attempts; decide that contract if retries are introduced. Do not imply that one command is a lifetime ban on Effect-level retries.
- Remove active direct-review protocol handling, its old Codex fallback, and code and references used solely by them. Preserve shared backend and rule-evaluation code required by the semantic evaluation command. Update current guidance and the authority map's forward-looking disposition without erasing historical evidence.
- Keep this task separate from dashboard restoration (#147) and future backpressure/configurable-limit policy (#139, #146). The fixed eight-request Jev pool and separate interim eight-job preparation bound are part of this task. A future Jev saturation queue can be considered under #139 without changing this task's immediate-unavailable rule.

## Testing Decisions

- The primary acceptance seam is a deterministic resident scenario with controlled Jev and native effects. Drive an admitted edit through the resident and observe actual request count, ordering, terminal outcome, and advice behavior rather than testing private helpers as the principal gate.
- Cover admitted review, denied review, incomplete evidence, pre-send invalidation, cancellation before and during execution, later source change, late and duplicate completion, clear, finding, backend failure, and timeout. Assert no request starts without the matching Bend command, and that command issuance alone never counts as a sent request. With eight active Jev calls and preparation work also active, verify that no ninth Jev call starts, the ninth ready work item is settled without a Jev wait queue, and preparation does not consume a Jev permit. Verify exact permit release after completion, failed pre-send execution, timeout, and settled interruption.
- Keep independent source-free canonical expected traces. Check every new event and command variant against the compiled Bend/TypeScript adapter contract, including identity and malformed or unknown results.
- Verify that installed Codex, Claude Code, and OpenCode paths reach the resident contract; distinguish source call-site inventory from supported runtime evidence. Check that the old stdin review protocol and Codex fallback have no active entry point after removal.
- Keep ordinary tests deterministic and offline. Do not print or commit source-bearing Jev responses or credentials. Live Jev validation, if needed at a declared milestone, requires a bounded plan and sanitized contract/timing evidence.

## Out of Scope

- Dashboard graph restoration (#147).
- A waiting queue or retry/backpressure policy for Jev saturation; broader configurable-limit choices (#139, #146).
- Automatic Jev retries in this task.
- A user-facing rule-debugging workflow or redesign of semantic evaluation documentation; preserve the existing evaluation command for that future work.
- Moving source text, credentials, raw Jev responses, network I/O, or Effect interruption into Bend.
- Deleting historical evidence solely because it records the old command.

## Further Notes

This is a focused follow-up to #116's single-authority goal. #137 closed the structural authority audit; it did not establish an explicit command for the physical Jev request. #147 restores the visual flow separately and must not invent request authority. The old direct review protocol is documented and manually callable, but current installed adapters use the resident; do not claim that repository search proves no external users ever invoked the old protocol. Its removal is an intentional product decision.

title: Integrate reviewed resident, graph, and candidate evidence work
body:
## What this branch changes

This draft combines #145, #142, #143, #148, #138, and the revised #147 diagram. It does not start an npm publication.

- **Feedback and resident work:** Claude can receive edit feedback through the immediate hook when it is ready, or through the bounded background and Stop paths later. The resident uses Bend commands for Jev request permission, keeps preparation and Jev request places separate, and exits after its idle grace period.
- **Cross-file review (#138):** A changed TypeScript type or top-level function can use related declarations from other selected files. This is now the normal direct-edit path on this branch, including when all required evidence is in one file. The same-file-only Jev input and its production rendering path are retired. Hapsland checks each supporting path before reading, keeps finite source/tree/request limits, sends only complete evidence, and checks freshness before Jev and before advice. Built-in Noul rules use the new input. Authored rule packs must declare exact type/function targets in schema 2; schema-1 authored packs fail configuration before source capture. Codex patch hunks and verified Claude edits identify the changed declaration. The quality comparison is a later task (#150), as the owner decided in #138.
- **Connected production diagram (#147):** The old connected visual structure from `packages/agent-flow-viz/src/diagram.ts` is back in the production view as positioned nodes and numbered arrows. The retired `Flow.step` reducer and its old TypeScript page are deleted; only the connected visual grammar remains. One view registry owns square content and identified-item placement. Active connections come from before/after checked state by stable ID, with explicit view rules for commands and supplied facts that state alone cannot join. Orange arrows show an accepted event/fact; purple dashed arrows show a Bend command without claiming its native effect occurred. The opening example now follows two edits through a waiting dispatch entry, two overlapping Jev requests, ready advice, and an acknowledged Stop response.

## Review the visual change

For the same default **guided step 25/35 (`collectionReady`, advice #10)**, compare [before inference](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/c2f6389/packages/agent-flow-viz/docs/assets/production-flow-before-inference-step-25.png) with [after inference](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/c2f6389/packages/agent-flow-viz/docs/assets/production-flow-inferred-step-25.png). Before: Pending advice said `ready #10`, but its incoming Review outcomes → Pending advice arrow stayed gray. After: that connection lights orange, with a route-key label naming advice #10 and the supplied native readiness fact. The adjacent Pending advice → Advice collection arrow is purple because Bend emitted `collectionEligible`; it does not claim host output.

Inspect [guided step 24/35](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/c2f6389/packages/agent-flow-viz/docs/assets/production-flow-inferred-step-24.png) for the boundary immediately before it: a Jev finding reaches Review outcomes, and `retainFinding` lights a purple command arrow toward advice while Pending advice still says `ready none`. The new projection does not invent a work-ID-to-advice-ID link, since the checked interface does not expose one. Route numbers stay fixed while stepping or rewinding; a changed square can light without an invented movement arrow.

The earlier #147 implementation had [separate boxes and route cards](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/d581f45/packages/agent-flow-viz/docs/assets/production-flow-canonical-finding-retained.png). Inspect the current [ninth Jev request refusal, guided step 29/34](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9a1f216/packages/agent-flow-viz/docs/assets/production-flow-inferred-jev-refusal.png): eight requests are in flight, the ninth ready check emits `jevRequestUnavailable`, and no Jev queue appears. Inspect the current [Stop wait, guided step 4/7](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9a1f216/packages/agent-flow-viz/docs/assets/production-flow-inferred-stop-wait.png): `waitForWork` loops at Advice collection while the round remains active. The concrete #147 decision requested from the owner is design acceptance of this connected, evidence-labeled projection after inspecting these cases in the interactive view. Passing replay or browser checks validates code behavior; it does not grant that visual acceptance or any release/platform support.

## Checks and limits

`npm run build` in `packages/agent-flow-viz` passed TypeScript, inferred-connection checks, the full projection trace check, and Vite. The rendered `npm run test:browser` passed after supplying the container's missing Chromium libraries in a temporary user-space directory; no repository or system packages were changed. Static authority checks passed. Two independent Astra medium review axes found three concrete gaps, all fixed and verified in second review passes: output-to-round evidence, unrelated-square highlighting, and a vacuous renamed-node browser assertion. The retried 19 Claude hook tests passed on an idle host. An earlier repository-wide run was stopped after host-sensitive Claude hook failures while other checks were competing for resources; the last completed integrated `npm test` at `a85ad29` passed 737 tests with 2 skipped.

The [owner decision brief](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/df792e2/docs/issue-149-owner-decision-brief.md) records the important owner choices, implementation assumptions, and evidence limits. Two Astra medium architecture reviews and independent per-issue reviews informed the fixes. No comparative live Jev advice study has run; #150 owns that later question. Unsupported or incomplete imports, excluded supporting files, and unverified changed-root attribution produce no Jev request for that unit. The current parser attribution fails closed on non-ASCII source until coordinates are converted. This PR remains draft and unmerged; #147 owner visual acceptance remains pending.

Refs #138 #142 #143 #145 #147 #148 #150.

title: Evaluate cross-file review advice after adoption
body:
## Current status — 2026-10-04

Incomplete later evaluation. The cross-file production path is integrated through #138 and merged PR #149; waiting for that PR to merge is no longer a dependency. A separately declared representative corpus, comparison protocol, bounds and source-free evidence are still required before running this study. This evaluates advice quality and cost, not agent-output causality (#95), and does not block the adopted implementation.

## Task scope and prior planning

## Purpose

After bounded cross-file review is enabled, compare Jev's advice with and without supporting declarations from other files. This is a later product-evaluation task, not an activation gate for #138.

## Questions
