- Does supporting source improve correct findings on representative edits?
- Does it increase incorrect or distracting findings?
- How much additional source, request time, and resident work does it cost?

## Scope

Choose and label cases, freeze the rule set and comparison inputs, run a bounded live comparison with sanitized results, and report the limits of the evidence. Keep live source and credentials out of the issue. Include type and function cases only where evidence is complete enough for a fair comparison. Report findings to the product owner without changing the enabled path automatically.

## Dependency

Start after #138's cross-file path is integrated and stable. This issue does not block #138, #147, or the already merged PR #149.

title: Handle Unicode in post-edit span coordinates for Add and Update
body:
## Current disposition — 2026-10-04

Complete for Unicode-aware Add and verified Update attribution. [Fix b8367ea8](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/commit/b8367ea83130f2115faee2e18137e4be7eb509b4) removes the blanket non-ASCII refusal and uses matching UTF-16 coordinates from parser nodes and verified spans. [Compatibility guidance](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/docs/review-contract-compatibility.md) now describes Unicode support and retains quiet refusal for missing/ambiguous spans. The current retained gate passed all 24 [Unicode attribution cases](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/src/direct-event/unicode-attribution.test.ts) across Add/Update, type/function roots and Unicode before/outside the root; runtime-specific uncertainty remains explicit.

[Commit 263630a0](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/commit/263630a02f9488e65a2da8421e46c8e28772e4f5) retains a [native Codex Unicode Update observation](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/9f3a5873e2642e99e7de564781bb3a42db3441c5/evidence/native-languages/codex-typescript-adoption-unicode-update-controlled-offline-1791039023270.json) with finding, repair and clear follow-up. It used a synthetic source-checkout fixture, Codex CLI 0.155.1 and zero provider calls; it does not validate a registry archive or normal-trust installed release. The old #149 non-ASCII note is historical and superseded by this change. Pi's separate ASCII profile is not broadened by this task.

## Original task scope

## Problem

The direct-edit pipeline skips type/function review for a TypeScript file whenever the captured file contains any non-ASCII character. This applies to **Add and Update**, even when the edit and the declaration being reviewed contain only ASCII and the non-ASCII character is elsewhere in the file.

The implementation checks `Buffer.byteLength(captured.text, "utf8") !== captured.text.length` before selecting the changed declaration. This guards against mixing Tree-sitter byte columns with JavaScript string columns, but the check is broader than needed. The current compatibility document and PR #149 owner brief describe the limit as applying to Update only.

## Expected behavior

A valid post-edit span should identify a changed type or function in a file containing Unicode text, once its position can be compared safely with parser positions. An Add should select its eligible named declarations regardless of unrelated Unicode text.

## Scope

- Correct coordinate handling or use an equivalent safe comparison for Add and Update.
- Cover Unicode before and outside the changed declaration in focused offline tests.
- Keep uncertain spans from selecting a declaration.
- Update the compatibility statement and PR #149 owner brief to match the implemented behavior.

This is a low priority follow-up to PR #149, not a blocker for the current owner discussion.

title: monkey-business: deterministic simulator for Hapsland’s Bend flow
body:
**Purpose:** Specify monkey-business, Hapsland's deterministic simulation package.
**Status:** Ready for implementation after publication and application of `ready-for-agent`.
**Authority:** Feature implementation specification synthesized from the user's agreed scope. Hapsland's existing accepted product contracts continue to own review, advice, admission and delivery behavior.
**Expected use:** Implement and assess the initial simulator through its public behavior; use the documented coverage boundary when interpreting a run.
**Lifecycle:** Maintain this issue's scope through implementation. At completion, record acceptance evidence and consolidate ongoing package/API guidance into maintained package documentation. Review scope when the modeled boundary, controls or replay contract changes. This issue is the specification owner; delete the superseded local interview draft after publication.

## Problem Statement

Hapsland's dashboard currently explains checked Bend transitions through finite examples and manually supplied events. A developer cannot run an ongoing, realistic coding-session workload, make Jev slower, increase edit demand, vary file/workload sizes, and observe the resulting review and advice behavior through one reproducible simulation.

The developer needs to explore the existing logic and test the new simulation machinery without launching a real agent runtime or contacting Jev. The simulation must remain independent of the diagram, reliably accelerate time, and preserve Bend as the owner of product decisions. A useful first version should expose current behavior and its limits without adding substantial product features merely to simulate more cases.

## Solution

Create a separate package named `monkey-business`, following the repository's package naming conventions. It runs the existing compiled Bend logic through the checked production adapters and supplies a deterministic synthetic environment around it.

One simulated agent receives generated coding tasks, makes edits at a configurable pace with modest seeded variation, encounters advice during work, and sometimes attempts to finish. It may ignore advice, choose not to act, attempt a repair promptly, or attempt a repair later. All are valid use cases. Repairs use ordinary fresh edit/revision activity already supported by the reducer. After the agent finishes a task, a modeled pause precedes the next task. A separate simulated user is unnecessary; task arrivals can carry a user-origin label if useful.

A single ongoing engine supports stepping, pause/resume and accelerated execution. Tests advance that same run to a virtual-time or event boundary. Live controls change edit demand, Jev delay/failure behavior and supported file/workload size facts. Seed, initial configuration, consumed logic identity and the recorded control timeline make runs reproducible.

The package emits checked transition observations that the existing flow projection can consume. The dashboard continues to own squares, layout, colors and arrows. Its eventual simulation UI is a separate consumer of this package.

## User Stories

1. As a Hapsland developer, I want a standalone simulation package, so that I can explore review and advice behavior without running the dashboard.
2. As a Hapsland developer, I want the simulation to exercise the same compiled Bend decisions used by production, so that experiments concern the actual product logic.
3. As a Hapsland developer, I want one simulated agent initially, so that the first version remains understandable and useful.
4. As a Hapsland developer, I want generated edits at a normal configurable pace with modest variation, so that an ongoing run resembles a coding session.
5. As a Hapsland developer, I want reviews to proceed while the agent continues working, so that multiple outstanding edits and reviews can arise naturally.
6. As a Hapsland developer, I want occasional finish attempts during unfinished review work, so that I can exercise Hapsland's Stop waiting and deadline logic.
7. As a Hapsland developer, I want advice collection opportunities during work, so that the simulation exercises existing middle-edit and background mechanisms.
8. As a Hapsland developer, I want the agent to be able to ignore advice or choose not to act, so that valid non-cooperative behavior is represented.
9. As a Hapsland developer, I want prompt attempted repairs, so that I can exercise the review/advice/fresh-edit cycle.
10. As a Hapsland developer, I want delayed attempted repairs, so that advice can interact with intervening edits, expiry and finish attempts.
11. As a Hapsland developer, I want repair edits to use existing admission and revision behavior, so that the simulator adds no new repair rule to Hapsland.
12. As a Hapsland developer, I want later tasks separated by configurable pauses, so that a run can include working and idle periods without a separate simulated user.
13. As a Hapsland developer, I want edit pace adjustable during a run, so that I can explore changing demand without resetting the simulation.
14. As a Hapsland developer, I want a bounded edit-burst action, so that I can inspect overload and recovery from a known workload increase.
15. As a Hapsland developer, I want Jev delays adjustable, so that I can observe the effects of slow review on outstanding requests and Stop decisions.
16. As a Hapsland developer, I want synthetic Jev failure and timeout scenarios, so that unavailable work remains distinguishable from clear results.
17. As a Hapsland developer, I want supported file and workload size facts configurable, so that I can explore the capacity and evidence boundaries actually modeled.
18. As a Hapsland developer, I want each size control's coverage stated precisely, so that a reservation-byte experiment is not mistaken for source capture or import traversal validation.
19. As a Hapsland developer, I want immediate saturation refusal displayed as the current reducer produces it, so that simulation does not invent a Jev waiting queue.
20. As a Hapsland developer, I want individually identified preparation, review, advice and output observations, so that I can follow concurrent work without treating all stages as one completion.
21. As a Hapsland developer, I want cancellations and late callbacks represented with their original identities, so that I can exercise the existing stale-result fences.
22. As a Hapsland developer, I want source-free synthetic inputs and outcomes, so that ordinary runs need no credentials or private working-tree source.
23. As a Hapsland developer, I want seeded generation and recorded controls, so that I can reproduce a run that exposed a problem.
24. As a Hapsland developer, I want replay to identify the consumed logic and simulation contract, so that incompatible runs are not silently described as exact reproductions.
25. As a Hapsland developer, I want to advance one event or a bounded interval, so that I can inspect a difficult sequence precisely.
26. As a Hapsland developer, I want pause and speed changes to preserve virtual outcomes, so that observation speed does not change the experiment.
27. As a Hapsland developer, I want every modeled duration and deadline to follow simulated time, so that accelerated runs remain internally consistent.
28. As a Hapsland developer, I want tests to stop requesting steps at a declared boundary, so that the same ongoing engine can run reliably in automation.
29. As a Hapsland developer, I want a driver limit to return resumable state and an explicit reason, so that a test limit cannot secretly act as the agent's Stop event.
30. As a Hapsland developer, I want existing Bend checks reused and their scope explained, so that additional simulator checks have a justified purpose.
31. As a Hapsland developer, I want run checks on command-following, identity, scheduling and replay, so that defects in the new synthetic environment are detectable.
32. As a Hapsland developer, I want independently expected directed scenarios, so that tests do more than compare the simulator's implementation with itself.
33. As a dashboard developer, I want checked before/after transition frames compatible with the existing projection, so that the diagram can consume the simulator without another product reducer.
34. As a dashboard developer, I want semantic observations without square names or coordinates, so that presentation remains a UI responsibility.
35. As a maintainer, I want unsupported commands and coverage gaps reported explicitly, so that an apparently successful run cannot hide unmodeled behavior.
36. As a maintainer, I want a minimal extensible configuration and observation contract, so that later scenarios and multiple agents can be added without coupling the engine to the UI.

## Implementation Decisions

- Introduce the UI-independent monkey-business package and its public run API. Its core can be consumed headlessly and by a future browser/dashboard driver. Keep Node-only runner concerns, rendering, real transports and wall-clock playback outside the deterministic core.
- Keep the checked canonical adapter as the production decision boundary. Reuse the compiled import-graph adapter where integration is straightforward and useful. Do not copy or reimplement admission, dispatch, request permits, capacity, advice selection, leases, continuation or closure policy in the simulator.
- Use one deterministic virtual event engine. Public operations initialize a run, advance one scheduled item or a bounded interval/event count, apply controls, expose current observations and export replay inputs. A bounded advancement call uses the same run and preserves its resumable state.
- Use integer simulated time and a documented deterministic total order for equal-time scheduled items. Choose a simple consistent tie rule, record it as part of the simulation contract, and test relevant same-time boundary cases. Workload generation, preparation, synthetic Jev responses, repair delays, task pauses and supported product time facts all follow that clock.
- Playback speed belongs to the driver. A faster driver requests more virtual advancement; it does not change seeded sampling, event ordering, deadlines or product outcomes. Headless execution, stepping and accelerated playback produce identical observations for the same replay inputs.
- Keep generated task arrival, simulation pause, suspension of future edit generation, agent finish attempts and Hapsland finish allowance distinct. A task arrival does not itself open a Hapsland round; existing admission and fresh-edit behavior determine that boundary.
- Represent the simulated agent with stable identity and configurable workload behavior. Provide an ordinary session preset with seeded pace variation, working/idle periods, concurrent review, middle-work collection and finish attempts. Defaults are illustrative and configurable, not claimed to be empirically calibrated Codex usage.
- Support ignoring advice, no action, prompt repair and delayed repair as selectable scenario behaviors. A simple deterministic configuration or seeded selection is sufficient. Lack of repair is not a simulator failure or a Hapsland delivery failure. An attempted repair is a changed synthetic revision; its next Jev outcome is a separate supplied fact.
- Implement a command-following synthetic environment. Use identities issued by Bend for subsequent facts. Preserve admission, lifetime, round, operation, request and output-token bindings. Distinguish issued commands, synthetic effect starts, supplied results, advice readiness, output submission and agent response.
- Honor existing preparation dispatch and Jev request behavior. Read applicable limits from checked output/configuration. Synthetic delays can keep permits occupied; a refused ready request does not become an invented Hapsland queue entry. This issue does not introduce future backpressure policy.
- Initial live controls cover edit pace, a finite edit burst, Jev delay/failure profiles and supported file/workload sizes. Validate controls, record their effective simulated time and ordering, and apply them at a deterministic step boundary. Changing a future-arrival profile must not leave duplicate obsolete arrivals scheduled.
- Choose the simplest deterministic latency-change convention: new synthetic requests use the current delay profile, while already scheduled completions keep their due time. Document the convention; elaborate in-flight rescheduling controls are unnecessary for the first version.
- Keep source bytes, evidence-tree bytes, review-unit/reservation bytes and encoded output bytes distinct. A size control must identify which existing boundary it exercises. Source and traversal claims require executing the existing graph model or an applicable existing checked boundary; simulated reservation facts alone cannot establish native capture-size enforcement.
- Apply the user's scope rule: reuse existing capabilities and add only small simulation-supporting features. For anything that requires substantial new product behavior, uncontrolled native effects or a major refactor, record the gap instead. Every gap names the missing capability, current demonstrated coverage and a revisit condition. Advertise only supported controls and scenarios.
- Replay inputs include the seed and random algorithm identity, initial scenario/configuration, stable synthetic inputs, consumed logic identity, simulation/replay format identity, recorded control timeline and explicit injected outcomes. Reconstruct from initial inputs; do not deserialize opaque Bend state directly or silently accept incompatible logic as an exact replay.
- Use stable identity domains for the initial agent and synthetic jobs. Keep randomness independent of rendering. Any later agent extension must be able to partition identities and random streams without changing the first agent's workload merely by adding another agent.
- Emit checked canonical event, ordered commands, before/after projections and rejection information, with separate simulated-time and synthetic-effect metadata. This is sufficient for the existing flow projection to map observations to stages; the dashboard retains all square and route presentation. Graph observations stay identifiable as a separate checked model when supported.
- Stream observations to consumers rather than requiring unbounded in-memory history. Replay input export must remain available; observation retention and any optional trace limits must be explicit and must never alter simulated outcomes. A consumer can choose how much rendered history to retain.
- Minimal run validation primarily protects the new engine and environment. Reuse adapter state checks. Report unhandled required effects, mismatched completion identities, invalid virtual scheduling or divergence from independent scenario expectations explicitly; preserve ordinary Bend refusals as valid observed outcomes.
- Keep the published issue as the specification owner and remove the superseded local interview draft. Maintain the glossary and package documentation with implementation; research remains advisory evidence and follows its declared consolidation/deletion lifecycle.

## Testing Decisions

- Use one primary acceptance seam: the public monkey-business run API exercising the existing checked compiled Bend adapters. Prefer complete source-free simulated scenarios and their externally observable events, commands, projections, effect observations and run status over private queue, helper or reducer internals.
- Reuse the repository's independently authored canonical and Jev-request conformance traces as prior art and initial expected scenarios. Reuse existing checked graph traces for any graph coverage. Existing Bend laws/proofs, artifact verification and adapter validation remain separate checks with their current scope.
- Establish expected results independently from the accepted product contract and curated fixtures. Do not calculate the expected Stop or capacity decision by duplicating Bend policy in test code, and do not use the simulator's own output as its sole oracle.
- Verify determinism through repeat runs, one-step versus batched advancement, pause/resume and varied playback pacing, with identical seeds and controls applied at identical simulated boundaries. Compare ordered events, commands, virtual timestamps, checked projections and relevant synthetic observations.
- Verify replay export and reconstruction after mid-run control changes. Reject incompatible consumed-logic/replay identities clearly. Include a delay-profile change where an existing request retains its scheduled completion and a later request uses the changed profile.
- Exercise a small connected normal-session scenario: fresh edits, overlapping preparation/review, advice during work, an agent finish attempt, continuation or allowance as commanded, and later fresh work. Verify all valid advice-response behaviors, including ignored advice and delayed attempted repair, without treating a synthetic repair as semantic proof of success.
- Exercise current saturation and accounting behavior with an independent scenario: keep the checked Jev request pool occupied, offer further ready work, observe immediate unavailability, settle a request and offer later work. Assert through public observations that no refused request started a synthetic effect.
- Exercise Stop with more than one unfinished work item, completion/deadline ordering, exact cancellation targets, and an intentionally late callback retaining its original identity. Verify existing Bend rejection/fencing and the subsequent same-round fresh repair path where continuation remains active.
- Exercise supported size boundaries and partial fan-out admission using distinct byte facts. If graph replay is included, cover a source/tree boundary, denied path without a read, and an incomplete/deadline outcome. Mark broader graph/native measurement coverage as deferred when unsupported.
- Add a focused negative harness scenario proving that a mismatched completion or unhandled required command is reported. These assertions check command/environment compliance, not a second implementation of product policy.
- Verify bounded advancement stops with an explicit reason and resumable state, without emitting an agent Stop or closing a round. For a declared recovery/drain scenario, stop arrivals and require the scenario's transient work to settle under its stated finite-effect/deadline assumptions. Do not require all cached/advice/round records to disappear.
- Verify a headless package consumer can initialize and execute a run without UI dependencies. Feed representative frames to the existing flow projection to establish future diagram compatibility. Dashboard browser wiring and visual acceptance remain follow-up work.
- Keep ordinary tests deterministic, offline and source-free. No credentials or live Jev responses are needed. Simulation checks establish behavior under the supported synthetic model, while native host enforcement, real source measurement and empirical performance retain separate validation scopes.

## Out of Scope

- A game, new square system, diagram layout, animations or complete dashboard control/playback UI.
- A separate simulated-user participant. User-origin task triggers can be workload events.
- Multiple simulated agents, cross-agent fairness or a claim that one agent covers production global-capacity contention.
- New Hapsland business rules, a Jev waiting queue, changed product capacity policy, new repair semantics or expanded runtime/platform support.
- Full deterministic execution of the native resident process, filesystem, sockets, credential services and real agent-runtime hooks.
- Real agent models, real Jev calls, semantic repair-quality validation or proof that submitted advice was seen by a real model.
- Exhaustive coverage of every reducer branch, replacing Bend proofs, or inferring real throughput/latency from synthetic virtual-time runs.
- Elaborate live rescheduling of in-flight Jev requests, full synthetic Jev infrastructure/service queues, checkpoint hydration, sophisticated trace compression or a dependency-heavy simulation framework.
- Independent npm publication or a substantial packaging/refactor project solely to make the first simulator possible. Begin with a separate repository package consuming the existing shared checked seam.
- Large new features required to simulate currently unsupported cases; record them with explicit coverage and revisit conditions instead.

## Further Notes

The inspected starting point is `integration/issues-145-148` at commit `2a7a7413d806ea4d0e6a68147a4fce45363d6ae0`. Implementation should use the current integration state and preserve its authority and pre-release compatibility guidance.

The UI already has a separate semantic flow projection and a presentation mapping from those stages to squares. This issue supplies generated ongoing activity and simulated effects for that existing contract. It changes no diagram, so it does not create a new visual diff or request owner visual acceptance.

Existing baseline evidence passed 57 independent canonical traces and 8 Jev-request traces. A separate headless witness repeated 15 selected cases, 140 steps per pass, through the checked adapter and flow projection with identical frames. These are existing-boundary results, not evidence that monkey-business has been implemented or accepted.

Many current canonical Bend proofs concern concrete expressions and cases; the separate graph model has general budget/finite-event theorems with external-response assumptions. Additional simulator run checks protect the engine's command interpretation, virtual scheduling and reproducibility; they must not be advertised as newly proving all product logic.

Related work: #116 owns authoritative Bend decisions; #147 owns the production diagram; #148 owns explicit Jev request commands/results; #138 owns production supporting evidence; #139 concerns future backpressure. monkey-business exercises their existing supported contracts and documents boundaries rather than implementing those product changes.

title: monkey-business: run and replay a deterministic review cycle
body:
**Purpose:** Specify this monkey-business implementation slice.
**Status:** Ready for implementation when its listed blockers are complete.
**Authority:** Implementation requirements under #152 and the user-approved dashboard addition. Existing Hapsland contracts retain authority over product decisions.
**Expected use:** Implement and verify the behavior and acceptance criteria below.
**Lifecycle:** Maintain scope through implementation; record completion evidence and move ongoing API and usage guidance into maintained package documentation. Review when the supported simulation boundary changes.

## Parent

https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/152

## What to build

Create a separate UI-independent monkey-business package. A developer can initialize a scripted run, advance it, inspect its observations, and reproduce it from exported inputs. One synthetic edit that contains no private source proceeds through preparation, a synthetic Jev response, advice submission and an agent finish attempt using the existing checked compiled Bend adapters.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The public run API executes a complete scripted review cycle through the checked production adapters. Product decisions remain in Bend; the synthetic environment follows issued commands and identities.
- [ ] One integer virtual clock and a documented total order for equal-time events govern modeled effects and deadlines. Wall-clock playback concerns remain outside the deterministic core.
- [ ] The same ongoing run supports single-step and bounded time/event advancement. Reaching a driver limit returns an explicit reason and resumable state without emitting an agent finish attempt or closing a Hapsland round.
- [ ] Replay export records the seed, random algorithm identity, initial configuration, synthetic inputs and injected outcomes, the identity of the Bend logic used and the replay format. Replay reconstructs the run from initial inputs and rejects incompatible identities clearly.
- [ ] The public API accepts validated controls at deterministic step boundaries and records their effective virtual time and ordering through one shared control timeline. Replay exports and applies that timeline; later tickets add specific workload, Jev and size controls through this mechanism.
- [ ] Consumers receive ordered events, commands, checked canonical before/after frames with the projections required by the existing semantic flow projection, rejection information and separate virtual-time and synthetic-effect observations. Streaming does not require retaining an unbounded observation history; retention and replay-input availability are documented.
- [ ] Independent expected scenarios verify the review cycle, repeated runs and single-step versus batched advancement. Existing adapter checks are reused. Negative scenarios report mismatched completion identities and unhandled required commands; ordinary Bend refusals remain valid outcomes.
- [ ] A headless consumer can run without UI dependencies, credentials, private source or live Jev access. Maintained package guidance explains the API, coverage boundary and how to run the example.
- [ ] Consolidate still-useful research decisions and executable witnesses into maintained package documentation and tests at the first deterministic replay implementation milestone, update inbound links, and delete temporary research artifacts when their declared cleanup trigger is met.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

title: Define inactivity closure for abandoned Hapsland virtual rounds
body:
**Purpose:** Define and implement bounded closure of a Hapsland virtual round when Stop never arrives.
**Status:** Accepted and implemented on 2026-09-30.
**Authority:** The accepted product rule is in `docs/advicing-target-contract.md`; this issue records implementation and validation evidence.
**Expected use:** Trace the decision, code, and checks for closure of a fully quiescent virtual round.
**Lifecycle:** Close after implementation and deterministic validation; revise the accepted contract if the owner changes the rule.

## Accepted behavior

- The first accepted attributed edit opens a virtual round. A pending pre-edit permit alone does not open it.
- An open round without Stop closes after **five minutes of continuous full quiescence** by default. The duration is user configurable and captured when the round opens.
- Quiescence requires no unfinished review work, pending advice, pending edit permit, active delivery, or Stop hold. A new permit or accepted edit breaks the quiet interval. Work still running at Jev and undelivered pending advice postpone closure; pending advice follows normal relevance expiry.
- Stop uses its own bounded hold. A Stop in progress interrupts the quiet interval. If Stop continues the agent, a new quiet interval can begin when the round is again fully quiet. If Stop allows finish, normal closure wins.
- A separate periodic check runs independently of IPC connections and resident process retirement. Bend stores the quiet start, checks source-free facts, compares monotonic time with the configured duration, and decides expiry. TypeScript reads the clock, observes native effects, schedules the check, and performs fenced cleanup.
- A late Stop or stale edit cannot reopen a closed round. A provably fresh edit can begin another virtual round, even during the same agent-runtime turn. The source-free closure marker records `quiescent`.
- Checks are periodic, so actual closure may occur after the nominal duration. No live agent-runtime timing claim is made here.

This accepted rule supersedes the earlier proposal to start an edit-based inactivity countdown while review work or advice remained pending. The 20-second resident process-idle check is separate from the five-minute virtual-round duration.

## Implementation and evidence

Commit: dearlordylord/hapsland@530af68.

- `packages/agent-flow-bend/Quiescence.bend` and `Canonical.bend`: quiescence decision, quiet-state tracking, admission and Stop resets, and closure fence.
- `src/resident/composed-delivery.ts` and `server.ts`: captured duration, periodic check, native facts, and cleanup.
- `src/configuration/types.ts` and generated schema/guide: user setting `virtualRoundQuietMs`.
- `docs/advicing-target-contract.md`, `CONTEXT.md`, and `docs/typescript-decision-boundary-ledger.md`: accepted behavior and TypeScript/Bend boundary.
- Deterministic tests cover threshold equality, multiple edits, permit expiry between checks, Stop hold and continuation, pending activity, two advicees, the 64-round slot, stale edit rejection, a new round, and source-free closure evidence.
- Validation: root `npm test` (762 passed, 2 skipped), root `npm run build`, root `npm run typecheck`, Bend package `npm test`, and focused quiescence tests (46 passed).

The checks establish reducer and resident behavior in controlled tests. Live agent-runtime timing and delivery visibility were not tested as part of this task.

title: Add deterministic monkey-business sessions, replay and dashboard controls
body:
Developers can now run an ongoing, reproducible synthetic coding session through Hapsland's checked Bend adapters and inspect it in the existing dashboard. Previously, the dashboard offered finite examples and manually supplied events.

Closes #153
Closes #154
Closes #155
Closes #156
Closes #157

## Implementation

- Add the UI-independent `@hapsland/monkey-business` package with an integer virtual clock, stepping and bounded advancement, streamed checked frames, bounded observation retention, replay compatibility checks and exact endpoint restoration.
- Generate seeded single-agent sessions with four advice responses and checked finish waiting, deadlines, continuation and allowance. Record pace, burst, arrival suspension, synthetic Jev profile and supported size controls in replay order.
- Exercise request saturation, exact cancellation, original late callbacks, partial review-unit admission and the separate checked import-graph size boundaries.
- Add dashboard start/reset, pause/resume, step, explicit applied playback speed, workload/profile/size controls and named scenarios. Numeric drafts preserve playback through blank or malformed edits; valid Apply changes active settings at the run endpoint.
- Use one square renderer for live and guided diagrams. Every checked state facet shows its exact count, including zero and singular labels; ID samples are bounded, and all categories remain visible in fixed-size squares.
- Share the static Review capacity chart with the simulation, including per-agent totals and history-aware checked occupancy. Clicking the selected square deselects it; bounded details and control history below the diagram prevent event-driven layout shifts.
- Distinguish pending advice from retained submitted advice; add durable outcome totals, focused stage/record lifecycle inspection, paused history selection, bookmarks, replay from start and replay file download/import.
- Mirror resident round-close advice removal and finite checked advice expiry; drive preparation and review work through checked dispatch cohorts.
- Add synthetic current-work/source-readability and credential availability/generation facts, checked final handoff validation, certain/uncertain/preauthorization-failed output profiles and lease expiry. Uncertain background output can reoffer once at Stop with its original advice identity, without another Jev call. Failed/unavailable review recovery uses fresh admission rather than automatic resends.
- Supply valid request lifecycle facts for synthetic never-sent and interrupted outcomes, preventing occupied request slots from blocking later findings. Add 12 bounded liveness/replay checks: all four failures, three seeds and two recovery cycles; retained advice, ready collection and submission must recover within 2,000 virtual ms under stated healthy-environment assumptions.
- Add six outcome-weight sliders with shared normalization and immediate updates, default finding/clear 50/50, deterministic one-outcome presets and a dedicated seeded outcome stream recorded in replay.

- Add approved conditional progress contracts and eight general Bend laws: finite request settlement in arbitrary responsive completion order, exact permit release, runnable advice handoff and recovery without reset. The proof drivers compose production dispatch and handoff functions; host responsiveness, fair scheduling and actual agent receipt remain outside the proof. Refactor dispatch tail recursion without changing its results so the independent kernel accepts the imported core.

## Review the new panel

The visual change is the new **Monkey-business · seeded simulation** panel; `master` has no simulation panel. The existing diagram's squares and routes retain their presentation mapping.

Run `npm run dev --prefix packages/agent-flow-viz` and open `http://127.0.0.1:5173/#monkey-business`. Follow the exact [seeded simulation walkthrough](packages/agent-flow-viz/README.md#seeded-simulation-walkthrough): seed `7`, edit interval `100`, reservation bytes `100`, Jev delay `50`; click **Start / reset**, then **Single step**. Inspect the checked transition on the existing diagram and its event/command/effect details, then try the burst, slow/failing Jev, recovery and replay cases.

Requested design decision: accept the added controls, state labels and inspection/history behavior for this supported synthetic scope. Acceptance permits merging this dashboard consumer; it does not establish native host enforcement, empirical Jev timing or release/platform support. This concrete panel/case review request follows [AGENTS.md's visual review guidance](AGENTS.md#review-requests-and-acceptance-decisions).

For the shared state-count change, inspect **Agent edit** in the live diagram after injecting a burst of 50: its **source queued** row must show the exact checked total, rather than just clipped IDs. Compare empty, one-item and 100-item presentation cases in the shared renderer; counts and category names must remain visible. **Source preparation**, **Advice ready / retained** and **Host output** must show all their state categories without resizing squares. Full identities remain in tooltips/inspection. Previously the two-line cutoff hid entire categories. Astra completed three bounded passes and measured 348 rendered rows with no overflow.

For the capacity/selection follow-up, inspect the simulation’s own **Review capacity** bar against the displayed checked event, including history navigation. Click a square twice to open and close its inspector, then Resume and inject a burst: the diagram must remain at the same vertical position. Previously selection moved it by 356 pixels and updates repeatedly shifted it; Astra checked the fix at 1440px and 900px widths.

For the follow-up control change, inspect the **Playback speed** field while running: clear it with Backspace, type `.` or `1..5`, and press Enter. Playback and the active speed must remain unchanged, with validation shown. Then type `0.5` and press Enter; active speed must change without Resume. Previously, clearing the field paused playback. For lifecycle inspection, use **Slow Jev**, click **Awaiting Jev result**, and select a request; inspect its related transitions. After a normal task drains, **Advice ready / retained** must distinguish retained submissions from undelivered backlog, and round closure must remove them.

For the new outcome mix, inspect the six outcome sliders: the default finding/clear mix is 50/50. Change finding to 25 while clear remains 50; probabilities and the active mix must immediately become 33.3%/66.7%. Set every weight to zero during playback: validation must persist, with playback and the last valid mix unchanged. Editing delay must work independently of an invalid mix draft, and vice versa. Export/load must restore the recorded mix. Existing requests retain their captured profile.

For keyboard and attention changes, press Enter while editing pace, burst, size, environment or output fields: only that form must submit, exactly once. Enter in replay JSON must insert a newline. Guided replay controls now precede the diagram; stepping must keep its position fixed. Scenario, decision, finish, capacity-transition and replay details start collapsed, and repeated technical paragraphs have been removed.

For delivery recovery, use the uncertain-output scenario, then Apply a certain-write profile without resetting. Confirm new host submissions while earlier uncertainty counts remain visible. Use temporary credential unavailability versus a generation change to inspect retained eligibility versus stale-advice retirement. These were previously unsupported synthetic cases.

## Validation

Validated after merging `origin/master` at `530af68` and updating replay's compiled Bend identity:

- `npm test`: 82 test files and 825 tests passed; 1 file and 2 tests skipped.
- 75 simulator tests passed through the public API, including lifecycle recovery, delayed callback fencing, once-only uncertain reoffer, normalized outcome sampling, live controls and exact replay.
- Root and simulator typechecks, root build and dashboard build passed.
- Existing dashboard and focused simulation Chromium suites passed, including checked bursts of 1/50/100, live 50-item queue display and 348 SVG text-width checks across empty/single/100-item shared square presentations. This environment used extracted local Chromium libraries via `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.
- Standards and Spec reviews completed within the three-pass cap for the recovery task; material findings were fixed. String-based UI actions and duplicated classification/accessor logic remain non-blocking heuristics.
- Failure-recovery follow-up: 75 simulator tests and simulator typecheck passed; the committed snapshot passed dashboard build and the focused Chromium suite. Full-suite rerun: 836 tests passed, 2 skipped and one Claude CLI batching timing case failed; that case passed on an isolated sequential recheck of the committed snapshot.
- Final dashboard build and both Chromium suites cover immediate Jev updates, independent invalid drafts, Enter submission, replay multiline editing and guided manual submission.
- Astra medium’s final whole-page attention review found no material remaining findings; guided diagram position stayed fixed across eight steps.
- Astra medium checked human-style editing during playback, stable square selection, uncertain-output recovery and weighted sliders, including keyboard operation, all-zero validation and replay restoration.

- Conditional progress: all eight proofs pass the Bend kernel verdict; 502 literal instances and ten compiling false mutations pass the falsification gate. Mutation reports distinguish own-law rejection from shared-lemma rejection.
- The old and refactored dispatch helpers agree on 4,572 small states. The isolated committed snapshot passes canonical conformance (60 traces, 676 round-uniqueness transitions, eight request traces), generated-artifact/authority checks and all 75 simulator tests after rebuilding and updating the replay fingerprint.

## Coverage limits

Runs are deterministic, offline and source-free. They do not establish native filesystem measurement/capture, live Jev behavior, semantic repair quality or multiple-agent contention. Graph frames remain a separate checked model. Generated output does not model actual encoded serialization size; explicit byte facts exercise the checked collection-fit boundary. Browser replay reconstruction is bounded to 100,000 events, and intermediate replay branching is outside this scope. Maintained package guidance records these limits and revisit conditions.

Root/configuration validity and physical native transport availability remain assumed. Remaining omissions include pre-edit permits, native revision supersession, tickets/notices/reuse/background waiters, quiet-round/inactivity expiry, native capture/transport and shutdown. Direct canonical fixtures can exercise additional checked boundaries; they do not establish complete resident orchestration. See the [maintained simulator coverage guide](packages/monkey-business/README.md).

title: Design process-wide freshness and a bounded Jev saturation queue
body:
## Current status — 2026-10-04

Incomplete future policy decision. #148 is implemented and retains immediate request-saturation refusal; no Jev wait queue has been adopted. This issue owns the possible bounded Jev waiter queue and the owner-expanded process-wide freshness lifecycle. #139 owns general resident-capacity backpressure. Existing pending-advice expiry and output retention remain the baseline, not an absence of all freshness checks. Decide the queue/lifecycle policy and coordinate output grouping before changing production behavior.

## Task scope and prior planning

## Purpose

Introduce a finite waiting queue specifically for review work that is ready to call Jev when all eight Jev request permits are occupied. This is future work; keep the current immediate `unavailable` behavior until the queue policy and implementation are accepted.

This queue is distinct from preparation-job scheduling, resident item/byte capacity admission, and the pending-advice store. The current Jev request contract is #148. General resident-capacity backpressure is #139; coordinate with it without treating a free Jev permit as free resident capacity.

## Decide before implementation

- Define when ready work enters the queue, how long it remains eligible, and the exact terminal outcome when its finite wait expires. Choose a validated user setting with a finite default and ceiling; capture the effective deadline when the work starts waiting.
- Define finite item and byte bounds for waiting work and source-bearing native state, plus explicit behavior when the queue is full. Keep all Hapsland policy decisions in Bend and native source/credentials outside its retained state.
- Define FIFO/order and fairness across advicee partitions, including whether newly ready work may bypass waiting work.
- Before issuing a permit after waiting, recheck original advicee/virtual round, current source and rule input, file eligibility, credential and consent, and the review work identity. Superseded or closed-round work must leave the queue without a Jev call.
- Specify cancellation, Stop deadline, virtual-round closure, resident shutdown/restart, and late callback behavior. No duplicate Jev evaluation or source-bearing persistence.
- Decide how waiting, expiry, queue-full, and actual Jev in-flight occupancy appear as source-free status and in the dashboard.

## Acceptance criteria for a later implementation

- At most eight actual Jev requests are active at once; a ninth eligible request can wait only within the accepted finite queue limits and deadline.
- Releasing a permit admits the next still-current eligible work according to the chosen ordering. Expired, superseded, cancelled, or closed-round work never calls Jev.
- Queue-full and expired outcomes are explicit and distinct from a clear review. Resident memory remains bounded by count and bytes.
- Offline deterministic tests cover permit saturation/release, fairness, exact expiry boundary, source or consent change while waiting, Stop/round closure, interruption, restart, and no duplicate call. The dashboard reflects the checked reducer state.
- Update the accepted review contract, glossary, and #139 coordination only when the policy is decided. Preserve historical #148 evidence as evidence of the previous immediate-unavailable contract.

## Related work

- #148: current eight-permit Jev pool and immediate saturation outcome.
- #139: broader capacity-unavailable backpressure; Jev saturation needs its own policy.
- Preparation dispatch now fills available slots directly. Jev waiting and process-wide freshness remain separate future decisions.


## Owner expansion: process-wide freshness lifecycle

Freshness/expiry must be accounted for across the entire resident process, not only the future Jev-saturation queue. Waiting preparation/review work, a future Jev waiter, completed pending advice, and advice retained because it did not fit an earlier response can all become too old to use. Define one resident-wide source-free lifecycle/sweep authority that can retire stale records at each stage, while allowing different validated age/deadline policies where the stages need them. Do not infer that all stages must share one duration.

Reconcile the existing pending-advice relevance expiry and output-overflow retention with this lifecycle. In particular, an item that remains for a later answer because of the 10 KiB response limit must not become immortal; revalidate its source and age before any later handoff. Specify what the resident removes, what diagnostic outcome is recorded, and how each removal releases all capacity and native handles. A resident that runs for the lifetime of the computer must retain a finite item/byte ceiling with no growth from expired work or advice.

Keep the current 10 KiB response-fit behavior until the separate product decision about whether findings from one edit may be split by output size. This issue should explicitly coordinate with that decision; it must not silently resolve it. The current immediate Jev-saturation outcome and existing advice expiry remain in force until this expanded design is implemented.

title: Add Rust type review with bounded Cargo module resolution
body:
Source-language rules now stay behind cohesive static adapters for TypeScript and Rust; stacked #168 adds Bend through the same contract. The shared analyzer and graph host consume normalized declaration/reference/location facts and adapter-owned graph sessions; Cargo context, namespace rebasing, grammar choice, and import candidate conventions stay inside language modules. TypeScript type/function extraction shares parser setup. Doctor probes come from adapter metadata. Superseded extractor/context paths were removed, and a structural architecture regression check guards the boundary.

A property test exposed unstable Tree-sitter wrapper identity producing a spurious declaration-name reference. Syntax comparisons now use node kind and source spans; the alias regression covers 1,000 generated cases and the reproduced counterexample.

Rust edits now produce type-shape reviews with bounded local cross-file context. Cargo metadata and explicit `mod` declarations establish crate/module roles; `use` aliases and supported qualified paths bind references to captured supporting declarations. Transitive traversal preserves reference-site spelling, terminates cycles, shares captures, and applies the existing rule evidence, privacy, graph-budget, and freshness gates.

The initial profile reviews top-level structs, enums, and type aliases. It requires an eligible Cargo manifest with a literal 2018/2021/2024 edition and supported library/binary targets. External crates, re-exports/globs, inline modules, macros/attributes, functions, trait-dependent types, and unsupported Cargo target layouts remain incomplete evidence. The [user-facing language table](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/feat/rust-support/README.md#supported-languages) and accepted review contract describe the limits. No compiler runs or dependency fetches occur during review; formats stay at version 1.

Validation:

- Final offline suite: 921 tests passed, two live tests skipped. Typecheck, build, native verification, and pinned clean tarball audit passed (127 files, nine native artifacts).
- Linux arm64 and [macOS arm64 package/setup conformance](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/actions/runs/36821309415) passed, including actual installed Cargo authority, cross-file preparation, rendering, source fingerprints, and currentness. macOS checked runtime checkpoint `8345cc3`; subsequent changes record validation only.
- Split-file live Jev validation through production preparation and Effect: bad models 0.87/0.84, good models 0.06/0.06 at a 0.7 threshold. Both Rust fixtures compiled; changing the supporting source invalidated preparation and restoring it made it current again. These four observations come from an eight-request combined stacked-branch experiment.
- The first full run had one existing TypeScript Claude hook child exit without a status. Isolation and the fresh full run passed; the termination cause is unestablished. No workaround or production change was made for it.
- Independent agent review checked module authority, Cargo target precedence, namespace/shadowing, budgets, forbidden reads, freshness, docs, and sanitized evidence. This is not a formal GitHub approval by another account.

[Reusable language-addition findings](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/feat/rust-support/docs/adding-language-support.md) explain the repeatable extraction/binding/traversal approach. [Rust evidence](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/tree/feat/rust-support/evidence/rust-support) retains the cross-file results and previous same-file/native demonstrations. The prior Codex acknowledgement/repair run predates this amendment. Live observations establish these synthetic cases, not general review accuracy or reliable native-agent response to cross-file advice.

The whole-repository architecture re-review covers TS as well as Rust/Bend: Standards 0 findings; Spec 0 findings. title: Deferred: consider TigerBeetle-inspired deterministic simulation improvements
body:
## Disposition

Deferred by the owner on 2026-10-01. This is an optional backlog idea, not a commitment or prerequisite for architecture documentation, README, website, social materials, or release videos. It may never be pursued. Do not begin implementation without an explicit decision to resume it.

## Context

Hapsland already uses source-free deterministic simulation of compiled Canonical and ImportGraph decision cores in `packages/monkey-business`: virtual time, independent seeded streams, exact replay, injected failures and bounded recovery checks. This is not simulation of the complete resident, filesystem capture, IPC, or real Jev transport.

TigerBeetle VOPR and TigerStyle suggest strengthening the existing seam, rather than adopting their database or simulator as a dependency:
- https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle/blob/main/docs/internals/vopr.md
- https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle/blob/main/docs/TIGER_STYLE.md

## Candidate follow-ups if resumed

1. Shared canonical frame invariant checks across scenarios, complementing existing graph per-frame checks.
2. Bounded randomized sequences of supported controls, with seed, event and control budgets and exact replay comparison.
3. Automatic source-free failing replay witnesses; sequence minimization is optional later work.
4. Explicit replay input/control budgets, refusing excess before mutation and preserving the last valid replay. Observation history is already bounded; recorded explicit inputs and controls can grow.

## Decision and acceptance if resumed

First compare against existing tests and choose one uncovered boundary. Exercise production decision code, avoid a parallel policy implementation, and retain a reproducible failure witness. Prove the test oracle detects an intentional violation. For replay limits, verify exact-limit and limit+1 behavior and intact replay after refusal. Keep ordinary tests offline and bounded. Do not turn logical resource charges into an RSS guarantee or promote synthetic facts to native enforcement evidence.

This task does not authorize a full resident simulator, process-memory audit, production changes, or new public assurance claims. Record a separate scope decision before expanding it.

title: Investigate removing retained Claude edit tickets while preserving collection authority
body:
Claude edit collection currently uses a retained ticket registry and a second set of ticket-unit states. Investigate whether those entities can be removed while preserving the authority of each response attempt.

This is a follow-up investigation, not authorization to remove checks or change hook behavior.

## Context and findings

- A runtime may report zero or many edits before a finish attempt. Every hook invocation is a new process; the resident retains work across invocations. Continuation can produce more edits and another Stop.
- The current Claude synchronous post-edit handler admits an edit, receives an opaque ticket, and polls collection. Background and Stop collect by advicee/root scope without inheriting those tickets.
- Edit B's response may include still-current findings from edit A in the same advicee/round. A ticket is not a container for one edit's result.
- Current responses are pending/empty/advice/unavailable. Historical ticket-wide clear/delivered outcomes must not justify retaining a duplicate outcome registry.
- Collection needs frozen authority for its particular invocation: accepted scope/tool binding, original resident lifetime, admission-time feedback opt-in, collector credentials, configuration reference, and authority deadline. Some facts already exist on admission/work/advice; admission-time collector feedback opt-in and collector expiry have no complete replacement there. Selected advice may originate from another admission, so its credential context cannot replace the collector's context.
- Ticket-unit state currently participates in supersession, joined-result callback guards, and delivery bookkeeping. These invariants must move to common work/member/delivery state before deletion.

## Candidate and alternatives

Evaluate one bounded admission-and-collection RPC, with frozen authority held in the active request context. It would issue no ticket nonce and retain no separately collectible ticket or duplicate ticket-unit outcomes. Hook timeout/disconnect must end the response context without cancelling independently owned resident review work.

A short-lived opaque lookup handle is a reduction, not full elimination of the registry. Looking up snapshots by existing tool/admission IDs merely recreates retention under another key. A signed client-held authority introduces a new integrity/restart-key boundary and currently lacks a demonstrated advantage.

This candidate is source-inspected feasibility, not implemented or runtime-validated elimination.

## Required checks before an implementation decision

- Multiple edits: B can collect A's eligible advice; no cross-advicee/root delivery.
- Concurrent invocations retain independent authority and exclusive delivery leases.
- Advisory admission cannot be elevated by later opt-in; revocation prevents an already authorized blocking response.
- Credential rotation/suspension, wrong tool/root/advicee, restart, and expired authority remain conservative.
- Source freshness, supersession, reuse joins, and late/duplicate callbacks retain their existing fences.
- Hook timeout/disconnect leaves resident work running; temporary authority and provisional delivery clean up completely.
- Preserve bounded IPC and final-handoff checks; keep the current version-one contract and remove superseded production paths if a replacement is accepted.
- Verify registry-free behavior directly; existing ticket tests establish current invariants only.

The owner's intended ordinary Claude behavior is to continue after an edit and receive advice soon afterward, as with Codex. Host delivery capability and any amendment to the currently accepted synchronous-feedback behavior are separate questions. First settle ticket necessity even with current behavior preserved.

## Sources

- [Accepted advice and delivery contract](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/55df50b/docs/advicing-target-contract.md): agent-facing sequence and collection batching/authority.
- [Resident implementation](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/55df50b/src/resident/server.ts): TicketRecord, admission, collection gates, final authority, ticket-unit callbacks and retirement.
- [Hook/client implementation](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/55df50b/src/resident/client.ts) and [IPC contract](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/55df50b/src/resident/protocol.ts).
- [Direct-edit blocking authority](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/55df50b/docs/adr/0003-claude-direct-edit-blocking-authority.md): explicit user authority, not a requirement for a retained ticket registry.

Follow-up from the feat/multi-agent-3d workbook's ticket-necessity audit (local commit 92cf283); no ticket or hook refactor has been implemented.

title: Remove retained Claude edit tickets while preserving response authority
body:
Claude edit hooks now use one bounded `admit-and-collect` RPC instead of admitting a retained ticket and polling a second operation. Each active request retains its own response authority; common work, revision, reuse-member and delivery state supply settlement and readiness.

Closes #170.

The RPC freezes root/advicee/tool binding, resident lifetime, original round, credentials, configuration reference, admission-time opt-in and authority expiry. Final handoff independently validates collector and selected-advice credentials, freshness, current opt-in, round authority, exclusive leases and encoded output size. Timeout/disconnect releases provisional delivery and discards response authority while independently owned resident review continues.

Claude delivery follows the owner's clarified decision: synchronous PostToolUse collection keeps its existing approximately 3.9-second bound; Stop and SubagentStop remain safety nets for late findings. The installer removes only Claude's asynchronous PostToolUse collector. Claude background invocations cannot collect or submit pending advice; retired Claude-background formatter/profile branches are deleted. Codex background delivery is unchanged. A finite hook deadline does not guarantee a result, and successful stdout submission does not prove model visibility.

Removed ticket retention, ticket/unit bookkeeping, TicketState.bend, ticket operations, and superseded fixtures/guard. Updated canonical artifacts, replay identity, maintained contracts and visualization projections. Version-one owned formats remain in place.

## Verification

Final serial `npm test` at `a32567b`: 1062 passed, 2 skipped across 100 files (99 passed, 1 skipped), exit 0. A preceding run had one Codex installation child exit with null status; its isolated rerun and this complete rerun passed. Test timeouts were not relaxed.

Typecheck and product build passed. Offline coverage includes invocation isolation and independent authority, B collecting A, exclusive leases, frozen opt-in/revocation, credential rotation/suspension, freshness, supersession/reuse/callback fences, expiry/restart/closed rounds, bounded output, disconnect during review and handoff, and registry-free response behavior. Claude fixtures verify quick synchronous delivery, quiet background invocation followed by six pending findings at Stop, unfinished-review Stop fallback, and installer update removing an owned async handler while preserving Stop/SubagentStop. Codex installation/background checks remain in the suite.

Bend normal proof checking and canonical conformance passed during the RPC implementation; the progress proofs pass the kernel verdict in npm test. The optional whole-package kernel verdict produced no result within its declared 15-second cap; no full-package kernel-verdict claim is made.

## Native evidence

The two original Claude Code 2.1.218 + real Jev observations are retained under evidence/issue-170: direct synchronous findings led to a repair; an injected delayed response emitted background findings without observed repair and Stop returned quietly. No delayed old-ticket baseline was run, so that gap was not established as an RPC regression. Original compiler-exit proxy limitations are explicitly amended in those records.

The new [declared sync/Stop run](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/task/issue-170/evidence/issue-170/claude-sync-stop-count-delayed-1790915731542-declaration.json) and [result](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/task/issue-170/evidence/issue-170/claude-sync-stop-count-delayed-1790915731542.json) use the updated Claude configuration, real Jev, and an injected five-second response-return delay. Both edit hooks returned quietly; Stop delivered findings, Claude subsequently made a native repair and named a delivered rule, and a final Stop returned quietly. There were two Jev requests, five across all three selected native runs. The final response did not affirm the APPLIED marker; reception/repair evidence is the conditional unprescribed edit after Stop plus naming a rule, not a protocol ACK. Follow-up review still found a finding, so no final-clean-review or general reaction-rate claim is made. Semantic compilation is recorded separately from the runner's reception/repair verdict.

Only source-free contract/timing evidence is retained, with pre-execution declarations and no credentials or raw host/backend responses. These observations do not establish installed-release support, macOS behavior or Claude Code 2.1.281 compatibility. Resident-local 50ms polling and the 32-connection limit remain; saturation with waiting native hooks was not measured. Historical checkpoint reports retain their separate #137 consolidation trigger.

## Standards

Original review findings (obsolete maintained documentation and a naming heuristic) were fixed and rechecked. The final Claude-only change's retired background formatter and impossible return-type findings were also fixed. Final incremental review: 0 remaining findings.

## Spec

The original #170 review found no violations. Final incremental review against the owner's Claude-only async removal, unchanged synchronous deadline and retained Stop safety net: 0 findings.

Review totals: Standards 0 remaining (all reported findings fixed); Spec 0. Neither axis has a remaining worst finding.
