title: Build an editable headless laboratory for architecture-teaching game balance
body:
## Current status — 2026-10-04

Incomplete optional-game laboratory; specification is ready, but implementation waits for the required shared Bend boundary/scenario/action capabilities from #176 and the continuous game consumer #199. Not all #176 slices are prerequisites: use the selected Coordinator/Packager/Parallelizer requirements to identify the necessary complete capabilities. The label change marks this dependency, not rejection or a new game-design decision.

## Task scope and prior planning

# Development-time architecture game balance laboratory

**Tracker owner:** [Laboratory issue #203](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/203).

**Purpose:** Specify a development-time laboratory for controlled experiments with editable architecture-teaching game mechanisms.
**Status:** Ready for implementation scheduling; the owner confirmed the headless shared-engine testing seam on 2026-10-02. Implementation waits for the required Bend Monkey Business capabilities. The owner selected Coordinator, Packager and Parallelizer as the provisional experimental set on 2026-10-02.
**Authority:** Owner-agreed laboratory scope and testing seam synthesized from the discussion, constrained by the accepted shared-simulator specification. Detailed implementation choices remain proposals within that scope. This issue does not change product policy, accept a final tower roster or establish educational effectiveness.
**Expected use:** Implement the smallest reusable experiment boundary and bounded comparison/search workflow, then use evidence to select or replace mechanisms.
**Lifecycle:** The published issue owns implementation scheduling. At completion of #203, **consolidate** enduring experiment/configuration contracts into the optional-game guide and testing matrix, transfer roster decisions to the game-design owner, update inbound links and **delete** this local specification snapshot and superseded handoff documents.

## Problem Statement

The owner wants to identify imbalance and make meaningful choices about architecture-teaching towers, their abilities, investment and workload difficulty. The existing tower roster is not final. Tuning all seven towers now risks preserving weak teaching mechanisms and spending effort balancing abilities that may be replaced.

The current prototype offers useful directed comparisons but hardcodes tower parameters and named purchase plans. Existing proof checks establish their explicitly stated properties, not strategic balance or human learning. The owner needs reproducible evidence about causal effects, contextual tradeoffs, ineffective investments and powerful combinations while retaining freedom to change the game.

## Solution

Provide a game-owned headless experiment laboratory over the shared public Monkey Business simulation boundary. Define a small enabled mechanism set, configurable parameters, source-free workload contexts, deterministic player actions/policies and finite execution limits. Run matched baseline/candidate experiments, record separate game and business observations, and reproduce outcomes using ordinary replay plus the game-owned experiment inputs.

Start with bounded explicit plan enumeration and controlled comparisons. Produce evidence for selecting, replacing or deleting mechanisms before precise numerical balancing. Do not build a new business simulator or automatically apply discovered changes to the playable game. A sophisticated parameter optimizer is a later decision after the foundation demonstrates useful experiments.

The optional game is a continuous-workload consumer under [#176](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/176) and [#199](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/199). Workload intensity profiles and finite evaluation windows replace authored waves in the laboratory's target architecture. Retain old wave scenarios only as clearly scoped reference evidence; do not recreate a wave scheduler.

## User Stories

1. As a game designer, I want to enable a small subset of mechanisms, so that I can investigate interactions without committing to the current roster.
2. As a game designer, I want to change costs and effect parameters within declared bounds, so that tuning does not require changing business policy.
3. As a game designer, I want to replace an ability while retaining the experiment boundary, so that evidence guides design rather than preserving old code.
4. As a game designer, I want to remove a mechanism and its obsolete action paths, so that rejected mechanics do not remain hidden compatibility obligations.
5. As a learner, I want each candidate mechanism linked to a concrete architecture lesson, so that I understand what its effect represents.
6. As a learner, I want a countercase where that mechanism cannot help, so that I do not mistake it for a universal solution.
7. As a designer, I want baseline and candidate runs with matched exogenous workload inputs, so that differences can be attributed to the intervention.
8. As a designer, I want comparable investment budgets and purchase timing, so that an expensive plan does not win an unfair comparison.
9. As a designer, I want explicit no-action and no-investment baselines, so that I can see the value of decisions.
10. As a designer, I want baseline, A, B and A+B comparisons, so that useful or excessive combinations become visible.
11. As a designer, I want several workload contexts, so that a context-specific niche is distinguishable from a universal winning plan.
12. As a designer, I want workload difficulty to vary independently of game presentation, so that changes have an identifiable cause.
13. As a designer, I want continuous workload evaluated over explicit finite windows, so that every automated experiment has a bounded endpoint.
14. As a designer, I want deterministic player plans with placement and upgrade actions where supported, so that a result identifies what the player actually did.
15. As a designer, I want a bounded enumeration of declared plans, so that I can search for dead investments and strong combinations without introducing RL.
16. As a designer, I want search scope and exhaustion reported, so that an unobserved exploit is not described as impossible.
17. As a designer, I want game health, investment and remaining budget separate from business progress and retention, so that one aggregate score does not hide a bad lesson.
18. As a learner, I want acceleration distinguished from acquiring a shared request permit, so that I understand the bottleneck.
19. As a learner, I want prevention distinguished from removal of observed advice, so that the game preserves the meaning of retention.
20. As a learner, I want output commitment distinguished from acknowledgment and retirement, so that faster output is not mistaken for permission to discard ownership.
21. As a maintainer, I want interventions translated through supported generic environment actions, so that game objects never enter the shared simulator.
22. As a maintainer, I want already issued facts preserved unless a supported targeted intervention changes them, so that parameter changes do not rewrite history.
23. As a designer, I want an explicit unsupported-intervention result, so that a tower is not simulated by patching Canonical when its action is unavailable.
24. As an engineer, I want the headless and interactive consumers to use the same game action mapping, so that the laboratory tests the actual mechanic.
25. As an engineer, I want replay and mechanism/configuration identity attached to results, so that changes can be traced and reproduced.
26. As an engineer, I want rendering, playback and observation retention excluded from experiment decisions, so that they cannot change the outcome.
27. As a designer, I want authored fixtures distinguished from randomized samples, so that percentages do not imply unsupported probability estimates.
28. As a designer, I want held-out contexts separated from tuning contexts, so that a patch can be tested beyond the examples used to choose it.
29. As a maintainer, I want game-absent application/dashboard builds preserved, so that the laboratory remains optional.
30. As a designer, I want parameter suggestions and roster findings to remain reviewable proposals, so that experiments do not silently redesign the game.
31. As an educator, I want proposed human prediction/explanation checks recorded separately, so that numerical results are not described as evidence of learning or enjoyment.

## Implementation Decisions

- The laboratory belongs to the optional game. Reuse the shared public create/step/bounded-advance/control/injection/observation/replay operations; Canonical and ImportGraph remain the production decision authorities.
- The primary experiment boundary accepts mechanism configuration, a source-free shared scenario, deterministic player schedule/policy, context identity and finite run/search budgets. It returns applicable actions and refusals, separate metrics, ordinary business replay plus the game configuration/actions needed to reproduce game observations, and explicit termination reasons.
- Reuse the game consumer's mechanic-to-environment mapping. Add only the game-owned experiment wrapper required for comparison; do not introduce another interpretation of product commands or effect scheduling.
- Complete this specification while Monkey Business is being rewritten in Bend. Begin laboratory implementation only after the new shared Bend consumer boundary and the scenario/action capabilities required by the selected mechanisms are available. Coordinate with the relevant complete slices of the shared-simulator and optional-game work; do not extend the old host into a fallback business engine. Unrelated deferred scenario families need not block the laboratory.
- Separate stable mechanism identity, display names, enabled catalogue, parameter settings and policy actions. Numeric tuning is configuration; ability replacement changes the corresponding mapping and focused scenarios. No universal plugin language is required.
- The owner selected dependency-targeted acceleration (Coordinator), future output batching (Packager), and launch pacing within fixed shared permits (Parallelizer) for the initial experiments. Implement them in small complete slices with no-action and pair comparisons, subject to supported environment-action availability. Preserve their teaching questions; names, precise abilities and the final roster remain editable. Unsupported mappings must be reported rather than simulated by patching product state.
- A mechanism descriptor records its intended lesson, intervention target, applicability conditions and business observation used to demonstrate its effect. This is experiment metadata, not a new product policy or in-run diagnostic architecture.
- Validate enabled mechanism references and declared numeric domains before starting. Disabled/removed mechanisms cannot be selected silently by a policy. Illegal placement, unaffordable purchase and inapplicable environment action remain explicit outcomes distinct from harness failure; never charge for a rejected action unless an explicitly chosen game rule requires it.
- The laboratory's minimal search is finite enumeration of declared plans/placements/timing/configurations. Specify limits and report which combinations ran, which were invalid and which were not explored. Do not declare global optimality or universal dominance from that search.
- Paired comparisons preserve the exogenous scenario and control schedule. Do not require identical realized event sequences after causal intervention: the intervention can legitimately change timing, business progress and subsequent endogenous player/workload responses.
- Where outcome assignment depends on issued-operation ordering, use existing supported explicit scripted outcomes for strict causal comparisons or identify the coupling limitation. The same seed alone does not prove identical per-item outcomes after a candidate changes request issuance. Do not require a new shared random-stream system in this task.
- Record initial budget, purchase/upgrade times, spent/remaining resources, placement, finite horizon and scenario assumptions. Continuous-game reward/accounting rules come from the game-design owner; do not reuse wave rewards or invent a persistent market. If that consumer has no accepted reward rule, begin with fixed experiment budgets and report the limitation.
- Preserve separate gameplay, business and teaching-observation metrics. Permit context-specific tradeoffs and pair interactions. Numeric thresholds and desired human difficulty are study-specific declarations, not arbitrary hardcoded acceptance targets.
- Hard correctness and teaching-boundary constraints are distinct from soft balance objectives. Optimization cannot change ownership, permits, freshness, authorization or committed output membership to improve the score. Game-only health/gold do not mutate business state.
- Replay remains input-oriented and formats remain version 1. Bind results to actual engine/game/mechanism identities and reject incompatible identities explicitly; no legacy replay shims or parallel formats.
- Keep business frames and experiment summaries in their appropriate structured formats. Reuse ordinary replay/test failure output; no automatic witness minimizer, special replay UI, comprehensive diagnostic taxonomy or dashboard game terminology is introduced.
- Treat the tower priority ranking as advisory source inspection. A high rank does not accept the ability, prove learning or require a new environment capability. Record unsupported translations rather than expanding shared scope to preserve a tower.
- Dependency/library choices and a later evolutionary, Bayesian or RL optimizer are deferred until bounded comparisons expose a concrete need. All routine experiments are offline, source-free and finite, with no credentials or live Jev.
- Delete replaced game-owned configuration/action/comparison paths when introducing their current owner. Earlier prototype deletion follows the existing owner-selection trigger, not automatic cleanup by this issue.

## Testing Decisions

- The highest seam is the game-owned headless experiment boundary over the shared public Monkey Business API. Test observable input-to-action, refusal, business observations, investment outcomes, metrics and replay; avoid tests mirroring private helper decomposition.
- Prior art includes existing actual-host paired balance matrices, causal risk/pressure ablations, directed campaign checks and saved-result validation; shared simulator replay, step/advance, environment and native/emitted conformance tests; and independent canonical boundary assertions.
- The test matrix includes identical experiment replay; baseline/candidate with equal fixed budgets; one meaningful positive causal case and one countercase per initial mechanism; A/B/A+B interaction; disable/remove and representative ability-replacement cases; invalid policy/configuration and unaffordable/inapplicable actions; deterministic finite exhaustion; and held-out-context separation.
- Expectations for the causal cases come from accepted business contracts and declared game rules. Compare a concrete permit, eligibility, retention or delivery observation and its timing/identity as appropriate; do not obtain the expected answer by running the same policy twice.
- Verify the game adapter does not patch Canonical and applies only supported environment actions. Exercise unchanged issued facts and committed output where relevant. Existing authority/proof gates remain authoritative; do not mandate an exhaustive new theorem inventory.
- Check step versus bounded advance, split advancement and presentation independence at matching control boundaries using existing simulator coverage where it suffices. New tests focus on the game mapping and experiment wrapper, not duplicate proofs of unchanged simulator internals.
- Reproduce applicable business traces under native Bend and emitted JavaScript using the shared conformance seam. Validate game-native mechanics on their actual supported lane; do not claim game/platform compatibility from business-lane equivalence alone.
- Demonstrate that representative intentionally wrong action mapping or metric accounting fails an independently expected scenario. This is test sensitivity, not a mandate for a new mutation-testing framework.
- Run documentation checks for specification changes. At implementation, select relevant optional-game/shared-simulator gates from the testing matrix; validate game-absent independence if dependency edges change. GitHub CI is not an additional completion gate.
- No participant study or live backend execution is required to accept the laboratory foundation. Report numerical scope, assumptions, unsearched combinations and human-validation gaps explicitly.

## Out of Scope

- Final tower roster, obligation to retain all seven towers or their current names/abilities, full game redesign, and global balance certification.
- Dynamic difficulty adjustment during play, automatic publishing/application of balance patches and self-modifying gameplay rules.
- A sophisticated optimizer, RL training, large statistical campaigns or a universal mechanism scripting/plugin language.
- Authoring waves or a duplicate business scheduler; restoring old wave compatibility after continuous-consumer migration.
- New product concurrency/capacity controls, retry/fairness/authorization semantics or simulator-wide diagnostic requirements not accepted in their contract owners.
- Live Jev, actual agent loops, source capture, transport or platform compatibility claims; formal proof of the complete game or of human enjoyment/learning.
- Synchronized game/dashboard networking, game terminology in shared business APIs, persistent player economies or trading systems.

## Further Notes

The owner's intended sequence is laboratory foundation, reversible mechanic selection/replacement, broader context comparisons, then precise development-time balancing if useful. Universal accounting and architecture constraints should be stable; prices, roster, abilities and game objectives remain editable study choices.

Specification work proceeds now, independently of the ongoing Bend rewrite. Implementation waits for the required new Bend Monkey Business boundary and selected mechanism capabilities. This work is downstream of the continuous consumer in #199 and reuses the public boundary from #176. It does not enlarge their already agreed scope or require every migration ticket to finish before specifying experiments. The strongest risk is optimizing a proxy or weak player policy while damaging the architectural lesson; preserve separate observations and retain a later human teaching check.

The source-inspected tower priority assessment and game-design context are prepared in the isolated `spec/game-balance-lab` worktree. They record proposed selection, unsupported mappings and follow-up decisions; no new balance experiment or learning validation is claimed. The owner confirmed the headless experiment boundary over the shared engine on 2026-10-02. This confirms the testing seam and permits publication/scheduling; implementation still waits for the required Bend Monkey Business scenario/action capabilities.

title: Add Pi runtime support through native hooks without previous-code state
body:
## Problem Statement

A user working in Pi cannot receive Hapsland's configured semantic reviews and actionable advice through Pi's native tool loop. Hapsland currently supports Claude Code and Codex CLI, while its OpenCode candidate is unavailable. The user already has Pi 1.0.0 configured locally with gpt-6-luna and wants Pi integration that preserves Hapsland's architecture: listen to runtime hooks, review attributed current source, and do not maintain previous-code state or a Git baseline.

## Solution

Add Pi as a user-selectable Hapsland agent runtime. A thin Pi extension translates native edit and finish events into the existing resident admission, semantic review, advice collection, and delivery flow. The user can set up, diagnose, update, repair, reinstall, and remove the integration through the ordinary Hapsland lifecycle.

The initial implementation and native validation target Pi 1.0.0 on the current Linux arm64 environment. The existing local gpt-6-luna configuration is the native validation model, not an adapter requirement. Source research for Pi 0.99.1 establishes a promising lifecycle but does not establish compatibility of the locally installed 1.0.0; inspect that exact runtime before enabling it.

The integration uses native event arguments/results and bounded current-source capture. It does not read and retain pre-edit file copies, build a prior-code history, or reconcile changes against Git at finish. If native evidence is insufficient to establish an attributed edit under the existing contract, the observation remains incomplete and produces no addressed review. Implementation begins by validating native attribution and completion boundaries; support is enabled only after these gates pass.

## User Stories

1. As a Pi user, I want to select Pi in Hapsland setup, so that review integrates with the coding agent I already use.
2. As a Pi user, I want to keep my existing model and provider configuration, so that installing review does not alter my coding environment.
3. As a Pi user, I want an exact preview of the owned extension changes, so that I can understand what setup will install.
4. As a Pi user, I want setup to use the selected Pi executable and agent home, so that isolated and custom profiles work predictably.
5. As a Pi user, I want unsupported runtime versions to be reported before installation, so that unavailable review is not mistaken for active support.
6. As a Pi user, I want my runtime's extension trust and restart requirements explained, so that installation and execution are distinguishable.
7. As a Pi user, I want native eligible edit attempts registered before the tool proceeds, so that late events cannot reopen closed review work.
8. As a Pi user, I want successful attributed edits to reach the existing semantic review pipeline, so that the same configured rules apply across runtimes.
9. As a Pi user, I want native edit arguments and results to establish the affected current type or function, so that review is tied to my actual edit.
10. As a Pi user, I want supported native writes reviewed when their evidence establishes exact attribution, so that write tools receive the same protections as edits.
11. As a Pi user, I want ambiguous or unsupported mutations reported as incomplete, so that Hapsland does not invent attribution or a clear review.
12. As a Pi user, I want file selection enforced before source capture and egress, so that excluded files remain outside Hapsland review.
13. As a Pi user, I want supporting declarations included through the existing bounded evidence tree, so that cross-file review keeps its present meaning.
14. As a Pi user, I want Hapsland to avoid previous-code snapshots and Git baselines, so that integration remains driven by native events.
15. As a Pi user, I want advice delivered to the originating session and working root, so that another session never receives my findings.
16. As a Pi user, I want nested and child events handled only with reliable attribution, so that advice is not misaddressed.
17. As a Pi user, I want repeated event notifications to start no duplicate review, so that hooks do not increase cost or repeat advice.
18. As a Pi user, I want failed and cancelled tools to release unused permits, so that failed edits do not leave pending admission behind.
19. As a Pi user, I want ready advice attached to an appropriate native model-visible interaction, so that I can continue working without a separate review queue.
20. As a Pi user, I want completion held for the existing bounded review wait, so that pending reviews have a chance to become advice before settlement.
21. As a Pi user, I want actionable findings to request a bounded continuation at completion, so that the agent can address them in the same virtual round.
22. As a Pi user, I want continuation limits and relevance expiry to remain shared Hapsland policy, so that the Pi extension does not create another repair loop.
23. As a Pi user, I want advice about superseded source withheld, so that delayed results do not ask me to repair an obsolete edit.
24. As a Pi user, I want review failures represented truthfully without invented findings, so that an unavailable backend is not confused with a successful review.
25. As a Pi user, I want aborts, session switches, reloads, and shutdowns to preserve isolation and bounded cleanup, so that later sessions do not inherit stale work or output.
26. As a headless Pi user, I want advice and supported completion behavior to work without UI prompts, so that automation follows the same contract.
27. As a Pi user, I want Hapsland to preserve unrelated extensions and settings, so that integration coexists with my existing tools.
28. As a Pi user, I want doctor and session activity to distinguish installed, ready, reviewed, and submitted states, so that I can diagnose the actual boundary that failed.
29. As a Pi user, I want update, repair, and reinstall to use the existing ownership and proposal workflow, so that lifecycle behavior is consistent across runtimes.
30. As a Pi user, I want uninstall to remove only Hapsland-owned unchanged artifacts, so that local modifications and other integrations are preserved.
31. As a maintainer, I want deterministic offline fixtures at the installed integration boundary, so that failures can be reproduced without model or Jev calls.
32. As a maintainer, I want native Pi observations separated from simulated and packaged checks, so that support claims match the evidence actually collected.
33. As a maintainer, I want existing Claude and Codex conformance retained, so that adding Pi does not change their delivery policy.
34. As a maintainer, I want one shared resident and authoritative policy engine, so that agent adapters do not fork review semantics.

## Implementation Decisions

- Pi is an agent-runtime adapter. Model provider and gpt-6-luna are secondary validation metadata, not new product targets. Keep the user's runtime model/provider settings unchanged.
- Validate the installed Pi 1.0.0 lifecycle and tool result shapes before activating that profile. Do not copy the earlier advisory report's 0.99.1 assumptions into a compatibility declaration.
- Use a thin Pi extension as the hook handler and the existing Hapsland command/resident transport as the integration boundary. The extension owns native event and response translation; the resident owns permits, virtual rounds, work scheduling, pending advice, leases, freshness, continuation budgets, and expiry.
- Obtain a source-free edit permit through the synchronous before-tool boundary, then consume it through the matching successful post-tool observation. Failure to register a permit means incomplete Hapsland admission, not authority to deny the user's native edit. Release failed, cancelled, expired, or otherwise unused permits according to existing policy.
- Derive edit attribution from native arguments/results and the current captured file. Native patch/result evidence may be inspected transiently; Hapsland must not capture or retain a separate pre-edit file image, store previous code, maintain a baseline, or compute a finish-time Git diff.
- The exact native evidence for edit and write is an implementation discovery gate. Distinguish whole-file write from file creation; matching current content alone does not justify an invented Add event or prove a changed span. Define the supported native shapes, preserve existing semantic selection rules, and withhold review when attribution cannot be established. If supporting a shape requires a new root-selection policy, obtain an explicit product-contract amendment rather than silently broadening review to every declaration.
- Apply configured selection, containment, protected-path, ignore, symlink, capture-size, and freshness rules before source capture and remote review. Reuse existing language analysis and bounded cross-file evidence for supported TypeScript, Rust, and Bend profiles.
- Extend runtime identity and resident protocol validation in place at format version 1. Identify the physical working root, Pi version, session, native tool call, and reliably supplied child identity. Nested tool calls are not automatically subagents. Do not infer child identity from a path, parent call identifier, or the latest session.
- Map Pi's actual pre-settlement boundary to the shared finish-attempt semantics only after confirming it is awaited by the installed runtime. A notification emitted after settlement is not a substitute. Preserve the existing safe deadline, finish decision, cancellation fence, bounded continuation, and quiescence behavior.
- Submit advice through supported model-visible Pi output or boundary entries. Preserve unrelated native tool content and extension contributions. Use the shared response-authority and acknowledgment rules; distinguish selected, authorized, submitted, model-visible, repaired, and follow-up-clear observations.
- Keep failed or uncertain submission truthful and bounded. Do not add adapter-owned retry, findings, evaluator, history, or turn-baseline state. Source-free transient transport identity may be retained only where needed to correlate lifecycle events and must be bounded and retired.
- Extend common setup, client selection, lifecycle operations, ownership checks, exact proposal digests, custom profile options, development installation, and package exports/assets for Pi. Preserve other extensions and user configuration; perform no package acquisition during edit hooks. Use the existing approval workflow inside the product rather than adding another installer policy.
- Keep review-provider integration through Effect Decision/DecisionModel and the existing Jev provider. Do not make Abide a dependency or add a second evaluator. Preserve pinned Effect packages and the shared authoritative policy boundary.
- Record the exact initially validated runtime/platform profile and unsupported cases in maintained support and installation guidance. Do not infer macOS, other versions, interactive trust, or published-package support from one local run.

## Testing Decisions

- Use the installed Pi extension-to-Hapsland boundary as the primary acceptance seam: drive native-shaped tool and pre-settlement events through the actual extension/command into the production resident with a controlled offline reviewer, then assert externally observable admission, requests, output, and cleanup. Prefer the existing isolated-profile package and native-integration harnesses over a new parallel test framework.
- A good test asserts an externally observable contract: whether eligible attributed source is reviewed, whether advice reaches the right session, whether completion waits or continues, whether a failure remains incomplete, and whether lifecycle operations preserve unrelated artifacts. Avoid assertions about private queues, implementation layout, or a particular module decomposition.
- Adapt prior art from composed edit/finish integration, resident protocol/collection, deterministic controlled-reviewer transport, setup ownership and package lifecycle checks. Add focused pure adapter fixtures only for evidence shapes that cannot be isolated cleanly at the primary seam.
- Cover valid native edit and supported write shapes; wrong/missing call identity; failed tools; malformed, ambiguous, oversized, and unsupported evidence; current-file mismatch; exclusions and symlinks; Unicode/newlines; overlapping writes and later argument/result mutation by another extension. Verify rejected evidence produces no review or addressed advice.
- Cover source-free permit ordering, matching consumption, repeated events, stale/missing/expired permits, closed-round fences, and failure/abort retirement. Verify the first accepted edit opens a virtual round and prompts or polls alone do not.
- Cover an offline delayed reviewer at pre-settlement, all-work completion versus safe-deadline cutoff, actionable continuation, no-advice finish, continuation exhaustion, stale-result suppression, review errors, worker failure/timeout, uncertain output, and release/cleanup. Operational failures alone must not trigger repair continuation.
- Cover session/root isolation, supported nested identities, session switch/reload/shutdown, headless execution, and competing extension contributions. Unsupported identity cases must remain explicitly unsupported rather than routed to the main session.
- Cover first setup, repeat setup, doctor, update, repair, reinstall, uninstall, changed-owned-file conflict, custom agent home, unsupported runtime version, packaged extension loading, and preservation of unrelated extensions/settings. Run the package and lifecycle gates selected by the testing matrix because registration and distribution change.
- Extend the existing native integration runner for Pi instead of introducing another per-runtime adoption runner. Use an isolated disposable project and the user's existing gpt-6-luna model/provider configuration; do not install into or mutate the user's ordinary profile without the existing exact-change workflow. Explicitly instruct the native fixture agent to act on actionable Hapsland findings.
- Keep ordinary checks deterministic and offline. Native agent runs and optional bounded live Jev validation are separate declared milestones; local model credentials are not evidence that Jev credentials are available. Retain sanitized contract/timing evidence only.
- Complete the required local documentation, typecheck, deterministic, build, package/lifecycle, and selected native checks before claiming support. Report native submission, observed repair, follow-up evaluation, and platform/package limitations separately. Do not wait for GitHub CI as an additional completion gate.

## Out of Scope

- OpenCode support, migration to OpenCode V2, or other new agent runtimes.
- Abide integration or dependency adoption, rule compilation from instructions, and Abide-style turn-diff review.
- Previous-code storage, pre-edit file snapshots, durable source history, Git-baseline reconciliation, shell mutation discovery, and filesystem watchers used to guess edit authorship.
- New rules, new review providers, a changed semantic input contract, or a Pi-specific policy engine.
- Unsupported custom tools, child runtimes, or nested mutations whose attribution cannot be established from the validated native profile.
- Changing the user's Pi model, provider, login, trust settings, or ordinary profile during validation.
- Broad cross-platform/multi-version claims, registry publication, and guaranteed agent compliance with advice.

## Further Notes

This issue specifies requested work; it is not implementation or native compatibility evidence. The no-previous-code-state constraint comes directly from the user. Additional interviews are unnecessary: remaining factual questions about native event fidelity belong to implementation discovery and conformance gates. A proposed change to accepted product behavior requires an explicit owner decision.

Current contract owners and prior art:

- [Product vocabulary](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/master/CONTEXT.md)
- [Advice and handoff contract](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/master/docs/advicing-target-contract.md)
- [Review contract](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/master/docs/review-contract-compatibility.md)
- [Installation workflows](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/master/docs/installation-workflows.md)
- [Testing matrix](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/master/docs/testing-matrix.md)
- [Claude-specific direct-edit authority decision](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/master/docs/adr/0003-claude-direct-edit-blocking-authority.md), which must not be silently generalized to Pi.
- [Pi/Abide advisory research](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland-research/blob/master/PRODUCT-RESEARCH-ADVISORY-2026-10-03-ABIDE-AGENT-SUPPORT.md), source/artifact inspection only; findings do not become requirements merely through citation.

No implementation was made while preparing this issue. Publishing the specification creates a ready-for-agent work item; it does not start implementation or declare runtime/platform support.

title: Pi: deliver advisory review after an installed native edit
body:
## Parent

https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/204

## What to build

A user running Pi 1.0.0 in an isolated profile receives advisory Hapsland feedback after a supported native edit. Deliver the complete installed-extension → Hapsland command → production resident → controlled reviewer → native tool-result path. Include minimal package assets and isolated installation/loading so the first demonstration exercises the agreed acceptance seam. Full user-facing installation lifecycle is a later slice.

Owner-approved refinement of #204: the initial profile supports native edit; native write is explicitly unsupported/incomplete. Do not infer file creation or changed spans from matching write content. Expanding write coverage requires native evidence or an explicit product-contract decision. Keep the existing Unicode limitation tracked by #151; this ticket tests its truthful refusal rather than fixing it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The packaged extension loads in an isolated Pi 1.0.0 profile and calls the production Hapsland transport/resident; no test-only bypass replaces the installed path.
- [ ] The synchronous before-tool boundary registers a source-free permit before the native edit proceeds. Registration failure means incomplete Hapsland admission, not authority to deny the native edit.
- [ ] A matching successful native edit consumes its permit exactly once, verifies native patch coordinates against bounded current source, and opens/joins the existing virtual round. No pre-edit file snapshot, previous-code state, Git baseline, or adapter-owned review queue is introduced.
- [ ] Existing file selection, containment, protected-path, ignore, symlink, capture limits, and configuration validity apply before source reads and review egress. Semantic roots and supporting evidence use the existing shared pipeline and supported language profiles.
- [ ] A controlled offline finding is submitted through advisory model-visible native tool output while preserving unrelated content. Declare what the Pi handoff/ack boundary actually establishes; later extension mutation must not be described as proven model visibility.
- [ ] Basic session/root identity, mismatched evidence, missing/expired permits, duplicate events, failed-tool permit retirement, current-source mismatch, unsupported write, and excluded/symlink paths produce no wrongly addressed review or advice.
- [ ] Pi identity and protocol validation are extended in place at format version 1; native tool identity is not confused with child-agent identity. Existing Claude/Codex behavior and provider/policy ownership remain unchanged.
- [ ] Deterministic installed-boundary tests exercise successful review and the essential negative cases. Required local checks for this slice pass; native observations, if collected, remain separate from fixture results. Do not enable or claim the complete Pi profile before the finish and final conformance gates.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

title: Pi: wait for pending review and continue at the native finish boundary
body:
## Parent

https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/204

## What to build

A Pi user attempting to finish gives admitted reviews a bounded opportunity to settle. Actionable advice can request another provider turn in the same virtual round; an allow-finish response closes it under shared Hapsland policy. Implement the installed Pi pre-settlement path with the existing resident finish collector rather than an idle follow-up or another extension-owned repair loop.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Confirm the exact Pi 1.0.0 pre-settlement boundary is awaited and can carry advice/continuation; validate it through the installed extension and production resident with a delayed controlled offline reviewer.
- [ ] Declare a Pi-specific safe hook deadline and preserve shared all-unfinished-work waiting, deadline cutoff, cancellation fences, no-advice finish, relevance expiry, and continuation exhaustion. Do not inherit Claude-specific edit blocking or timeouts.
- [ ] Post-edit output remains advisory; finish continuation uses shared policy. Prompts, native turns, polls, or another extension cannot reset the virtual round or its continuation budget.
- [ ] Specify and test the native submission/acknowledgment boundary separately from final committed visibility and actual continuation. Returning a boundary entry alone must not be claimed as model receipt or repair.
- [ ] Test later extensions replacing boundary entries or continuation flags, aborted settlement, and final canContinue refusal. Preserve their contributions and shared response authority without another findings queue, automatic replay, or fresh continuation allowance.
- [ ] No actionable finding means no Hapsland repair continuation; backend errors and operational notices alone do not justify one. Safe finish cleanup prevents late results from being delivered in a later round.
- [ ] A controlled installed-path demonstration covers delayed-review wait, actionable continuation, allow-finish, and bounded cutoff. Required local checks pass, with evidence claims limited to the exercised boundary.

title: Pi: preserve review isolation across failures and session lifecycle changes
body:
## Parent

https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/204

## What to build

Pi users can abort work, switch sessions, reload extensions, or recover from review/transport failures without transferring review or advice to another session or retaining obsolete work. Extend the already-correct installed edit/finish path to the remaining lifecycle, concurrency, and composition cases.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Session/root partitions remain distinct through session switch, reload, shutdown, and resumed fresh activity; late callbacks never use whichever session happens to be current.
- [ ] Abort, failed tools, expired permits, worker crash/timeout, resident loss, and unavailable reviewer retire or expire owned resources under shared policy and remain truthful incomplete/unavailable outcomes.
- [ ] Delayed old findings after a newer edit, repeated notifications, overlapping writes, and other extensions mutating arguments/results cannot produce duplicate review or stale/misattributed advice.
- [ ] Failed and uncertain submissions follow existing lease, response-authority, acknowledgment, and expiry rules. Recovery does not replay uncertain advice or reset the continuation budget.
- [ ] Nested tool calls and supplied child identities are accepted only with demonstrated exact attribution. Unsupported custom/child cases remain explicitly unsupported rather than being routed to the main session.
- [ ] Supported headless execution needs no UI prompt; competing extensions preserve their output and behavior while Hapsland makes no claim beyond its actual submission boundary.
- [ ] Use deterministic controlled-reviewer scenarios through the same installed extension/command/resident seam, covering cleanup followed by a provably fresh eligible edit. Extend existing native negative scenarios rather than adding a parallel per-runtime runner.
- [ ] Retain the no-previous-code-state constraint, shared resident/policy ownership, existing Unicode limitations, and native-write unsupported profile. Required local checks pass without introducing unrelated runtime support claims.

- https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/206

title: Pi: support the complete owned installation lifecycle
body:
## Parent

https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/204

A user can select Pi and manage its Hapsland integration using ordinary setup, doctor, update, repair, reinstall, and uninstall. Build on the minimal packaged extension from the first slice; this work can proceed alongside finish and fault handling. Preserve existing Pi model/provider configuration and unrelated extensions/settings.

- [ ] Pi appears in common client selection and explicit lifecycle commands, including the existing version-1 automation interface and selected/custom executable and agent-home options.

- [ ] Doctor is read-only and distinguishes installation, runtime readiness/trust, credential availability, and observed activity. Incomplete full-profile validation must not be reported as verified review support.
- [ ] Update, repair, and reinstall target the selected retained package and handle existing ownership, interrupted operations, and conflicts consistently with other runtimes.
- [ ] Uninstall removes only owned eligible artifacts, refuses conflicting local modifications, and preserves unrelated extensions/settings. Custom profiles and repeat lifecycle operations have deterministic witnesses.
- [ ] Package assets/exports and the development-installation workflow include Pi; hooks perform no package acquisition or credential prompts. Native trust/restart requirements are explained rather than silently bypassed.

Validate the combined feature through the existing package/native harnesses and publish an accurately scoped support declaration for Pi 1.0.0 on Linux arm64. This is an integrated user workflow, not a ticket to postpone tests from earlier slices.

title: Document Hapsland review resource and limit management
body:
Update the documentation to explain that Hapsland manages review resources and limits, including concurrent classifier requests.

Owners: [classifier dispatch pool](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/master/packages/agent-flow-bend/Dispatch.bend), [provider abstraction](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/master/src/review-providers/live.ts), and [provider limit catalog](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/master/src/review-providers/catalog.ts).

title: Investigate review skipped by unrelated Unicode comments
Package Hapsland with Bun and reduce hook startup overhead
body:
Package Hapsland as standalone executables containing the application and pinned Bun runtime, following the inspected OpenCode build approach: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/907b3bc518fa48e90e8ec24dd327d13eee71c36c/packages/opencode/script/build.ts

This work incorporates #213 by owner instruction. Reduce hook startup overhead by deferring administrative/setup/evaluation imports and using narrow Effect imports where applicable. Preserve Effect-based review providers, hook deadlines, the process-start admission clock, protocols, shared resident/policy ownership, and agent extensions.

Replace package-owned Node distribution and retire superseded installed production paths in place at version1. Preserve required native assets and owned installation lifecycle. Pin build/runtime version; distinguish target compilation from actual platform execution evidence. Runtime command launching and physical asset paths must work in compiled executables without requiring system Node/Bun. Keep host-loaded JS extensions as necessary integration assets. Explicitly preserve configuration behavior, including Bun automatic config/env loading.

Compare real installed variants: existing Node package, Node package with lighter imports, and Bun executable (bytecode where compatible). Measure actual hook registration against the same healthy resident without coverage and separately cold-resident behavior; report declared sample count, provenance, successes/failures and durations. About100ms is acceptable to the owner, not a new hard deadline; no existing product budget is relaxed. Test source/coverage behavior separately from installed timing claims.

Acceptance: packaged edit/review/advice and installation lifecycle checks pass; required local gates pass; publishing/runtime documentation describes new distribution and exact empirically validated platforms. Comparison evidence must identify what improved and what remains unverified. No native latency claim from --version alone. See https://bun.sh/docs/bundler/executables

title: Reduce shared CLI cold-start overhead for hooks under coverage and load
body:
Cold startup of the shared CLI can exhaust the 2.5-second pre-edit admission window in local source/coverage runs under load. Eager imports load onboarding/installation and evaluation workflows even for hooks; argument parsing also reaches installation checks through client-lifecycle. This is measured test-environment evidence, not a demonstrated latency claim about normal installed use, nor proof of slow Effect execution.

Evidence from two independent worktrees:
- `fix/claude-hooks-gate`, `/workspace/typescript/jev-worktrees/claude-hooks-gate`: PRE startup 3.57s; paired master 2.38–3.58s versus unfinished patch 1.99–2.53s. Aggregate `effect` imports measured 583–904ms versus `effect/Effect` 107–166ms. Logs `/tmp/hapsland-narrow-*.log`, `/tmp/hapsland-stop-nocoverage.log`.
- Pi branch: resident returned `rejected-stale` / `StaleInvocation` for healthy registrations; process age before ensure was 3.46s and 4.13s. Source-free evidence `/tmp/pi-register-response-trace.jsonl`, `/tmp/pi-register-response-diagnostic.log`.

Evaluate deferred administrative imports, a lightweight CLI-command module, and narrow Effect imports without changing hook deadlines, process-start clock, parsing, or protocols. Evaluate compiled-CLI fixtures/coverage changes separately so they do not hide source-path behavior. Full quality is unconfirmed; the previous isolated Codex installation failure has no established cause.

Unfinished candidates: uncommitted Claude worktree above; Pi candidate preserved separately on local `task/cli-cold-start`, commit `b861c843`, worktree `/workspace/typescript/jev-worktrees/cli-cold-start`. Typecheck passed; runtime improvement/full quality unverified. Its import-boundary test hit the five-second watchdog under load; Astra also requested removing superseded client-lifecycle re-exports and updating remaining imports.

Done when shared hook startup avoids unnecessary workflow loading, source/installed behavior and coverage remain correctly attributed, and required deterministic checks pass with existing product budgets. This issue is deferred from the current Pi patch-verification task by owner instruction.

title: Ship Bun executables and reduce hook startup overhead
body:
Hook commands previously started the package-owned Node distribution and eagerly loaded administrative and installation code. Hapsland now ships four standalone commands per platform with pinned Bun 1.3.14, defers administrative/evaluation imports, and uses narrower Effect imports. Physical native assets, host-loaded Pi extensions, v1 IPC and records, product deadlines, and explicit configuration loading remain supported.

The installed comparison recorded 15 ready-resident registrations per variant and three cold registrations per variant, all successful. Ready-resident medians were 1044 ms for baseline Node, 627 ms for optimized Node, and 309 ms for the Bun candidate. The measured candidate predates the final IPC connection/listener ordering and paused-socket cleanup fixes; the timing is not a measurement of the final archive.

Validation: current Linux arm64 archive passes setup, clean-package controlled review, and client lifecycle conformance. Source-free hook import tripwires catch review-engine evaluation. Actual IPC regression checks cover Node and Bun. Package conformance uses an isolated Bun install by default, retains explicit npm selection, and installation does not run coverage. Optional repeated installed/timing cases were removed while preserving their source owners and essential installed lifecycle cases.

Platform limits: Linux arm64 commands have actual installed execution evidence; Darwin arm64 commands were cross-built only. Controlled credential fixtures do not establish real Secret Service/Keychain or paid native-agent compatibility. The candidate archive is approximately 268 MB compressed and 737 MB unpacked.

Local validation: full `npm run quality:check` passed with fresh coverage, strict CRAP threshold 8 and strict missing evidence; 1907 tests passed and two preexisting cases were skipped. Typecheck, docs checks and diff checks passed. Final Astra Spec and Standards reviews reported no blockers, including the remaining test/tooling delta.

Development checks now print failing assertions, stacks and values immediately instead of waiting for the final suite summary. Slow repeated installed scenarios and mixed recovery assertions were removed while retaining owner checks. The installed Claude Stop smoke now uses one ready finding. The Bend kernel subprocess runaway guard allows 15 seconds, with proof validity, all laws/mutation witnesses, and product deadlines unchanged. The testing matrix reserves complete runs for review-ready milestones or confirmed fixes.

Implements #212 (incorporating #213).

title: Cancel verification early when declared inputs change
body:
Full verification currently checks its source digest after archive preparation and at the end of the test run. A relevant input change during a long stage can therefore waste the remainder of a run whose final result will be rejected.

Scope: add early cancellation for changes to the declared verification inputs in scripts/test-harness/prepare-archive.mjs. This is a follow-up; the current change narrows that scope and changes local check selection, but does not implement observation or cancellation.

Acceptance:
- Observe relevant additions, modifications and deletions during long stages and check input identity between stages.
- Stop the active child process and descendants and admit no subsequent stages after invalidation.
- Retain completed stage results and a failure naming changed paths; an invalidated run cannot pass.
- Ignore changes outside verification inputs, including quint-specs/quint.lock and unrelated research documents.
- Preserve exclusive-lock ownership until children have stopped, bounded observation cost and a final identity check.
- Exercise a relevant change during a deliberately long child, an unrelated concurrent document, and child cleanup deterministically without running the full production suite.

Motivation: the 2026-10-04 configuration rename lost a 13m44s successful test run to a newly created unrelated quint.lock; its creation was detected only at the end. Narrowing the scope fixes that incident, while this task prevents wasting time after actual verification-input changes.

title: Audit slow integration tests and plan faster in-memory Effect coverage
body:
The full local quality gate takes roughly 10–13 minutes. Many integration tests launch processes, use real sockets/files, or wait for idle timers. Audit which behavioral scenarios can move to fast deterministic Effect tests, and produce a prioritized migration plan.

This issue covers **the audit and plan**. Implement agreed changes in follow-up work.

### Baseline

Start with retained evidence: `.test-runs/20261004213056947-1596608-304c73` recorded 1,917 passing tests and a 611-second full gate. The gate remained red on eight pre-existing CRAP findings; this audit does not include their remediation.

Existing `src/resident/client.test.ts` uses `Layer.succeed(ResidentStartup)` with injected time for deadlines and retries. `src/resident/runtime.test.ts` avoids subprocesses but still uses real files and sockets. Distinguish those approaches from genuinely in-memory I/O.

### Audit

For each expensive test or related scenario group, record:

- Concrete test/file, observed duration, timing evidence and major costs (startup, real waits, I/O, teardown).
- Its behavioral guarantee, unique acceptance value and regression it catches.
- Whether to retain, narrow, consolidate, or move behavior into in-memory Effect layers with `Deferred`, injected time or `TestClock`.
- Dependencies that must remain real, evidence lost through doubles, and the smallest boundary checks needed to preserve it.
- Estimated savings, confidence and a bounded focused validation command for the follow-up.

Assess process lifecycle/lock release, Node versus Bun behavior, OS signals, Unix sockets, filesystem permissions and installed-package wiring explicitly. A recent Bun resident closed its socket after idle while keeping its process and lock alive; Node-based checks missed this. Preserve a real native witness for this boundary rather than assuming doubles or Node establish Bun behavior.

### Acceptance

- Post a prioritized candidate table and concrete follow-up recommendations in this issue; a new Markdown report is not required.
- Separate measured timings from estimates and explain expected wall-clock savings, accounting for parallel execution rather than summing test durations.
- Explain how each proposed replacement preserves behavioral assertions and which real-boundary evidence remains necessary. Coverage percentage alone does not establish equivalence.
- Use existing logs first; gather missing evidence with bounded focused measurements. Do not rerun the full gate solely to collect a baseline.
- Do not perform a broad migration in this issue or weaken quality-gate, coverage or CRAP policy. Propose an achievable duration target only if the evidence supports one.

title: Audit CLI output consistency and human-readable package doctor diagnostics
body:
During the macOS user-installation trial, running `"$HOME/.local/bin/hapsland-doctor"` printed a dense single-line JSON object containing the complete diagnostics report. This is difficult to read in a terminal. Human-readable CLI output was intended across user-facing commands; investigate where that intent is implemented and where it is missing.

Confirmed implementation: `src/package-doctor.ts` unconditionally writes `JSON.stringify(output)` and exits according to package readiness. Other commands already have human/JSON modes, so assess consistency rather than introducing another independent output convention.

### Scope

- Inventory public CLI entry points and commands, including package doctor, integration doctor, setup/update/removal, status, credentials and explain. Include success, failure and recovery output.
- Identify the owning contracts and documentation for human versus machine output, existing format flags and defaults, and automation consumers that parse current JSON.
- Propose readable default output for commands used interactively, with an explicit JSON mode (prefer the existing `--json` convention where appropriate). Review piped/non-TTY behavior explicitly; do not assume every non-TTY consumer wants JSON.
- Distinguish public user commands from hook, IPC and versioned JSON automation interfaces. Preserve machine contracts and clean stdout for those interfaces.
- Define concise summaries, failed checks, actionable recovery, stdout/stderr usage, exit statuses and secret-redaction requirements.

### Acceptance

Post an inventory and prioritized implementation plan in this issue, including a concrete before/after example for `hapsland-doctor`, affected source/tests/docs, automation impact and focused verification commands. Determine how the installer and other package-diagnostic consumers will request machine output explicitly. Verify that planned formatting changes preserve diagnostic meaning and exit statuses.

This is an investigation/planning task; broad CLI changes belong in follow-up work. Use offline source inspection and bounded focused checks. No live Jev requests or full-gate reruns are needed solely for the audit.

title: Make doctor and installer outcomes visually clear; consult Astra on presentation
body:
During the user-installation trial, a successful doctor or installer response was not visually obvious. Plain diagnostic lines do not make the final outcome easy to identify. Investigate and improve outcome visibility for package doctor, integration doctors and installation/setup/update flows.

**Consult Astra before choosing the presentation.** Ask Astra to review concrete current output and proposed success, warning/partial and failure examples. Use that consultation to decide the visual hierarchy and conventions; do not treat emoji as the only possible solution.

### Scope

- Show a prominent final outcome with a clear text label and an appropriate visual marker (for example a symbol, emoji or restrained terminal styling).
- Make success, partial completion, warnings and failure distinguishable. Keep the meaning clear without color and in terminals that cannot display Unicode or support styling.
- State exactly what succeeded: package integrity/readiness, hook installation, local configuration/credential availability, or an observed real review. Installation and offline readiness must not imply that a Jev request or review succeeded.
- Keep necessary next actions visible, including restart/trust steps. Distinguish a completed installation from an integration that still needs user action.
- Use consistent outcome conventions across package doctor, client doctors and installer flows. Assess TTY, redirected output and accessibility.
- Preserve machine JSON, hook/IPC output, diagnostic meaning, exit statuses and secret redaction. Keep presentation in the human-output path.

### Acceptance

- Record Astra's recommendations and the chosen presentation with concrete before/after examples for successful doctor and setup, plus partial/warning and failure cases.
- Identify affected commands, source, tests and documentation, and implement the agreed human-output treatment.
- Verify the final outcome is easy to spot, meaningful without color, and accurately bounded by the evidence collected. Add focused checks for rendered outcomes and unchanged machine output/exit behavior.

Coordinate with #217, which audits human-readable versus machine CLI output. This issue owns visual outcome clarity and accurate success messaging; avoid duplicating or conflicting format conventions.

title: Define classifier credential names and explicit selection across Effect 4 providers
body:
Investigate classifier credential naming and backend selection in one task.

The current default TYPESAFE_API_KEY is provider-specific and is not an extensible classifier credential contract. Keep that public name unchanged for now. Installer key names, provider names and replacement commands must be rendered from the same definitions used by configuration, CLI parsing and provider execution, so future changes do not leave stale text.

Scope:
1. Check the actual credential parameter and environment-variable names used by other classifier backends, including the currently integrated Cloudflare Clef/Clef-flash and applicable Effect 4 decision providers. Use primary documentation and the pinned source; distinguish documented claims from observed behavior.
2. Determine the explicit selection rule when several classifier configurations or credentials exist. Record current Hapsland behavior, decide how users choose a classifier, and define precedence/ambiguity handling. Mere presence of multiple keys must not silently select a backend.
3. Inspect Effect 4 Decision / DecisionModel and provider layers: establish whether credentials belong to the provider-neutral API or individual providers, and identify their exact credential options and environment configuration names.

Acceptance:
- One comparison of actual backend key options and environment names, with source/version references.
- One explicit decision for multiple-backend selection and credential precedence, covering configuration, setup, verification and hooks.
- A proposed extensible credential contract, including whether TYPESAFE_API_KEY remains the Jev default and how provider-specific references are represented.
- Implementation scope and focused offline tests derived from that decision; do not introduce a generic key name or alter provider selection just from advisory research.

Current installation UX constraint: save user-entered keys independently of a network/rate-limit/timeout verification result; external failures produce a warning, without instructing users to restart setup. Definite authorization rejection may offer interactive correction of the selected source.

title: Expose editable JSON rule packs and support explicit unattended setup
body:
## Problem Statement

During setup, users cannot see which review rules are active, where they live, or how to supply their own. The shipped nine-rule set is assembled in TypeScript, despite local rule packs already having declarative configuration and Effect Schema validation. Calling this set “Noul” confuses its content with TypeSafe's Bernoulli probability result type. Guided setup also needs a discoverable unattended workflow for systems where prompts are impossible.

## Solution

Show the effective rule inventory and concrete source files during setup and through a standalone rules command. Materialize the shipped Hapsland default pack as editable JSON alongside personal packs, support project packs, and load all selected packs through the same Effect Schema and compilation boundary. Provide minimal rule management without launching an editor or making classifier calls. Offer unattended setup using separate prompt-suppression and application-authorization controls, following the Terraform model and reusing the current setup engine.

## User Stories

1. As a new user, I want to see the shipped rules during setup, so that I understand what Hapsland will review.
2. As a user with custom packs, I want to see my complete effective inventory, so that setup reflects my actual configuration.
3. As a user, I want rule names and descriptions to come from the rule definitions, so that displayed information agrees with execution.
4. As a user, I want each rule's pack, enabled state, scope, and source path, so that I know where to change it.
5. As a user, I want to inspect rules after installation, so that I do not need to reinstall or read documentation to discover them.
6. As a user, I want to inspect a rule's question, criteria, feedback, threshold, applicability, and review targets, so that I understand its behavior.
7. As a user, I want disabled rules to remain visible, so that I can enable them again.
8. As a user, I want an explicit warning when no rules are enabled, so that I understand edits will receive no rule evaluations.
9. As a user, I want to know I can author my own questions about supported types and functions, so that I can enforce my own concerns.
10. As a user, I want minimal creation of a valid custom pack, so that I can start without reconstructing the schema from documentation.
11. As a user, I want to connect an existing pack, so that I can reuse authored rules.
12. As a user, I want to choose personal or project scope, so that rules affect the intended repositories.
13. As a teammate, I want project packs to be committable with the project, so that collaborators share their definitions.
14. As a user, I want personal defaults and custom rules in one discoverable rules directory, so that their locations are understandable.
15. As a user, I want to edit shipped rule JSON directly, so that Hapsland does not restrict ownership of local files.
16. As a user, I want removing a rule from a selected JSON pack to remove it from the inventory, so that hidden fallback definitions cannot restore it.
17. As a user, I want a custom pack in the defaults directory to work like any other explicitly selected pack, so that directory naming does not impose artificial restrictions.
18. As a user, I want unreferenced JSON files to remain inactive, so that file placement cannot silently enable review behavior.
19. As a user, I want precise local validation errors for invalid packs, so that I can repair them without network access.
20. As a user, I want configuration and pack operations to avoid opening an editor or running paid example checks, so that their effects are predictable.
21. As an automation operator, I want setup with no prompt attempts, so that installation works without a terminal.
22. As an automation operator, I want prompt suppression separate from permission to apply changes, so that unattended preview cannot silently install hooks.
23. As an automation operator, I want to apply a previously generated plan, so that the applied changes match what was reviewed.
24. As an automation operator, I want credentials resolved from existing configured sources, so that secrets do not appear in command arguments or output.
25. As an automation operator, I want actionable failures and structured results, so that missing inputs and installation conflicts are detectable.
26. As a user, I want repeat setup to preserve authored pack files, so that installation does not erase my work.

## Implementation Decisions

- Noul denotes TypeSafe's Bernoulli probability result/wire type, corresponding to Effect Decision.probability. The shipped nine rules are Hapsland default rules; custom rules use the same supported probability result form.
- Replace TypeScript-authored default rule content with a shipped JSON pack. Remove superseded production definitions rather than retaining a second authoritative copy or legacy loading route. Ship and validate the JSON asset through the installed-package boundary.
- Every selected shipped or user-authored pack uses the existing Effect Schema, semantic validation, and compiler. Keep Hapsland-owned formats at version 1. If display titles are needed, define them in the pack schema and original definitions; do not maintain a parallel UI inventory.
- Materialize the shipped pack into the personal rules directory on initial setup. Its editable materialized file is the active authority, not an additional unconditional embedded pack. Do not overwrite an existing authored file during repeated setup.
- Directory names distinguish organization only. A selected custom file in defaults is valid. Do not scan directories to auto-enable arbitrary JSON: active packs are explicit configuration references.
- Respect existing personal/project configuration layers, qualified identities, override semantics, repository path containment, and rule eligibility. Do not introduce new nested configuration inheritance.
- Minimal rules management covers listing/details, enable/disable configuration, custom-pack creation, and connecting an existing pack. Show actual paths; do not launch an editor. Users edit JSON themselves. Changing a shipped question through an override is unnecessary; users can author a distinct rule or directly edit the local JSON.
- Offer personal/project scope when creating or connecting a pack; project is the default selection. Show scope and target files before interactive writes. Headless operations specify their scope explicitly.
- During setup, show one concise effective inventory per invocation, rather than repeating it for every selected agent. Include disabled states, custom packs, and the current repository context. Enabled count does not imply every rule runs on every edit.
- Preserve the limited supported type-shape/function review inputs and declared evidence requirements. Do not present arbitrary repository, diff, or conversation checks as supported.
- Reuse the existing setup core and structured preview/digest/apply protocol. Add convenient CLI access for unattended use without creating another installation engine.
- Prompt suppression and authorization to apply changes are separate controls. A validated saved plan authorizes its specific application. Without authorization, unattended mode previews or reports that application authorization is required; it does not mutate installations.
- Without a terminal, do not attempt prompts or implicitly select clients/approve writes. Explain the explicit unattended invocation needed. Exact option names must originate in the command definition, and all help/prompts/templates consume those definitions.
- Use existing credential resolution. Do not introduce a secret-valued API-key CLI option. Unattended setup does not prompt for replacement keys or perform live verification.
- Preserve installation conflicts, unrelated hooks, digest validation, and existing user-owned trust requirements. Distinguish installation completion from unknown native trust or unverified review readiness in results.

## Testing Decisions

- Prefer existing high-level configuration-loading and guided/structured setup tests. Exercise observable effective inventory, source paths, filesystem effects, prompts, outputs, and exit behavior instead of mirroring internal functions.
- Verify the shipped JSON and equivalent local JSON pass the same schema/compiler and yield equivalent effective rules. Reject malformed definitions with sanitized actionable diagnostics.
- Test direct edits/removal within the active default JSON, custom packs in either directory, explicit-only loading, user/project composition, disabled visibility, zero enabled rules, and eligibility-aware descriptions.
- Test minimal creation/connection through the common configuration operation: valid generated content, registration, scope/path reporting, preservation of existing files, invalid-input rejection, and no editor/network invocation.
- Extend existing setup integration seams to cover inventory once across multiple clients, TTY and non-TTY entry, no prompt attempts, preview without writes, explicit authorized application, saved-plan application, stale plan rejection, conflicts, missing inputs, credential sources, and repeat-run preservation.
- Test installed-package loading of the JSON asset; source-checkout tests alone do not establish packaging correctness.
- Use deterministic offline tests. Run check:fast, focused affected owner/consumer tests, affected installation/packaging integrations, and documentation checks according to the repository testing matrix. Broaden to the full gate only if the implementation creates an unbounded cross-cutting impact.

## Out of Scope

- A full interactive editor for every rule field, editor launching, and classifier-based example validation/calibration.
- Automatic generation from instruction files, arbitrary review input kinds, automatic discovery of all JSON in a directory, and new format versions.
- Detecting modified shipped defaults by baseline hashes and warning/merging during upgrades. This is deferred follow-up, not permission to overwrite existing edited files in this feature.
- Classifier credential naming and multi-provider selection design, tracked separately in #219.
- Publication, deployment, or a new release-support claim.

## Further Notes

Accepted user-visible locations:
- Personal shipped defaults: `~/.config/hapsland/rules/defaults/hapsland.json`.
- Personal custom example: `~/.config/hapsland/rules/custom/my-rules.json`.
- Substitute an applicable `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` for `~/.config` according to existing configuration conventions.
- Project custom example: `<Git repository root>/.hapsland/rules/custom/my-rules.json`.

The user explicitly accepted these locations and confirmed the design discussion was complete. Implementation should settle low-level mechanics consistently with existing configuration ownership. Do not silently recreate a deleted connected default pack; report its missing source through normal pack validation. An empty rules array is valid and results in the explicit zero-rules warning.

Terminology correction was performed in the worktree by Astra before this issue: documentation/type checks and focused tests passed; website browser execution was blocked by missing libatk, and the comparison generator encountered an existing frozen fixture digest mismatch. This is contextual evidence, not validation of the feature specified here. Current runtime pack identifiers still use `noul`; implementation must distinguish identifier changes from the probability type and update affected references coherently if renaming them.

Future default-update work should track shipped baselines and detect locally edited/deleted content before replacement, naming affected rules/files in warnings. No update reconciliation is implemented or accepted by this issue.

title: Load editable shipped JSON defaults through the common review pipeline
body:
## Parent

Specification: #220.

## What to build

Authorized initial setup materializes and explicitly connects Hapsland's shipped default rules as editable JSON. The selected JSON drives actual review through the same Effect Schema, semantic validation, and compilation boundary as custom packs. Editing or removing individual definitions changes subsequent effective review.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Ship the nine default rule definitions as JSON; remove superseded TypeScript-authored production content and unconditional parallel default loading.
- [ ] Use the personal defaults location accepted in #220, respecting existing XDG conventions. Connect the materialized file explicitly through configuration.
- [ ] Initial provisioning occurs only under setup application authorization. Preview does not write pack files or configuration; repeated setup preserves existing authored content.
- [ ] Every selected pack uses common Effect Schema and semantic checks, with formats remaining version 1.
- [ ] Changes and removal of individual rules in the active JSON change effective evaluation. Empty rules are valid; missing or malformed connected sources report actionable errors without silently restoring defaults.
- [ ] Directory placement does not activate a pack or change its semantics; a custom pack placed in defaults works when explicitly connected.
- [ ] Preserve configuration layering, identity checks, project path containment, and existing eligibility behavior.
- [ ] Verify the shipped asset from an installed package and exercise edited definitions through an existing high-level review seam using an offline backend.
- [ ] Update affected maintained contracts and pass check:fast, focused configuration/rules/review tests, affected packaging/setup integrations, and documentation checks.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

title: Show and toggle effective rules in CLI and guided setup
body:

- [ ] Any added display metadata lives in the version-1 pack schema/definitions; do not duplicate rule names or CLI options as unrelated strings.
- [ ] Tests through existing CLI/setup and configuration/review seams establish outputs, disabled visibility, toggle effects, custom packs, and empty inventories.

title: Create and connect custom rule packs with explicit configuration scope
