title: Support unattended setup with separate preview and application authorization
body:
## Parent

Specification: #220.

## What to build

Expose a convenient unattended setup frontend over the existing preview/digest/apply engine. Suppressing prompts alone never authorizes mutations; explicit application authorization or a validated saved plan allows the selected changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Separate prompt suppression from authorization to apply, following the accepted Terraform model. Derive exact flags, allowed values, help and templates from the actual command definition.
- [ ] Explicit unattended calls and non-TTY handling never attempt selection, confirmation, masked-input or verification prompts. Missing required choices report actionable instructions.
- [ ] Preview leaves installations, pack files and configuration unchanged. An explicit apply authorization or saved plan applies only validated selected changes; stale plans are rejected.
- [ ] Reuse existing setup, credential resolution and digest checks rather than implementing another installer engine.
- [ ] Do not add secret-valued API-key arguments, reveal secrets, perform paid verification, or treat prompt suppression as authorization for conflicts/overwrites.
- [ ] Preserve unrelated hooks, conflict/partial outcomes and native trust requirements. Distinguish installation completion from unverified review/native trust readiness.
- [ ] Provide actionable diagnostics, documented outcome/exit semantics, and structured output suitable for automation.
- [ ] Existing high-level CLI/structured setup tests cover preview/no writes, apply, saved plans, stale plans, missing inputs, credentials, conflicts, idempotence and no prompts/network verification.
- [ ] When editable-default provisioning is present, combined integration checks prove its file/configuration writes participate in authorization and plan binding and preserve authored content. This is integration acceptance, not a blocking dependency on rule tasks.
- [ ] Pass check:fast, focused tests, affected installation integrations and documentation checks.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

title: Add opt-in local inspection history and a live user dashboard
body:
# Hapsland: opt-in local inspection history and live dashboard

**Purpose:** Specify opt-in local inspection history and a live user dashboard for Hapsland.
**Status:** Ready for implementation; the owner confirmed the product scope and the primary testing boundary in the originating conversation.
**Authority:** Accepted feature requirements from the owner, with engineering decisions for implementation. Existing accepted review, file-selection, advicee, delivery and source-free analytics contracts remain authoritative. No implementation, executable-model verification, visual acceptance or platform validation is claimed.
**Expected use:** Implement and review this feature against the user stories, decisions and external testing boundary below.
**Lifecycle:** Update this issue when an owner-approved scope or acceptance decision changes. During implementation, consolidate shipped requirements into the maintained configuration, status and inspection contract owners. Retire the local publication draft once the issue is published; replace the type-only sketch with the executable behaviour model. Review these requirements if capture, storage, feed or handoff boundaries change.

## Problem Statement

When a coding agent edits source, a Hapsland user cannot inspect the complete observed path from the edit reaching a resident to classification and advice submission. The user needs to see which edits were observed, their fate, which related files and declarations contributed, exactly what the classifier was given, what it returned, and whether Hapsland passed the resulting advice to the intended agent runtime.

The existing developer dashboard explains checked transitions through example replay and simulation. It is not connected to live resident activity. Existing optional analytics provide source-free totals and bounded details; they intentionally do not retain file paths, source, classifier answers or advice text. Neither currently provides the requested user view.

Users should not accumulate source-bearing history without opting in. They also should not need to keep a browser or web server open to record useful history, or have optional inspection slow down ordinary review work.

## Solution

Add a separately opted-in, bounded local inspection history written by Hapsland residents, and a read-only live browser dashboard launched by an explicit foreground command.

The dashboard opens the combined feed of all discovered local residents for the current OS user, without inferring a default project from the launch directory. Project/working root, agent runtime, resident and session are filters. Selecting an edit reveals its preparation, review units, exact classifier requests and answers, findings, and advice-submission evidence. Review outcome and agent handoff are separate dimensions, including mixed outcomes from multiple units.

Recording starts when the effective inspection setting is enabled. Disabling stops future recording and leaves existing records subject to retention. Recording is independent of the web server and browser. Default retention is seven days, with a shared 128 MiB per-user inspection-storage limit; both are configurable. Known disabled intervals, data loss and expiry/eviction are shown honestly. Recording failures are tolerated; review work does not wait for successful history persistence.

## User Stories

1. As a Hapsland user, I want inspection history to be disabled by default, so that source-bearing data is not stored without my choice.
2. As a Hapsland user, I want to enable inspection for a project, so that I can inspect that project's reviews without recording unrelated projects.
3. As a Hapsland user, I want a user-level inspection default with project overrides in either direction, so that I can control recording consistently across my projects.
4. As a Hapsland user, I want source-free analytics and source-bearing inspection to have distinct opt-ins, so that enabling compact analytics does not silently retain code and answers.
5. As a Hapsland user, I want enabling inspection to start recording at that point without reconstructing earlier work, so that the history accurately represents its observation coverage.
6. As a Hapsland user, I want disabling inspection to stop subsequent capture while preserving retained history, so that stopping collection does not unexpectedly erase useful evidence.
7. As a Hapsland user, I want repeated enable/disable periods to appear as separate observed intervals, so that I do not mistake missing data for inactivity.
8. As a Hapsland user, I want current recording state and the last retained event to be displayed separately, so that historical records do not imply recording is still enabled.
9. As a Hapsland user, I want recording to continue while the web server is stopped or the browser is closed, so that I can inspect earlier work later.
10. As a Hapsland user, I want bounded history with seven-day and 128 MiB defaults, so that inspection does not accumulate unlimited local data.
11. As a Hapsland user, I want to configure retention duration and storage capacity, so that I can choose the appropriate local cost.
12. As a Hapsland user, I want known expiry and capacity eviction to be explained, so that disappearing older records are not misleading.
13. As an agent runtime user, I want review work to continue when inspection storage is unavailable or its queue is full, so that an optional feature does not block my agent.
14. As a Hapsland user, I want to launch the dashboard through an explicit command, so that I control when its web server exists.
15. As a Hapsland user, I want the command to accept listening host and port arguments, so that I can choose a suitable local endpoint.
16. As a Hapsland user, I want the server to run in the terminal until interrupted, so that its lifecycle is visible and simple.
17. As a Hapsland user, I want stopping the dashboard to leave residents and recording unaffected, so that viewing does not own review lifetime.
18. As a Hapsland user, I want loopback binding by default and access through an SSH tunnel when necessary, so that the first version remains local.
19. As an agent runtime user, I want my agent to be able to invoke the same dashboard command, so that it can help me open the inspector without a separate privileged control path.
20. As a Hapsland user, I want one initial feed across discovered local residents, so that launching from different directories behaves identically.
21. As a Hapsland user, I want project, working-root, resident, runtime and session filters, so that I can narrow the feed without needing a resident per project.
22. As a Hapsland user, I want each source's identity and connection health to be visible, so that an unreachable resident does not make the remaining feed appear complete.
23. As a Hapsland user, I want one edit row for each captured valid ingress observation, so that accepted, refused, duplicate and unsupported observations can be inspected.
24. As a Hapsland user, I want an edit's selected review units and their distinct outcomes, so that a partially reviewed edit is not collapsed into a success badge.
25. As a Hapsland user, I want edited paths, selected root declarations, preparation reads and actually included supporting source distinguished, so that I know what reached the classifier.
26. As a Hapsland user, I want recorded exclusions and completeness omissions with reasons, so that I can understand why a file or declaration was not evaluated.
27. As a Hapsland user, I want the exact captured classifier HTTP request body and its byte length, so that I can inspect precisely what Hapsland submitted to transport.
28. As a Hapsland user, I want readable structured input, source and rule questions alongside the exact-body view, so that I can understand the request without confusing presentation with original bytes.
29. As a Hapsland user, I want exact-body copying to preserve Unicode, escaping, tabs, line endings and whitespace, so that copied evidence matches the dispatched body.
30. As a Hapsland user, I want prepared-but-unsent input distinguished from a dispatched attempt, so that rejected dispatch is not shown as a classifier request that occurred.
31. As a Hapsland user, I want validated classifier answers, applied thresholds and configured finding messages distinguished, so that I can understand how backend judgments became advice.
32. As a Hapsland user, I want invalid answers, errors, timeouts and interruptions shown explicitly, so that silence and failure are not presented as a clear review.
33. As a Hapsland user, I want joined requests, cached evaluations and reused existing advice linked to their original provenance when available, so that reuse does not look like another fresh classifier call.
34. As a Hapsland user, I want controlled-provider activity separated from live activity, so that test traffic does not inflate live request totals.
35. As a Hapsland user, I want findings that become stale, suppressed, expired or discarded to retain their observed fate, so that an earlier result does not silently disappear from retained history.
36. As a Hapsland user, I want the exact captured advice text and runtime envelope associated with its intended recipient, so that I can inspect what Hapsland returned for submission.
37. As a Hapsland user, I want advice-ready, write-attempted, output-written, resident-acknowledged, failed and uncertain evidence distinguished, so that I can assess what was actually handed off.
38. As a Hapsland user, I want edits, findings and advice batches linked in both directions, so that batched delivery remains understandable when a batch contains several edits.
39. As a Hapsland user, I want advice submission kept separate from agent reading, agreement or repair, so that the dashboard does not claim behaviour it did not observe.
40. As a Hapsland user, I want live updates without changing my selected edit or reading position, so that new activity does not interrupt inspection.
41. As a Hapsland user, I want to pause display while recording continues and later return to live, so that I can inspect a stable view.
42. As a Hapsland user, I want reconnect replay to avoid duplicate rows and counts, so that temporary disconnection does not corrupt the view.
43. As a Hapsland user, I want unavailable payloads and known history gaps labelled with their reasons, so that missing records are not invented or called exact.
44. As a Hapsland user, I want resident restarts to retain distinct lifetime identities, so that pending or historical work is not joined to an unrelated new process.
45. As a Hapsland user, I want retained history readable after a resident exits, so that viewing old evidence does not require restarting review work.
46. As a Hapsland user, I want captured content displayed safely as text through a local read-only interface, so that inspection does not execute code or expose review-control operations.
47. As a Hapsland user, I want keyboard-accessible controls and usable narrow-screen details, so that I can inspect sessions with my usual browser and input methods.

## Implementation Decisions

### Confirmed scope and ownership

- Introduce a dedicated source-bearing inspection setting named `sessionInspection`, false by default, using existing user/project configuration precedence. It is a separate opt-in; source-free analytics retain their existing contract and enablement. Opening the dashboard never grants recording consent. Inspection does not implicitly enable source-free analytics, and analytics alone do not enable inspection.
- Support configurable inspection retention duration and per-user allocated-storage limit, defaulting to seven days and 128 MiB. The size limit covers inspection records, payloads, indices and temporary storage across residents and projects. It is separate from existing operational/source-free analytics storage; neither contract is silently replaced.
- Settings changes take effect when observed at the applicable capture boundary. Refresh effective settings at ingress and before source-bearing request/result/advice capture. Disabling prevents subsequent source-bearing captures after that observation and drops unpublished queued source-bearing material. Already published records remain readable; there is no retrospective capture or promise of instantaneous observation of an externally edited config file.
- Age retained inspection data from its capture time rather than indefinitely renewing an old event whenever its session receives new work. Prune expired data, then oldest retained data to satisfy the shared size bound. Scope cleanup coordination across writers and refuse additional inspection data when capacity cannot be safely established; review continues. Routine storage maintenance can be triggered by resident recording and history reads, without depending on a browser or continuously running HTTP server.
- A resident remains shared across working roots and agent runtimes. Preserve existing advicee partitioning by canonical physical working root, runtime/supported version, session and supplied subagent identity. The inspector is a view over those scopes, not a new owner of review state.
- Residents own capture and bounded persistence; a separate foreground dashboard process owns local discovery, read access, subscriptions and browser serving. Neither browser nor web-server lifetime owns inspection recording. Opening history does not launch a resident, read fresh project source or request a review.
- Provide an explicit dashboard CLI command with host and port arguments, loopback defaults, printed listening URL and ordinary interrupt shutdown. No daemon, background mode, automatic launch or process manager. Use Effect HTTP server facilities consistent with the project's Effect cohort; do not introduce Express.
- First-version access remains loopback/local, with SSH tunnelling for another device. Listening arguments select supported local addresses and ports; direct unauthenticated non-loopback exposure is rejected rather than silently broadening the local access contract.
- Default to the combined feed of all discovered authorized local sources. Do not infer or select a project from the launch directory. Filters identify existing physical working roots and advicee/session metadata.

### Capture and evidence

- Capture valid ingress observations before the admission decision where effective recording can be established. Inspection failure may omit any event. Do not persist raw malformed IPC, full hook payloads or credential-bearing dispatch context. The feed covers captured resident observations, not every native tool invocation or filesystem edit.
- Preserve resident endpoint/lifetime identity, per-source sequence, ingress receipt identity, review-unit identity, actual request-attempt identity, finding identity and advice batch/attempt identity. Semantic input equality alone does not identify a fresh request. Relations must represent edit fan-out, shared evaluation reuse and many-to-many batch membership.
- Capture observed edited paths, selected root declarations, preparation reads and contributing supporting declarations as distinct facts. Reuse existing preparation provenance; perform no extra source capture or traversal for display and never bypass file selection or protected-path rules.
- Capture the immutable DecisionModel input and the actual encoded provider request body at the transport invocation boundary. Capture applicable questions/criteria, wire-ID mapping, thresholds and configured messages. Preserve exact HTTP-body bytes rather than reconstructing the pinned provider's body later from a serializer or current disk source.
- Distinguish prepared input, authorization, transport invocation and a returned/validated backend result. Transport invocation does not prove remote receipt. Exact-body copy returns retained original bytes; readable/prettified views are labelled separately. Missing, truncated, redacted or rebuilt values cannot be advertised as exact.
- Retain validated classifier answers before finding interpretation and the resulting configured findings. Backend probabilities, threshold decisions, configured messages and formatted agent advice are separate data. Arbitrary response/error bodies and authorization headers are outside capture. Report expected malformed-response failures without logging credentials or arbitrary server content.
- Maintain independent evaluation, provenance/reuse, advice eligibility and submission evidence. One edit can have several completed and unfinished units simultaneously. Reuse routes do not add fresh request counts; notice-only output is distinct from findings.
- Capture formatted advice/runtime envelopes and explicit batch membership. Resident RPC output is prepared handoff material, not proof of a successful hook or native extension write. Record existing writer-boundary evidence through bounded reporting correlated with the batch/attempt. Reporting itself is optional and cannot make a successful edit or submission fail.
- Keep output-written evidence separate from resident acknowledgement. A write interrupted after it may have started is uncertain, not definitely absent. Neither acknowledgement nor successful output proves model visibility or repair. Do not alter runtime-specific blocking authority or feedback wording.

### Feed, resource bounds and local access

- Introduce a bounded asynchronous recording queue and independent writer scope. Review paths must not wait for filesystem persistence, browser delivery, inspection locks or replay. Enqueue only bounded immutable data; avoid full-state serialization inside canonical commits. Drop inspection data on overflow/error rather than applying review backpressure.
- Bound inspection queue bytes/items, individual payloads, journal segments, connections, replay pages and payload transfers. Choose and test internal bounds during implementation; the previously proposed internal numeric limits are not owner-approved requirements. A dropped or oversized payload has an absence reason where that fact was itself captured.
- Use per-source committed journals and a materialized edit projection. A snapshot has a watermark; replay begins strictly after it. Publish payload availability only after the captured object is readable. Retrieval racing eviction returns a typed absence, never unrelated bytes.
- Use an isolated read-only inspection access boundary with independent quotas. Inspection subscribers must not exhaust hook-control IPC slots or occupy review capacity. Prefer a separate private inspection socket; version-one resident IPC may be extended in place only where bounded writer evidence needs to enter the resident.
- The browser-facing HTTP API supplies bounded snapshots, payload retrieval and an SSE feed. Reconnection uses per-source cursors, idempotent replay and snapshot refresh after retained history is insufficient. Source sequence supplies order within a resident lifetime; cross-resident timestamp ordering is a presentation order, not a causal claim.
- Discover the standard per-user endpoint and inspection-enabled additional endpoints through a private bounded registry. Verify user ownership, private endpoint permissions, non-symlink paths and lifetime identity. Support historical store reads after exit. Do not scan arbitrary filesystem locations or accept browser-supplied socket/file paths. “All residents” means all discovered authorized local sources; show known/connected coverage.
- Keep local storage private and outside project directories. Scope access to the current OS user. Serve bundled assets, validate Host/Origin and protect source-bearing API/feed/payload access against unrelated browser origins. Display captured values as text; exclude credentials and external analytics/services. Do not add a data-export subsystem in this feature; exact-body/advice copy is an explicit inspector action.
- Separate known recording-disabled intervals, disconnection, expiry/eviction and loss. A persistent capture failure can also lose its diagnostic; no complete interval census is promised. Show known problems and unavailable coverage without blocking operation or claiming that no edits happened.
- A disconnected endpoint is not automatically a dead resident. Verified retirement or replacement establishes lifetime loss; missing terminal evidence remains unknown, never clear. New lifetime records cannot reuse old process identity accidentally.

### User view and model

- Build an edit-centred list/detail view, reusing compatible visualization controls, typography, disclosures and history-navigation patterns. Existing architecture replay and simulation controls do not become live evidence. Optional reducer diagnostics may reuse checked projection only when actual committed transitions were captured; they are not required for the core inspector.
- Provide edit details for Files, Classifier request, Results, Agent handoff and Timeline. Summaries use explicit units and mixed outcomes rather than a single success badge. Show recording state and last saved event independently of historical coverage.
- Keep selection and reading position stable as new events arrive. Pause display freezes the viewed projection while recording continues; returning to live applies new facts without inventing evicted payloads. Provide accessible keyboard navigation and responsive narrow-screen details.
- Complete the initial Quint state-shape sketch into a bounded executable behaviour model before feature implementation. Model recording enablement, evidence provenance, source lifetime, queue loss, retention, snapshot/replay and handoff uncertainty; preserve separate evaluation and submission lanes. Use sampled simulations/witnesses to falsify design mistakes and report their scope. Do not label the existing type-only sketch verified or require exhaustive model checking as part of this issue.
- Preserve the existing production authority split: Bend owns review decisions; TypeScript records observations and performs native effects. The inspector does not introduce a second production policy reducer. Hapsland-owned persisted/configuration/IPC formats remain version 1 and are updated in place during pre-release.

## Testing Decisions

### Owner-approved primary acceptance boundary

Use one primary external feature boundary: the production dashboard HTTP/feed and rendered inspector, supplied by existing real-resident scenario fixtures and production runtime-adapter/provider/writer paths. Drive edit ingress and supported handoff routes through the existing fixture/harness entry points, control only external classifier responses, clock/retention inputs and failure conditions, and inspect public feed/payload responses and user-visible browser behaviour.

Prefer the existing resident scenario fixture, controlled Effect HttpClient, native-output writer fixtures, process harness and Playwright conventions. Do not introduce a test-only event bus, fake frontend reducer or fabricated inspection history as the sole acceptance source. A small number of installed-process checks establish transport and shutdown boundaries; deterministic fixture-backed coverage handles the richer outcome matrix.

The highest-seam scenarios establish:

1. End-to-end provenance: an attributed edit expands to selected declarations and supporting files, invokes the actual provider serializer with an offline transport, yields validated answers/findings, and produces captured advice through the supported writer boundary. The public inspector links these facts to the correct advicee and shows mixed outcomes truthfully.
2. Byte fidelity: exact-body copy matches the actual captured transport body for Unicode, tabs, CRLF, escapes and trailing newlines. Captured output copy matches the actual writer payload. Prepared-only, unavailable and evicted values never pass as sent or exact.
3. Lifecycle independence: enabled recording produces inspectable history before the HTTP server is launched, while it is stopped, and after it is restarted. Interrupting the server stops only that process and leaves resident review and recording intact.
4. Non-blocking failure: blocked storage, failed writes, a saturated recording queue and a slow/disconnected viewer do not prevent the provider call or supported advice handoff completing under the existing finite process/review deadlines. Exercise a writer that cannot settle while review still progresses, not just a writer that immediately throws.
5. Configuration/coverage: disabled by default, project/user precedence, no source-bearing captures from analytics alone, repeated enable/disable intervals, disabling during in-flight work, preserved earlier history and no retrospective reconstruction.
6. Retention: exact seven-day boundary under a controlled clock, shared 128 MiB allocated-storage cap across multiple residents/projects, oldest-first eviction, concurrent cleanup, read/eviction races and available/missing payload consistency. Pruning cannot delete unrelated directories or follow symlinks.
7. Identity and reuse: separate residents, restarts, projects, runtime sessions and subagents; joined/cached/existing-advice routes without duplicate fresh-request counts; bidirectional edit/finding/batch relations; controlled versus live totals.
8. Reconnect/display: snapshot watermark consistency, repeated records, disconnection/replay, expired cursors, visible known gaps, stable selection, pause/resume and narrow-screen/keyboard operation. Browser arrival and display latency use event-driven readiness and finite test bounds, not ungrounded product latency promises.
9. Truthful handoff: preparation is not submission, successful classification with suppressed advice remains visible, interrupted writes remain uncertain, lost acknowledgements do not erase captured output evidence, and no path labels an agent read/repair as observed without independent host evidence.
10. Local access and shutdown: host/port validation, loopback default, rejection of unsupported direct network exposure, unauthorized-origin handling, bounded public payload access, safe source rendering, and prompt foreground cleanup on interrupt. Merely reading history neither starts residents nor issues classifier requests.

### Focused checks and prior art

- A good test observes externally visible review, request, writer, feed, storage and UI behaviour. It must distinguish plausible failures, not restate the implementation's fields or require arbitrary sleeps.
- Extend existing configuration, resident analytics/reuse/delivery, activity storage, provider HTTP-wire and writer-boundary tests where they already expose the relevant behaviour. Use lower focused seams only when the high boundary cannot isolate a defect efficiently; no extra public API solely for testing.
- Use the existing process harness for actual CLI, IPC and HTTP lifetimes, with finite deadlines, retained failure evidence and physical child cleanup. Browser tests use the existing Playwright conventions against the production-facing server/feed for new-view acceptance, rather than only the developer replay page.
- Tests remain offline and deterministic; controlled provider calls establish serialization and outcome mapping, not live classifier quality. This feature does not require paid Jev validation or native agent sessions to prove its local inspector behaviour.
- Follow the repository testing matrix. Implementation changes require fast TypeScript/configuration checks, focused changed-owner and consumer tests, plus affected process/transport/package integration checks. This cross-component feature has a final declared milestone full gate: it establishes the deterministic suite, authority boundaries and fresh complexity/coverage evidence beyond the focused inspector checks. Freeze the candidate, declare duration/stop time and use the finite runner deadline. Do not wait for GitHub CI as an extra completion gate.
- Complete Quint typechecking, action witnesses and sampled invariants for the new design model. State explicitly that these are model evidence; byte fidelity, access control and native/process behaviour are established by the boundary tests.
- Report design acceptance, deterministic runtime/browser evidence, model-simulation evidence and installed/platform claims separately. No visual implementation has yet been rendered or accepted.

## Out of Scope

- Remote-resident aggregation, direct unauthenticated public/LAN serving, accounts, cloud storage, external telemetry and hosting deployment.
- Foreground-server daemonization, background flags, automatic browser/server launch and a process manager.
- Recording without explicit inspection opt-in, reconstructing disabled intervals, filesystem-wide edit surveillance and guarantees of complete or durable audit history.
- Blocking, retrying or failing review work to make history complete; crash-proof exact event counts or a guaranteed diagnostic for every lost record.
- Proving classifier quality, remote receipt, model visibility, agent agreement, adoption or repair from submission evidence.
- Additional source traversal, full-file backups, edit-diff/transcript collection, excluded-source capture, credentials/authorization headers or arbitrary error-response logging.
- Changing rule semantics, thresholds, file-selection authority, review scheduling, native blocking authority, feedback wording or existing source-free analytics guarantees.
- New agent-runtime/platform support, a data-export/import subsystem, replacement of the developer simulation dashboard, or legacy format/migration paths.

## Further Notes

The owner confirmed the product scope after the design interview and then approved the primary external testing boundary. Defaults are seven days and 128 MiB across the local user’s inspection store; the view starts with all discovered local sources, and the web server runs only in the foreground. Internal queue, payload and segment sizes are bounded implementation choices rather than owner-prescribed values.

An Astra consultation informed the proposed edit-centred UX and the separation of evaluation from submission. It is design advice, not rendered UX acceptance. The existing Quint artifact is a type-only sketch and supplies no checked transition or simulation guarantee.

This issue is the originating implementation specification and is labelled `ready-for-agent`. Update maintained configuration/status/inspection documentation as the feature is implemented. Existing operational analytics and developer architecture replay remain separate owners. The publication does not establish implemented behaviour or installed/platform support.

title: Use one Bend simulation runner for the TypeScript API and native consumers
body:
## Problem

The simulator still has two implementations of top-level execution:

- `packages/monkey-business/src/index.ts`: TypeScript `Run.step`, `beginAdvance`/`advance`, and host orchestration.
- `packages/monkey-business-bend/NativeRun.bend`: Bend `step`/`advance` and orchestration for native consumers.

Both use the same Bend Engine code, Canonical, scheduler and workload generator, but TypeScript `Run` does not delegate execution to `NativeRun.advance`. Sharing individual decisions and comparing selected scenarios does not give us a single owner for the complete event → command → scheduled-result loop. Changes can require parallel fixes and leave consumer-dependent behavior.

## Relationship to existing work

Focused follow-up under #176, which already requires one shared Bend simulator with a thin TypeScript boundary. Coordinate this consolidation with #178–#180 and the scenario slices; #199 owns the game consumer and #200 owns final coverage/removal verification. This issue isolates the remaining duplicated runner; it does not open another simulator project or mark those issues complete.

## Required change

Use one Bend implementation for simulation execution, called directly by Bend consumers and through compiler-emitted JavaScript by the public TypeScript API. Extend/consolidate the existing shared runner rather than introduce a parallel replacement API.

The common owner must handle input consumption, virtual-time progression, command interpretation, scheduling resulting events, and the applicable scenario state transitions. Keep TypeScript responsible for validated API conversion, integration with its host environment and presentation-facing adaptation. Replay orchestration may call the common runner, but must not independently implement its scheduling or business execution rules.

First identify differences between the two current runners and the public API obligations. Do not assume NativeRun already covers every supported TypeScript behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Public `Run.step` and bounded `advance`, and native consumers, execute through the same Bend implementation. A renamed wrapper around the existing TS execution loop does not satisfy this.
- [ ] Preserve the public `createRun`, `step`, `advance`, `applyControl`, `schedule`, `observe`, `subscribe`, replay export and reconstruction contracts, including supported scenarios and immutable observations.
- [ ] Preserve equal-time ordering, finite advancement, rejection behavior, callback identity/freshness, captured deadlines, controls, independent random streams and state-preserving recovery. Preserve the distinction between queue takes and product observations, including metadata-only progress.
- [ ] Preserve exact replay endpoints and ordering of controls, listener-triggered controls and advance normalization. Retain format 1 and source-identity checks; do not add a legacy runner or migration shim to accept incompatible recordings.
- [ ] Check independently expected intermediate and terminal behavior from existing contracts, plus native/emitted-JS agreement. Preserve existing applicable scenario coverage instead of relying only on two wrappers calling the same implementation.
- [ ] Validate affected dashboard playback/step/pause/seek/replay and the native game consumer. The common runner and dashboard remain usable with the optional game absent.
- [ ] Delete superseded TS simulation execution logic and obsolete wrappers. Update the maintained package guidance, navigation and testing matrix to identify the one runner and the remaining adapter responsibilities.

## Validation and boundaries

Choose required local checks from `docs/testing-matrix.md`: `npm run check:fast`, focused simulator/adapter/replay tests, affected browser consumer checks, and applicable finite native/emitted-JS comparisons. Include affected generated-artifact/build checks and `node scripts/run-game-consumer.mjs` for the game integration. State the evidence scope and finite deadline before long runs. Follow the repository criteria for selecting any full gate; completion depends on the required local checks, not waiting for CI.

This is consolidation of simulator execution. It does not change production review/advice policy, move real resident I/O into the simulator, or introduce gameplay changes. No universal proof of simulator correctness or new platform-support claim is implied by the consolidation.

title: Investigate same-time edit requeueing after round opening
body:
## Problem

In the simulator's base edit path without edit-permit settings, `Driver.edit` returns `OpenRound` and `retry: true` when no round exists. The TypeScript `Run` queues `OpenRound` followed by the original edit at the same virtual time, marking the retry `recurring: false`. `NativeRun` also requeues the original job. Once the round exists, the driver emits `AdmitObservation`.

This introduces orchestration and an observable intermediate boundary. The rationale for requeueing instead of an explicit continuation or a composed reducer transition needs investigation.

## Scope

Investigate and recommend. This issue does not pre-approve a change to reducer semantics or require removal of the retry.

## Questions

- Trace both TypeScript and native paths, including which owner changes generator, scheduler, pending-opening, and Canonical state.
- Which requirements depend on separating round opening from observation admission? Which depend specifically on requeueing the original edit?
- Compare the current mechanism with an explicit continuation without requeueing and a composed core operation. Inspect the existing `consumePermit` round-opening path as a comparison, without assuming it is equivalent to observation admission.
- Examine rejected opening and round limits, multiple edits at the same timestamp, pending-opening deduplication, activity/lifetime invalidation, preservation of original source facts, and prevention of duplicate workload generation.
- Determine whether progress remains bounded when opening continues to fail.
- Identify effects on same-time ordering, intermediate observations, replay/checkpoints, and business guarantees. Distinguish semantic equivalence from deliberately changed behavior.

## Deliverables

- A scoped call/state trace and comparison of alternatives.
- Bounded deterministic evidence for cases that distinguish the alternatives, with independent expected outcomes rather than implementation agreement alone.
- A recommendation to retain or simplify the mechanism, with concrete tradeoffs, affected owners, and focused validation required for any follow-up implementation.

Preserve existing required scenario scope. No format-version bump or parallel legacy path is implied. Record findings in this issue or an existing owner document; a new report file is not required.

## Starting points

- `packages/monkey-business-bend/Driver.bend`: `edit_round`, `edit`.
- `packages/monkey-business-bend/AdmissionAttempts.bend`: pending-opening bookkeeping.
- `packages/monkey-business-bend/NativeRun.bend`: `edit_planned`, `retry_edit`.
- `packages/monkey-business/src/index.ts`: the no-round edit branch in `Run.step`.
- `packages/monkey-business/src/outcomes.test.ts`: original source tuple and replay across the same-time retry.
- `packages/agent-flow-bend/Canonical.bend`: opening, observation admission, and permit consumption.

Related: #176.

title: Investigate simulator preparation workspace accounting
body:
The simulator currently configures preparation reservation bytes independently of its generated file tree and traversal facts. Production derives an initial logical workspace reservation with `captureWorkspaceBytes` and resizes it with `analysisWorkspaceBytes`.

Investigate how generated sources, graph facts, preparation reservations, and resulting review-unit sizes should relate so the simulation represents the same business resource accounting. Compare the TS Run and Bend NativeRun paths, including tower defence.

Deliver a short recommendation in this issue: current gaps, intended ownership, which production calculations to reuse or model, and focused acceptance examples for capacity admission/refusal and release. Research only; implementation follows a separate decision.

title: Separate action requests from result events in canonical outputs
body:
`Canonical.Command` mixes requests to perform an action (`Prepare`) with facts about changes already committed by the reducer (`PreparationReleased`, `UnitAdmitted`). This obscures the domain contract and encourages consumers to treat notifications as instructions.

Separate action requests from result/domain events in the core output contract. Audit every variant by its semantics, not just its name; decide where any other output categories belong. Update Bend and TypeScript boundaries, production consumers, both simulator runners, and tower-defence consumers as affected.

Acceptance:
- Types and names distinguish requested actions from already-established facts.
- Consumers react to facts without reapplying the state changes they report.
- Preserve transition behavior, output ordering, and deterministic replay; remove the superseded mixed contract in place.
- Update affected documentation and run the focused checks required by the testing matrix.

title: Specify and verify game projection laws for identity, branching, queues, and scheduled work
body:
## Problem

The current motion-law work establishes bounded discrete movement and preservation of selected actor fields. It does not establish that the complete game projection faithfully represents simulator events, scheduled work, queues, or branching.

We need laws for the mapping from simulator state and events to visible actors. A mob is a presentation identity associated with domain state; it is not necessarily one work item throughout splitting and merging.

## Relationship to #234

Related to #234, specifically its [configuration-semantics and dashboard follow-up](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/234#issuecomment-6005910691).

That follow-up investigates when settings are captured and which scheduled facts survive configuration changes. This issue owns the game projection of those facts, including actor identity and lifecycle. Use the resulting scheduling contract rather than inventing a second execution model in the game. Coordinate with #199 for the game consumer.

The discrete movement foundation is on branch `task/game-motion-laws`, commit `a78cac5e`: five state laws checked by Bend and its kernel, nine source-lowered arithmetic laws checked by Lean, and fourteen rejected mutants. The U32 language correspondence remains trusted. This evidence does not prove the full game mapping or calendar agreement.

## Proposed work

First trace actual implementation owners and representative event sequences. Distinguish simulator facts, projection state, visual movement, and renderer artifacts. Propose precise laws with premises and proof boundaries before implementing proofs.

Investigate these candidate properties; they are not yet approved laws:

- **Identity and lifecycle:** unchanged logical presentation entities retain identity and position across observations; actors are created, replaced, and retired only by explicit mapping transitions. Distinguish intentional overlapping representations from stale ghost copies.
- **Branching and merging:** multiplicity and provenance match actual domain transitions. Cover preparing/review-unit creation, concurrent Jev requests, per-rule visual fragments, clear results, and findings. Do not equate request concurrency, rule count, review-unit count, and finding count.
- **Queue representation:** distinguish waiting, admitted, executing, and completed work. Show the actual reason for waiting; do not invent a known release time where the simulator has not scheduled one.
- **Calendar agreement:** once an applicable deadline is captured, show its relationship to operation progress and completion. Define what happens if the deadline arrives before the visual route finishes, and what happens after a supported rescheduling control. Avoid silently making game travel a second authority over simulator execution.
- **Projection continuity:** extend the existing local movement guarantees through observation ingestion, waypoint changes, queue transitions, and split/merge boundaries. State explicitly where continuity is required and where a new actor identity may begin.

Conditional progress guarantees must name their fairness, resource, and event-delivery assumptions. Do not claim eventual completion for permanently blocked work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Identify the executable owners and propose a reviewed law inventory, including assumptions and exclusions.
- [ ] Trace concrete cases for ghost copies, preparing multiplicity, clear/finding branching, queue waits, and staggered completion inside Jev. Identify real defects separately from valid but confusing behavior.
- [ ] Demonstrate that native gameplay executes the implementation covered by the laws; distinguish renderer checks from state-core proofs.
- [ ] Prove approved properties where practical, and clearly label bounded tests or runtime evidence where universal proof is unavailable.
- [ ] Reject meaningful mutants for identity/lifecycle, multiplicity, and calendar projection; include consumer checks for any changed wiring.
- [ ] Fix demonstrated game-projection defects without duplicating scheduling or business rules. Changes to simulator scheduling semantics belong with #234 or an explicitly coordinated owner.
- [ ] Document the resulting guarantees and remaining trust boundaries in the existing game guidance; keep game/lab/proof checks optional for production releases.

## Validation boundaries

Select focused local checks from `docs/testing-matrix.md` according to the changed owners. Use finite proof and execution deadlines. Include applicable native/emitted-JS integration and visual traces when their boundaries change. Passing local motion laws alone does not establish full projection correctness, continuous render interpolation, queue liveness, or native platform qualification.

This issue concerns faithful game presentation, not tower balancing, new tower abilities, or a general proof of simulator correctness.

title: Add standalone file and line rule checks
body:
## Summary

Users can test an enabled rule against a file and one-based line without an agent edit or resident.

```text
hapsland rules check --path FILE --line N [--id RULE] [--json]
  select one enclosing supported declaration
  prepare bounded related code using the shared review pipeline
  discover the configured classifier key using the existing credential service
  return probabilities, thresholds, findings and selection diagnostics
```

Ambiguous selections, excluded files and missing evidence do not dispatch a request. Source changes invalidate results. JSON includes the captured classifier input; help explicitly explains external calls and possible charges. Exit 0 means evaluated, including findings; exit 6 means skipped or unavailable.

README now answers “What leaves my repository?” and “Does my rule work?”, including dashboard recording through `sessionInspection`. A linked “Write your first rule” walkthrough starts with the editable defaults, covers CLI creation or adding a hand-written JSON file, and tests `no-primitive-obsession` with bare domain IDs versus distinct ID types. The example links Refactoring.Guru, notes the existing `bare_domain_value` default, and replaces the removed delivery-specific example. The existing marked Markdown generator derives default counts and IDs, command examples, configuration fields, exit codes, validated example JSON and source-line coordinates from their code owners; the pre-commit `config:check` rejects stale output. `rules create` now writes a `.jsonc` starter with short comments explaining type/function inputs and evidence options; both `.json` and `.jsonc` rules use the existing JSONC loader. Rule docs, help and messages use enabled/disabled terminology and omit connected qualifiers. Generated CLI documentation and the website’s rules link are updated. README and docs remove redundant “supported”/“bounded” qualifiers and name concrete eligibility, size, retention and deadline restrictions where needed; Astra reviewed the substitutions.

## Evidence

- **Before:** checking a custom rule required an eligible agent edit; no standalone file/line command was available.
  **After:** CLI tests exercise standalone selection without stdin, resident state or an agent session. Offline transport tests cover exact shared input, type/function selection, Rust/Bend declarations, threshold behavior, normal key discovery, stale source, missing evidence and ambiguous lines—including multiple roots with only one enabled rule.
- Focused tests passed for the checker, CLI, shared preparation/graph/parser boundaries, provider execution, import boundaries and generated documentation. Astra’s targeted development-experience review found no remaining blocker.
- Documentation follow-up: verified the walkthrough’s create/edit/enable/show/explain commands, authored JSON and both example line selections (2 and 10), including required related-type evidence, in an isolated Git fixture without classifier requests. Astra reviewed the walkthrough and file/line section; corrected working-directory and credential-lookup wording. Astra also approved the replacement primitive-obsession example. `npm run docs:check` and `npm run config:check` passed.
- `npm run check:fast`, `npm run docs:check`, build typechecking and website typechecking passed.
- Website scenario assertions passed with Vite’s native config loader. The standard runner hit a Vite/Rolldown config-bundling error; its normal invocation is not claimed to pass.
- Classifier tests use an offline fake transport; no live classifier validation or full-project coverage claim.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

No format migration or persistent state change. The new command sends source to the configured classifier when explicitly invoked; JSON output is source-bearing.

**Blast Radius:** review

Source preparation and evaluation are shared with agent hooks. Existing hook preparation retains its original advicee, and focused hook/consumer tests passed.

title: Review and clean up default rules with weak or noisy findings
body:
## Problem

Some shipped default rules have not demonstrated useful findings in our recorded examples. Review their inclusion and wording before presenting them as reliable defaults or using them in CLI help and onboarding.

The clearest candidate is `r1_inferred_case`: the compact matrix recorded **0/6 defects detected, 0/3 clean warnings and 0/2 checked repairs**. All six defective observations stayed below the finding threshold. This is evidence about these selected synthetic examples, not proof the rule never works.

## Recorded evidence

[Per-rule execution evidence](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/44966bdb/evidence/function-resource-native-current/effective-comparison.json) separates detection from native repair:

| Rule | Defects detected /6 | Clean warnings /3 | Checked repairs /2 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `r1_inferred_case` | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `r3_split_correlations` | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| `r5_absence_confusion` | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| `r8_name_claims_resource` | 6 | 0 | 0 |
| `r7_name_wider_than_type` | 6 | 0 | 2 |
| `r9_body_reaches_undeclared` | 6 | 0 | 2 |

Zero checked repairs is not zero useful findings. Investigate question quality, evidence availability, actionable feedback and agent adoption separately. In particular, `r3` succeeded in the separate larger map-camera examples, so the compact repair result alone does not justify removing it.

Also inspect `r4_duplicate_fact` for noisy findings: its separate compact matrix detected 12/12 defects and produced 12/12 checked repairs, but warned on 6/6 clean observations. Its larger attachment-manifest examples had no clean warnings. Do not pool different fixture batches or count repeated observations as independent examples.

Supporting records: [compact per-rule account](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/44966bdb/docs/abide-contextual-review-study.md#results-by-rule), [separate duplicate-fact matrix](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/44966bdb/evidence/abide-contextual-current/comparison.json), [larger examples and counterexamples](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/44966bdb/docs/abide-large-declaration-study.md#results).

## Requested cleanup

- Start with `r1_inferred_case`. Decide whether to rewrite/narrow its question and criteria, disable it by default, or remove it from the shipped defaults. Identify concrete examples that demonstrate its unique acceptance value; avoid retaining it solely to preserve the nine-rule count.
- Review the other weak/noisy results above, distinguishing detection failures, false warnings, missing evidence and failure to repair. Record a disposition for each; do not automatically remove rules because an agent did not adopt valid feedback.
- Evaluate proposed revisions against predefined positive, negative and edge-case examples. Retain unfavorable outcomes and report detection, clean warnings and repair separately. Do not lower thresholds merely to manufacture success.
- Update affected shipped JSON, default provisioning, generated inventories/tests, default counts, CLI examples and maintained docs. Remove superseded production definitions rather than adding parallel legacy variants. Do not silently overwrite user-edited rule files.

## Acceptance

Each reviewed rule has an evidence-backed disposition and an explicit supported concern. Rules retained as active defaults demonstrate useful findings without unexplained systematic clean warnings in the selected validation set. Removed or revised defaults are reflected consistently in setup, tests and user-facing documentation; required focused local checks pass. Historical execution evidence remains clearly distinguished from validation of revised rules.

This issue authorizes a cleanup investigation and implementation, not a claim of general classifier accuracy. Keep Hapsland-owned formats at version 1.

title: Improve installation usability and fix native package preparation
body:
## Summary

Make the installation guide lead with the available local checkout workflow while the public npm package returns 404. Explain prerequisites, supported clients, user-wide hooks, credential sources, retained executable paths, and troubleshooting; include Pi consistently in the client guides.

```diff
 native parser binding selection
- choose the first existing local/retained/published binary
+ choose the first binary matching the target OS and architecture

 macOS package fixtures
- compare /var paths with canonical /private/var paths
+ canonicalize the temporary fixture root
```

A Linux dependency binding previously overwrote the maintained macOS binding during source builds. Rejecting foreign binaries preserves the valid target artifact. Canonical fixture roots also prevent false rule-path and resident-ownership failures.

## Evidence

- **Before:** the native-selection regression chose a Linux binary for macOS; source packaging then failed its parser load probe.
  **After:** `node --test scripts/native-artifact-selection.test.mjs scripts/native-bindings.test.mjs` passes; the native build and release artifact verification pass.
- **Before:** macOS package setup failed the editable-rule path assertion, and the clean-package runner failed resident cleanup because `/var` and `/private/var` differed.
  **After:** both runners pass against the freshly built local development archive using npm installation. Setup passes seven journeys with zero provider calls. Clean-package checks pass installed parser/resident/hooks, controlled review, local update, recovery, scoped removal, and Rust/Bend supporting-code expansion.
- `npm run docs:check` and `npm run check:fast` pass. Focused boundary verification passes 103 Vitest tests (four skipped), plus two Node checks.
- Broader exploratory checks exposed 26 installation fixture failures and one doctor credential-isolation failure; those fixtures are not repaired by this PR. No full-project quality gate, real-agent trial, paid Jev trial, native credential lifecycle trial, or registry release validation is claimed.
- The clean-package run skips native credential lifecycle. Earlier audit checks included saved-credential lookup paths; this work does not establish that the user's Keychain was never read. Repeated Keychain prompts remain an unresolved usability issue.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Documentation and build/test tooling changes can be reverted; no configuration format or installed hook behavior changes.

**Blast Radius:** packaging

Native candidate selection now rejects foreign-format or wrong-architecture bindings. Header checks do not replace the existing parser load probe. macOS/Linux platform advertising still requires its separate evidence.

title: Integrate explicit CLI interactions and replay diagrams
body:
## Summary

Start production integration of #244 using the accepted Effect approach and the owners delivered by #243.

```text
Administration Interaction service + scoped terminal session
├── Agent selection: guarded Continue, installed defaults, Escape/Exit
├── Credential capture: built-in Prompt.Hidden, scoped TTY, redacted cleanup
├── Login: availability → hidden input → native credential owner
├── Maintenance: inspect recovery → per-agent approval → apply/activate
├── Update: discover → preview all → group approval → apply/activate per agent
├── Rules: scope → preview → full-line approval → existing rule owner
│   └── stale digest → fresh preview and fresh approval
└── Production replay → Mermaid MD + source-current freshness check
```

This integration replaces the old agent selector, custom secret reader and rule confirmation path, preserves full-line exactly-y approval and unattended rule behavior, and keeps revisions, command identity and owner digests separate. Ctrl+C retains interrupt identity at the session boundary. Diagram commands refresh compiler outputs through #243's workspace build before replay, including on a checkout without `dist`.

The branch also retains the six-workflow prototype and advisory research, and repairs Darwin build receipt evidence using actual dyld library resolution while preserving Linux ldd observation. #241/#243 are integrated from master. #248 tracks the separately requested project/user credential destinations; #244 retains current credential storage behavior.

Setup/pilot and verification production reducers, the single overall administration Effect runtime, remaining production diagrams, source/installed Linux execution, final quality qualification and prototype cleanup remain pending. The PR stays draft. After integration and required validation, consolidate adopted contracts/tests/generators and delete superseded prototypes and temporary evidence.

## Evidence

- Latest master through `c08754c9` is integrated (merge `87c34e76`). Post-merge `check:fast`, 51 focused login/rules/root-routing tests and six credential-guard/standalone-environment tests pass.

- **Before:** Enter with an empty initial selection could exit; rules used the old confirmation path.
  **After:** guarded Continue, installed defaults, Back without writes, exact-y approval, stale-plan reapproval and headless rules contracts pass focused tests.
- `check:fast` and 27 focused tests pass across rules CLI/conversation, selection, session and terminal transport. `docs:check` passes after cleaning all 23 production owners' compiler outputs. Five independently asserted production interpreter replays generate the rules diagram.
- **Before review fixes:** raw-mode Ctrl+C returned exit 0; diagram checks could replay stale `dist`; an obsolete formatter remained.
  **After:** pinned Bun 1.3.14 native PTY witnesses return Ctrl+C=130 and Escape=0 with terminal settings restored. A temporary reducer source mutation makes the public diagram check fail without modifying MD; restored source checks successfully. The obsolete formatter and its old-only assertions are removed. One Astra review pass ran across separate Standards and Spec axes.
- Credential capture now uses built-in `Prompt.Hidden`; cancellation still exits. `check:fast`, 66 affected source/CLI tests and `docs:check` pass. Five source-guard tests pass after repairing their pre-existing package-path fixture mismatch; mutations witness rejection of unredacted input, removed cleanup and a replaced built-in hidden prompt.
- Eight native macOS Bun 1.3.14 PTY cases cover Enter/Escape/Ctrl+C/Ctrl+D with redirected stdin, and the same cases with redirected stderr and `TERM=dumb`. Keys are absent from output; terminal settings are restored, accounting only for Darwin's documented transient PENDIN state. Hidden input remains interruptible, while acquired redacted wrappers are released. Separate Astra Standards and Spec reviews found no issues in this credential-entry stage.
- Login now runs through a production reducer and Effect owner service, preserving the native owner and explicit stdin behavior. `check:fast`, 24 focused login/capture/CLI tests and `docs:check` pass. Five independently asserted login replays retain stored/busy/indeterminate outcomes and cancellation without a save; keys stay out of models, transitions and Mermaid. One Astra review pass identified inherited input-error cancellation and a generator-finally cleanup issue; explicit cancellation typing and Effect.ensuring repair both, with focused regressions passing.
- Grouped update now uses its production reducer, native Effect owner service and shared input session. Nine independently asserted production replays cover approval, decline, Back/Exit, EOF, current, partial, activation failure, busy and indeterminate results. Mutation outcomes remain distinct from activation outcomes. 149 focused tests across 13 affected files passed; `docs:check` passed with all three production diagrams current. Static complexity analysis reports zero guaranteed CRAP failures; this is not coverage qualification. One Astra review pass found no Standards issues and one Spec issue: nonterminal update lost its automation guidance before session acquisition. An early terminal check and source CLI/PTY regressions address it; the final fast gate and all 42 update/interactive tests passed in 57 seconds.
- Maintenance now runs repair, reinstall and uninstall through its production reducer and Effect owner service. Per-agent consent forwards the actual owner digest; inspected recovery operations and no-change/uninstall/empty-reinstall exceptions are preserved. Observed mutation results remain distinct from activation. The fast gate and 59 focused maintenance/CLI tests pass, including native source PTY uninstall approval/decline with an unrelated profile preserved. Thirteen independently asserted interpreter replays generate the maintenance diagram; `docs:check` passes for all four production diagrams. One Astra review pass found no Standards or Spec issues in this stage. The user-supplied task/batch acceptance policy patch is integrated into current AGENTS/CHECKS/testing-matrix guidance.
- Existing isolated prototype qualification passed all six synthetic workflow families, source/compiled PTY cases and diagram freshness checks. This remains prototype evidence.
- Darwin build/toolchain receipt fixes passed real macOS builds and focused receipt tests. Linux ARM64 toolchain observation and Linux library tests passed; these do not establish complete Linux product execution.

Validation uses controlled inputs and isolated repository fixtures. No real credential-store access or paid provider requests were performed. No full production quality-gate or completed #244 claim is made.

See [production maintenance diagram](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/research/setup-interaction-model/docs/cli-interactions/maintenance.md), [production update diagram](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/research/setup-interaction-model/docs/cli-interactions/update.md), [production login diagram](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/research/setup-interaction-model/docs/cli-interactions/login.md), [production rules diagram](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/research/setup-interaction-model/docs/cli-interactions/rules.md) and [prototype commands and evidence](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/research/setup-interaction-model/prototypes/setup-interaction/README.md).

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Code changes are reversible; existing rule owners remain the authority for user-approved writes. No persisted-format migration is introduced. Keep this draft until #244 integration and required validation are complete.

**Blast Radius:** administration

Interactive setup selection, credential entry, grouped update, maintenance and rule editing, shared input lifetime, generated documentation checks, and native build receipt tooling. Remaining production conversation paths retain their current behavior until their integration stages.

title: Separate hook runtime from setup with cached dependency-aware builds
body:
## Problem Statement

Hapsland's administration and hook handling currently share a CLI source closure. A frequently invoked hook can reach setup, credential mutation and other administration concerns, even when a bundler removes unused exports. Contributors also need dependency-aware compilation and executable assembly so an administration edit does not rebuild unrelated runtime components. A folder or package layout alone cannot establish either isolation or build correctness.

## Solution

Separate the installed hook entry and its allowed dependency closure from administration/setup while preserving one installable release, standalone Bun runtime components, existing agent-runtime behavior and compatible resident reuse. Adopt a simple, enforced dependency declaration and an incremental, cached build workflow for development and production. Preserve domain ownership and vertical capabilities through architectural-agent reviews at implementation milestones.

## User Stories

1. As a Hapsland user, I want hooks to run through a dedicated standalone Bun executable, so that frequent hook invocation retains the chosen runtime and avoids administration initialization.
2. As a Hapsland user, I want one installable release containing the required components, so that separation does not introduce manual package coordination.
3. As a Hapsland user, I want setup and update to register the correct retained-release hook paths, so that installed integrations continue to execute the intended release.
4. As a Hapsland user, I want repair and diagnostics to understand the separated components, so that installation problems remain actionable.
5. As a Claude Code user, I want existing edit and finish behavior preserved, so that restructuring does not change accepted response authority.
6. As a Codex CLI user, I want existing edit and finish behavior preserved, so that restructuring does not change attribution or advice delivery.
7. As a Pi user, I want native extension assets and transport preserved, so that the host-loaded integration continues working with the packaged runtime.
8. As a Hapsland user, I want compatible resident reuse preserved across installations and worktrees, so that restructuring does not fragment review state.
9. As a Hapsland user, I want hooks to read the required runtime settings and credentials without importing credential-management operations, so that read-only execution has a clear dependency boundary.
10. As a Hapsland user, I want concise operating-system and architecture guidance with evidence status, so that I can distinguish intended distribution from verified compatibility.
11. As a contributor, I want an administration-only edit to compile and assemble only affected components, so that unrelated hook, resident and parser builds are reused.
12. As a contributor, I want missing or stale dependencies built before their consumers, so that package builds never consume obsolete output.
13. As a contributor, I want shared runtime implementation changes reflected in every executable embedding them, so that unchanged declarations do not conceal stale runtime code.
14. As a contributor, I want public-type changes checked in affected consumers, so that incompatible interfaces fail before publication.
15. As a contributor, I want development watch and production builds to use consistent dependencies, so that working development output matches production behavior.
16. As a contributor, I want watch mode to reject failures and recover with current output, so that errors do not silently leave a publishable stale result.
17. As a contributor, I want unchanged builds to reuse cached task outputs, so that repeated work avoids unnecessary compiler and assembly processes.
18. As a contributor, I want cached outputs restored after deletion, so that caching provides usable artifacts rather than only replayed success logs.
19. As a contributor, I want cache invalidation to account for dependencies, build adapters, toolchain and platform changes, so that cache hits cannot return incompatible or stale executables.
20. As a contributor, I want dependency declarations in the simplest and most elegant single authority, so that maintaining the build graph does not require parallel hand-written graphs.
21. As a contributor, I want undeclared imports and disagreement between declarations and derived graphs rejected, so that conventions cannot silently drift.
22. As a contributor, I want static, transitive, lazy, aliased and type-only imports included in boundary enforcement, so that an apparently small entry cannot conceal forbidden ownership.
23. As a contributor, I want unaccounted loader targets and unsupported analysis rejected, so that missing evidence does not masquerade as isolation.
24. As an implementer, I want shared types and code owned by genuine domain concepts, so that sharing does not accumulate in an omnibus common package.
25. As an implementer, I want vertical capabilities retained across their process and package boundaries, so that feature ownership remains understandable after extraction.
26. As an architectural reviewer, I want to review actual structure and dependency direction at each milestone, so that the final packages comply with domain design and agreed requirements.
27. As the project owner, I want tooling selections and proposed or revised architectural decisions presented at milestones before dependent integration, so that their rationale, evidence and trade-offs are visible.
28. As a maintainer, I want superseded routing, build paths and temporary documents removed after consolidation, so that contributors have one current implementation and contract owner.

29. As a Hapsland user, I want the old and separated installed hook startup times compared on the same system, so that the claimed performance benefit is measured rather than inferred from a smaller dependency graph.

## Implementation Decisions

- Keep Bun as the runtime for standalone Hapsland executables, particularly the user's hook executable. Preserve host-loaded Pi assets and platform-specific native helpers within one release. This is a runtime/distribution decision, not a new latency or platform-support claim.
- Create a dedicated hook composition entry. Its transitive source closure and emitted runtime contributions must exclude administration, installation/mutation and review-provider execution. Lazy loading does not make a forbidden owner permissible. Share permitted resident IPC and read-only runtime inputs through explicit interfaces. Apply this source-ownership boundary to every maintained host-loaded hook execution entry, including Pi; validate emitted contributions using each surface's actual compiler, resolution conditions and runtime packaging. Preserve host-loaded assets' existing runtime requirements; Pi's extension does not become a Bun executable.
- Split credential reading from login, logout and credential mutation where the current mixed ownership would violate the hook closure. Preserve existing credential precedence and accepted installation behavior.
- Before extraction, inventory every maintained hook-facing command, event variant, registration and asset against its current accepted contract owner. Map each to its replacement entry and behavioral test, covering applicable direct, composed, background, before, stop and prompt flows and all maintained agent runtimes. Identify obsolete or provisional paths explicitly; preservation or removal follows their current contract rather than a legacy filename. Validate the inventory after installation and updates.
- Preserve existing resident/Bend policy and state authority, compatible resident IPC/reuse, parsing ownership and review/advice contracts. Preserve current Claude response authority and Codex/Pi runtime behavior; the restructuring does not amend them.
- The finer structure is a recommendation: administration, hook, resident, parser and doctor composition roots plus Pi extension assets; domain packages for setup, hook runtime, resident client, review execution, read-only inputs and cross-boundary contracts; one release assembly. Actual names, package count and folder/package seams remain implementer/reviewer decisions.
- Preserve vertical capabilities: onboarding, rule management, review/advice across processes, inspection, activity/status and evaluation. Composition roots wire capabilities; shared implementation must have a domain owner rather than displacing feature ownership into generic buckets.
- Domain-wide shared concepts may justify a shared package. Concepts shared by only particular consumers or a domain sub-area may justify a narrower package. Type-only usage does not justify importing a forbidden administration owner. Implementers and architectural reviewers converge on shared package names, scopes and dependencies.
- Prefer package manifests as the single dependency authority, based on the prototype. Derive/check TypeScript references and scheduler relationships from that authority. A central typed graph remains permissible only if evidence shows it is simpler or more reliable. Require agreement with actual source imports and build inputs; no separately maintained competing graph.
- Carry Turborepo as the first orchestration candidate. Nx is excluded. Keep workspace/tooling decisions distinct from retaining Bun. Before integration, notify the owner of the selected tooling, rationale, evidence, trade-offs and unresolved limits; the prototype recommendation is not unconditional adoption.
- Compile dependency packages before consumers and assemble standalone executables from current emitted JavaScript. Distinguish package compilation, consumer type checking, executable assembly and task-cache hits. Shared implementation changes invalidate embedded executable consumers even when declarations remain unchanged.
- Production adoption requires caching. Prove warm task hits, restoration of missing outputs and invalidation for source, dependency/interface, manifest/export, build-adapter, relevant environment, toolchain, platform and target changes. Ensure cache hits preserve boundary checks and cannot publish stale or failed artifacts. Relevant cache identities must also include boundary policies, checker/resolver versions and options, generated dependency/reference configuration and native/host-loaded asset inputs. Cached isolation results must identify the source closure, build configuration and artifact inventory they validate. Reject or regenerate invalid evidence before publication. Remote caching is optional, not a prerequisite.
- Integrate isolation enforcement into ordinary build/publication, including cached paths. Select the smallest reliable checker after comparison with relevant Turbo boundary facilities and the prototype source-checking candidate. Account for compiler inputs and emitted contributions separately from source ownership; unsupported analysis or unaccounted loader targets must fail rather than silently omit an edge.
- Capture the current installed Bun hook baseline before extraction and compare it with the separated hook using the same Bun version, platform, fixture and timing method. Include the real installed launcher path. Distinguish process launch-to-handler readiness, completed hook invocation against a ready resident, and invocation requiring resident startup. Build speed, executable size and a synthetic entry are not substitutes for installed startup measurements. Preserve hook protocol/output and keep timing observation outside its response channel.
- Run an architectural-agent review specifically of package/folder structure at dependency extraction, executable separation, build integration and installed-validation milestones. Review actual imports, domain scopes, shared concepts, vertical capabilities, resident/Bend authority and isolation. Record findings and disposition; tests do not replace structural review. For each shared package record its domain concept, actual consumers, allowed dependency direction and capability contract/test owner. At every milestone, present any proposed or revised architectural decisions to the owner with scope, rationale, alternatives, evidence, trade-offs and unresolved limitations before dependent integration proceeds. State explicitly when no architectural decision changed. Required owner decisions remain pending until answered; do not treat elapsed time or a passing test as acceptance.
- Update launcher routing, owned hook registrations, retained-release paths, release inventory and affected integration fixtures together. Remove superseded shared-CLI hook routing and build paths rather than retaining compatibility shims without an accepted contract requirement.
- Keep existing installation/platform documentation concise. Record OS/architecture/version bounds and validation status, including the standalone Bun hook choice for performance and controlled runtime compatibility. Do not infer new support from cross-compilation.
- A provisional sequence is dependency mapping/extraction, dedicated hook entry, build/cache/enforcement integration and installed validation. Implementers may refine milestones with reviewers while preserving these requirements. Complete tooling validation before adopting its production structure.

## Testing Decisions
