- Prefer the existing installed-release/package boundary as the highest shared behavioral seam: build and pack the real product, install into isolated homes, run ordinary setup/update/repair/diagnostics, inspect owned registrations and exercise installed hook routing and resident communication. Reuse existing clean-package, setup-package, installed-release and runtime-adapter fixtures.
- Add one build-workflow acceptance harness around ordinary development/watch and production build commands. Verify emitted output freshness, actual executable behavior, unchanged unrelated artifacts, cache restoration, failed publication and dependency rejection. Do not make internal task counts or a synthetic package layout the behavioral contract.
- Reuse focused domain tests for owners and affected consumers; do not replace resident protocol, canonical authority, rule, inspection or delivery tests with a new low-level abstraction. Keep ordinary validation deterministic and offline.
- Build cases: clean dependency ordering; no-op; administration-only change; shared implementation with unchanged declarations; used public-type incompatibility and repair; delete/rename; missing outputs; upstream failure; manifest/export change; watch error/drift rejection and recovery. Account separately for emitted projects, assembled executables and cache hits.
- Cache cases: warm repeats; deleted emitted/executable outputs restored; source/dependency/toolchain/adapter/target changes miss correctly; failed or incomplete work cannot create a reusable successful result; cached tasks cannot bypass source isolation or declaration-drift rejection. Validate current artifact behavior after restoration, not just cached logs. Include warm-cache boundary-policy/checker/resolver/generated-configuration changes, undeclared-edge mutation, and corrupted or incomplete restored artifacts; invalid evidence cannot permit publication.
- Isolation cases: allowed domain-owned shared types/code and forbidden direct/transitive/reexport/literal-lazy/aliased/type-only dependencies. Include computed/generic/aliased loaders, unsupported syntax and literal edges omitted by the analyzer. Check source ownership, actual Bun compilation inputs and emitted contributions; use selected executable sentinels without claiming a complete executable-byte inventory. Exercise package subpath/conditional exports, aliases and actual development/production resolver conditions; reject a forbidden branch selected by any supported configuration. Explain expected graph differences from erased type-only imports and tree shaking: agreement means every relevant edge or contribution is accounted for and authorized, not identical graph membership. Cover both standalone hook and host-loaded hook execution surfaces.
- Installed hook performance uses the existing installed-package seam and prior installed startup-comparison approach, adapted for the current Bun baseline and dedicated Bun hook. Before execution, declare exact artifact identities, environment, clock method, sample counts, warm-up treatment, deadline and comparison criteria. Interleave baseline/candidate runs on the same host to reduce time-order bias; use a new hook process per sample and measure warm/ready-resident and fresh-resident cases separately. Fresh resident is not a cold OS file cache; record file-cache conditions without assuming control. Record the resident executable identity and prove whether each sample reused a ready resident or started a fresh one, so compatible cross-release reuse cannot confound the comparison. Retain failures/timeouts and report absolute timings, differences, median and spread, with sufficiently sampled percentiles only. Use a parent monotonic clock for elapsed process timings; do not subtract unrelated process-relative clock values.
- Add bounded initialization observation if needed to separate loading from resident/IPC work. Reuse ordinary installed command routing and representative native hook validation; keep fixture inputs/configuration equivalent and offline, with no live backend calls in startup measurements. Record OS/architecture, hardware/load, runtime/tool versions, command/event and artifact hashes. Compare platforms only within like-for-like cells. Measure each claimed performance/platform cell; unmeasured cells remain explicitly unverified.
- At installed-validation milestone present the before/after performance evidence, limitations and any architectural decision it warrants. Investigate material regressions under predeclared comparison criteria; no unmeasured speedup, universal percentile or arbitrary millisecond guarantee.
- Installed cases preserve accepted setup authorization/credential handling, separate hook routing, retained-release reuse, diagnostics, Pi assets and native helper resolution. Native agent-runtime execution and each claimed OS/architecture/version cell require their appropriate existing installed checks.
- Select local checks from the testing matrix by changed behavior: fast TypeScript checks and focused owner/consumer tests, affected packaging/process/installation integration checks, and documentation checks. Use the full quality gate at declared milestones or when impact cannot be bounded. Do not use GitHub CI as an extra completion gate unless a release contract requires it.
- Every structural milestone must include architectural-agent review, recorded disposition and presentation of architectural decisions, if any. Completed milestones distinguish observed behavioral results, structural conclusions and unverified platform/performance claims.

## Out of Scope

- Replacing Bun with Node, adopting Nx, splitting into independently published products or switching away from standalone distribution without demonstrating reasons and a separately considered decision.
- Changing review/advice policy, Bend authority, attribution, rule semantics, credential precedence or runtime trust behavior.
- Implementing unrelated inspection, rule-management or simulator/game features while reorganizing their owners.
- Automatic expansion of supported platforms/OS versions, or a general hook-latency guarantee.
- Mandatory remote caching, dependency visualization or a centrally typed graph. Graph data/Markdown views remain optional and low priority.

## Further Notes

This specification promotes the listed owner requirements into implementation scope; research reports and prototype layout remain advisory. The bounded prototype passed 18 build assertions and 17 isolation cases on Linux ARM64. Its task cache was deliberately disabled; no cached production adoption was demonstrated. Output-inventory repair and conservative assembly freshness were custom adapters. Isolation was a separate experiment, not an integrated publication gate. A permissive-parser bypass was retained and rejected after strict parsing was added. Native assets, other platforms, conditional exports and alternate loaders remain unproven by the prototype. Supported production resolver branches and hook-facing surfaces must be covered during implementation; unsupported loader mechanisms must be rejected or explicitly constrained, not silently treated as isolated.

Prototype evidence and the finer recommendation are captured in the prepared research worktree on branch `research/hook-setup-followup`, commits `63861390` and `bead9b6b`. Ensure those source/evidence artifacts are accessible to the implementation agent; recorded results alone do not replace rerunnable evidence.

All hanging threads are explicit milestone obligations: final domain package/folder names and scope; workspace and dependency-authority wiring; orchestration selection; incremental compile/assembly integration; cache hits/restoration/invalidation; source-checker comparison and cached build/publication enforcement; actual production source closures including read-only credentials; native/install/platform evidence; installed hook startup/load-time before/after comparison; and consolidation/cleanup. Each milestone report records which obligations were resolved and which remain, with evidence and the next required action. No prototype result silently closes an untested obligation.

Implementation starts with an actual import/domain-ownership map and a tooling-validation checkpoint; then implement against current contract owners. Notify the owner before tooling integration. At completion, consolidate accepted architecture/build/platform decisions into maintained owners, update inbound links and delete temporary proposal/research/prototype artifacts after preserving still-useful evidence in its owner. Existing domain and product contracts remain authoritative for behavior not explicitly changed here.

Astra reviewed this specification before publication: no critical architectural contradiction; the hook inventory, host-loaded isolation, cache-evidence identity, resolver-condition coverage, resident benchmark identity and shared-domain review clarifications above incorporate its important findings. This was a specification review, not empirical production validation.

title: Implement explicit CLI interactions with workflow reducers and idiomatic Effect
body:
## Problem Statement

Hapsland's human-facing CLI interactions are spread across separate imperative flows and input implementations. Users face inconsistent selection, approval, navigation, cancellation and recovery behavior. Maintainers cannot inspect the whole conversation independently of terminal rendering and owner operations. Setup alone is insufficient: rules, updates, maintenance, login and credential verification have related interactions but different consent and recovery contracts.

The existing installation approval behavior is already implemented and tested, including manual testing confirmed by the user. The change must preserve that behavior while making the conversations explicit and consistently presented.

## Solution

Provide consistent CLI interactions backed by workflow-specific pure reducers, a shared interaction module and idiomatic Effect orchestration. Users see named choices, actual owner previews, explicit approvals, available Back/Exit actions and truthful durable outcomes. The existing installation, rule and credential owners retain authorization, mutation and recovery responsibility.

Extend the existing throwaway prototype across representative interactive workflows before production integration. Integrate the accepted behavior across all applicable CLI inputs, retaining deliberate direct-output and structured-input exceptions. Preserve current credential storage behavior; create a follow-up task for additional project/user file-saving choices during integration. Validate Linux execution near the end of integration.

## User Stories

1. As a user, I want consistent selection and navigation across applicable CLI workflows, so that I do not have to relearn every dialog.
2. As a user, I want the first setup dialog to focus Continue with no implicit new selection, so that immediately pressing Enter cannot exit or authorize changes.
3. As a user, I want empty Continue to display a warning and remain on selection, so that I understand what is required.
4. As a user, I want Space to toggle an agent or Select All, so that selecting agents is distinct from continuing.
5. As a user, I want Select All to reflect none, some or all agents selected, so that I can understand the current selection.
6. As a user, I want inverse selection removed, so that the first dialog contains useful, understandable actions.
7. As a user, I want Enter to submit the visibly focused option, so that Approve cannot accidentally submit Decline.
8. As a user, I want Escape to equal Back on menus that offer Back, so that keyboard navigation matches the visible action.
9. As a user, I want Escape to exit the initial selection dialog, so that a screen without a prior step has a clear escape route.
10. As a user, I want explicit Exit and interruption to terminate input safely, so that I can stop without leaving my terminal damaged.
11. As a user, I want hidden-input cancellation to retain its existing exit behavior, so that credential entry is predictable.
12. As a user, I want selected agents to remain selected when I go Back, so that I can adjust a choice without starting over.
13. As a user, I want existing registrations labeled accurately, so that selection does not conceal what is already installed.
14. As a user, I want unchecking an installed agent to leave its hooks intact, so that skipping setup does not uninstall anything.
15. As a user, I want each selected agent's hook changes previewed and approved independently, so that approval covers the intended registration.
16. As a user, I want default-rule changes included with their own authorization, so that hook approval does not hide additional writes.
17. As a user, I want Back to retain completed and partial outcomes, so that navigation never falsely claims to undo applied changes.
18. As a user, I want selecting a destination or moving focus to authorize no write, so that consent remains explicit.
19. As a user, I want changed previews to require renewed approval, so that stale consent cannot authorize different writes.
20. As a user, I want my credential source explained without exposing the key, so that I know which credential will actually be used.
21. As a user, I want existing native saved-login and environment/file lookup behavior preserved, so that integration does not change authentication unexpectedly.
22. As a user, I want key entry hidden and outside chat, so that credentials do not appear in conversation or command transcripts.
23. As a user, I want cancellation before saving to preserve my previous credential, so that abandoning entry does not remove working access.
24. As a user, I want locked, unavailable, interaction-required, busy and uncertain storage outcomes explained accurately, so that I can recover without repeated automatic prompts.
25. As a user, I want explicitly interactive structured setup to use the controlling terminal even when stdin carries JSON, so that the existing authorized setup path continues working.
26. As an automation user, I want explicit credential-stdin behavior preserved, so that scripted login does not acquire an unsolicited prompt.
27. As a user, I want every paid key-check request separately approved, so that navigation and installation approval cannot spend credits.
28. As a user, I want key checks bounded by the existing request limit and timeout, so that verification cannot retry indefinitely.
29. As a user, I want verification failures to preserve stored credentials and distinguish rejection from incomplete verification, so that service failures do not force unnecessary replacement.
30. As a user, I want native replacement, file correction/recheck and process-environment guidance distinguished, so that recovery respects the effective source.
31. As a user, I want rule scope presented as Project or Personal, so that I can choose its reach without interpreting an inverted yes/no question.
32. As a user, I want rule changes previewed and applied using the same plan digest, so that approval binds the actual change.
33. As a user, I want rule create/connect activation semantics preserved, so that the new interaction does not change which rules become active.
34. As a user, I want update to preview all applicable clients before one grouped approval, so that I understand the batch before committing it.
35. As a user, I want update to preserve already-current, skipped, partial and failed results per client, so that one failure does not erase other outcomes.
36. As a user, I want staged and retained packages explained honestly after Back or failure, so that navigation does not imply acquisition or activation was undone.
37. As a user, I want repair, reinstall and uninstall to preserve per-client approval, so that maintenance does not silently broaden consent.
38. As a user, I want repair to follow the inspected recovery operation, so that an interrupted uninstall is not mistaken for installation.
39. As a user, I want unrelated hooks, settings and credentials preserved by their existing owners, so that a UI refactor cannot weaken ownership protections.
40. As a user, I want durable outcomes to distinguish installation, credential availability, verification and native trust, so that setup success does not imply a real review occurred.
41. As a user, I want readiness guidance to say Codex, so that the agreed product wording is preserved.
42. As a user, I want doctor and rules list/show/explain to remain direct output, so that inspection commands do not become unnecessary dialogs.
43. As a user, I want logout to retain its explicit command and recovery semantics, so that consistency does not introduce an unsolicited wizard.
44. As an automation user, I want version-one JSON and unattended preview/apply contracts preserved, so that human-input improvements do not break scripts or add implicit consent.
45. As a terminal user, I want input scopes, echo, cursor, raw mode and listeners restored after completion or failure, so that the CLI leaves my terminal usable.
46. As a user, I want readable hints and safe errors in narrow, resized and no-color terminals, so that state and recovery remain understandable.
47. As a maintainer, I want all human-input entry points inventoried and migrated or explicitly excepted, so that an onboarding-only refactor is not mistaken for holistic coverage.
48. As a maintainer, I want workflow transitions independent of terminal and owner operations, so that behavior can be tested through typed inputs and observations.
49. As a maintainer, I want late answers and completions rejected and repeated commands controlled, so that Back and retries cannot replay consent or mutation.
50. As a maintainer, I want setup Mermaid Markdown generated from actual reducer replays, so that documentation reflects declared executable scenarios.
51. As a reader, I want diagram coverage limits visible, so that freshness is not mistaken for exhaustive behavior or correctness.
52. As a maintainer, I want a follow-up issue for additional project/user credential destinations, so that scaling remains tracked without changing this integration's storage scope.
53. As a Linux user, I want actual source and installed CLI execution validated on Linux arm64, so that compilation alone does not stand in for platform evidence.

54. As a maintainer, I want each modeled interactive CLI flow to emit replay-generated Mermaid Markdown, so that the rest of the dialogs are documented in the same inspectable way as setup.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Dependency and sequencing:** production integration is blocked by the accepted implementation of [#243](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/243). Reuse its established composition roots, domain ownership, credential separation, release assembly and build enforcement. Isolated prototype extensions, workflow design and test planning may proceed while blocked, without adopting production package/tooling decisions or starting competing production extraction.
- **Administration-only interaction:** the shared interaction module, terminal adapters, workflow reducers and interpreters belong to administration. Dedicated standalone hooks and host-loaded hook entries, including Pi, must not import this implementation directly, transitively, lazily or through type-only dependencies. Genuinely shared credential/runtime concepts remain with their permitted domain owners and must not be re-exported through administration.
- **Package and build choices:** follow the package scopes, dependency authority, tooling and enforcement accepted through #243's owner milestones. Do not independently select package names/count, adopt a build tool or introduce another dependency graph. If an interaction change requires revising an accepted architectural decision, present the concrete revision and evidence before dependent integration. This issue does not preempt future owner decisions required by #243.
- **Installed routing and release assembly:** integrate through #243's administration entry and retained active-package routing. Setup, update, repair and reinstall must operate on and register the correct separated hook executables and host-loaded assets. Update affected release inventory, build inputs and installed fixtures together; do not restore shared-CLI hook routing or compatibility shims.
- Use workflow-specific pure reducers, typed events and commands, safe views, and Effect interpreters. The shared module handles interaction/rendering/lifetime conventions; existing owners retain domain policy. Do not implement a universal wizard, universal command union, or duplicate owner logic.
- Cover setup, rules mutation, update, maintenance, login and credential verification/replacement. Preserve bare setup, explicit-client setup, legacy pilot, explicitly interactive structured setup, default-rule authorization and active-package routing. Doctor, rules inspection, logout and ordinary structured/headless commands remain deliberate direct-output/input exceptions.
- Extend the throwaway prototype with representative rule, batch-update, maintenance-recovery and verification/replacement flows through the shared conventions before integrating production owners. Emit Mermaid Markdown for each modeled interaction workflow, bounded to its executable replay scenarios.
- Share a small interaction interface for typed single/multiple choices, full-line confirmation, hidden input and durable presentation. Supply live and scripted adapters. Workflows specify legal navigation and translate interaction results into their own events.
- Keep the accepted initial selection behavior: Continue initially focused, empty Continue warned and guarded, Space toggles, Enter submits, inverse selection absent. Preserve production existing-registration labels/default selections. Back retains current selection and prior outcomes.
- Escape dispatches Back where offered; it exits the first selection dialog. Hidden-input cancellation continues exiting the session. EOF and process interruption remain distinct from Back and cannot reopen an input loop without available input.
- Preserve production full-line write confirmation with a nonaffirmative default and owner digest binding. The prototype's arrow-key approval is not authorization to replace this contract. A focused option's submitted value must never fall back to another option.
- Reuse the read-only credential interfaces and administration-side mutation authority established by #243. Extract the remaining setup/login/verification conversation from within those accepted owners, without creating another credential resolution or mutation implementation. Structured setup and human workflows share accepted operations and preserve precedence, eligibility, locks, recovery and safe observations. Read-only runtime consumers remain independent of capture, login, logout, replacement and interactive recovery.
- Keep Prompt.Hidden for the hidden prompt; do not introduce a custom hidden prompt. Preserve the authorized controlling-terminal path with redirected JSON stdin and the separate explicit credential-stdin path. The prototype's terminal adapter is not a drop-in production adapter: it lacks full-line input and controlling-terminal support.
- Keep captured keys outside serialized models, generic events, views, transcripts and command caches. Hidden capture happens inside the credential interpreter; its value is consumed by the credential owner, with only safe outcomes and correlation returned. Redaction does not establish memory zeroization.
- First production integration presents current credential behavior and storage choices. Create a separate follow-up task during integration for additional project/user file-saving choices, covering defaults, approval, private permissions, safe targets, overwrite preservation, precedence, recovery and Git-ignore policy.
- Preserve per-client setup/maintenance consent and grouped update consent. Default rules retain their separate digest. Rules retain Project/Personal scope and current explicit unattended semantics. Changed proposals invalidate approval; selecting a destination is not consent.
- Preserve verification's fresh consent for every request, maximum three checks, 15-second timeout, no automatic retries, built-in sample payload and sanitized results. Source-specific replacement/recheck remains a separate credential conversation reused by setup.
- Use idiomatic Effect throughout orchestration, with one top-level Effect execution boundary per invoked administration process and scoped session resources. Separately invoked standalone components retain their own composition roots and process runtimes; this issue does not merge them or alter resident reuse. Use services/Layers for concrete shared dependencies where useful; keep pure helpers pure. Output, discovery, reporting and exit updates become Effects or safe returned outcomes interpreted at the CLI edge. Do not transplant repeated prototype runtime bridges or nested synchronous runtime/cache creation.
- Correlate input sessions and commands; reject stale answers/approvals/completions. Session deduplication is not process-wide exactly-once evidence. Existing locks, proposal validation and recovery journals remain authoritative.
- Preserve observed completed, partial, busy and indeterminate owner outcomes during navigation and interruption. Do not map arbitrary failures to cancellation or claim rollback. Preserve target acquisition, activation, routing and retention behavior.
- Resolve success presentation during integration using real owner observations. Distinguish configured installation, credential availability, verified authorization, native trust and actual observed review. Emit Codex in readiness guidance without indiscriminately renaming unrelated client-label consumers.
- Generate deterministic Mermaid inside Markdown for every modeled interactive CLI workflow (setup, rules mutations, update, maintenance, login, and credential verification/replacement) from named scenarios replayed through each actual reducer/interpreter. Keep workflow-specific diagrams rather than inventing one universal wizard. Direct/headless exceptions remain explicitly documented without manufactured dialog states. Retain sanitized revision/command correlation; separate state-changing edges from ignored-input self-loops. Provide explicit regeneration and a non-writing freshness check. Document bounded coverage beside the diagram and its owner guidance. Independent assertions determine behavior correctness.
- Update Hapsland-owned version-one formats in place only where required by an accepted contract; preserve unattended/public behavior. Remove superseded production input/orchestration implementations as replacements land rather than keeping parallel systems or migration shims.
- Complete work in a branch/PR rather than master. Consolidate accepted architecture into an ADR and behavior into maintained owner documentation; after production integration and required validation are complete, delete all prototypes created or extended for #244, including demo/fake-owner code, isolated manifests, temporary replay Markdown and superseded qualification evidence. First move adopted behavior, useful tests and generators to their production owners, update inbound links, and retain maintained production Mermaid documentation. Unrelated repository prototypes are outside this cleanup scope; Git history retains the experiments.

## Testing Decisions

- Require explicit regeneration and non-writing Mermaid Markdown freshness checks for each modeled interactive workflow. Keep sanitized replay correlation and bounded coverage guidance; do not claim diagrams for unimplemented models.

- Extend #243's ordinary source-isolation and cached build/publication checks to cover the interaction module and its dependencies. Demonstrate that administration-only interaction changes rebuild affected administration outputs while reusing unrelated hook/resident/parser outputs, and that genuinely changed shared inputs invalidate their consumers. Verify that cached results cannot bypass updated dependency policy or artifact inventory; do not introduce a parallel checker or task graph.
- Run Linux arm64 source and installed interaction checks against the actual separated release produced by the accepted #243 build, using isolated fake stores. Cover controlling-terminal credential entry, terminal cleanup, consent, active-package administration routing and retained hook registrations. Earlier prototype execution, #243's platform evidence and cross-compilation do not substitute for exercising the final #244 candidate.
- Maintain a final acceptance matrix covering setup, rules mutation, update, maintenance, login, verification/replacement and explicit non-dialog exceptions. Record implementation disposition and observed tests for every surface; an unchecked surface prevents completion even when setup passes.
- Test external behavior, authorized operations, observed outcomes and resource lifetime, not reducer implementation branches, renderer internals or snapshots accepted merely because output changed.
- Prefer the existing highest workflow seams with injected owners. The shared interaction interface is the new common seam: live terminal and scripted adapters exercise the same interface. Use workflow entry points for decisions and owner calls; reserve real process seams for physical input/output, launcher and packaging behavior. Do not scatter new mocking seams through domain owners.
- Preserve and extend existing pilot, confirmation, rules, update, maintenance and credential-verification behavior tests. Prior art includes explicit digest forwarding, decline without mutation, missing/stale authorization rejection, all update previews before one approval, per-client failure continuation, maintenance recovery, bounded paid consent and hidden-input cancellation.
- Exercise initial/repeated empty Enter, individual/Select All toggles, removed inverse selection, focused Approve/Decline submission, Escape/Back equivalence, explicit Exit, selection preservation, stale responses, changed proposals and partial results.
- Verify actual owner digests and approval grouping. Witness destination selection issuing no write, stale consent issuing no mutation, and paid checks never occurring without fresh consent. Keep independent assertions separate from controller equality and diagram freshness.
- Verify keys and raw owner/provider payloads absent from models, views, traces, cached command results and stdout/stderr. Use fake/injected credential and network owners for ordinary checks; do not read the user's real credential store.
- Extend existing PTY/process checks for terminal restoration, cleanup of listeners/input scopes, no leaked typeahead across prompts, Ctrl+C/EOF/signals, resizing, narrow/no-color output, redirected channels and durable outcomes. Test full-line confirmation and controlling-terminal secret input explicitly.
- Preserve explicit interactive JSON setup with redirected stdin and controlling-terminal key entry. Ordinary headless/JSON callers must not initialize prompts, assume selections, approve mutations or make paid requests. Preserve explicit credential-stdin behavior.
- Verify installed launcher lifetime, active-package routing, acquisition/retention, activation, mutation locks and partial recovery using the existing appropriate physical seams, not only source-level reducer tests.
- Run local fast checks plus focused owner and affected-consumer tests, affected integration/packaging checks, and documentation/generated-artifact checks according to the repository testing matrix. For this broad CLI migration, run the full quality gate on the frozen candidate with declared duration and finite deadline. Diagnose retained stage failures before rerunning; do not relax coverage or quality policy.
- Execute relevant source and installed flows on actual Linux arm64 near the end of integration with isolated fake stores. Record platform/executable identity, outcomes and terminal cleanup. Linux compilation alone does not satisfy acceptance.
- Assess success presentation using real production owner outcomes. The user will review visual readability; PTY input success does not establish visual legibility.
- Completion requires every interactive entry point migrated or explicitly excepted, unchanged consent/unattended contracts, observed stale-reply rejection, truthful partial recovery, no secret leakage, terminal cleanup, Linux execution evidence, and completed prototype cleanup/consolidation. Required local checks determine completion; GitHub CI is reported separately.

## Out of Scope

- Implementing the additional project/user credential file-saving feature in this integration; creating its follow-up task is in scope.
- A universal wizard, a new rule editor, or dialogs for read-only inspection commands.
- Replacing existing owner authorization, locks, journals, credential precedence or runtime-native trust/permissions.
- Custom hidden-input prompts or changing hidden cancellation to Back.
- Screen-reader work in this iteration.
- Exhaustive diagram coverage, formal verification, process-wide exactly-once claims, or memory-zeroization claims.
- Provider/review-core redesign, unapproved live provider requests, real-user credential-store experiments, and changing public format versions.

## Further Notes

The user accepted the setup flow and confirmed having manually tested the existing production hook-approval process. Success presentation remains an integration deliverable rather than an already accepted rendering. This spec incorporates the now-read holistic CLI handoff; the owner subsequently extended Mermaid Markdown generation to each modeled interactive CLI workflow; each graph remains bounded to its executable replay scenarios.

The existing prototype, research, replay diagrams and scoped evidence are available in [draft PR #242](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/pull/242). They inform implementation; synthetic outcomes do not replace production owner or platform validation.

The inspected update, maintenance and credential-verification baseline passed 76 existing tests. Targeted production pilot approval and confirmation tests also passed. A broader pilot run exposed an existing readiness wording mismatch: the test expects Codex and production emits Codex CLI. Fix production output as agreed; do not rewrite the expectation to accept Codex CLI.

Related existing contracts include [unattended setup #224](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/224), [rules visibility/toggling #222](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/222), and [editable rules/unattended setup #220](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/220). Existing accepted architecture and ownership contracts remain constraints.

title: Support evidenced Bend generic parameters and non-type arguments in review extraction
body:
## Problem

Nightly inspection on 2026-10-07 showed accepted Bend edits stopping before Jev preparation. Current Hapsland extraction marks syntax used in bendvy as unsupported, loses required type-closure evidence, and excludes closure-dependent rules.

Confirmed minimal reproductions against the current extractor:

```bend
import Base
type Generic<S: Data> is Data:
  Generic{id: U32}
```

Produces an unsupported reference to Generic. The otherwise identical parameter spelling `-S: Data` is accepted by the extractor.

```bend
import Base
type Items is Data:
  Items{items: List<&2,U32>}
```

Produces an unsupported reference to Items. A plain U32 field is accepted.

Real examples include `src/ecs/schedule-provision.bend` in bendvy: parameters such as `S: Data`, `C: Type`, and field types such as `List<&2,Requirement<S>>`.

The retained bendvy journal contains 394 unsupported-reference, 72 missing-evidence and 71 no-applicable-rule events. These are event counts, can describe the same causal chain, and are not counts of independent failed reviews. Two simple Bend declarations did reach Jev successfully.

## Requested implementation

Support the evidenced Bend parameter and type-argument forms in the language-owned extractor and graph interface. Validate syntax and binding meaning against the pinned Bend toolchain before extending extraction; preserve the distinction between datatype references, bound parameters and non-type arguments such as `&2`.

Resolve local and imported references accurately, so declarations using these forms retain the capabilities required by applicable rules and reach review preparation. Do not bypass evidence requirements, weaken rule capability checks, or label incomplete evidence complete.

Owners: `src/direct-event/languages/bend/extractor.ts`, `src/direct-event/languages/bend/adapter.ts`, and affected graph/preparation consumers.

## Acceptance criteria

- Compiler-valid fixtures cover ordinary Data/Type parameters, the already-supported parameter form, nested applications, and `List<&2,T>` with bound, local and imported T.
- Extracted references include actual datatype dependencies; parameter names and non-type arguments do not become invented graph dependencies.
- Deterministic pipeline tests establish that these edits prepare the applicable closure-dependent rules and reach the controlled offline reviewer with the expected evidence.
- Representative minimized bendvy declarations reproduce the original failures before the fix and pass after it.
- Unsupported or ambiguous forms continue to produce explicit omissions; existing limits and refusal behavior remain intact.
- Run `npm run check:fast`, focused Bend analyzer/pipeline and affected graph/rule consumer tests, and the relevant compiler checks selected from `docs/testing-matrix.md`. Report only checks actually run.

## Scope and follow-up

This is an implementation task for the confirmed syntax/evidence failures. Worktree routing, rejected-stale admission, ambiguous-update attribution and the eight parse events need separate diagnosis; this task does not claim to explain all nightly omissions. Reinspect the preserved journal after implementation.

The private local backup is `/home/node/.local/state/hapsland-log-backups/night-20261007-20261007T122214Z/`: inspection and activity archives, a per-file SHA-256 manifest and archive checksum. All 5,121 archived files were verified after creation. The live writer was not stopped; this is a fixed file inventory copied during the backup, not a globally atomic resident snapshot. Source-bearing journal payloads are kept locally and are not attached to this public issue.

title: Pin each virtual round to the first edited worktree and route advice independently of cwd
body:
## Problem Statement

An agent or subagent can run from one directory while editing a sibling Git worktree or another Git repository. Hapsland currently selects the working root from runtime cwd and rejects legitimate edited targets outside that root. Those edits do not reach semantic preparation or Jev, and the agent can miss advice.

The bounded fix must preserve existing file-access policy, reliable agent attribution, source isolation, stale-advice protection, and virtual-round limits. It must not require complete multi-root review within one virtual round.

## Solution

The first accepted attributed eligible edit pins the agent's virtual round to the physical working root of that edit. Later edits in other roots are explicitly skipped until normal closure; existing reviews and pending advice stay active. Returning to the pinned root resumes review in the same round.

An agent started in A and consistently editing B therefore receives review under B's settings and advice addressed to that agent, regardless of current cwd. A long-lived virtual round may span runtime turns and leave edits in C unreviewed; the user accepts this limitation for the first implementation.

Completion includes reconciling documented vocabulary and expectations, and creating a linked research follow-up for complete multi-root support without this skip policy.

## User Stories

1. As an agent editing a sibling worktree, I want Hapsland to discover the root from my edited target, so that my legitimate edits reach review.
2. As an agent editing another Git repository, I want the same target-based behavior, so that shared Git metadata is not a prerequisite.
3. As a user, I want the first accepted eligible edit to select the round's root, so that merely invoking a hook does not choose it.
4. As a user, I want failed or rejected edits to leave root selection available, so that an unsuccessful operation does not consume the round's root choice.
5. As an agent editing content with no reviewable declarations, I want accepted-edit lifetime semantics to remain consistent, so that findings do not determine when the round opens.
6. As an agent editing several files in one invocation, I want deterministic root selection, so that asynchronous filesystem timing does not choose my review scope.
7. As an agent making concurrent edits, I want one atomic active-round choice, so that different roots cannot independently open parallel rounds for me.
8. As an agent temporarily editing a different root, I want those edits to be skipped without cancelling existing work, so that previously accepted reviews and advice remain useful.
9. As an agent returning to the pinned root, I want review to continue in the same round, so that switching directories does not reset allowances.
10. As an agent starting fresh work after normal closure, I want a new root to be selectable, so that the previous round does not permanently bind my session.
11. As a user, I want delayed events from an earlier round to remain fenced across roots, so that skipped old work cannot open a new round.
12. As a main agent, I want my round independent of identified children's rounds, so that their work does not change my root or advice.
13. As a subagent, I want advice addressed using my reliable runtime identity, so that it is not delivered to my parent or a sibling.
14. As a user, I want source isolation retained between roots, so that identical relative filenames and declaration names do not mix revisions or evaluations.
15. As a user, I want each accepted edit to use its target-root settings snapshot, so that cwd settings cannot override the edited project.
16. As an agent adding a file or directory, I want safe root discovery before the target exists, so that new files can be reviewed.
17. As a user, I want ignored and unused edit permits retired correctly, so that skipped work does not leak resources or reset the round.
18. As a user, I want protected paths, exclusions, Git-ignore semantics, symlink checks, and capture limits preserved, so that the fix does not broaden source access accidentally.
19. As a user, I want supporting-source traversal confined to the pinned root and its context policy, so that other-root edits do not grant cross-root reads.
20. As an agent changing cwd before advice arrives, I want delivery to find my pinned round, so that my current location does not hide existing findings.
21. As an agent running outside a Git tree after an edit, I want identity-only delivery opportunities to remain usable, so that source discovery is not required to identify me again.
22. As an agent receiving advice, I want the file path to identify the edited target without root headings, so that I can find the right working copy.
23. As a user, I want skipped other-root hooks to gain no synchronous blocking authority from the pinned project, so that delivery remains within its existing authorization.
24. As an agent repairing source, I want stale findings suppressed against their original physical source, so that a root or dependency change does not produce obsolete advice.
25. As a user enabling inspection, I want recording consent and analytics associated with the pinned source root, so that cwd changes cannot misattribute source-bearing history.
26. As a dashboard user, I want other-root edits shown as skipped and linked to their round, so that I can distinguish intentional omissions from backend failures.
27. As a user, I want existing invocation, capacity, deadline, and continuation bounds preserved, so that root discovery does not multiply resource allowances.
28. As a contributor, I want vocabulary, contracts, documentation, and code/test expectations reconciled with the new behavior, so that future work does not rely on obsolete cwd/root assumptions.
29. As a product owner, I want a research follow-up created at completion with the unresolved multi-root context, so that the deliberate skip limitation has an explicit next step.

## Implementation Decisions

- Keep Git as the working-root discovery and file-eligibility mechanism. A working root is the physical root of one Git working copy; linked worktrees and independent clones are both supported targets. A Git-ignore file is optional; no shared Git directory is required.
- Recipient identity uses runtime/session/reliably identified agent or subagent independently of source root. Preserve existing runtime identity semantics and version scoping where applicable; missing child attribution must not become reliable through root discovery.
- Retain root-bearing source partitions for settings, source freshness, revisions, evaluations, and capacity ownership as needed. Add recipient-to-active-round routing with resident lifetime, round identity, and pinned physical root; do not globally remove root from existing keys.
- Runtime turns and virtual rounds have independent boundaries. Neither cwd changes, runtime turn identifiers, nor target-root switches close/reopen the round. Existing finish, continuation, quiescence, cancellation, and resident-lifetime rules remain authoritative.
- Select the pin on the first successfully admitted attributed eligible edit, before semantic preparation. Existing file/configuration/admission checks define eligibility. An admitted edit that later produces no declarations still pins; a permit, failed tool, rejected admission, backend response, or finding does not.
- Normalize target paths once against the tool's actual path base established by its adapter, independently of hook process cwd. Audit all supported adapters, including tools with explicit directory arguments.
- Use stable native candidate order within a mixed-root invocation: first admissible candidate chooses the root; retain eligible same-root candidates and retire other-root candidates as skipped. Concurrent invocations choose the winner through atomic resident admission. Discovery completion order must not influence the winner.
- Pre-edit target discovery must support absent target files/directories through suitable existing ancestors and revalidation after the edit. Preserve symlink rejection rather than resolving away a rejected path, physical root replacement detection, and stable capture.
- Capture settings for target roots at pre-edit. Multiple provisional root-specific permits may exist before pinning; admission chooses one root and retires unused/skipped permits without opening extra rounds. Never borrow another root's settings or silently recover invalid configuration by falling back to cwd settings.
- Once pinned, the root supplies the existing round settings and quiet-expiry policy. Other-root edits neither alter settings nor reset continuation/capacity allowances. Skip and deduplicate them rather than queueing them for future review.
- Preserve a recipient-level closed-round fence across root changes. Releasing the pin must not permit an event begun during the old round to open another root's fresh partition. Only a provably fresh admitted edit after normal closure can choose a new pin.
- Reuse the canonical file-access decisions: target-root exclusions/privacy protections, protected paths, Git administrative-path restrictions, tracked/ignore semantics, file kind, source/capture bounds, and physical safety all apply before source capture. Supporting-source traversal remains within the pinned root under its context policy.
- Preserve source/revision/evaluation identity where it isolates roots, and stale-advice revalidation for the original root and supporting snapshots, newer revisions, round closure/cancellation, and resident restart. A recreated directory or caller cwd must not rebind advice to a different source copy.
- Route authorized delivery opportunities by recipient to the pinned round, even if current cwd changes or is outside Git. Hook names and native output channels remain adapter details.
- Skipped other-root edit responses must not gain synchronous blocking/advice authority from the pinned root. Existing advice remains deliverable through authorized background/finish channels; new cross-root synchronous delivery is excluded. Preserve the existing user-only opt-in boundary for Claude direct-edit blocking.
- Keep file/declaration-oriented feedback without root headings. When cwd differs, render a target-identifying file path so the message cannot ambiguously point at another copy.
- Associate inspection and analytics with the pinned source root and its consent/settings. No mixed-root source-bearing message recording is introduced. Record other-root work as skipped without capturing its source or reporting it as reviewed; make receipt-to-round membership observable for subsequent measurement.
- Preserve event-wide candidate/byte/time/output bounds and idempotency across splitting/discovery. Skipped permits, pending work, leases, and callbacks must preserve canonical resource/lifetime ownership.
- Update owned schemas/contracts in place at version 1. No legacy execution path, migration shim, or parallel format is introduced. Routing changes alone do not require deleting retained debug history; define any necessary incompatible-record cleanup explicitly without silently discarding evidence.
- Documentation reconciliation is a required deliverable: audit domain glossary, accepted advice/review contracts, architecture/configuration/status guidance, dashboard explanations, navigation/testing guidance, and relevant comments, type/schema descriptions, assertion messages, and test expectations. Distinguish recipient from source partition and runtime turn from virtual round; remove superseded assumptions. Keep implementation details out of the domain glossary.
- Before completion, create and link a separate research issue to compare and select complete multi-root review options that do not skip edits solely because another root is pinned. Transfer this issue's retained research context, accepted limitations, alternatives, measurement caveats, and primary-source Abide evidence into it. Include a bounded brief, discriminating evidence, invariants, and a recommended later implementation path; executing that research is not required here.
- The completion report must link the follow-up and identify reconciled documentation/code expectations. Source/context cleanup and follow-up creation are completion requirements, not discretionary post-task work.

## Testing Decisions

Prefer the existing highest product seam: resident admission, preparation/reviewer dispatch, and collection/delivery driven through real temporary Git working copies with a controlled deterministic offline reviewer. Observe which target/settings reach the reviewer, which recipient gets feedback, skip outcomes, and lifetime behavior; do not test private map layouts or mirror implementation branches. Reuse existing resident fixtures, edit-settings snapshot scenarios, permit/round lifecycle tests, stale-advice collection tests, and adapter/IPC boundary runners. Add lower-level owner checks only for properties that this seam cannot establish, especially canonical authority and native path translation.

Required behavior cases:

- Runtime started in A edits B: B pins; B's settings reach review; the correct agent gets actionable feedback with a target-identifying file path.

### Overnight evidence and projection limits

On 2026-10-07, three Luna agents with maximum reasoning independently analyzed session logs, the inspection journal, and counterfactual limitations. The fixed window is 01:00–12:00 UTC, equivalent to 2026-10-06 21:00 through 2026-10-07 08:00 in Montreal. The sanitized overnight aggregate retained in the repository inspection evidence retains counts, scenario definitions, transition identities, and journal record references, without captured source or model messages.

The Codex session pass examined 177 rollout logs, excluded inherited fork history, and deduplicated tool calls. Within the window, it counted 429 nested `apply_patch` invocations in 415 outer calls, 17 agent sessions, and 78 native turns. Current Git discovery resolved 548 of 556 patch targets to 10 working roots; 8 targets remained unresolved. Matching file-change results confirmed 416 completed invocations; 13 remain unconfirmed. Other edit tools and shell writes are outside these counts.

Observed target-root switches:

- 6 switches across 4 of 17 agent sessions (23.53% of sessions with counted edits).
- 2 switches within 2 of 78 native turns (2.56% of turns with counted edits).
- No counted patch invocation or outer wrapper call contained targets from multiple resolved Git roots.

Thus within-turn switching was uncommon in this observed night, but cross-session switching was materially more frequent. The frozen workspace inspection snapshot contains 3,048 records: 464 edit receipts, 353 accepted and 111 rejected-stale. There are 219 `repository-boundary` omission records across 167 accepted receipts and 119 unique target paths. Of these omissions, 137 are `.ts`/`.mts` path attempts. The journal contains 4 actual prepared units and 4 Jev transport invocations, producing 3 clear outcomes and 1 finding outcome. One unique finding was recorded as delivered; 103 collection suppressions concern that same advice, not 103 lost findings.

Counterfactual **path admission**, holding stale rejections fixed:

| Pinning scenario | TS/MTS boundary attempts reaching the selected root | All boundary records whose root gate could be removed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First accepted TS/MTS target for the recipient during one resident lifetime, retained across the observed session | 115 / 137 = 83.94% | 160 / 219 = 73.06% |
| First accepted TS/MTS target for each mapped native turn during one resident lifetime | 133 / 137 = 97.08% | 166 / 219 = 75.80% |

These are two explicitly defined diagnostic scenarios, not an estimate interval or exact virtual-round prediction. The eligibility proxy is accepted admission plus `.ts`/`.mts` extension and a currently resolvable Git root; it does not establish destination settings, protected-path eligibility, applicable rules, semantic declarations, or successful model requests. Other file formats contribute to the all-boundary column when they share the selected root but may still be ineligible for semantic review. Round pinning on the true first eligible edit may differ from the proxy; there is no receipt-to-virtual-round membership in the retained inspection format.

401 of 464 receipts were linked to native-turn evidence; all 137 TS/MTS boundary omissions were linked. The 63 unmatched receipts were accepted and contained no TS/MTS candidate. Seven boundary omission records lacked a native-turn link. Current-root discovery is present-time filesystem evidence, not a reconstruction of historical device/inode identity.

No numeric percentage of **recovered advice** or **recovered Jev checks** is justified: the omitted paths have no recorded declaration units or backend answers. The figures quantify removal of one preparation blocker. The separate 111 stale admissions and Bend analyzer limitations are not presumed fixed. Even a restored path may produce no applicable declaration, no applicable rule, or a clear Jev result.

The user accepts longer virtual rounds and unreviewed edits in other roots as limitations of the selected first implementation. The measurement supports the scope choice but does not establish switching frequency over actual virtual-round lifetimes. Record skipped-root work and receipt-to-round membership so that frequency can be measured after implementation.

### Abide primary-source evidence for the follow-up

**Research scope (2026-10-07):** Determine whether Abide already handles one identified agent editing several working roots in one host turn, and whether its root selection, state, continuation limits, or freshness controls resolve this proposal. This is a named-candidate architecture pass, not ecosystem discovery. The existing-solution baseline is Abide's own hooks/adapters; complete per-root rule selection and final-turn coverage would overturn the conclusion that this needs distinct Hapsland design work. | Claim | Exact proposition and evidence | Source class / verification state | Limitation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AB-MR-01 | [Post-edit handler](https://github.com/coldteadotai/abide/blob/0fc600f92672ead28e360afa373636e88f4a66d7/packages/cli/src/hooks/postToolUse.ts#L40-L50) chooses the root from the **first edited file**, falling back to event cwd; it uses that one root for all files' exclusions, rules, paths, and event records. A mixed-root invocation is not grouped per root: B is evaluated using A's rubric/exclusion context and a path relative to A. This is not complete multi-root support. |
| AB-MR-02 | [Codex patch paths](https://github.com/coldteadotai/abide/blob/0fc600f92672ead28e360afa373636e88f4a66d7/packages/cli/src/lib/diff.ts#L150-L174) are resolved against input cwd; Claude-style paths are taken directly from `tool_input.file_path`. | SRC / SOURCE-INSPECTED | Path semantics still depend on the host payload; target discovery does not establish correctness of every relative-path case. |
| AB-MR-03 | [Turn storage](https://github.com/coldteadotai/abide/blob/0fc600f92672ead28e360afa373636e88f4a66d7/packages/cli/src/lib/session.ts#L28-L31) is keyed by session and prompt/turn ID, without root. File-start records use absolute paths, but blocked/checked records use relative paths. [Turn start](https://github.com/coldteadotai/abide/blob/0fc600f92672ead28e360afa373636e88f4a66d7/packages/cli/src/hooks/turnStart.ts#L27-L58) stores one root and one Git baseline. | SRC / SOURCE-INSPECTED | Root-free turn storage is not sufficient: equal relative paths across roots can share block/checked identities (INFERRED from these keys). The [hook schema](https://github.com/coldteadotai/abide/blob/0fc600f92672ead28e360afa373636e88f4a66d7/packages/schema/src/hooks.ts#L9-L20) has no separate subagent field; isolation depends on host-supplied session/turn identities and is not established for every host. |
| AB-MR-04 | [Final-turn diff](https://github.com/coldteadotai/abide/blob/0fc600f92672ead28e360afa373636e88f4a66d7/packages/cli/src/hooks/stop.ts#L153-L184) explicitly returns incomplete if baseline start root differs from the root discovered from current cwd. Its file-snapshot fallback skips paths outside that current root. The [upstream test](https://github.com/coldteadotai/abide/blob/0fc600f92672ead28e360afa373636e88f4a66d7/packages/cli/test/stop.test.ts#L183-L191) expects silence and zero model calls after changing worktree. | SRC / SOURCE-INSPECTED | With unchanged cwd, the baseline diff covers only the original worktree; target-root post-edit checks do not extend final-turn coverage to all edited roots (INFERRED). Changing worktree does not close/reopen a coherent multi-root turn here; it declines the final check. |
| AB-MR-05 | [Constants](https://github.com/coldteadotai/abide/blob/0fc600f92672ead28e360afa373636e88f4a66d7/packages/cli/src/lib/constants.ts#L20-L24) allow two blocks per rule/file/turn and two final checks. [OpenCode adapter](https://github.com/coldteadotai/abide/blob/0fc600f92672ead28e360afa373636e88f4a66d7/packages/cli/opencode/abide.mjs#L219-L242) permits one repair follow-up; [Pi adapter](https://github.com/coldteadotai/abide/blob/0fc600f92672ead28e360afa373636e88f4a66d7/packages/cli/src/pi/extension.ts#L245-L275) separately caps repair continuation at one. | SRC / SOURCE-INSPECTED | These are different limits, not one universal once-per-turn check. They do not establish any equivalent Hapsland restriction or live-host enforcement. |
| AB-MR-06 | [Checked edits](https://github.com/coldteadotai/abide/blob/0fc600f92672ead28e360afa373636e88f4a66d7/packages/cli/src/hooks/postToolUse.ts#L89-L124) are evaluated synchronously and retain before/after blob IDs where available. [Final check](https://github.com/coldteadotai/abide/blob/0fc600f92672ead28e360afa373636e88f4a66d7/packages/cli/src/hooks/stop.ts#L284-L321) compares checked chains against current file content to skip already-covered unblocked changes. | SRC / SOURCE-INSPECTED | No post-await source revalidation appears in these handlers before formatting/delivery. Blob-chain coverage and unchanged-block suppression are not Hapsland's delayed-advice freshness contract; concurrent mutation during a model request remains untested. |

**Verdict:** Abide offers useful target-file root discovery for individual post-edit events, but the inspected code explicitly declines final-turn checks across a root switch and does not provide per-root rule/state separation for mixed-root edits. It is not evidence that the complete multi-root workflow is already solved. Neither changing cwd nor a root-free session/turn directory makes source identity unnecessary.

| Intended use | Advisory classification | Reason / handoff |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Discover the working root from an edited target rather than agent cwd | BORROW | AB-MR-01/02 support the direction; Hapsland must apply it independently to every target and preserve its own access protections. Take to implementation/specification. |
| Use root-free recipient/turn identity together with absolute source records | BORROW | AB-MR-03 is a partial pattern; add explicit root-qualified review/revision/block identities rather than copying relative-path keys. Take to specification and focused multi-root tests. |
| Silently omit final review when working root changes | REJECT | AB-MR-04 fails the requested cross-root coverage. Abide does not establish close/reopen semantics that resolve pending advice, cancellation, or budgets; the selected Hapsland design retains the existing round and skips only other-root edits. |
| Reuse Abide's final diff and freshness behavior as the multi-root solution | REJECT | AB-MR-04/06 do not satisfy complete root coverage or delayed-advice revalidation. No dependency recommendation follows from this pass. |

Unexecuted future research checks: a deterministic mixed-root patch fixture with distinct rubrics and duplicate relative paths would measure the inferred collision/wrong-settings cases; a fixture mutating the file while `runCheck` waits would measure freshness. Native subagent identity and continuation behavior require separate host observations. These checks were not run and do not block the narrower source-inspection conclusion.

- Treat native child identity and continuation enforcement as separate host observations. Start with deterministic offline fixtures; any live validation must be explicitly bounded and record only sanitized contract/timing evidence.

## Recommended later implementation path

Prefer source-specific work state under one recipient round as the first design to falsify, because it preserves existing recipient lifecycle and allowance semantics. Produce an alternatives table with counterexamples, an owner-ready contract amendment, bounded highest-seam acceptance fixtures, and a separately scoped implementation ticket.
