Unexecuted future research checks: a deterministic mixed-root patch fixture with distinct rubrics and duplicate relative paths would measure the inferred collision/wrong-settings cases; a fixture mutating the file while `runCheck` waits would measure freshness. Native subagent identity and continuation behavior require separate host observations. These checks were not run and do not block the narrower source-inspection conclusion.

title: Model credential lookup and approved file/native saving from one typed policy
body:
## Problem Statement

Hapsland currently saves login keys in native storage. Repeated macOS storage-access prompts make that a poor default for the owner's workflow, and users cannot explicitly choose project-only or user-wide credential-file saving through the production interaction.

Credential policy is also scattered across environment/file loading, native fallback, setup and terminal guidance. Handwritten documentation can drift from actual lookup and save behavior. Hapsland needs one strongly typed, serializable model that governs both execution and generated documentation.

This is the credential-destination follow-up to #244, extended by the owner's accepted design decisions on 2026-10-07. It does not reopen #244's completed integration.

## Solution

Offer these destinations in the production credential conversation:

- **Every project on this machine — default:** the user `.env` file under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/hapsland`, normally `~/.config/hapsland/.env`.
- **This project only:** `.env.local` at the repository root.
- **Native credential store:** macOS Keychain or Linux Secret Service, as an explicit alternative.

Show the exact validated target, scope and any higher-priority active source. Capture the key with hidden input, then require a separate full-line, nonaffirmative-default save confirmation bound to the current owner proposal. Back discards the entered key and returns to destination selection; cancellation preserves the previous credential. Save safely and report both the storage outcome and the effective credential source.

Represent lookup and save policy as executable, serializable data. Derive business plans and documentation from that same model, extended with safe contextual observations and rendered through separate views.

Lookup precedence is environment, project `.env.local`, project `.env`, user `.env`, then eligible native storage. Saving does not change that precedence or override an environment-selected key.

## User Stories

1. As a Hapsland user, I want user-wide file saving to be the default, so that routine file-backed credential lookup does not require native-store access.
2. As a Hapsland user, I want the user-file option to describe its local plaintext storage, so that I understand what I am approving.
3. As a Hapsland user, I want to choose project-only saving, so that other repositories do not use that project key.
4. As a Hapsland user, I want native storage to remain an explicit option, so that I can choose my platform's credential store.
5. As a Hapsland user, I want the destination's scope and exact target displayed before approval, so that I do not save to an unexpected place.
6. As a Hapsland user, I want my XDG configuration location respected, so that credentials follow my existing user-directory configuration.
7. As a Hapsland user, I want hidden credential entry, so that the key is not echoed into terminal output.
8. As a Hapsland user, I want a separate final save confirmation that defaults to declining, so that entry alone does not authorize replacement.
9. As a Hapsland user, I want Back to discard entered key material and return to destination selection, so that changing my destination cannot reuse stale approval.
10. As a Hapsland user, I want cancellation, EOF and input interruption to preserve the previous credential before saving, so that navigation cannot accidentally replace it.
11. As a Hapsland user, I want approval invalidated when the target or owner proposal changes, so that only the changes I reviewed can be applied.
12. As a Hapsland user, I want unsafe, symlinked or otherwise rejected targets refused, so that saving cannot redirect my secret into an unintended file.
13. As a Hapsland user, I want owner-only file permissions, so that other local users are not granted access by the save operation.
14. As a Hapsland user, I want atomic replacement, so that readers do not observe a partially written credential file.
15. As a Hapsland user, I want concurrent changes detected and protected, so that one save cannot silently overwrite another change.
16. As a Hapsland user, I want unrelated dotenv entries preserved, so that saving a key does not destroy other project or user settings.
17. As a Hapsland user, I want a failed replacement to preserve the old credential whenever failure is known to precede commitment, so that I retain a usable configuration.
18. As a Hapsland user, I want indeterminate outcomes reported honestly, so that I am not told a write succeeded or the old key survived without evidence.
19. As a Hapsland user, I want project saving refused when the target is tracked or not Git-ignored, so that the save flow does not put a secret into ordinary version-control changes.
20. As a Hapsland user, I want actionable instructions when project saving is blocked, so that I can fix exclusion and review a fresh proposal.
21. As a Hapsland user, I want environment credentials to retain first priority, so that saving a file does not silently override my launch environment.
22. As a Hapsland user, I want an explicitly present empty environment credential to stop lookup, so that an invalid explicit selection cannot silently fall back to another key.
23. As a Hapsland user, I want missing or empty dotenv fields to allow the next source, so that a file without the selected key does not conceal a later eligible source.
24. As a Hapsland user, I want unreadable or rejected credential files to stop lookup, so that an unsafe source is not hidden by a successful fallback.
25. As a Hapsland user, I want explicit configured credential references to retain environment/file-only authentication, so that native fallback cannot defeat my configuration.
26. As a Hapsland user, I want the selected source reported after saving, so that I can distinguish a stored key from the key actually used in this project.
27. As a Hapsland user, I want login, setup and guided replacement to use the same credential policy, so that their choices and explanations agree.
28. As a Hapsland user, I want saving and paid key verification to require separate consent, so that saving cannot authorize an external request.
29. As an automation user, I want explicit direct-input operations to remain free of unsolicited terminal dialogs, so that existing automation does not start prompting.
30. As an agent-runtime user, I want captured hook credential input to remain authoritative, so that a resident cannot substitute its own environment or files.
31. As a Hapsland maintainer, I want schema-checked, serializable credential policy and safe observations, so that programmatic consumers can exchange them without executable closures or secrets.
32. As a Hapsland maintainer, I want lookup execution and save selection derived from the model, so that behavior does not depend on a second handwritten precedence or destination list.
33. As a documentation reader, I want README and credential-guide sections generated from the same model, so that their defaults and lookup order match the product.
34. As a Hapsland maintainer, I want production-replay Mermaid documentation, so that diagrams reflect actual reducer and interpreter behavior.
35. As a Hapsland maintainer, I want keys excluded from models, events, traces, diagrams and logs, so that inspection and generation do not leak credentials.
36. As a Hapsland maintainer, I want deterministic owner and conversation tests plus controlled source and installed checks on macOS and Linux, so that acceptance covers both behavior and physical execution.

37. As a Hapsland developer, I want dev-install setup and explicit new-key replacement to use the same credential model and save flow, so that development snapshots behave like the installed product.
38. As a Hapsland developer, I want credentials to survive development snapshot rebuilds and activation, so that updating code does not require saving the key again or moving it into a package snapshot.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Accepted default amendment:** the user `.env` file replaces native storage as the default for the destination-selection conversation. Native storage remains an explicit alternative. This supersedes the original issue's instruction to retain native as default pending a reviewed decision.
- Use a pure credential-policy module in the existing **runtime-inputs** package. Define schemas and derive strongly typed discriminated unions for readable sources, save destinations, execution context, safe observations and plans. The policy values must be serializable; schema implementations and interpreters are separate executable code.
- Keep readable-source and save-destination types distinct. Project `.env` is a lookup source but is not offered as a managed save target. The ordered source descriptors, destination descriptors and default designation are the single policy authority.
- Derive lookup and save plans from that policy and safe context. Runtime interpreters and documentation projections must consume those derivations; remove superseded handwritten precedence arrays, fallback policy and destination/default lists.
- The **runtime-environment** package continues to own provider identities, platform coordinates and XDG path resolution. The pure policy accepts resolved contextual data rather than reading process state itself.
- The **runtime-inputs** package interprets read-only environment and file requests. Preserve the existing bounded regular-file, no-symlink credential reader and Node dotenv parsing semantics. Effect configuration primitives may support execution, but a standard dotenv loader must not weaken these protections or redefine empty/error behavior.
- The **credential-storage** package owns native and file mutation adapters, target validation, private permissions, proposal revalidation, locks, atomic replacement, credential-generation coordination and truthful recovery. Refactor orchestration currently coupled to the native adapter into the credential owner rather than creating a parallel owner.
- The **administration** package owns the production credential reducer, interpreter, contextual extension and terminal view. Reuse the established shared interaction service and one scoped input session. Consolidate login, setup/new-key and guided replacement onto the credential-specific policy and conversation; keep paid verification's consent separate.
- The contextual extension derives safe availability, validated paths, blocked reasons, source precedence notices and proposed effects. Views format these facts without deciding lookup policy, availability or authorization.
- The model-to-documentation route uses the existing **scripts/build-tooling** generation pipeline: model, safe extension/projection, Markdown view. Replace relevant handwritten README and credential-guide sections with marked generated sections. Extend existing production interaction replay generators rather than introducing another framework or putting credential policy in the canonical review-flow projection package.
- No new package or Bend core is required. New modules inhabit the existing owners. Hooks and Pi may consume the pure/read-only policy without acquiring administration or credential-mutation capabilities, including through type-only or lazy imports.
- Preserve reference explicitness independently of the environment-variable name. An explicitly configured reference permits environment and eligible files but prohibits native fallback even when it names the built-in variable.
- Correct the existing empty-environment inconsistency deliberately: explicit environment presence, including an empty value, stops lookup; an empty selection is not a usable key and must not select files or native storage. Missing/empty dotenv fields continue. Unreadable or rejected files stop with a safe diagnostic.
- Preserve existing scope/provenance contracts: callers without repository scope retain their current environment/native-only lookup; captured hook values and captured absence must not cause resident environment/file rediscovery. Native fallback remains subject to reference eligibility and capture provenance.
- The save owner prepares a validated, secret-free proposal. Approval is bound to the selected destination, actual current proposal identity and conversation revision. Revalidate immediately before mutation; a stale proposal cannot write and requires a fresh preview and approval.
- Secret input stays interpreter/owner-private and is tied to the current proposal. Back, cancellation and scope exit discard it. Serializable records contain no secret values, secret-derived fingerprints, Effect values, callbacks or filesystem handles.
- Require project targets to be untracked and Git-ignored before writing and recheck at commit. Report blocked saving with recovery instructions; do not silently edit tracked files, stage secrets or commit them.
- Distinguish precommit failure, known completed writes and indeterminate outcomes. An interruption after commitment must not be described as preservation or rollback. Saving and active-source resolution are separate observations; later resolution failure must not erase a known save.
- Keep Hapsland-owned input and persisted formats at version 1. Remove superseded production paths and documentation rather than retaining compatibility shims unless an accepted contract specifically requires them.

- **Development-mode compatibility:** the existing dev-install workflow must use the same credential model, destination selection and source reporting through its packaged guided setup, including explicit `--new-key`. Ordinary rebuild/update/activation must preserve previously saved credentials and must not request fresh credential entry merely because the snapshot changed. Resolve project credentials against the reviewed repository and user credentials against the configured user directory, never against the package prefix, build directory or retained snapshot. Never copy credential files into snapshots, archives, build caches or worktrees; a missing project credential in another worktree remains missing and is reported through normal lookup. Preserve the existing fixed-packaged-snapshot development workflow.

## Testing Decisions

- The accepted seams are the existing credential-owner interface, production credential conversation/reducer, and representative source/installed CLI execution. Prefer those established seams to additional internal interfaces; use the highest seam that can establish the required behavior.
- Test externally observable behavior and independently expected outcomes, not private function structure, duplicated policy calculations or snapshots copied from implementation. Follow existing credential-owner, login-conversation, shared-interaction, source CLI/PTY and installed-setup fixture patterns.
- Prove policy serialization and schema decoding, source-versus-destination distinctions, selected default, reference eligibility and plan interpretation without putting keys into serializable observations.
- Exercise actual read-only loading through its public interface: lookup order, source absence, empty environment stopping, empty file continuation, explicit references, rejected files, missing repository scope and authoritative hook capture.
- Exercise credential owners with controlled file/native fixtures: permission safety, symlink and unsafe-target refusal, preservation of unrelated entries, atomic replacement, stale proposal rejection, contention, known precommit failure and honest recovery observations. Bind replacement and generation behavior to real consumers where required.
- Exercise the production conversation with scripted interaction: destination selection, preview, hidden capture, separate confirmation, decline, Back, cancellation/EOF/interruption, stale observations, fresh reapproval and key exclusion. Check saved-versus-active reporting and setup/replacement consumers.
- Generate Mermaid from actual interpreter/reducer replays with independent assertions for the named outcomes. Generate README/guide views from the policy and extensions; freshness checks establish generated consistency, not exhaustive correctness or platform support.
- Run controlled macOS and Linux source and installed execution checks, including destination saving/loading and the physical interaction/session boundary. Use isolated credential fixtures, not personal keys, and make zero provider requests. Record platform and candidate/archive provenance; one platform or an earlier archive cannot establish another candidate's execution.
- Select required local checks through the repository checks policy and testing matrix. Run relevant cheap prerequisites and focused consumers before costly gates, use finite deadlines, and claim only executed evidence. Implementation completion is based on the required local checks; GitHub CI is not an additional completion gate.

- Include controlled development-workflow acceptance on macOS and Linux through the existing dev-install/setup/update consumers: save/load through guided setup and `--new-key`, preserve credentials across a rebuilt snapshot and activation, retain the reviewed project/user lookup coordinates, and verify exclusion from package/build artifacts. Reuse the established source and installed seams and runners; do not introduce a separate development credential system or runner solely for this issue.

## Out of Scope

- Changing environment/file/native lookup order beyond the explicit empty-environment correction.
- Offering project `.env` as a managed save destination, arbitrary credential paths, new model-provider selection or a new generic secrets framework.
- Automatically migrating or deleting existing native keys, user files or project files. Native logout does not gain authority to delete file credentials.
- Automatic Git staging, committing, or silent alteration of project ignore rules.
- Redesigning native-store signing/access-control behavior, or claiming that this work explains the owner's observed macOS prompts. File-backed lookup avoids native access for that selected source; native operations may still require interaction.
- Paid provider validation, changing paid-verification consent, or sending private source during credential tests.
- Changing the existing deliberate no-repository lookup scope, resident capture authority, or direct credential-stdin automation contract.
- A new package, universal wizard, generic projection framework, or formally verified credential core.
- Treating generated diagrams, source inspection or deterministic fixtures as exhaustive platform support or native-agent acceptance.

## Further Notes

**Purpose:** Specify #248's credential destinations and shared executable policy model. **Status:** Ready for implementation. **Authority:** Owner-accepted product decisions from this conversation, constrained by the accepted administration interaction and credential contracts. **Expected use:** Implement and qualify this issue through its named owners. **Lifecycle:** At implementation acceptance, consolidate durable behavior and architecture into their maintained contract owners and generated documentation; retain this issue as the tracker decision and acceptance record.

The owner accepted the proposed user-file default and flow, then accepted the two Astra architectural assessments on 2026-10-07. Those assessments recommended existing-package ownership and identified the empty-environment mismatch. The owner subsequently requested synthesis into this existing issue rather than a further interview.

Abide's inspected source informed the user-file/project-local choices; no Abide dependency is adopted. Classification: **BORROW** the destination pattern. Source class: **SRC**. Verification state: **SOURCE-INSPECTED**, not runtime-tested. Hapsland's approved policy and safety requirements govern this implementation.

The existing direct credential-stdin route remains an explicit automation exception and must not acquire unsolicited dialogs or silently change its native-save contract. This issue's new default governs the modeled destination-selection flow. Programmatic policy/plans are serializable; adding another automation CLI contract is separate scope.

No implementation or validation result is implied by publishing this spec. Record actual checks and any observed limitations separately at acceptance.

title: Add optional OpenAI Decisions API review provider through Effect DecisionModel
body:
Add OpenAI Decisions API as an optional Hapsland review backend through Effect's provider-neutral `Decision` / `DecisionModel` boundary.

This is deferred future work. Implementation should recheck the OpenAI API and Effect provider support before choosing the adapter approach.

Context checked on 2026-10-07:
- Hapsland currently supports Jev through `@effect/ai-typesafe` and Cloudflare Clef/Clef Flash; OpenAI is absent from the provider configuration and catalog.
- OpenAI documents a public-beta `POST /v1/decisions` endpoint with `gpt-6-luna`, supporting predicate, choice, and score questions.
- Inspection of published `@effect/ai-openai@4.0.2` found no DecisionModel adapter or `/decisions` client implementation. This observation is time-bound and must be rechecked.

Official API guide: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/decisions
Effect provider source: https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/tree/main/packages/ai/openai/src

Proposed scope and acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Recheck current API availability, supported models, request limits, refusal behavior, and Effect integration. Prefer an upstream OpenAI DecisionModel adapter if available; otherwise implement a bounded adapter through Effect's DecisionModel API.
- [ ] Map Hapsland's probability rules to OpenAI predicate questions, preserving shared input, question identity, answer validation, and existing rule threshold semantics. Choice/score support is outside the initial scope.
- [ ] Add an explicit optional OpenAI provider selection, model/destination identity, credential configuration, consent/egress handling, and vendor limits to the existing provider owners. Preserve the current default backend.
- [ ] Route requests through the existing review transport and content-isolation boundaries; cover refusals, malformed/missing answers, HTTP failures, request limits, and cancellation/deadline behavior.
- [ ] Add deterministic offline adapter and HTTP-wire tests, plus affected configuration and provider-wiring coverage. Select required local checks using CHECKS.md and docs/testing-matrix.md.
- [ ] Update the maintained provider/configuration documentation. Keep Hapsland-owned formats at version 1 and Effect packages pinned to one mutually compatible exact cohort.
- [ ] At a declared validation milestone, perform a bounded live check if credentials are available; retain only sanitized contract/timing evidence. State explicitly if live validation was not performed.

Implementation entry points:
- `packages/review-execution/src/jev-decision.ts`
- `packages/review-execution/src/review-providers/live.ts`
- `packages/review-execution/src/review-providers/transport.ts`
- `packages/review-definition/src/review-providers/catalog.ts`
- `packages/runtime-inputs/src/configuration/types.ts`
- `docs/review-providers.md`

This issue proposes future scope; it does not establish current OpenAI support, live validation, or an accepted replacement for Jev.

title: Validate Cloudflare decision providers and assess upstream Effect integration
body:
Deferred follow-up for Hapsland's Cloudflare decision backend (Workers AI Clef and Clef Flash).

Cloudflare support already exists through a local Effect `DecisionModel` adapter. This task concerns verifying current upstream support and completing the remaining validation and limit boundaries, rather than adding a duplicate backend.

Current repository evidence, inspected on 2026-10-07:
- `packages/review-execution/src/review-providers/cloudflare.ts` maps probability decisions to Workers AI questions and validates Noul answers.
- User configuration supports explicit Cloudflare model/account selection and `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` or a user-owned credential reference.
- Offline checks cover transport shape, question identity, response validation, and native question/body limits.
- `docs/review-providers.md` explicitly claims no live Cloudflare requests, quality comparisons, latency measurements, or native runtime/platform validation. Token budgets are declared but unmeasured; preventing upstream truncation is unresolved.

Proposed scope and acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Recheck Cloudflare's current decision models, wire contract, limits, truncation behavior, and credentials using primary sources. Record documented claims separately from observed behavior.
- [ ] Check whether Effect now provides a maintained Cloudflare DecisionModel adapter. Adopt it only if it preserves Hapsland's required semantics, explicit destination identity, shared transport, and content isolation; delete the superseded local implementation if adopted. Otherwise retain the existing adapter with a documented reason.
- [ ] Validate Clef and Clef Flash probability mapping, criteria, qualified rule IDs, exact answer/model matching, sanitized failures, and cancellation/deadline behavior against the current API contract.
- [ ] Resolve the token-budget/truncation gap: propose and explicitly decide an adequate measurement/admission policy before implementation. Do not claim exact enforcement from a character or byte estimate, silently truncate source, or introduce splitting/fallback/retries without an accepted behavior decision.
- [ ] At a declared validation milestone with credentials available, perform bounded live contract and latency checks for both supported models. Keep ordinary tests deterministic and offline; retain only sanitized evidence and disclose untested boundaries.
- [ ] If comparing review quality, define the labeled corpus, metrics, and acceptance criteria before execution; report results separately from transport correctness. A live smoke check alone does not establish quality or native runtime support.
- [ ] Run affected offline provider/configuration/wire checks selected through CHECKS.md and docs/testing-matrix.md, and update maintained provider guidance with the actual results and remaining limits.

Primary documentation to recheck:
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/models/clef/
- https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/models/clef-flash/

Implementation/evidence owners:
- `packages/review-execution/src/review-providers/cloudflare.ts`
- `packages/review-execution/src/review-providers/request.ts`
- `packages/review-execution/src/review-providers/transport.ts`
- `packages/review-definition/src/review-providers/catalog.ts`
- `src/review-providers/cloudflare.test.ts`
