Coordinate credential/selection decisions with #219. Related future OpenAI provider task: #249. This issue proposes future work and does not establish live Cloudflare validation or change the default Jev backend.

title: Bind CLI user journeys to generated terminal flow diagrams
body:
## Summary

Require generated Markdown diagrams for every registered administration terminal flow. This branch also contains the two #248 credential-saving commits already merged into local master but not yet published to GitHub.

```text
closed flow registry
  → typed production input and child-flow dispatch
  → complete replay-generator mapping
  → generated journey index and six flow documents

compiler/workspace entry
  → reject unregistered input, missing diagrams or missing generators
product build
  → replay every flow and reject stale diagrams before assembly
```

Generate command syntax from the same command and parameter declarations used by the CLI parser; remove handwritten command strings from the journey registry. Index eight user journeys by actual CLI commands, with typed production handler bindings and root-flow reachability checks. Generate one setup journey by composing the real agent-selection, per-agent setup, login and verification interpreters; remove the separate selection document. Login replays cover all three saving destinations, and rules replays cover create, connect, enable and disable. Remove the unused confirmation implementation, export and tests. The index contains commands and diagram links; setup uses one connected graph with its outcomes. Public diagrams use readable choices and outcomes; test-scenario tables, revision counters and historical navigation/test logs are removed from Markdown while executable replay assertions remain.

## Evidence

- **Before:** Six generated diagrams had a handwritten inventory and hardcoded generator list; compiler entry points did not require new flows to have diagrams.
  **After:** Negative tests exercise the real compiler entries and reject unregistered prompts, missing diagrams/generators, low-level and namespace dispatch bypasses, undeclared child flows and stale diagram output.
- Passed 87 focused production tests, eight flow-enforcement tests, four compiler-selection tests and the documentation-runner test.
- Passed source typechecking, affected package TypeScript compilation, lint/format, configuration-boundary and module-architecture checks. All seven registered input flows map to six current generated documents. The latest candidate passed 35 affected CLI/conversation tests, all eight enforcement tests, typechecking and lint/format; composed setup and every diagram match their maintained Markdown.
- The command-syntax candidate passed 10 affected parser/CLI/diagram tests, the parser-command/flag rename mutation test, all eight enforcement tests, source typechecking, lint/format and diagram freshness. The mutation changes `rules create --id` to `rules author --identity` in an isolated source copy and verifies both generated syntax and real parsing. Lifecycle binding names remain constrained by the parser command union.
- Standards and specification reviews are clear after fixing their findings.
- Heavy gates remain paused at the owner's request. Full product build, full-project gate and installed/platform validation were not run. Finite replays establish diagram freshness, not exhaustive transition coverage.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Reversible code and documentation changes; no persisted-format migration.

**Blast Radius:** administration

Changes setup navigation ownership and compiler/build prerequisites. New prompt owners must register their input, composition and replay diagram. Stale diagrams block product assembly.

title: Distinguish capture size refusals from unavailable reads and preparation admission failures
body:
# Explain capture and preparation refusals with typed diagnostic facts

**Purpose:** Specify #252's capture/preparation diagnosis and its interface with parallel #256 work.
**Status:** Accepted owner design, ready for implementation; producer changes have begun but are unqualified.
**Authority:** Accepted decisions from the originating issue and owner interview, synthesized through to-spec. Existing review, file-policy, resource, consent and inspection contracts retain authority except for the explicit diagnostic and validation decisions below. Source findings and earlier observations are evidence, not proof of installed causality.
**Expected use:** Implement #252's producers and qualify its own acceptance independently of #256.
**Lifecycle:** Update this issue for accepted scope/interface amendments. Consolidate shipped behavior into maintained review-resource and inspection/status documentation. This issue owns the specification; temporary research is consolidated and deleted when #252 closes.

## Problem Statement

An operator sees an edit received and accepted by Hapsland but no subsequent review preparation. The retained explanation, `capture-unavailable`, combines source-capture failure with preparation admission refusal and does not identify which boundary stopped work. Acceptance of an edit is not successful capture, preparation, classifier invocation or a clear review.

The original observation was made on 2026-10-08 using Codex 0.160.1 and installed snapshot `snapshot-fdLz9j`. Receipt `22244077-6c12-42dc-9773-913ea881f1ba` recorded an update, membership in the same pinned root with no skipped paths, accepted admission, preparation skipped and a `capture-unavailable` omission. The observed file was 275,536 bytes against the then-current 262,144-byte capture ceiling. No classifier invocation was established. The size discrepancy was discriminating evidence, not a definitive installed causal reproduction.

A later installed receipt, `6709aeaf-4882-4557-bb4f-d5bbcda8df80` from `snapshot-p0z9Lb`, retained two source-read observations and the same ambiguous omission. Subsequent source diagnostics found successful stable capture of a 27,030-byte file, unknown analyzer preflight, and a 136,470,128-byte workspace reservation against a 33,554,432-byte recipient budget. These diagnostics distinguish a plausible preparation-accounting cause without establishing the original installed branch. The issue's comments retain exact observation provenance and limitations.

## Solution

Explain refusals using a closed tree of diagnostic codes and bounded code-specific factual arguments, attributed to the stage and boundary that actually observed them. Persist facts rather than error messages; the shared inspector derives wording. An operator can distinguish source size refusal, missing or inaccessible source, unstable capture, failed root/path validation, aggregate capture-budget refusal and preparation resource refusal.

Keep the existing capture, preparation, resident and inspection architecture. Preserve bounded reads, full-source requirements and current capacities. Improve lossy ledger results in place where existing authoritative decisions provide the necessary information. Successful capture never implies admitted materialization or completed review.

#252 owns capture/preparation producers and their diagnostic results. [#256](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/256) owns the shared persisted representation, validation, rendering and early native observation coverage. The issues are implemented concurrently in separate branches and qualify independently.

## User Stories

1. As an operator, I want an accepted edit that never reaches preparation to have an observed explanation, so that I can identify the boundary that stopped work.
2. As an operator, I want source size refusal distinguished from unavailable reading, so that I do not mistake a configured bound for a filesystem failure.
3. As an operator, I want the effective capture limit displayed, so that I can understand a refusal under a lowered project limit.
4. As an operator, I want observed file size included when reliably measured, so that I can compare the source with its effective limit.
5. As an operator, I want exact-limit and below-limit sources distinguished from over-limit sources, so that the explanation reflects the actual capture decision.
6. As an operator, I want disappearance identified when observed, so that I can distinguish a missing file from resource saturation.
7. As an operator, I want access failure identified when observed, so that I can recognize an inaccessible source without receiving sensitive OS error text.
8. As an operator, I want unstable reads identified when observed, so that concurrent mutation is not represented as successful capture.
9. As an operator, I want root and Git identity validation failures identified when observed, so that a changed physical source is not mistaken for an oversized file.
10. As an operator, I want path binding and file-kind validation distinguished from reading failures, so that I understand why a candidate could not become a trusted snapshot.
11. As an operator, I want unsupported source encoding or NUL content identified without retaining rejected contents, so that capture validation is explainable.
12. As an operator, I want an unavailable capture mechanism distinguished from source size refusal, so that platform-boundary failure does not look like policy exclusion.
13. As an operator, I want aggregate file or byte capture-budget refusal identified, so that I do not assume an individual source exceeded its own limit.
14. As an operator, I want successful reading separated from analyzer materialization admission, so that source-read evidence does not imply preparation succeeded.
15. As an operator, I want initial capture-workspace refusal visible, so that a candidate refused before reading still has a truthful explanation.
16. As an operator, I want a materialization resource refusal to report its requested bytes, so that the preparation charge is understandable.
17. As an operator, I want an authoritative limiting constraint preserved where available, so that useful ledger evidence is not discarded.
18. As an operator, I want an unspecified limiting pool to remain unspecified, so that later state is not used to invent the cause of an earlier refusal.
19. As an operator, I want stale-round or wrong-stage admission distinguished from capacity exhaustion, so that lifecycle refusal does not look like saturation.
20. As an operator, I want unexpected internal failures represented by a bounded panic diagnostic, so that they remain distinct from ordinary filesystem or lifecycle failures.
21. As an operator, I want missing or dropped evidence to remain unknown, so that incomplete history is not mistaken for panic or a precise refusal.
22. As an operator, I want an eligible candidate to remain selected after capture failure, so that its later failure is not mislabeled as file exclusion.
23. As an operator, I want refused candidates accessible through the inspector's existing show-all control, so that debugging does not need a new dashboard.
24. As an operator, I want diagnostic meanings preserved after reload and replay, so that retained facts remain explainable over time.
25. As an operator, I want receipts and later facts kept separate from classifier evidence, so that accepted ingress does not appear as successful or clear review.
26. As an operator, I want code-based explanations without source, credentials or raw exception strings, so that diagnostic recording does not disclose rejected content or secrets.
27. As an operator, I want new installed reproductions separated from historical hypotheses, so that reported receipt causality is not overstated.
28. As a contributor, I want capture results to expose success or a typed observed diagnosis, so that callers cannot silently discard the reason.
29. As a contributor, I want preparation admission results and cached refusals typed, so that a refusal is not later reduced to a misleading Boolean.
30. As a contributor, I want ledger outcomes improved without duplicating policy, so that the checked canonical decisions remain the source of authority.
31. As a contributor, I want production outcome types independent of inspection and views, so that review behavior remains usable without enabling debugging.
32. As a contributor, I want one shared closed diagnostic representation with explicit parallel ownership, so that #252 and #256 do not create conflicting formats or renderers.
33. As a contributor, I want focused unit tests and type safety to cover diagnostic permutations, so that this debugging feature does not add an unnecessarily expensive integration matrix.
34. As an operator, I want actual installed verification through the public inspector, so that source-only passes are not presented as native evidence.

## Implementation Decisions

### Diagnostic vocabulary and producer results

- Use closed discriminated outcomes with bounded, code-specific arguments. Preserve capture and preparation stage distinctions; a code is supported only by an actually observed branch.
- Capture returns either a captured stable snapshot or an unavailable result carrying its diagnosis. Materialization admission returns admitted or refused with a preparation diagnosis. Cache typed refusals rather than only rejected path membership.
- The finite capture codes are `capture-size-limit`, `capture-budget-limit`, `capture-unavailable`, `capture-unstable`, `capture-validation-failed`, and the shared `panic` code at the stable-capture boundary.
- Size refusal carries observed bytes and effective limit bytes. Aggregate refusal carries the files/bytes resource discriminator, used amount, requested amount and limit.
- Capture unavailable uses a closed missing/access/I/O/mechanism/unknown reason list. Unknown means that a precise cause was not established; it is not permission to infer a cause.
- Unstable capture can identify descriptor stability or disagreement between the two reads. Validation failure uses a closed root identity, Git identity, path binding, file kind, text encoding, source NUL byte or invalid capture-budget argument list.
- The finite preparation codes are `preparation-resource-refused`, `preparation-unavailable`, and shared `panic` at the review-preparation boundary.
- Preparation resource refusal carries capture-workspace/materialization phase and requested bytes. Preserve the existing authoritative global/recipient item/byte constraint only where supplied by the decision. Preparation unavailable distinguishes stale-round and wrong-stage.
- Numeric facts are finite, safe, nonnegative integers. Size facts come from the capture's descriptor observation, not a pathname stat performed after failure. Do not retain source text, raw native stderr, exception messages, templates, stacks or arbitrary detail dictionaries.
- Panic represents an actually observed unexpected application or protocol failure at a named boundary. Expected filesystem failures and missing/dropped history are not panic. Invalid internal measurements or capabilities remain typed precondition failures and are classified according to their observed context.
- Production capture/preparation types remain independent of inspection storage and rendering. The exact exported producer shapes and contributor handoff are published in [the interface discussion](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/252#issuecomment-6062912018) before exported failure signatures change.

### Capture and ledger authority

- Preserve descriptor-anchored bounded matching reads, root/path validation, cleanup and full-source capture. Refusal never returns partial source as review input. Preserve interruption rather than converting it to a successful diagnostic outcome.
- Native helper failures must carry the same truthful closed meanings as production capture. Distinguish failed stat from a measured identity mismatch and validate helper frames before trusting a success or precise failure.
- Align helper behavior with already accepted source ceilings where source inspection exposes a mismatch. This is an implementation parity repair, not an automatic increase to configured capture, graph, review-input or resident capacity limits.
- Identify aggregate capture refusal before reading as a budget decision, not an unavailable file or per-file size refusal.
- Improve initial preparation admission and resize results in place using the existing canonical command and rejection information. Initial resource refusal has no limiting-pool discriminator; retain that limitation. Resize already has an authoritative constraint and must preserve it.
- Keep invalid measurements, invalid reservation capabilities and canonical stale-round/wrong-stage rejection distinct from capacity refusal. Increment capacity-refused reporting only for an observed capacity refusal.
- Do not add a second policy reducer, pool-inference logic, a new resource service, parallel detailed/legacy methods, or Bend policy/ABI changes for this result projection.
- The measured-empty-TypeScript accounting repair already landed as commit `8772653`; do not reimplement it or expand supported callable analysis. Unknown parsing or expansion remains bounded and may be refused.

### Parallel ownership and inspector integration

- #252 proceeds in branch `task/252`; #256 proceeds concurrently in `task/256`. Contributors may inspect the other checkout read-only.
- #252 owns detailed capture/preparation vocabulary, producer results, ledger result improvements, numeric refusal facts and resident producer emission.
- #256 owns native metadata transport, initial selection outcomes, root receipts, common persisted diagnostic schema/validation, shared rendering and request-only default filtering.
- Coordinate overlapping adapter capture-result consumers and resident preparation-emission sections. Integrate changes through the assigned contributor rather than overwrite shared owners.
- #252 does not independently implement another persisted schema or renderer. #256 incorporates the finite producer vocabulary in the shared closed contract and derives wording from facts.
- Preserve existing receipt correlation, source/lifetime identity and immutable append-only facts. Where candidate identity is known, later diagnosis identifies the original candidate. Missing correlation remains incomplete rather than reconstructed from current disk state.
- Keep the existing request-only default list and show-all control specified by #256. Refused candidates need the show-all view; missing retained request evidence does not prove no invocation occurred.
- Keep owned formats at version 1 and remove superseded production paths in place. Do not introduce arbitrary future-code acceptance, compatibility shims or parallel legacy diagnostic formats.
- Preserve existing root-specific inspection consent, bounded best-effort recording, source confidentiality and independent recorder resources. Diagnostic recording does not authorize review or change scheduling.

## Testing Decisions

- The owner already accepted the seams: type safety and focused capture/preparation/ledger unit tests for deterministic permutations, plus manual actual installed Codex hook → resident → private journal → public inspection API/browser verification, including reload and retained history replay. No further seam interview is required.
- Prefer existing fixtures and public behavior. Test that observed failures produce the right distinct explanations and block partial inputs or classifier work; do not merely assert private field assignments or mirror implementation branches.
- Unit-test configured lower limits, below/exact/above threshold capture, disappearance, access, unstable reads, root/path validation, encoding/file-kind failure, aggregate budget refusal and materialization refusal. Typecheck affected callers so unavailable capture or refused admission cannot be mistaken for success.
- Ledger tests distinguish actual canonical resource refusal from invalid measurement/capability and stale-round/wrong-stage rejection. Preserve resize's exact authoritative constraint without asserting an unavailable initial limiting pool.
- Use existing source/preparation/resource fixtures for these value cases. Do not expand heavy integration matrices merely to repeat the complete diagnostic permutation list; this is a debugging feature rather than new review policy.
- Manually exercise a supported, stable eligible edit below its effective limit through ordinary installed Codex apply_patch. Observe receipt, admission, preparation and its actual subsequent outcome.
- Exercise otherwise eligible over-limit source: show the size refusal and effective limit, without partial review input or a claimed classifier call. Exercise unavailable capture separately from successful capture followed by preparation resource refusal.
- Inspect the actual public rows/details through the existing show-all control, reload and history replay. Distinctions remain preserved; dropped facts, absent correlation and retained old imprecise evidence remain explicitly unknown.
- Identify the exact installed candidate and retain only sanitized receipt/outcome and timing evidence. Source diagnostics, clean builds and owner-reported earlier focused passes do not prove the installed branch or additional platform support.
- Manual testing is authorized; ordinary automated tests remain offline and deterministic. No paid live Jev run is required.
- Select required local checks from repository checks policy and testing matrix. Run fast TypeScript checks, focused affected owners/consumers and required physical checks appropriate to changed boundaries. This spec does not justify a full gate or waiting for GitHub CI.
- Closure still requires resolving the reported omissions' causal explanation using actual available installed evidence. A new-candidate reproduction and a plausible historical explanation are different evidence. If the old exact branch cannot be established, retain that limitation and do not silently count the historical item as resolved.
- #252 and #256 complete independently against their own required checks and observations. #256's broader native coverage acceptance is not added to #252's diagnostic test matrix; #256 generic handling does not complete #252.

## Out of Scope

- Silent increases to source, graph, review-input or resident resource ceilings; source truncation or partial review inputs.
- A broader unknown-preflight/fallback redesign, new callable support or JavaScript review support.
- A new diagnostics framework, generic event bus, resource service, second policy reducer or new storage/replay engine.
- Pool accounting telemetry, full charge inventories, or limiting-pool inference from a later snapshot.
- Reimplementing #256's early native coverage, metadata transport, shared persisted schema, renderer or request-only filtering.
- Additional runtime/tool/operation support, broad cross-root grouping or historical backfill.
- Raw exception/stderr/source/credential logging and rendered error-message persistence.
- New heavy integration matrices for diagnostic permutations or paid live Jev validation.
- Claims of classifier invocation, backend receipt, successful/clear review, agent visibility, adoption or repair from edit admission or source-read evidence.

## Further Notes

- This is the owner-confirmed synthesis after grilling and Astra review. The owner explicitly delegated ledger-result design to implementation review: improve it elegantly where possible, otherwise adhere to its existing authority.
- Initial and later installed observations remain historical evidence with the limitations stated above and in the issue comments. An adjacent receipt omitted for `import` is separate; do not conflate it with these capture/preparation omissions.
- The previously installed accounting-repair candidate was `snapshot-ubO1NT`, archive SHA-256 `e71bdc8e3de47b7a86d4c9140e2d87897d500baff34584788a6bf50136394a18`. The then-running Codex process relaunched the older resident; installed verification was pending restart/trust renewal. This is an earlier observation, not a claim about the current active executable.
- [#225](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/225), [#227](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/227) and [#228](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/228) retain broader inspection authority. [#256](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/256) owns the common diagnostic foundation and parallel interface expectations.
- Producer edits have begun in the isolated #252 branch. They are unqualified work in progress: this specification claims no passing runtime tests, installed diagnosis, classification or completion.

title: Repair the failing in-root Git administration selection fixture after classifying root discovery
body:
## Reproduced failure

On source commit `26256a5a` (2026-10-08, Linux arm64, Node 24.20.0), `src/direct-event/selection-capture.test.ts` fails at line 126 in `rejects the structured in-root Git directory without prefix overreach`.

The fixture moves `.git` to `git-admin`, writes `.git` as `gitdir: git-admin`, and adapts a native patch targeting `git-admin/evidence.ts`. It expects an observation containing the physical Git directory; the adapter returns undefined instead. This does not establish unsafe access or a production regression: root discovery may intentionally refuse a candidate inside Git administration, leaving the fixture's observation assumption obsolete.

## Evidence

- Initial focused run: 14 passed, 1 failed; both configured root-source-cap tests passed.
- Isolated repeat with `--testNamePattern=structured`: same failure, 1 failed and 12 skipped; compilation passed; total 8.048 seconds.
- Runner IDs: `20261008041142674-1383043-83a4ad` and `20261008041259200-1399155-e56374`.
- No production or fixture edits were made during diagnosis.

## Required resolution

Trace the current root-discovery/eligibility contract and classify this as a fixture assumption failure or a supported-root implementation defect before repairing it.

Preserve both acceptance boundaries: source inside the actual Git administration directory is refused; a similarly named ordinary source directory (`git-admin-sibling`) is eligible. If early adapter refusal is correct, establish root identity through an ordinary eligible source candidate and independently prove administration-path refusal. Do not weaken path protections merely to restore the fixture.

Run the complete affected selection/capture test file and affected root-discovery consumer tests after repair. Pin the tested candidate and report the classification; do not treat the current failed file as passing capture qualification.

title: Specify callable review for const arrows and Effect wrappers, with precise overload exclusions
body:
## Observed use case

Hapsland received ordinary Codex `apply_patch` edits to Dalph's `pendingActiveRefreshG2OperationFor`, an exported TypeScript const arrow function. Receipt `d699777f-be9e-4a4f-82c3-685fdc0282e4` in `/workspace/typescript/dalph-retained-history-cpu` was admitted but preparation was skipped with two `import` omissions. No classifier execution is established.

The actual 230934-byte source file is eligible and current production capture succeeds with two stable reads. Current parser reports no syntax error. The function analyzer returns undefined for the complete file; removing its top-level overloaded-function group in memory makes analysis available (37 types, zero functions). Production `collectFunctionFact` rejects names present in function signatures, and `collectDeclarationFact` collects `function_declaration`, not const arrow callables. The edited callable therefore remains absent even when the unrelated overload group is removed. No project source was changed for these diagnostics.

## Task

Decide and specify bounded review of ordinary const arrow functions and Effect-wrapped callables, and isolation of unrelated unsupported overloads, then implement the accepted scope. This is a supported-use expansion/diagnostic task, not a claim that current deliberately conservative behavior violates an existing arrow-function support contract.

Explain actual function-extraction exclusions instead of reporting the legacy same-file type analyzer's `import` reason for a failed function branch. Coordinate inspection details with #228; capture/resource omissions remain #252. Do not infer complete review from admitted ingress.

## Required decision and acceptance cases

- An exported named const arrow function is edited through normal native Codex apply_patch, with no instructions forcing a special coding style. Define which forms are supported and establish edited-root selection, source location, signature/body and bounded dependency evidence.
- A callable declared through idiomatic `Effect.fn`/`Effect.fnUntraced` is edited. Explicitly accept its representation or report unsupported form; do not silently claim it was reviewed.
- An unrelated overloaded function in the same file must have a specified outcome: bounded isolation of supported roots or a precise whole-file refusal. Do not silently discard a requested supported root with an unrelated `import` label.
- Unsupported dynamic bindings, shadowing, ambiguity and incomplete dependency evidence remain explicit. Do not invent exact references or relax confidentiality/resource ceilings.
- Receipt/admission, preparation exclusion and actual classifier outcome stay distinct in the public API/dashboard, including replay.

Map accepted cases to focused extractor/root-selection tests and a real installed Codex -> resident -> inspection consumer. Preserve current source isolation and input limits. Verify the real Dalph pattern after acceptance; editing application style purely to make a probe pass is not completion.

title: Resolve npm-owned tooling correctly when repository scripts run through Bun
body:
## Reproduced tooling failure

The repository declares `packageManager: bun@1.3.14`, but `mise exec -- bun run typecheck:source` fails in `scripts/check-development-imports.mjs` with four `Cannot find module '../package.json'` errors whose require stack points to `/home/node/.local/share/mise/installs/bun/1.3.14/bin/bun`.

On source commit 26256a5a1b0bb1061e484b9dd6d3268d605d5bf0, 2026-10-08, Linux arm64 and Node 24.20.0, TypeScript compilation, package graph and release identity checks completed before this failure. `bun run docs:generated:check` also passed. No helper or dependency modifications were made during diagnosis.

`scripts/npm-tooling.mjs` uses `process.env.npm_execpath` as the default entrypoint and immediately passes a defined value to `checkedRequire`, which requires `../package.json` and demands package name npm. Bun's script environment supplies the Bun executable instead. The absent-env fallback is never reached.

## Required repair

Make the tooling helper work under the repository's declared Bun script runner. Distinguish the package manager's script-runner path from a verified npm CLI entrypoint needed to access npm-owned packlist/Arborist dependencies. Preserve genuine explicit override validation, authoritative package ownership and errors for invalid inputs; do not merely hide import validation failures or remove the check.

## Acceptance

- Run the actual `bun run typecheck:source` consumer on Linux arm64, including development-import validation, and observe completion.
- Focused helper tests cover Bun-provided npm_execpath, a verified npm CLI entrypoint, absent environment with PATH discovery, and invalid explicit overrides.
- Exercise affected package-file/packlist consumers against the same environment, preserving source/packaging selection.
- Record exact candidate and prerequisites; no full quality gate is required solely for this bounded helper repair.

title: Record excluded native edits with shared coded inspection diagnostics
body:
# Explain native edit exclusions with a shared inspection diagnostic foundation

**Purpose:** Specify #256's native observation coverage and the diagnostic foundation shared with #252.
**Status:** Accepted owner design, ready for implementation; no implementation or installed validation claim.
**Authority:** Accepted product decisions from the originating design interview. Existing review, advicee, file-policy, resource, consent and inspection contracts remain authoritative except for the explicit inspection amendments below.
**Expected use:** Implement #256 and coordinate parallel #252 work against the interface and ownership split below.
**Lifecycle:** Update this issue for accepted scope/interface changes. Consolidate shipped behavior into maintained inspection/status documentation. This local publication staging file is temporary: after publication to #256, delete it; the issue owns the specification.

## Problem Statement

An operator cannot distinguish a native edit filtered out before resident recording from an event that never reached Hapsland. The original #256 report observed three ordinary Codex `.mjs` edits with inspection enabled and no matching receipts; earlier supported TypeScript edits had receipts. Unsupported-language review is not required, but the missing coverage explanation makes debugging misleading.

#252 exposes a related problem later in the process: ingress is recorded and accepted, but capture or preparation refusal collapses into an ambiguous diagnostic. The issues share diagnostic representation and display machinery, while owning different observation boundaries and separate acceptance scenarios.

## Solution

Record bounded metadata for valid native edit observations before review filtering can discard them, across the existing Codex CLI, Claude Code and Pi integrations. Explain the initial eligibility of each candidate without capturing excluded source or requesting review. Keep observation, selection, capture, admission, preparation and request evidence distinct.

Use a shared closed diagnostic vocabulary with code-specific typed arguments. Persist facts rather than rendered error messages. The inspector derives wording and presentation from those facts.

The default edit list continues to focus on edits with captured request attempts. Its existing filter lets the operator reveal excluded and otherwise unreviewed observations with their precise explanations. Recording remains consented, bounded and best effort.

## User Stories

1. As an operator, I want an unsupported native edit to have a captured observation when inspection is enabled, so that silence is not mistaken for review or hook failure.
2. As an operator, I want supported and unsupported edits in one session to be distinguishable, so that I can understand the integration's coverage.
3. As an operator, I want the same explanation model across existing runtime integrations, so that runtime differences do not change diagnostic meanings.
4. As an operator, I want an explicit unsupported-language or extension reason, so that I do not infer a backend failure.
5. As an operator, I want configured language disablement distinguished from an unsupported extension, so that I can identify an actionable configuration choice.
6. As an operator, I want include, exclude and protection decisions distinguished, so that I can explain why a candidate did not proceed.
7. As an operator, I want all observed candidates in a mixed patch represented, so that review of one file does not obscure exclusion of another.
8. As an operator, I want candidate decisions that were not evaluated to remain explicit, so that a short-circuited path is not presented as selected.
9. As an operator, I want source capture failures separated from selection exclusions, so that an eligible file is not mislabeled as prohibited.
10. As an operator, I want preparation resource refusal separated from source capture failure, so that successful reading is not mistaken for successful preparation.
11. As an operator, I want stable diagnostic codes and typed arguments in history, so that message templates can change without changing historical facts.
12. As an operator, I want unexpected failures represented by a bounded panic diagnostic, so that known errors remain distinct from unanticipated faults.
13. As an operator, I want useful debugging metadata including paths under inspection consent, so that the diagnostic can identify the affected candidate.
14. As an operator, I want excluded source and credentials absent from metadata recording, so that irrelevant secrets do not enter the journal.
15. As an operator, I want observation recording independent of review credentials, so that credential failure does not erase ingress evidence.
16. As an operator, I want root-specific consent respected for mixed-root native observations, so that one project's consent does not enable another project's recording.
17. As an operator, I want review routing refusal distinguished from file eligibility, so that a pinned working root is not mistaken for a language exclusion.
18. As an operator, I want initial candidate metadata and its known selection results retained together, so that their explanation cannot be independently dropped at initial publication.
19. As an operator, I want later facts appended to the same root receipt, so that the inspector can explain the observed progression without rewriting history.
20. As an operator, I want request attempts distinguished from model input, so that the default list does not claim that prepared input reached transport.
21. As an operator, I want failed request attempts visible in the default list, so that transport failure is not confused with absence of a request attempt.
22. As an operator, I want excluded and unreviewed observations accessible through the existing filter, so that debugging does not require a new dashboard.
23. As an operator, I want reused evaluations linked without adding fresh request counts, so that reuse remains distinguishable from transport invocation.
24. As an operator, I want missing retained request evidence described honestly, so that a hidden edit is not proof that no request occurred.
25. As an operator, I want disabled recording, unavailable consent, dropped facts and known expiry/eviction distinguished, so that partial history is not presented as complete coverage.
26. As an operator, I want metadata-only recording not to create review work or wait for persistence, so that debugging does not change review scheduling.
27. As an operator, I want replay and reload to preserve diagnostic meanings, so that the same retained facts explain the same observed behavior.
28. As a contributor, I want #256 and #252 to share a stable diagnostic interface with explicit ownership, so that their producers and consumers can be implemented in parallel.
29. As a contributor, I want each issue qualified independently, so that a completed coverage fix does not falsely establish capture diagnostics or causal verification.

## Implementation Decisions

### Native observation and identity

- Separate bounded native metadata extraction from file selection, stable source capture and verified review attribution. Valid runtime identity and named candidates establish an observed native candidate, not a successful attributed source snapshot.
- Apply this separation across existing Codex CLI, Claude Code and Pi native edit integrations. Preserve their accepted native event profiles and bounds; do not introduce new runtime, tool, operation or malformed-event support.
- Keep the original candidate position and operation/path metadata. Preserve supported move metadata where actually available; do not infer missing endpoints or operation support.
- Partition by positively discovered physical working root. Create one resident-owned receipt per root projection of a received native observation, reusing that receipt during routing attempts within that ingress operation. Do not introduce cross-root row grouping or a durable native-event deduplication subsystem.
- Include the root-local original candidates and their already-known initial selection outcomes in a single immutable receipt fact. Outcomes distinguish selected, excluded with a precise code, unavailable with a precise code, and not evaluated. Selection does not imply successful capture, attribution, admission or review.
- Append later observed facts linked to the receipt. Preserve source/lifetime and sequence journal identity. No row rewrite, generic atomic event bundle or second policy reducer is introduced.
- Respect current routing and pre-edit settings authority. A skipped other-root observation is a routing/admission result, not file exclusion; record only under that root's own inspection consent.

### Recording transport and consent

- Normal review admission carries native metadata alongside the existing review observation. When adaptation or dispatch terminates before admission, use an explicit bounded metadata-only recording request instead. These are mutually exclusive submission paths for one terminal hook outcome.
- The metadata-only request does not accept arbitrary journal facts, credentials, source payloads or caller-selected journal identities. It does not join a review round, acquire review capacity, resolve credentials or dispatch a classifier.
- Preserve the resident-owned asynchronous recorder and its consent epochs/publication checks. Refresh inspection consent independently for each recorded root. Review selection continues to use the established pre-edit policy snapshot rather than rereading settings to rewrite a historical decision.
- Inspection is a deliberately enabled debugging facility. Useful paths, including protected filenames, may be disclosed under that consent. Excluded contents, private-key material, credential values, authorization headers and raw hook payloads have no place in the metadata envelope.
- An unknown target root or a hook failure before recording remains outside positively observed coverage. Never synthesize a receipt or exclusion from current filesystem hashes.

### Shared diagnostic contract and parallel ownership

- Diagnostics use a closed discriminated union. Each code has a bounded, code-specific argument schema; stage and code combinations are validated. Persist code and structured factual arguments, not message text, templates, stack traces, raw exception strings or arbitrary detail dictionaries.
- Preserve stage-specific facts. Selection exclusion, capture failure and preparation refusal remain separately attributable even when rendered by common diagnostic presentation logic.
- A panic catch-all represents an actually observed unexpected failure at a named boundary. It carries only bounded diagnostic metadata appropriate to that code. Missing/dropped history is unknown coverage, not panic. A precise code must be supported by the observed branch; never guess from filesystem state or an ambiguous old reason.
- #256 owns the common persisted representation/validation and shared dashboard renderer, native metadata transport, root receipts and selection outcomes. #252 owns the detailed capture/preparation outcome vocabulary and producer-side typed results, numeric size/limit facts, and resource-refusal distinctions. Production outcome types must remain usable without importing the inspector or its view layer.
- Before changing exported failure signatures, publish the finite #252 code/argument list and producer result shape in the #252 discussion, referenced from this issue. #256 incorporates that list in the closed persisted contract. This is an implementation handoff between contributors, not another owner interview or approval gate.
- #256's initial foundation must accommodate the agreed stage distinction without implementing #252's diagnosis. An existing imprecise capture failure may remain explicitly unavailable until #252 supplies an observed precise cause; do not claim #252 complete from #256's generic handling.
- Coordinate shared-file sections before editing; use isolated checkouts for implementation where appropriate. #256 owns shared receipt/schema/rendering sections; #252 owns capture and preparation producers and their resident diagnostic emission. Changes to a shared owner go through its assigned contributor rather than competing edits.
- Preserve version-one owned formats and remove superseded maintained paths when replacement is implemented. No compatibility shim, arbitrary future-code acceptance or parallel legacy diagnostic format.

### Inspector and other reporting

- Default row visibility requires a retained transport-invocation fact directly correlated with the receipt. Model-input evidence alone is insufficient. Missing or oversized payload bytes do not negate an observed invocation.
- Keep failed transport attempts visible. Do not infer remote receipt, review completion or clear outcome from invocation.
- Reused/joined/cached edits without directly correlated request attempts remain hidden by default. Their relation to original evaluation evidence remains accessible through the existing filter; an original request is not counted again as a fresh request for the consuming edit.
- Retain the existing control for revealing observations without retained request evidence. Hidden-count wording must describe retained evidence rather than categorically claiming that calls did not occur. Excluded observations display their per-candidate codes through derived labels/details.
- Keep the filter provider-neutral and preserve controlled/live distinctions; deterministic controlled requests are not evidence of live Jev calls.
- Known all-excluded observations use the existing skipped activity state. Operational failure and incomplete/unavailable capture remain distinct. No new analytics feature is introduced.
- Keep current immutable storage, independent fact retention and read/replay machinery. Later facts without a receipt remain incomplete; absent admission remains unknown. Known expiry/capacity removal, replay/view limits and recording state preserve their existing meanings.

## Testing Decisions

- The owner already accepted the primary external seam: a real installed native Codex hook consumer through resident recording, private journal, public inspection HTTP/SSE and rendered browser. Retain that seam; this specification adds no new test-only bus or fabricated-history acceptance source.
- Good tests observe actual native ingress, recording, provider invocation and user-visible distinctions. They must distinguish plausible missing-ingress, policy-exclusion and operational-failure outcomes without asserting only internal field assignments.
- Use the existing real-resident, offline provider, native adapter and public inspector/browser fixtures for the richer deterministic matrix across existing integrations. Ordinary tests remain offline; this issue requires no paid live Jev run.
- In one installed Codex session with inspection enabled, make a supported TypeScript edit and an unsupported `.mjs` edit without special agent instructions. The public feed and show-all view must establish real ingress and distinct outcomes. The unsupported edit must not produce source capture or a classifier request.
- Exercise a supported mixed patch: initial metadata preserves selected and excluded candidates; only eligible attributed candidates proceed. Verify root-specific consent/routing using existing root-routing fixtures, without adding general multi-root product support.
- Verify enabled/disabled/unavailable recording, credential failure before admission, known all-excluded status, and truthful unknown coverage. Reuse recorder, consent, IPC and replay fixtures for their existing boundaries.
- Verify the closed code/argument schema and derived labels through public feed/browser behavior. Reload and replay must preserve meanings. No rendered error message should be required in persisted diagnostic records.
- Verify request-only filtering using actual transport observations: model input without invocation stays hidden; attempted failed transport is visible; excluded/reused edits remain accessible through the existing control; replay counts no identity twice.
- #252 separately qualifies threshold boundaries, unavailable/unstable reads, access/root validation, preparation resource refusal and causal explanation of its reported installed omissions. These do not become #256 completion requirements.
- Select required local checks through the repository testing matrix and checks policy: fast TypeScript checks, focused affected-owner/consumer checks, and affected transport/install/browser checks. Full-gate selection follows that policy; publishing this specification does not justify a full gate or a validation claim. Do not wait for GitHub CI as an extra completion gate.
- Installed evidence must identify the exact installed candidate and retain sanitized receipt/outcome evidence. Native observations establish only the exercised host/runtime boundary, not additional platform support or complete audit coverage.

## Out of Scope

- JavaScript review support, additional agent runtimes, generic shell-write discovery or checkpoint discovery.
- Expanded malformed/oversized native event profiles, a new general event framework or durable audit guarantees.
- Source capture for excluded candidates, source truncation, credential/error-body logging or automatic source/resource ceiling increases.
- Full cross-root dashboard design, receipt grouping across roots, durable native-event deduplication or new analytics metrics.
- New storage engines, atomic multi-fact bundles, all-or-nothing edit retention, historical backfill or filesystem-derived receipts.
- #252's detailed capture/preparation implementation and its installed causal verification; that work proceeds independently against the shared interface.
- Claims of backend receipt, agent/model visibility, adoption, repair or successful review from ingress/admission evidence.

## Further Notes

- This is the accepted 2026-10-08 design amendment after the owner interview and Astra consultation. It chooses recording of valid excluded native candidates; the original alternative of intentionally leaving unsupported edits unrecorded is superseded.
- The original observation involved three `.mjs` edits in the Hapsland repository. A read-only monitor observed changed hashes at 04:28:54 UTC but no matching receipt/admission/preparation facts; supported `.ts` edits in the same root/session had such facts. These observations do not prove the precise installed hook branch; installed reproduction remains required.
- [#225](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/225), [#227](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/227) and [#228](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/228) retain their broader inspector authority. This issue extends the early observation boundary; it does not promise every native invocation or filesystem edit is recorded.
- [#252](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/252) partially intersects at diagnostic representation and presentation. Its reported edits already had receipts; this issue's reported edits did not. Neither acceptance set subsumes the other.
- The owner can begin #252 producer diagnosis and focused tests immediately. Integration of exported failure shapes and shared schema/rendering uses the explicit contributor handoff above. The shared interface is specified here but not yet implemented.
- #256 and #252 complete independently after their own required local checks and native evidence pass. Neither issue should credit the other's unfinished acceptance, and neither should silently expand the agreed scope.


## Parallel #252 implementation coordination (2026-10-08)

#252 is being implemented concurrently in `task/252` (`/workspace/typescript/hapsland-252`); #256 uses `task/256` (`/workspace/typescript/hapsland-256`). Read-only inspection of the other checkout is encouraged. Ownership remains as specified above; coordinate overlapping adapter capture-result consumers and resident preparation-emission sections rather than overwriting them.

The owner-confirmed finite capture/preparation diagnostic vocabulary, typed result shapes, ledger improvement and proportionate validation scope are published in [#252's interface handoff](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/252#issuecomment-6062912018). #256 incorporates those codes and arguments in its existing closed persisted schema and renderer; #252 supplies production outcomes and emits their facts. Types remain independent of the inspector. No independent second schema/renderer or version bump is introduced.

For #252 diagnostic permutations, the owner selected type safety and focused unit tests plus manual installed/public-inspector verification (including reload/replay), rather than expanding heavy integration matrices. #256 retains its own accepted external seam and qualification requirements. Parallel implementation and accepted interfaces establish no runtime validation or completion claim.


The owner-confirmed #252 interview has now been synthesized through `to-spec` into the [complete #252 specification](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/252), with `ready-for-agent` applied. Its Testing Decisions record the already accepted unit/type-safety and manual installed-inspector seams; the interface handoff above remains the precise contributor coordination reference. #252 producer edits are unqualified work in progress, not a completed diagnosis or validation claim.

title: Reconcile retained build custody and stale group registrations after failed development installation
body:
The ordinary development installation failed at check-workspace-imports (computed callable extraction in flow-input.ts). Its retained product-build custody then prevented a focused consumer from compiling.

Observed on Linux arm64, Node 24.20.0 / Bun 1.3.14:
- The failed dev-install exited, but product-build/lock, lease.json and groups remained.
- After proving the initial owner absent, clearing only the abandoned lock allowed a new build lease. A subsequent source compilation failure triggered `Invalid build group registration`: the groups directory still contained registrations from the previous lease token.
- Manual reconciliation preserved the records and proved every recorded PID and group leader absent before clearing the retained lock, groups and lease. Subsequent focused workspace compilation and UI tests passed.

Investigate why the failed install retained custody, and provide a documented, exact stopped-writer reconciliation path covering the lock, lease and all registered groups together. Do not silently delete ambiguous records or weaken live-owner exclusion. Add a focused real failed-child/recovery regression demonstrating that stale-token registrations cannot poison a safely reconciled next build.

Evidence retained locally: /tmp/hapsland-dev-install-20261008.log, /tmp/hapsland-build-audit-20261008-0503, focused runs 20261008050300812-1673583-9bcc39 and 20261008050458249-1691378-73cbec. No full test run was requested or credited.

title: Reconcile resident updates without unnecessary hook reinstallation
body:
**Purpose:** Specify shared-resident updates and independently scoped runtime-hook updates.
**Status:** Accepted owner decisions, ready for implementation; not implementation or validation evidence.
**Authority:** Product contract synthesized from the owner discussion on 2026-10-08. This issue owns the feature decisions; the advice contract owns general correctness and transient-work-loss policy.
**Expected use:** Guide implementation, review, and acceptance by developers and coding agents.
**Lifecycle:** Maintain this specification through implementation. At completion, consolidate shipped contracts into their maintained documentation owners and retain validation evidence separately; delete superseded temporary research.

## Problem Statement

An installed update can select new packaged code and rewrite hooks while an existing shared resident continues serving the previous build. Equal package versions do not establish equal builds, and restarting an agent does not establish that the resident changed. Users therefore cannot reliably tell whether an intended resident fix is active.

Updates also needlessly repeat setup if every release reinstalls native hooks. Resident updates and runtime-hook updates have different scopes: the shared resident naturally serves all its callers, whereas updating Codex hooks should affect only Codex hooks. Compatible callers should continue working quietly; genuinely incompatible callers need actionable agent-visible guidance.

## Solution

Use the existing installed-update workflow to select and activate a shared resident target, and update only the runtime hooks explicitly selected. Report actual activation, pending activation, or unavailability accurately. Preserve native registrations when they still apply. Expose actual caller incompatibility through ordinary resident communication and let capable hooks emit a short update-needed warning, independently throttled per agent to once per ten minutes during a resident lifetime.

Prefer the smallest correct replacement design. Corner-case loss of transient reviews, advice, or round state is acceptable; misleading success, stale authority, or invalid output is not.

| Business goal | Required outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Make intended fixes available | The selected resident is actually serving, or pending activation/unavailability is explicit. |
| Avoid repeated setup | Resident releases without hook-facing changes require no hook reinstall or renewed native trust. |
| Explain actual incompatibility | An incompatible caller receives actionable update guidance through normal communication. |
| Avoid distracting reminders | Compatible deprecated hooks remain silent; incompatible-call warnings have an independent ten-minute budget per agent. |
| Keep hook updates scoped | Updating one runtime's hooks does not switch or break another runtime's hooks or require their reinstall. |
| Keep updates simple and correct | Transient work may be lost; surviving behavior respects correctness boundaries. |

## User Stories

1. As a user, I want a resident update to activate the selected resident build, so that the intended fix becomes available.
2. As a user, I want activation to be observed rather than inferred from rewritten hooks, so that update success is trustworthy.
3. As a user, I want equal package versions with different build identities distinguished when relevant, so that stale resident code is detectable.
4. As a user, I want pending activation explicitly reported, so that selection is not confused with a running replacement.
5. As a user, I want replacement launch failure reported as unavailability, so that I can take an informed recovery action.
6. As a user, I want bounded recovery attempts, so that a failed update does not hang indefinitely.
7. As a user, I want the selected target retained after launch failure, so that the system does not silently roll back my choice.
8. As a user, I want resident updates to apply to the shared resident, so that all its callers use the intended resident behavior.
9. As a user, I want a Codex-hook update to change only Codex hooks, so that other installed runtime integrations remain usable.
10. As a user, I want resident selection independent of runtime-hook selection, so that a hook update cannot silently switch unrelated hooks.
11. As a user, I want resident-only releases to leave applicable hook registrations and implementations alone, so that I avoid unnecessary setup.
12. As a user, I want compatible hook implementation updates behind unchanged applicable native definitions, so that native trust need not be requested again merely because packaged code changed.
13. As a user, I want genuinely changed native definitions handled through the normal approval workflow, so that the runtime retains its authority over hook trust.
14. As an agent, I want compatible deprecated hooks to work silently, so that harmless deprecation does not interrupt my work.
15. As an agent, I want actual hook/resident incompatibility explicitly identified, so that I know an update is necessary.
16. As an agent, I want the incompatibility notice to reach model-visible output at an eligible hook opportunity, so that I can act on it.
17. As an agent, I want repeated incompatible calls to share one ten-minute warning budget, so that different hook events do not flood my context.
18. As an agent, I want my warning budget independent of another agent's budget, so that their activity does not hide my update guidance.
19. As a reliably identified subagent, I want my own warning budget, so that my update guidance is independent of the parent agent.
20. As a developer, I want cooldown state bounded and resident-local, so that warning delivery does not introduce persistence infrastructure.
21. As a developer, I want incompatible, malformed, or unknown communication to remain unsuccessful or unavailable, so that it cannot masquerade as a clear review.
22. As a developer, I want obsolete work invalidated during replacement, so that abandoned state cannot authorize replacement behavior or invalid output.
23. As a developer, I want permissible transient work loss instead of mandatory draining or replay, so that replacement remains simple.
24. As a developer, I want already installed hooks to resolve the selected resident target after retirement, so that they cannot respawn the previous resident accidentally.
25. As a developer, I want existing installed-update tests extended with focused policy checks, so that acceptance covers real boundaries without a new broad test matrix.
26. As a developer, I want compatibility checks and warnings to add bounded hot-hook work, so that update support does not make routine checks expensive.
27. As a developer, I want the pre-release warning baseline made explicit, so that historical hooks are not promised behavior they cannot implement.
28. As a developer, I want development updates supported only when they naturally share the published-update design, so that optional convenience does not expand the architecture.
29. As a developer, I want optional journal identities limited to already-available actual process information, so that diagnostics do not create another storage or version-history system.

## Implementation Decisions

- Published installed updates are mandatory scope. Development snapshots are optional: include them only if the same design handles them elegantly; otherwise explicitly defer them. Do not build a separate development update system.
- Extend existing administration, installed package selection/launching, resident lifecycle, IPC, and hook output owners. Preserve the existing administrative reducer/interpreter and hook dependency boundaries. Avoid a general deployment coordinator or capability registry.
- Keep shared resident target selection independent from each runtime's hook selection. Existing retained hook implementations must launch/connect to the selected shared resident, not accidentally resurrect their own older package's resident. A global administrative selection must not switch unrelated runtime hooks. Preserve coherent executable/assets selection.
- Identify the actual serving resident using a minimal build/install identity sufficient to compare against the selected target. Package version equality alone is insufficient. Avoid expensive source hashing or package scans on each hook call.
- Select and verify the target through the existing update workflow. Observe replacement before reporting activation. Pending activation must be explicit and bounded; launch failure leaves the selected target in place and reports unavailable. Recovery may retry within existing bounds; no automatic rollback.
- Choose the smallest safe replacement mechanics during implementation. Both idle and busy replacement must be correct. No required draining, handover, migration, or preservation of transient work. Abandoned work must not produce false clear/success, invalid source or recipient output, or stale authority. Do not stop an unrelated process or unlink another owner's endpoint. The ordinary automatic inactivity-retirement contract remains separately scoped.
- A release with no hook-facing changes must not rewrite hook code or native registration. When compatible hook code changes, preserve native definitions, their source/scope/order, and trust-relevant settings if still applicable. Actual definition changes use normal native approval behavior. Do not bypass trust or promise loaded extensions will hot reload.
- Compatibility is an explicit minimal caller/resident contract, not package-version inequality or deprecation alone. Compatible deprecated hooks continue working without update warnings. Actually incompatible calls are not processed as successful reviews.
- Ordinary resident protocol communication must expose incompatibility explicitly to hooks implementing this baseline. Use existing transport/projection/output owners rather than a separate notification channel. Keep owned IPC at version 1 in this pre-release phase; update the baseline in place, without parallel legacy APIs or migration shims.
- Historical strict-schema hooks cannot necessarily decode new metadata or render the warning. Older installations enter the baseline through ordinary hook update/restart. Do not promise agent-visible warnings from code unable to render them; unknown or malformed communication never counts as successful review.
- Deliver a short actionable update-needed warning at an existing model-visible hook opportunity. Reserve its budget before granting emission. Failed or uncertain emission may consume the budget; no acknowledgement/replay guarantee. Do not block agent completion solely to deliver a reminder.
- Use an independent budget keyed by the existing reliable agent recipient identity, including reliably identified subagents. Share it across hook events and rounds; changes to build, runtime version, turn, or selected target must not bypass it. No more than one emission authorization per ten minutes for a recipient during a resident lifetime.
- Store budgets in a bounded resident-memory map using the existing clock abstraction. At capacity suppress new warnings rather than evict an unexpired budget and permit duplicates. Expire entries normally. Resident restart may reset budgets; no durable or cross-restart guarantee.
- Optional journal enrichment may record already-available actual Hapsland resident/hook build or version identities through existing best-effort inspection machinery. Missing identity remains unknown. Do not overload agent-runtime version metadata. Omit this if it needs new transport solely for diagnostics, exhaustive history, reconstruction, correlation machinery, or update dependence on journal availability.
- Preserve #252/#256 bounded best-effort inspection, interruption, missing-evidence, source-free fact, and single-owner semantics. Those specifications do not require lossless resident replacement or dictate native approval mechanics.
- Simplicity, development experience, check performance, and bounded hot-hook overhead are acceptance constraints. Prefer existing seams and deterministic time; do not introduce a new storage engine, policy reducer, or universal compatibility framework.

## Testing Decisions

- Extend the existing installed-update consumer as the primary acceptance seam: real installed packages, public lifecycle/update commands, owned hooks, and real resident IPC. Verify observed identity and public outcomes rather than incidental internal sequencing.
- Cover old idle and busy residents, successful activation, failed replacement launch without automatic rollback, and subsequent caller resolution of the selected resident. Busy tests may observe permitted loss but must establish correctness of surviving results and obsolete-work invalidation.
- Verify unchanged applicable native registrations for resident-only updates and compatible hook changes. Verify selected-runtime hook updates preserve unrelated runtime selections and registrations. Make native permission-prompt claims only when corresponding native behavior was actually exercised; byte equality alone is narrower evidence.
- Add focused protocol/output checks for compatible deprecated silence, explicit incompatibility, model-visible guidance, and malformed/unknown communication remaining unsuccessful. Cover supported warning paths without expanding into a full runtime/platform matrix.
- Use injected clocks for independent agents/subagents, events and rounds sharing a budget, the exact ten-minute boundary, concurrent reservation, bounded capacity, and accepted restart reset. No ten-minute wall-clock sleeps or durable-delivery tests.
- Optional development/journal behavior receives proportionate checks only if included. Journal absence must not prevent updates; dropped identity must remain unknown under existing inspection semantics.
- Select required local checks from the repository testing matrix under CHECKS policy. Do not introduce a full gate or unrelated live/backend suite solely for this feature. No GitHub CI completion gate is added.

## Out of Scope

Lossless review/advice/round preservation; draining/replay/state migration solely to prevent permissible loss; automatic rollback; warnings for compatible deprecated callers; durable notification state or delivery acknowledgements; warning guarantees across resident restart; a general capability registry or deployment coordinator; parallel legacy IPC versions; exhaustive build history; new inspection infrastructure; mandatory development-only machinery; seamless Pi extension migration or universal runtime hot reload; a new runtime/platform test matrix.

## Further Notes

The original incident involved a selected new development snapshot while an idle shared resident still ran the previous snapshot, both reporting package version 0.1.0. It established the selection-versus-serving gap. The original proposal to preserve in-flight work is superseded by the owner's explicit correctness-over-preservation decision. Development support is now optional; published updates are required.

General transient-work-loss policy is discoverable in the maintained advice contract under “Correctness and transient work loss.” The internal update business context is linked from the repository agent navigation map. These are developer/agent documents, not customer instructions or claims of shipped behavior.

The accepted inspection specifications are [#252](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/252) and [#256](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/256). Coordinate changes through their existing owners rather than introducing parallel schemas or recorders.

Research included source inspection, installed-update probes, and an Astra consultation. Research/model illustrations are advisory evidence, not validation of this implementation. Astra's simplification review recommended independent selections, minimal incompatibility metadata, resident-memory warning budgets, explicit baseline limitations, and no required replacement sequence. No implementation acceptance checks have been run for this specification.

title: Investigate actionable debug reasons with single ownership across inspection and dashboard
body:
## Purpose and scope

Investigate how Hapsland can expose specific, actionable debug and inspection reasons without duplicating decision logic, reason definitions, or explanatory text across preparation, IPC, logs, replay, and dashboard code.

Requested by the owner on 2026-10-08 after an ordinary TypeScript edit was visible in inspection but its exclusion could only be understood by reading source. This is a bounded investigation and design proposal, not authorization to implement a new diagnostic framework or expand supported review forms. Research conclusions remain advisory until accepted.

## Observed example

In `/workspace/typescript/dnd`, with `sessionInspection: true`, real Codex `apply_patch` updates to `packages/shared/src/check-difficulty.ts` reached the installed resident and public dashboard snapshot:

- Receipt `8baa1208-1366-4bb2-bf49-fc00d27c0d51`: temporary comment after the import.
- Receipt `c1d40fb9-93fd-47c7-a16e-50ab81ff0ba3`: remove that comment and temporarily change the function body's `Math.max(1, Math.floor(n))` to `Math.max(2, Math.floor(n))`.
- Both retained `edit-received`, `round-membership`, and `edit-admission: accepted`, followed by preparation reads, `preparation-skipped`, and omissions labelled `import` and `ambiguous-update`.
- No classifier invocation or completed review was established for these receipts. All temporary source changes were subsequently removed; Git confirmed the file was restored.

The labels did not explain which decision failed, why the two reasons appeared together, or what evidence would distinguish the possible causes. The running resident was installed under `snapshot-ubO1NT`; the dashboard process was under `snapshot-fdLz9j`. Preserve their exact candidate identities when reproducing; do not assume the installed binaries match a source checkout.

Source inspection at `a071b9b58315924cdc5a5c5768b76c818c167dcc` showed `packages/review-execution/src/direct-event/pipeline.ts` collapsing several paths into `ambiguous-update`: unavailable verified post-edit spans, ambiguous edited-root attribution, and a caught selection failure. Other entry paths can use the same label for multiple matching declarations. This establishes the diagnostic information-loss problem in inspected source; it does not yet identify the exact causal branch for the installed receipts above.

## Investigation questions

1. Trace where current broad reason labels lose the actual decision cause. Start with `ambiguous-update` and the observed `import` pair; sample capture/admission refusals only to assess whether the same design composes with #252. Identify what is observed, inferred, and unavailable.
2. What minimum typed, structured detail can be produced at the decision point? Distinguish, where evidence permits, unavailable or unverified spans, spans outside a declaration, multiple candidate declarations, extraction/refinement exclusions, and internal selection failure. Do not fabricate a specific explanation from a broad retained label.
3. How can that canonical outcome travel unchanged through preparation, resident transport, inspection recording, debug output, replay, and dashboard? Consumers should render recorded evidence, not rerun parsing, selection, source traversal, or failure classification.
4. Where should human-readable explanation and actionable guidance be owned so each cause is maintained once? Compare a small extension to existing outcome types with a shared formatter or other bounded alternatives. Recommend the smallest adequate design; a universal registry, parallel taxonomy, or separate reason-to-text tables in every consumer are not predetermined solutions.
5. Which metadata is necessary to make the explanation useful: decision stage, cause, confirmed span/location, candidate count, effective bound, or evidence availability? Keep correlations with the relevant receipt/root explicit. Explain why a metadata field is needed before adding it.
6. How should the interface distinguish an actual review finding, an intentional preparation exclusion, a resource refusal, an internal failure, and unknown/missing/dropped evidence? A received or accepted edit must never imply review completion.
7. How should source-free explanations remain useful under consent, confidentiality, storage limits, and dropped/truncated inspection history? Do not include source text, credentials, full hook payloads, arbitrary exception messages, or sensitive filesystem details in a general debug record. Preserve existing bounds and the pre-release version-one format policy.

## Required investigation outcome

- Reproduce the observed example through the installed Codex -> resident -> public inspection path and identify the causal branch, or document exactly which missing evidence prevents that conclusion. Include a function-body-only update to separate import/top-level edits from a declaration edit.
- Map the owning producers and consumers and show at least two distinct underlying causes currently sharing a broad reason. Describe the more specific operator explanation each should produce and how unsupported certainty stays explicit.
- Compare bounded designs, their maintenance/coupling cost, confidentiality and storage implications. Recommend one with a clear single owner for each cause and its presentation; distinguish the proposal from accepted product requirements.
- Demonstrate the proposed diagnostic shape with sanitized example debug output and dashboard details. The operator should understand what happened, why review did not proceed, and what to inspect next without opening source. Do not promise a remedy when the evidence supports only a limitation.
- Define focused implementation acceptance scenarios: distinct causes remain distinct through transport, reload/replay and rendering; consumers cannot manufacture details absent from the recorded outcome; a real installed omission is explained consistently in the debug and inspection surfaces.
- Publish findings and the proposed bounded implementation scope in this issue or its existing owning documentation. Create implementation follow-ups only after owner acceptance; no new standalone maintained report is required.

## Related ownership; avoid duplicate implementation

- #252 owns capture-size versus read/access/stability versus preparation-admission diagnostics.
- #254 owns callable extraction support and precise overload/function exclusions.
- #228 owns the full edit inspector, contributing-source and classifier request/result presentation.
- #225 owns opt-in local inspection history and its dashboard.

This task owns investigation of the shared diagnostic representation and explanation ownership, plus the ambiguous-update example. It does not replace those implementation tasks, raise resource limits, alter support/admission decisions, or claim a skipped review is clear.

title: Unify Bend simulation execution and categorize canonical outputs
body:
Public TypeScript and native simulator consumers now execute through one Bend runner. Canonical outputs distinguish requested actions, established domain events and policy decisions, so consumers can handle facts without reapplying reducer changes.

Closes #234
Closes #237

## Delivered

- Consolidate execution in `NativeRun.bend`, with compiler-emitted JavaScript behind the validated TypeScript API. Preserve bounded advancement, controls, callback custody, immutable observations and format-1 replay; remove the superseded TypeScript execution loop.
- Audit all 215 canonical output variants: 3 action requests, 84 domain events and 128 policy decisions. Update production, simulator, visualization and optional game consumers in place.
- Add [the package-impact CLI](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/031b30f56f2f7d19e506a658560f4503224f9337/scripts/package-impact.mjs) and [usage guidance](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/031b30f56f2f7d19e506a658560f4503224f9337/docs/agents/navigation.md#analyze-package-impact). It accepts revision pairs, merge-base branch reviews and dirty worktrees; reads the existing manifest graph at both endpoints; accounts for renames, removed packages/edges and untracked files; emits ASCII or JSON.
