title: Recover retained build custody and document build requirements
body:
A failed source build can retain its lock, lease and process registrations, blocking the next build. Recovery now verifies stopped writers and archives the complete custody atomically while excluding concurrent builders.

- Preserve ambiguous records and both build/cleanup errors; prevent stale-token registrations from poisoning a fresh lease.
- Document internal recovery requirements and the manual procedure. Add document audiences and generator metadata, omitting redundant labels in ADRs and public READMEs; preserve seven frozen artifacts byte-for-byte and record their audiences in the owning index.
- The extended 12-case recovery regression remains manual-only. The native gate requires a C compiler and Node-API headers for source builds, with no added prerequisite for users of ready-made executables.

Validation: both code-review axes cleared; focused ownership and affected build/install consumer checks passed; manual recovery 12/12 passed; documentation links, generated diagrams/pages, and `check:fast` passed. The documentation follow-up passed focused checks and commit hooks. Documentation additionally reviewed with Astra: no material findings. Full quality gate and Darwin qualification were not run. Local validation used the branch based on `3fd27264`; merge compatibility with fetched master `6d43b36d` was checked without incorporating those later native-packaging commits.

The original incident’s initial retention cause remains unconfirmed; recovery does not repair its triggering source failure.

Addresses #257.

title: Restore CI source checkout and production complexity checks
body:
The CI quality gate stopped before tests because `vendor/bendlib` was uninitialized. Recursive checkout now supplies the pinned source input in Offline checks and macOS package conformance.

After that fix, CI exposed 23 production functions across the original and concurrently updated master above the existing complexity ceiling. Split state transitions, credential file operations, CLI login, decoding and graph validation into named functions while preserving operation order, stale-target checks and outputs. Quality thresholds and test selection remain unchanged.

Validation:
- Fresh shallow checkout reproduced missing submodule, then actual sourceSnapshot passed with recursive initialization and the exact pinned gitlink.
- Existing submodule identity regression passed (dirty/untracked bytes included).
- Complexity preflight: zero guaranteed CRAP failures.
- Focused runners passed: 195 original-owner tests, 77 native tests, then 180 capture/protocol/hooks/pipeline/preparation/setup tests after merging the latest capture diagnostics.
- 1872 old/new login reducer cases matched, including unchanged-object identity.
- check:fast and commit hooks passed.
- Workflow YAML parsed and checkout inputs checked.

Current master is merged into this branch. Full CI validation is running on the latest head. Prior runs passed source identity, harness preflight and lint before identifying complexity failures.

title: Separate resident updates from runtime-hook installation (#258)
body:
Implements #258: resident updates select and activate the shared resident independently of runtime-hook updates. Compatible hook updates preserve native definitions and trust settings; releases with unchanged hook code retain hook selection. Actual incompatibility uses ordinary IPC and a bounded per-recipient ten-minute warning budget. Replacement fences the observed resident lifetime; failed activation retains selection and reports unavailable rather than rolling back.

Documentation generation and drift checks are now manual operations (`npm run docs:generate` / `npm run docs:generated:check`), removed from fast/full gates, Git hooks, builds and CI. Internal business context records correctness over preservation of transient corner-case work.

Validation: Linux arm64, Node 24.20.0 and Bun 1.3.14. Final `check:fast` passed in 16.4 seconds; 18 tooling tests and offline documentation links passed. The 196-test focused selection initially passed 192 with four stale assertions; corrected affected files passed all 43 tests. Installed resident replacement/failed-launch/scoped-hook scenarios, the installed Pi canary, and setup/package conformance through both Bun and npm passed against archive SHA-256 `4d874c669c3ed275dc5875c67687940a61196494f46810c9609b8da39c1c4044`. Independent standards/spec reviews found no outstanding issues.

Latest master integration adds only its release-pin change; production code is the locally qualified implementation. Full quality/CI was not used as an additional completion gate. macOS and actual native permission prompts were not tested. Optional development-update stability and journal version enrichment remain deferred as accepted.

title: Design executable layout for hook and resident startup without coupling architecture to npm delivery
body:
The current shared-runtime package remains in use. Design the executable layout around fast hook startup, resident startup, process isolation and a self-contained installation. npm upload size is a delivery constraint, not the architectural objective. Do not revert packaging solely because of the preliminary help-command comparison.

Current layout: one compiled Bun CLI per platform; hook/resident/parser/doctor are minified ESM bundles launched through the embedded runtime. Previous layout: five separate compiled executables with bytecode per platform. The archive decreased from approximately 337 MB to 66 MB.

Actual installed-artifact measurements on macOS arm64, pinned Bun 1.3.14, without coverage or provider requests:

| Scenario | Samples per variant | Old median / p95 | Current median / p95 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pi before-edit registration, verified ready resident reused | 40 | 117 / 190 ms | 169 / 261 ms |
| Before-edit registration starting a fresh resident | 8 | 248 / 326 ms | 511 / 571 ms |
| Direct resident launch until successful stats response | 8 | 140 / 189 ms | 241 / 280 ms |

Hook variants were interleaved, all registrations succeeded, all healthy-resident identities remained unchanged, and retirement/cleanup succeeded. Fresh-start samples used separate isolated directories. Direct resident readiness was measured separately. OS file cache was uncontrolled. With eight samples p95 is effectively the maximum, not a population estimate. Historical and current source revisions differ: this compares artifacts and does not isolate packaging as the sole cause.

A diagnostic Linux arm64 container run under partially concurrent host load also passed all 96 registrations: ready-resident medians 154 → 227 ms; fresh-resident medians 316 → 554 ms. Treat these numbers as diagnostic, not an unloaded-platform benchmark.

Baseline archive SHA-256: `090dfc52b40f149746ae42dbe1fc3fed06e8ff85859a91a6b93b651e459e4b1e`.
Current archive SHA-256: `988c087205b39adda27f53ba917a91b9b9810a301e4f829c7373cd29809b2f99`; source `6da1fa4dcfde83a49d2c95dfc82016a5a9e58ec6`.
Captured runners, raw samples and metadata are retained locally in the common Git artifact store at `hapsland-artifacts/startup-measurements/2026-10-08/`.

Acceptance:

- Compare executable designs using the same source revision and pinned toolchain. Evaluate bytecode, role dispatch/import initialization, standalone role executables and platform-specific distribution without presupposing a winner.
- Preserve public command interfaces, independent process lifetimes, native asset resolution, environment isolation and installation without external Node/Bun.
- Measure real hook calls with a verified ready resident, first-call resident creation, and direct resident readiness on macOS arm64 and Linux arm64. Declare samples, deadlines and acceptance thresholds before qualification; do not substitute `--help` for these scenarios.
- Make the installed-startup runner reusable for dedicated-hook versus dedicated-hook comparisons and both standalone/shared process identities on both platforms; current repository runner assumes Linux and CLI-versus-hook comparison.
- Verify archive publication feasibility separately, including platform packages if useful. The present local 64 MiB budget must not dictate runtime architecture.
- Keep release preparation/reuse, untracked generated binaries, source-bound receipts, archive integrity and installed-package checks.

This follow-up is not a release blocker under the owner's current instruction to keep using the shared-runtime layout.

title: Add rule calibration workflow separate from runtime feedback
body:
## Purpose

Add a repeatable rule-calibration workflow separate from ordinary agent feedback, so rule authors can assess applicability, incorrect findings and missed concerns before deciding whether to change or enable a rule.

Requested by the product owner following the agentlint architectural comparison (2026-10-08). This issue records a proposed feature; the detailed interface and amended product contract still need to be decided during the task. Creating this task does not adopt agentlint or change current runtime semantics.

## Existing foundation

Hapsland already has `hapsland rules check --path ... --line ... --id ...` for one selected declaration. It uses normal capture, related-code resolution, evidence admission and provider evaluation; it does not modify source/settings or send agent feedback. It currently evaluates enabled rules only. Build on this existing path rather than introduce a parallel evaluator.

- [Current rule-check contract](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/master/docs/rules.md#try-a-rule-on-a-file-and-line)
- [Rule authoring walkthrough](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/master/docs/write-first-rule.md)
- [agentlint calibration](https://github.com/aurelienbobenrieth/agentlint/blob/4d933d3e18a2907c3914006054973745de98fceb/docs/guide/calibration.md)

## Proposed scope

- Define a bounded corpus of positive, negative and uncertain cases, each with a reviewer label and short rationale. Distinguish concern presence/applicability from whether a resulting message is useful.
- Record the exact rule definition, effective threshold, provider/model, selected declaration/context and evidence completeness for each evaluation. Identify source-bearing data and keep sanitized summaries separate.
- Reuse the production source-selection and evaluation owners. Decide how an explicitly selected draft/disabled rule can be evaluated without enabling it in ordinary review; preserve normal privacy and resource boundaries.
- Produce per-case results and an aggregate calibration report: false positives, missed concerns, uncertain/unassessable cases, coverage and request/timing evidence. State denominators; unavailable, skipped or incomplete cases must not count as clear or correct.
- Keep calibration labels and reports outside resident advice, reuse/continuation authority and ordinary inspection history. No automatic threshold tuning, rule activation, approval or source modification.
- Make live evaluation explicit and bounded; declare case/request limits before a run. Ordinary tests remain offline and deterministic. Calibration results do not by themselves prove repair effectiveness or production accuracy.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Specify the user-facing workflow, case/label model, output/privacy policy and live-run bounds in the existing rule/evaluation contract owners; preserve version-one formats and update them in place where necessary.
2. Demonstrate one positive, one negative, one uncertain and one unavailable/incomplete case, with unavailable evidence excluded from accuracy denominators.
3. Verify that calibration leaves source, rule activation/settings and resident advice state unchanged, and follows existing source-exclusion and input-admission rules.
4. Verify the real selected CLI/consumer boundary with deterministic provider fixtures, including failure handling and exact rule/input attribution; do not rely only on reporting-helper tests.
5. Run local checks selected from CHECKS.md and the testing matrix for the actual implementation. Any later live evidence must name its frozen corpus, provider, bounds and limitations.

## Relationship to existing work

#150 is a particular cross-file advice-quality study; this task supplies a reusable rule-authoring/calibration workflow and does not reopen or duplicate that study. Agentlint's deterministic labels are an architectural precedent, not a substitute for evaluating our probabilistic rules.

title: Research agentlint ideas for Hapsland rules, review and exception handling
body:
## Purpose

Investigate which ideas from agentlint's README Hapsland should borrow, optionally integrate, or reject. Produce actionable advisory recommendations grounded in Hapsland's current contracts, rather than adopt agentlint or change runtime behavior in this task.

Requested by the product owner on 2026-10-08. Starting source: https://github.com/aurelienbobenrieth/agentlint#readme. The initial conversation examined documentation only; it did not verify implementation or native-runtime enforcement.

## Research scope

This is a targeted named-candidate investigation, not an ecosystem survey. Pin the inspected agentlint revision and follow README claims into relevant official docs, source and tests where necessary.

Evaluate:

- Separation of standard, detector and binding: guidance, evaluator, applicability and exception authority.
- Positive, negative and borderline fixtures; calibration before enabling/enforcing a rule. Relate findings to #265 rather than duplicate its implementation scope.
- Review UI showing the policy beside the evaluated code/context, proposed disposition and supporting evidence.
- Explicit exception records with rationale, actor and authority; storage, privacy, headless behavior and whether decisions should be committed to Git.
- Semantic fingerprints and explicit review epochs: when decisions survive formatting/moves, and when changes to related context, rule definitions or policy invalidate them. Compare with Hapsland's existing freshness and evaluation-reuse contract.
- Outcomes attached to findings: useful interception, correction, false positive, unnecessary review or later incident. Separate observed delivery from demonstrated repair/usefulness.
- State rules versus change rules, including the actual evidence needed to judge a before/after transition.
- Deterministic local/CI gates and optional coexistence with Hapsland's probabilistic Jev reviews; host-specific authority, deadlines and failure behavior.

## Method and contract boundaries

Follow the sibling research repository's [PRODUCT-RESEARCH-METHODOLOGY.md](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland-research/blob/master/PRODUCT-RESEARCH-METHODOLOGY.md).

For each proposed use, classify it as BORROW, DEPEND ON, OPTIONAL INTEGRATION or REJECT. Keep source class (DOC/SRC/RUN/etc.) separate from verification state (DOCUMENTED/SOURCE-INSPECTED/RUNTIME-TESTED/etc.). README claims are not runtime evidence. Any dependency recommendation requires the methodology's dependency gates; unresolved gates remain explicit.

Map recommendations against the advice/handoff contract, editable-rule and review-input contracts, freshness/reuse, inspection history and source-egress boundaries. Hapsland currently does not require an agent to acknowledge or accept each finding; adopting a mandatory acceptance gate would need a separate explicit product decision. Preserve version-one formats; propose changes in place rather than parallel legacy/new paths.

No implementation, installation, new hooks, automatic approvals, source sharing or live Jev calls are required by this research issue. If a bounded experiment is necessary, declare its scope and evidence limits first and use existing authorization rules.

## Deliverables and acceptance

1. A pinned-source evidence ledger and compact comparison mapping agentlint ideas to Hapsland's existing capabilities, gaps and conflicts.
2. A decision matrix for every scoped idea: intended use, classification, benefit, counterargument, uncertainty and required specification decision or prototype check.
3. A prioritized recommendation with the smallest coherent next steps. Explain whether agentlint can satisfy a neighboring workflow as an optional tool and what would overturn a borrow/build recommendation.
4. Concrete invalidation and authority scenarios for any proposed exceptions, and false-positive/unavailable-evidence scenarios for calibration and gates. Do not claim native enforcement without evidence at that boundary.
5. Link #265 and relevant existing inspection/rule work; recommend follow-up tasks only for distinct gaps.
6. Publish the advisory findings in this issue, or in a canonical sibling-research report linked here if the investigation warrants one. No new Markdown file is required solely to complete the task. Any new document must follow repository lifecycle metadata rules.

Completion means the scoped recommendations and uncertainties are recorded with traceable evidence. It does not approve a design, dependency, rollout or platform-support claim.

title: Add bounded Python and Go user-model review with local declaration traversal
body:
## Problem Statement

Hapsland users work with explicit domain/data models in Python and Go, but the current source-language adapters cover TypeScript, Rust and Bend. Those users cannot obtain the existing rule-driven review for their Python/Go models with reliable local supporting evidence.

The user wants a bounded, complete addition, followed by evidence about whether further coverage is worth its cost. They do not want a promise to support 90% of every language construct, a mandatory chain of future stages, or traversal of installed/system libraries.

**Purpose:** Specify bounded Python/Go user-model review and its coverage handoff.
**Audience:** Product/specification owners, contributors including implementation agents, and evaluation reviewers.
**Status:** Owner-approved implementation task specification, 2026-10-09; the owner confirmed the functional and native-package testing boundaries before publication.
**Authority:** The owner's selected scope and existing accepted review/privacy/runtime contracts govern this task. Research informs decisions but does not independently create requirements. The owner approved this specification and testing boundaries for publication; accepted repository contract owners must be updated with the implemented profile during this task.
**Expected use:** Implement and locally qualify this scope; use the separately linked coverage follow-up to decide whether to extend it.
**Lifecycle:** At task acceptance, consolidate implemented language/root/import boundaries into the existing review contract and language-support guidance. This issue remains the accepted work/decision record; temporary research is consolidated or deleted according to its lifecycle. The completion handoff must keep the linked coverage issue usable without the original chat.

Coverage follow-up: [#268 — measure model-review coverage and preserve continuation handoff](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/268). It does not block completion of this bounded implementation. Closing this task requires updating #268 with the actual implementation/evidence handoff described below.

## Solution

Add two cohesive source-language profiles for review of explicitly declared user models: Python and Go. An attributed edit selects a supported model/type artifact; Hapsland follows only relevant, safely resolved user declarations within its existing limits, admits only rules with sufficient evidence, and uses the existing review/advice path.

The bounded implementation is complete when its named behavior and required local checks pass. A separate coverage follow-up reports useful supported/missed model-edit cases and the cost of closing important gaps. Ninety percent is a revisable aspiration, not this implementation's acceptance condition.

## User Stories

1. As a Python developer, I want edited explicit model declarations reviewed, so that I can improve domain representations while using my existing agent runtime.
2. As a Go developer, I want edited named types reviewed, so that I can improve domain representations without changing my language.
3. As a rule author, I want the new language inputs admitted only for applicable rules, so that support does not imply unsupported analysis capabilities.
4. As a Python developer, I want ordinary annotated model classes recognized, so that explicit fields do not require a particular framework.
5. As a Python developer, I want dataclass models recognized through actual import bindings, so that aliases work and a shadowed decorator is not mistaken for the standard library.
6. As a Python developer, I want class-form TypedDict models and required/optional markers represented, so that missing fields are distinguished from nullable values.
7. As a Python developer, I want explicit type aliases, unions, Literal alternatives and nominal NewType declarations retained, so that review can see intended domain distinctions.
8. As a Python developer, I want statically identified Pydantic model classes and local base classes represented, so that custom model bases do not disappear from review.
9. As a Python developer, I want local import aliases and relative imports resolved, so that naming style does not change the evidence identity.
10. As a Python developer, I want explicit package reexports followed, so that a public package import can lead to its actual local declaration.
11. As a Python developer, I want unambiguous flat and src-layout package roots recognized, so that source locations match my project structure.
12. As a Python developer, I want TYPE_CHECKING imports and simple forward annotations understood as static type intent, so that review does not need to execute annotations.
13. As a Python developer, I want unknown decorators, computed fields and dynamic schema factories handled honestly, so that review does not invent runtime guarantees.
14. As a Go developer, I want structs, aliases and defined types distinguished, so that review preserves nominal identity.
15. As a Go developer, I want pointer, container, generic and embedded-field structure retained, so that review sees the actual declared representation.
16. As a Go developer, I want related declarations in other active files of the same package found, so that no artificial import is needed to expose supporting types.
17. As a Go developer, I want relevant typed constants and iota alternatives included, so that a named scalar state's declared alternatives are visible.
18. As a Go developer, I want local module imports and ordinary import aliases resolved correctly, so that package names are not guessed from the path suffix.
19. As a Go developer, I want analysis to respect the declared build context, so that mutually exclusive platform/tag files are not merged into a fictional package.
20. As a developer, I want library/system types left opaque unless bounded built-in knowledge is sufficient, so that Hapsland does not crawl installed dependencies.
21. As a developer, I want supporting source limited to reachable declarations, so that a large package does not mean its entire contents are sent for review.
22. As a developer, I want excludes, containment and ignore rules applied to every source read, so that language support does not weaken privacy.
23. As a developer, I want edits to unrelated siblings to stay unrelated, so that advice targets exactly my changed artifact.
24. As a developer, I want ambiguous or unavailable bindings recorded as omissions, so that missing evidence is never presented as a clear assessment.
25. As a developer, I want independent eligible roots to proceed when another root is unsupported, so that a safe omission does not unnecessarily suppress useful review.
26. As a developer, I want supporting-file and authority-metadata changes to invalidate prepared evidence, so that stale advice is suppressed.
27. As a developer, I want language analysis to remain bounded, so that difficult models do not stall my agent or trigger unbounded reads.
28. As an end user, I want the installed product to include the new grammar assets on its declared platforms, so that development-only parser success is not mistaken for support.
29. As a contributor, I want existing TypeScript/Rust/Bend behavior preserved, so that adding profiles does not regress current users.
30. As a product owner, I want a coverage follow-up containing failures, denominators and estimated expansion costs, so that I can choose a smaller scope when ninety percent is expensive.
31. As a future implementation/evaluation agent, I want exact scope, source revisions, executed checks and open questions in the task handoff, so that I can continue without reconstructing this chat.

## Implementation Decisions

### Shared review boundary

- Extend the existing language-adapter, artifact, rule-admission and native-asset owners. Reuse stable source capture, changed-root attribution, bounded reference traversal, review-unit preparation, provider transport and advice delivery.
- Target models/types only. Functions and methods are not independent edited review roots in this issue. A model declaration can contain supporting method/validator source; that does not add function-review inputs or whole-program call traversal.
- One selected root produces one review unit. Supporting declarations do not become new changed roots. No whole-file/raw-diff fallback and no re-review of unchanged dependents.
- Extend artifact/root representation explicitly for Python model classes and Go defined types where needed; do not call every class a struct or equate a Go defined type with an alias. Update Hapsland-owned version-one formats in place, consistent with current pre-release policy.
- Admit new language/rule combinations only where the existing criterion has meaningful semantics and sufficient evidence. Preserve idiomatic language interpretation; do not prescribe TypeScript-only representation repairs.
- Missing external information does not automatically suppress the whole file or every rule. Keep external references explicit and apply the existing per-rule evidence gate: a root-only rule may proceed if its actual needs are met; a rule needing unresolved semantics must not run.
- Existing primitive/container understanding or statically recognized framework markers do not authorize reading system declarations. No standard-library, installed-package, module-cache, vendor or generated-SDK traversal is added.
- Read only eligible source and required static authority metadata inside the admitted physical project root. Existing capture/tree/file/depth/work/deadline ceilings, source-free skip reporting, confidentiality and freshness contracts remain controlling. Do not raise limits to obtain a target percentage.
- Package/module indexes are discovery authority, not permission to include all discovered declarations in review. Any indexing must have a bounded read/work policy, use the same file exclusions/containment, and fingerprint every read that establishes identity or membership. If this cannot be established within the existing budget, report incomplete evidence rather than bypassing it.

### Python profile

- Edited roots are explicitly annotated model classes, standard dataclasses, class-form TypedDict, statically identified Pydantic BaseModel classes, explicit aliases including supported type-statement syntax, and statically declared NewType wrappers. Preserve declared fields/bases, optionality, unions/Literal alternatives, generics and relevant field metadata without evaluating them.
- A candidate ordinary class must expose explicit declared model fields; not every arbitrary class is automatically a domain model. Do not infer fields from assignments inside arbitrary methods.
- Dataclass, typing/typing_extensions and Pydantic markers are recognized through imported identities and lexical binding, including supported aliases; spelling alone is insufficient. Local base classes are followed transitively only through resolved eligible source. Unknown external bases/behavior remain opaque.
- Support explicit named member imports, module imports with statically resolvable qualified references, import aliases, relative imports, project-local absolute imports and explicit named reexports through package initializers. Use unambiguous captured flat/src layout and static packaging metadata to establish import roots. Multiple conflicting roots, custom loaders and ambient path modifications remain unsupported.
- Understand static TYPE_CHECKING bindings and literal/simple forward annotations without executing imports or annotation evaluation. Conflicting runtime/type bindings remain explicit uncertainty. Do not evaluate expressions to discover fields, exports or schemas.
- Source roots are Python source files. Local stubs can provide static supporting type evidence but never implementation bodies or synthetic runtime constructors. Notebook cells and environment-wide stub discovery are outside this profile.
- Preserve exact class declaration source for the selected model, including visible supporting validators/configuration. No silent field-only substitute for an oversized class. Root selection is driven by model header/bases, model fields, schema-defining metadata/configuration and recognized model decorators. Edits confined to ordinary methods are outside this issue's target; validator-only edits are recorded as a follow-up gap rather than expanding function analysis implicitly.
- Pydantic support means static authored model evidence, not execution of validators, complete coercion/schema semantics or proof of every constructible runtime value. Unknown decorators/computed model behavior may make particular rules inapplicable.
- Functional TypedDict/NamedTuple factories, broader ORM/attrs support, wildcard exports, metaclasses and dynamic model construction are coverage follow-up candidates, not hidden implementation requirements.

### Go profile

- Edited roots are named structs, explicitly defined scalar/container/model types, aliases and named interfaces/generic type declarations with statically inspectable declared structure. Preserve grouped declarations, pointers, containers, embedded fields/interfaces, tags, generic parameters/constraints and instantiations without inventing a closed implementation hierarchy.
- Preserve defined-type versus alias identity. Relevant statically declared typed constant/iota groups are supporting evidence for the referenced named type; do not claim all runtime values of a Go scalar are restricted to those constants.
- Resolve same-package user types across active eligible files and normal imports to packages in the captured local module. Imported bindings are file-scoped; package declarations are package-scoped. Read the imported package's declared name rather than guessing it from its directory/path suffix.
- The supported initial authority envelope is an unambiguous local module and a declared build context. Capture module boundaries, explicit package membership and the metadata used to select files. Respect platform suffixes and simple statically evaluable build constraints. Unknown build context, conflicting active declarations, cgo-dependent authority or unsupported constraints produce omissions rather than guessing.
- Ordinary/default/aliased imports can establish bindings. Blank imports establish no type binding. Dot imports remain explicit unsupported/ambiguous evidence for affected references; no unqualified-name guessing.
- Multi-module workspaces, local replacements, vendor/external source resolution, generator execution and external test-package handling beyond explicit existing file policy are not promised by this first profile. They remain observed follow-up categories.
- A receiver method is not a changed root and no method/function dependency closure is added. Relevant method signatures already inside an interface or visible model evidence may be retained as declared structure.

### Grammar and installation

- Evaluate pinned maintained Tree-sitter Python/Go grammars with the existing runtime and native loading/distribution path. Pin exact adopted versions and document admitted syntax plus tested platforms; the research's evaluated cohort is not automatically the selected production cohort.
- Known current probes include a Python type-parameter-default grammar gap and a compact Go constant-block parse gap. Retain explicit unsupported behavior or adopt a reviewed compatible fix; do not conceal parser errors or rewrite user source to make parsing succeed.
- Loadability, exact span extraction, binding authority and installed delivery are distinct acceptance facts. A local Node parse is not an installed-platform support claim.

### Bounded completion and coverage follow-up

- This task is complete when the declared Python/Go profiles work through the existing review path and the required local checks for the acceptance candidate pass. Do not wait for GitHub CI as an extra gate unless the owner explicitly requests it or an accepted release contract requires it.
- Coverage follow-up is separately tracked and does not block this bounded implementation. There is no automatic commitment to subsequent feature stages or to functions/methods.
- At completion, update the coverage follow-up with the final accepted profile and omissions, implementation/evidence revisions, exact checks run and their scope, useful rule-input combinations, installed/native platforms actually exercised, and the first unresolved coverage questions. Completion without this handoff is incomplete.

## Testing Decisions

- Primary functional seam: the existing direct-edit review pipeline from an attributed Add/Update observation through stable capture, changed-root attribution, graph preparation and rule admission to the exact provider-boundary input and controlled result/advice outcome. Prefer observable input/outcome assertions; do not test private traversal order or merely mirror AST node queries.
- Reuse existing direct-event pipeline/controlled DecisionModel fixtures, local Git/source fixtures, content-isolation cases, freshness/reuse cases and the native cross-file edit runner. No new test-only production API or independent language-specific review pipeline.
- Positive cases: same-file and cross-file Python models; alias imports, package reexports and local inheritance; Go split-package types, local imported aliases and typed constants; header/field edits; independent multiple roots; unchanged siblings; both prepared evidence and language/rule admission.
- Negative cases: shadowed framework markers, ambiguous package roots/names, unsupported/dynamic imports, inactive/conflicting build files, unresolved external semantics, excluded/outside-root source, oversized/deep evidence, parse failures and ordinary method-only edits. Observe no wrong target, forbidden read, fabricated declaration, stale advice or provider request for a rule missing required evidence.
- Exercise authority mutation/removal and source restoration, including package initializer, module/build metadata and related declaration changes, so that freshness protects the binding identity as well as emitted source.
- Controlled clear/finding/provider-failure results verify the existing delivery semantics. Do not claim the real Jev classifier is accurate from a controlled fixture or declare a live semantic study necessary for every ordinary regression test.
- New native grammars require separate installed-package/platform asset checks because that boundary cannot be established by the functional seam. Use the existing package/native conformance seam and a bounded real-agent cross-file scenario with a controlled provider. Assert only actually exercised hosts/platforms.
- Choose exact local checks using the repository's checks policy/testing matrix for changed owners and consumers. The issue adds no speculative full-gate or remote-CI requirement.

## Out of Scope

- Independent function, receiver-method, callback, constructor or accessor review roots in Python/Go.
- Ninety-percent ecosystem coverage, a fixed large benchmark corpus or mandatory 90% release gate.
- Automatic traversal/download of system libraries, installed dependencies, module caches, vendor or provider SDK implementations.
- Executing application imports, decorators, validators, build backends, generators, package drivers or repository build scripts during analysis.
- Full type inference, whole-program state proofs, exact dynamic framework/runtime behavior, or closed-world enumeration of structural interface implementers.
- Notebook identities, arbitrary ORM/descriptor/metaclass models, dynamic schemas/wildcard imports, and unsupported workspace/build configurations.
- Increasing source/egress/work budgets or changing runtime blocking/delivery authority to improve the coverage number.
- Unrelated languages, runtime adapters, provider migrations or a general TypeScript expansion.

## Further Notes

### Persistent continuation context

The linked coverage issue must be usable without this chat. At the end of this task, append a completion handoff with:

1. Final specification authority and links to the accepted language contracts; exact implementation commit(s), branch/PR and evidence revision. Distinguish proposed, implemented, tested and supported behavior.
2. Per-language capability matrix: edited roots, supporting declarations, import/layout/build contexts, recognized framework markers, opaque external references, rule combinations and explicit unsupported forms.
3. Actual validation: commands, environment, grammar/runtime versions, fixtures, installed artifact digests and observed outcomes; known failures/limitations and GitHub CI reported separately. Do not carry forward unexecuted checks as passes.
4. Corpus state: immutable repository revisions, selection/exclusion rules, source digests, measured counts and their denominator. AST/parser success is not review coverage; declaration counts are not edit prevalence.
5. Existing graph/capture limits and read/egress/freshness policy; no system/dependency crawl. Large Go packages need selective authority discovery, not wholesale context upload.
6. Owner decisions: Python+Go are the two vectors; models/types are the bounded initial scope; methods/functions are not independent targets; 90% is negotiable if closing gaps is costly; no mandatory stage chain or fixed 40-repository benchmark.
7. Ranked unresolved gaps with concrete examples, suspected cause, resolving experiment and relative cost. Preserve uncertainty rather than silently expanding the accepted profile.
8. Next executable action and stop condition for the coverage task. If useful target-user cases cannot be acquired, report discovery-only evidence and do not advertise an ecosystem percentage.

### Research provenance to retain

The workspace currently contains the language advisory, Python/Go coverage reports, shared coverage proposal and source-only JSON/script evidence from 2026-10-09. At drafting time these research assets are untracked: do not create remote blob links or claim another checkout contains them. Preserve the useful evidence with a tracked implementation/evidence revision and stable links during this task, or re-run the pinned read-only inventories if those assets are unavailable. The coverage issue includes the essential research findings and immutable upstream pins so that missing local notes do not lose the decisions.

Research was performed by three subagents (Python, Go, shared measurement plan), with a parent grammar probe. The original language comparison consumed exactly two Astra consultations; no new consultation quota is implied.

The user corrected the interpretation of research percentages: Go 53.1% refers to sampled production roots in directories with more than eight non-test Go files; Python 59.5% refers to methods among sampled function definitions. Neither measures current Hapsland misses or actual user edit frequency. Do not carry those figures forward as a coverage promise or as justification to transmit every package file.

title: Measure Python and Go model-review coverage and preserve continuation handoff
body:
## Problem Statement

After bounded user-model review is added for Python and Go, we still will not know which intended-user model edits obtain useful review and which missing capabilities deserve more complexity. Parser success and source declaration counts do not answer that question.

The owner initially suggested at least 90% of use cases, then explicitly allowed a smaller target/profile if reaching 90% is not reasonably simple. A future agent needs this decision and the actual implementation handoff, not a requirement to broaden support indefinitely.

**Purpose:** Specify a persistent, bounded follow-up measuring useful Python/Go model-review coverage and identifying worthwhile gaps.
**Audience:** Product/specification owners, evaluation reviewers and contributors including coding agents.
**Status:** Owner-approved coverage follow-up specification, 2026-10-09; the initial profile implementation/evidence is a declared execution prerequisite for adapter coverage measurement.
**Authority:** Owner-requested follow-up and the final accepted initial profile; research metrics/corpus sizes remain advisory. This issue defines an evaluation task, not new language-support guarantees.
**Expected use:** Resume from the initial task's completion handoff, measure model-review availability with explicit denominators, and recommend retaining or extending the profile.
**Lifecycle:** Update this issue with the initial implementation handoff and measured results. At evaluation completion, consolidate any accepted support change into its existing contract owner and preserve evidence under a stable revision; separately scoped future work requires its own decision. This issue remains the follow-up work/evidence record.

Initial implementation task: [#267 — bounded Python and Go user-model review](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/267). Coverage measurement depends on its accepted implementation/evidence handoff; this follow-up does not block #267.

## Solution

Evaluate the useful-review availability of the implemented Python/Go model profiles on a small, independently selected application corpus and realistic completed model edits. Report failures and marginal expansion cost. Recommend an explicit next decision: keep the profile, extend particular low-cost gaps, run a larger measurement, or accept a lower target. Completion does not require any particular percentage or additional feature implementation.

## User Stories

1. As a product owner, I want Python and Go measured separately, so that success in one language does not conceal failure in the other.
2. As a product owner, I want intended model-edit cases labeled before observing adapter support, so that narrowing capability cannot manufacture high coverage.
3. As a developer, I want missing supporting user types and imports counted, so that parse success is not mistaken for useful review.
4. As an evaluator, I want exact changed-root and expected-binding labels, so that wrong identities cannot count as success.
5. As an evaluator, I want applicable rule needs fixed for each case, so that an easy unrelated rule cannot inflate the result.
6. As a product owner, I want application-domain models distinguished from SDK wire models and framework internals, so that evidence matches our users.
7. As a product owner, I want gaps grouped by cause, so that I can compare import/layout, framework, syntax and budget work.
8. As a product owner, I want the cost and useful reach of each proposed expansion, so that I can choose a smaller target when 90% is expensive.
9. As a developer, I want no system/dependency crawl introduced by evaluation, so that measurement respects the product's intended boundary.
10. As a future agent, I want exact revisions, executed checks and the next action in a persistent handoff, so that I can resume reliably without the chat.
11. As a product owner, I want functions/methods kept as a separate opportunity category, so that a model-only result is not described as all-language coverage.
12. As a product owner, I want uncertainty and sampling limitations reported, so that convenience samples are not marketed as ecosystem percentages.
13. As an evaluator, I want a finite pass and explicit stop condition, so that we do not tune on a holdout until it happens to pass.
14. As a contributor, I want new scope decisions recorded before implementation, so that evaluation findings do not silently become requirements.

## Implementation Decisions

- Start adapter coverage measurement after the initial task has an accepted local-check candidate and an evidence handoff. Corpus acquisition/labeling can be prepared earlier, but no pre-implementation parser inventory is an adapter coverage result.
- The initial task's actual accepted profile is the baseline. Model/type roots are the first measurement scope; methods/functions, notebooks and broader runtime-generated models are separate unmet-demand categories. Do not silently call them covered or hide their requested share.
- Use one outcome per independently labeled intended changed root, with event-level attribution reported as well. Distinguish the broad desired-model denominator from the accepted-profile subset and from capture/runtime-ineligible cases.
- Numerator: correct attribution and root identity/source, sufficient evidence for at least one pre-labeled relevant rule, and correct rule admission at the existing provider-boundary seam. Controlled clear results count as available review; the count is not the number of findings. Wrong binding/forbidden read/invented completeness never counts as success.
- Report parsing, extraction, required binding completeness, useful rule admission and operational preparation separately. Do not multiply marginal percentages as independent stages. Delivery/platform and semantic classifier quality are separate evidence claims.
- Begin with a cost-bounded pilot declaration, rather than imposing the earlier research proposal of 40 repositories/600 roots as a requirement. Proposed first acquisition: three independent application projects per language, up to ten relevant model roots per project, paired with realistic Add/Update or consented historical edits. Cap project contributions and include more than one organization/style. Freeze the manifest/labels before examining adapter output. If fewer cases can be acquired, report the shortfall and limits.
- Discovery frameworks and generated wire models cannot substitute for application-heavy evaluation. Include ordinary small projects, Python dataclass/TypedDict/Pydantic/plain annotated families, and Go split-package models/constants/local imports. Record method/validator-only edits and opaque external-type needs when they affect intended models.
- Preserve unsupported and unresolved desired cases in the denominator; report exclusions and their reasons. A case can be outside the initial accepted scope without disappearing from broad unmet-demand reporting.
- Provide per-language/per-project/family counts and pooled/macro results with weighting sensitivity. The pilot is descriptive; do not claim a statistically supported population 90% bound from approximately thirty roots. A larger independent holdout or confidence-bound protocol is optional later work only if the decision needs it.
- Rank failures by useful cases recovered, engineering/maintenance cost, trust/budget consequences and confidence in the proposed repair. Separate observed frequencies from estimated future reach/cost.
- If common cases require expensive dynamic inference, dependency traversal, large budget increases or broader root semantics, recommend retaining a smaller scope/target. Do not implement those expansions as part of evaluation.
- One frozen evaluation ends with results and a decision recommendation. If implementation is later changed using these failures, a new independent validation set is required before claiming generalization.

## Testing Decisions

- Reuse the initial task's existing direct-edit pipeline/provider-input seam with a controlled reviewer, plus captured source snapshots and independently labeled expected roots/bindings. No new production evaluation API is required.
- Good evaluation checks compare externally observable prepared evidence, rule admission/omission and outcomes with independent labels; they do not count AST nodes as successes or assert private traversal order.
- Include negative controls for unrelated sibling changes, shadowed names, unresolved external semantics, excluded source, metadata changes and stale evidence. A high availability fraction cannot excuse privacy/identity failures.
- Keep semantic usefulness/actionability separate from input availability. A bounded later live Jev study is optional and must have its own declared cases, budgets and evidence boundary; ordinary measurements remain deterministic/offline.
- Follow current local check policy for any evaluation harness changes. Only actually executed checks qualify; remote CI is separate unless specifically required by a release contract.

## Out of Scope

- Automatically implementing expanded language features or independent function/method review.
- Guaranteed 90% ecosystem coverage, a fixed large corpus, mandatory confidence-bound gate or repeated tuning on the same holdout.
- Crawling installed/system libraries, executing project imports/builds/generators or increasing source/egress limits for measurement.
- Re-running the broad language-popularity/Astra consultation pass without new evidence or an owner request.
- Treating source percentages as actual user edit prevalence or treating correct safe omissions as useful review successes.

## Further Notes

### Required completion handoff from the initial task

The initial task must populate this issue with its accepted profile, implementation/evidence commits and PR, capability matrix, executed local commands/environment/results, grammar/native versions and digests, actual rule inputs/omissions, installed host/platform evidence, known gaps and next executable measurement step. Retain the source-only discovery manifests/replayers with stable links; do not depend on an uncommitted workspace or this chat. No measurement should start by assuming every proposed profile row was implemented.

### Conversation decisions that govern continuation

- Product: Hapsland; Jev is its external review backend. Source-language profiles are separate from agent-runtime adapters.
- Python and Go are the two chosen vectors. The initial deliverable is bounded user-model/type review; no mandatory chain of stages is agreed.
- Existing traversal starts at the changed root and expands relevant declarations within budgets. For TypeScript it follows local declarations/relative imports, not installed/system declarations. Bend's bundled Base declarations are an explicit separate mechanism, not authorization for broad library crawling.
- In Go, discovering same-package declarations may require examining eligible sibling files. Discovering package authority is not sending every file to the backend; no directory-size percentage predicts evidence size.
- Ninety percent is an aspiration. The owner explicitly permits a smaller target/profile when the last gains require disproportionate complexity. Do not revive the earlier broad type/function/method family gate or fixed 600-root research budget as accepted requirements.
- Methods were frequent in selected source (Python focused corpus 30,616/51,458 definitions = 59.5%; Go production sample 988 receiver methods versus 898 ordinary functions). These explain possible broader demand, not the initial model profile's measured failure rate.
- Go 53.1% means sampled production roots located in directories containing more than eight non-test Go files. It does not mean 53.1% require more than eight supporting captures, that those files are transmitted, or that coverage is 46.9%.
- Research authority is advisory. Metadata, source inspection and runtime syntax inventories establish different facts; none establishes useful-review coverage. Exactly two Astra consultations were already used; no additional consultation is authorized by this handoff.

### Immutable discovery source pins

These upstream revisions preserve the research frame even if local research notes are absent. They are discovery evidence, not the required evaluation corpus:

| Language / project | Upstream revision | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Python / Pydantic AI | https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/tree/352b19899b37f0637ee1dc7e321b59b15fa98694 | AI framework and associated packages |
| Python / OpenAI Agents | https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/tree/125efa029b4bfd84238bd2c4fd69c3406f802663 | AI framework |
| Python / LangGraph | https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/tree/26356227c434b9bac191beb7ad67c73dc07a1d3d | Graph/state framework packages |
| Python / Khoj | https://github.com/khoj-ai/khoj/tree/ae229ca894c0b80ad84664afcfdde523b5e87057 | AI application |
| Python / FastAPI template | https://github.com/fastapi/full-stack-fastapi-template/tree/7257e606cb94eada1dca40173e2b7f99dd549bc6 | Backend application template |
| Python / LiteLLM | https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/0519882fefb99250aa441d3179363d1acec2172b | AI gateway |
| Go / Eino | https://github.com/cloudwego/eino/tree/58d184303f4e73413c454a9626f79c17af0fd9fb | AI framework |
| Go / Ollama | https://github.com/ollama/ollama/tree/eab97e9f92b9a25c2d52d2cc6c1b1c99bd9fae21 | AI runtime/infrastructure |
| Go / PocketBase | https://github.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/tree/6f370ea741f33adf889eef02e3c1b884a47aa522 | Application/backend |
| Go / Prometheus | https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/tree/2213c3c192574b8a339acd336ea6385974a7567b | Service infrastructure |

Source-only inventory used Python AST 3.11.2 for Python (4,403 focused files; one newer-syntax failure retained), and Node 24.20.0/linux-arm64 with Tree-sitter runtime 0.25.1/Go grammar 0.25.0 for 320 Go files (no syntax errors). A shared synthetic probe using Python/Go grammar 0.25.0 accepted 16/17 fixtures each; Python PEP696 defaults and a compact Go const block failed. Python PEP758 syntax failed the older AST inventory tool but was accepted by Tree-sitter. No Hapsland Python/Go adapter, compiler acceptance, binding closure, package/native host or actual user edit coverage was established by those runs.

### Resume procedure and stop condition

1. Read the linked initial task and its completion handoff, then the current accepted review contract, adapter guidance and checks policy. Resolve source revisions and verify that evidence links/artifacts exist.
2. If the initial profile is not accepted yet, prepare independent labels/corpus only; do not report adapter percentages. If the handoff is missing, request/produce it from actual implementation evidence rather than reconstructing claims from research.
3. Freeze a small application-heavy pilot and expected root/rule/binding labels. Run the existing seam once and retain outcome counts and failures.
4. Deliver per-language coverage tables, meaningful examples, ranked expansion costs and a recommendation to keep, extend, measure further or reduce the target. The follow-up is complete with that evidence and explicit decision proposal; no particular percentage or expanded implementation is required.

title: Review explicit Python models in one file through installed pipeline
body:
## Parent

[#267 — bounded Python and Go user-model review](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/267).

**Purpose:** Deliver the complete same-file Python model-review slice of the parent specification.
**Audience:** Implementation contributors, including coding agents; product/specification owners and acceptance reviewers.
**Status:** Owner-approved vertical implementation ticket, 2026-10-09; ready-for-agent. Publication creates the task and does not start implementation.
**Authority:** Parent owner-approved scope; the precise selection/evidence clarifications here were approved with the breakdown. No broader function or runtime-schema guarantee.
**Expected use:** Implement this vertical slice through existing review/provider/advice and installed grammar seams.
**Lifecycle:** Temporary local draft; after published issues and relationships are verified, delete drafting copies. Consolidate accepted support boundaries into existing contract/guidance owners during implementation; the published issue retains task/evidence history.

## What to build

An attributed Add/Update to a supported explicit Python model in one eligible source file produces the correct independent review unit, admitted type-rule input and controlled advice outcome in the installed product. The slice includes annotated model classes, standard dataclasses, class-form TypedDict, statically identified Pydantic BaseModel classes, explicit supported aliases and NewType declarations. Same-file supporting model references and local bases are available; unavailable cross-file user types remain honest omissions until the next slice.

Class and framework recognition follows lexical/import identity, not names alone. The framework marker is a bounded static interpretation; analysis neither imports its implementation nor claims full runtime validation. This slice establishes the exact changed-root/class-source contract and shared kind/rule/native changes required for its user-visible behavior, rather than landing a parser alone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All promised same-file root families have exact identity/source/ranges and an explicit evidence/rule matrix. Plain annotated classes require declared class-level fields or resolved local model ancestry; arbitrary classes and fields inferred from method assignments are not admitted.
- [ ] Class Add selects eligible added models; supported decorator/header/base/field/schema-configuration edits select the corresponding class once; mixed field+method edits select it once. Ordinary-method-only and validator-only edits do not select a model. Pure removed classes do not produce a post-edit root; field removal selects a surviving class only when existing attribution evidence establishes it. Uncertain attribution produces no guessed target. These cases are recorded as an explicit amendment to the general smallest-enclosing-root rule.
- [ ] Selected classes preserve the complete exact declaration and applicable decorators, including visible method/validator source. The complete evidence tree must fit existing limits, including 20 KiB canonical evidence; oversized roots are explicitly unavailable, with no field-only fallback.
- [ ] Supporting type references are collected from static field annotations, bases, supported type expressions and type-bearing schema metadata/configuration. Arbitrary default/validator/method calls do not acquire a function/helper traversal. Unknown executable behavior never establishes complete runtime constraints; lack of required evidence blocks only affected rules.
- [ ] Canonical dataclass, typing/typing_extensions and Pydantic markers are recognized via supported named/qualified imports and aliases; same-named local bindings or shadows fail recognition. Unsupported/computed decorators/bases are explicitly uncertain where relevant. Supported framework marker forms and expression subsets are listed in accepted guidance and fixtures.
- [ ] Add Python type inputs to the shipped rule inventory where justified, beginning with concrete `meaningless_combinations`, `absence_confusion` and `bare_domain_value` matrix entries for applicable explicit model shapes; preserve their declared evidence requirements. Each promised edited-root family has at least one actual applicable type-rule combination, including clear controls for fieldless/nominal families, or is explicitly identified as supporting-only rather than claiming useful root support.
- [ ] Unknown external references remain opaque. No synthetic framework declarations or fake complete closure are emitted, and custom root-only test rules are not used as the sole witness of useful shipped support.
- [ ] A positive control and a clear/omission control exercise the existing observation→capture→root/evidence→provider input→controlled result/advice seam. Separate eligible roots proceed when a neighbor is unsupported; unchanged siblings and ordinary functions/methods do not become new targets.
- [ ] Shared artifact/rule/inspection/format representations admit the new profile consistently in place at version one, with existing TS/Rust/Bend behavior preserved. No legacy/parallel production format or gratuitous standalone prefactor is introduced.
- [ ] The adopted grammar/runtime cohort is exactly pinned, known syntax gaps are retained as explicit unsupported outcomes or addressed by a reviewed compatible fix, and native assets are wired through existing packaging. Existing required installed-package/platform checks and a bounded native edit scenario qualify only their actually exercised boundary.
- [ ] Privacy/exclusion, source/tree/work budgets, missing-required-evidence and stale-advice negative cases pass through existing public seams. Acceptance lists the actual checks/versions/platforms and limitations and contributes them to the parent/coverage handoff.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

Go's first slice can also start immediately. Shared artifact/rule/native owners require coordination of edits; that is not a product dependency on completing Go. Any unavoidable shared changes must land with this slice's green consumers and follow pre-release in-place format policy.

title: Review Python models through local packages and inheritance
body:
## Parent

[#267 — bounded Python and Go user-model review](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/267).

**Purpose:** Deliver complete Python model review through supported local packages, reexports and inheritance.
**Audience:** Implementation contributors including coding agents; product/specification owners and acceptance reviewers.
**Status:** Owner-approved vertical implementation ticket, 2026-10-09; ready-for-agent. Publication creates the task and does not start implementation.
**Authority:** Parent scope and the prerequisite Python model slice; precise authority/freshness clarifications were approved with this breakdown.
**Expected use:** Extend the same installed review path to cross-file user-model evidence; no independent review pipeline.
**Lifecycle:** Delete local drafts after verified publication. During implementation consolidate accepted import/layout boundaries into existing contract/guidance owners and retain the published issue's evidence/handoff.

## What to build

A model edit obtains sufficient supporting user declarations through statically resolved local imports, package reexports and local inheritance. The installed product prepares the correct cross-file provider input, applies the actual eligible type rules and preserves binding freshness even when resolution alternatives are created, removed or renamed.

This closes the Python parent profile rather than adding functions or executing models. Pydantic custom local base classes use the same module/inheritance authority; they do not require a separate framework pipeline.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Support named member and module imports, aliases/qualified names, relative imports, unambiguous project-local absolute imports and explicit named initializer reexports, including bounded chains/cycles with honest omissions.
- [ ] Freeze and document the initial authority forms: conventional flat layout or conventional src layout plus a single unambiguous static project root from captured metadata. Do not execute build backends, discover arbitrary editable installs or infer ambient PYTHONPATH. Conflicting roots, custom loaders and unsupported namespace layouts remain unavailable.
- [ ] Static TYPE_CHECKING names and the declared subset of literal/simple forward type expressions resolve without evaluating annotations. Runtime/type conflicts, rebindings and shadowing do not guess a target.
- [ ] Define source/stub precedence explicitly for this source-review profile: available eligible `.py` is the source authority; local `.pyi` can supply supporting type evidence when no source implementation is available, never a replacement method body/constructor. Conflicting alternatives are not silently merged, and stubs are not newly attributed model roots.
- [ ] Cross-file dataclass/TypedDict/ordinary/Pydantic local model ancestry is preserved as exact source evidence; bases/fields are not flattened into an invented runtime model. Unknown external/framework behavior remains opaque and is gated by the affected rule's requirements.
- [ ] Discovery and source/metadata reads consume explicit existing file/read/work/deadline budgets and use unchanged containment/exclusions. An index is not a free path around the eight-file ceiling or permission to send every discovered declaration.
- [ ] Freshness covers positive bindings and the bounded set of alternatives/membership facts establishing uniqueness. Create/delete/rename a sibling module/package/initializer and observe invalidation or safe ambiguity, including previously absent alternatives. If absence/membership cannot be revalidated within budget, decline the affected result.
- [ ] Metadata authority reads have an explicit policy when source-oriented includes are configured; no user/project exclusion is bypassed merely to obtain import roots.
- [ ] Cross-file positive cases, alias/reexport/inheritance shadow negatives, excluded/outside-root cases, changed dependencies and restored source exercise the same actual provider-input/rule-admission seam. No omitted needed edge is called complete.
- [ ] A bounded installed cross-file edit scenario demonstrates the finalized Python profile and its controlled advice delivery. Capture read volume, input/tree size and tested host/platform facts separately from semantic classifier accuracy.
- [ ] Publish the final Python root/import/framework/rule/unsupported matrix and exact acceptance evidence into the continuation handoff for #268; include known validator-only, dynamic-schema and budget gaps without extending the scope.

## Blocked by

- [#269 — Python models in one file](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/269): supplies the accepted Python artifact/selection/rule/native vertical path extended here.

No Go blocker. Do not add a dependency solely because both tracks edit a shared schema or registration owner.

title: Review Go models and typed constants in the active local package
body:
## Parent

[#267 — bounded Python and Go user-model review](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/267).

**Purpose:** Deliver complete Go user-model review for an active local package, including same-package evidence and typed constants.
**Audience:** Implementation contributors including coding agents; product/specification owners and acceptance reviewers.
**Status:** Owner-approved vertical implementation ticket, 2026-10-09; ready-for-agent. Publication creates the task and does not start implementation.
**Authority:** Parent user-model scope; the specific build-context and constant/membership clarifications were approved with this breakdown.
**Expected use:** Implement an independently verifiable package-level model review slice through existing installed review boundaries.
**Lifecycle:** Delete local drafting copies after verified publication. Consolidate accepted package/build/type boundaries into existing contract/guidance owners during implementation; keep the published task/evidence record.

## What to build

An attributed Go named-type edit is reviewed with the relevant user declarations and constant groups from its active local package, without inventing imports between sibling files or transmitting the whole package. The installed pipeline preserves defined-type/alias identity, admits actual applicable type rules and delivers controlled advice.

The slice includes named structs, scalar/container defined types, aliases, interfaces/generic type declarations, embedded members, tags, generic parameters/constraints and relevant typed constants. Independent functions and receiver methods remain outside scope.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Exact root identity/source/ranges are retained for single/grouped type declarations. Defined types and aliases remain distinct; interfaces/type-set constraints do not become a closed hierarchy of runtime implementers.
- [ ] Package-scoped type names resolve across eligible active sibling files; file-scoped imported names and local/type-parameter shadows are not confused with package bindings. External/local-module imports requiring another package remain explicit omissions until the next Go slice.
- [ ] Build-context authority is explicit and reproducible: use a frozen Hapsland analysis-configuration snapshot to declare target GOOS/GOARCH and user build tags. Do not implicitly take the review host's environment as the target. An unconditional package may proceed without additional target settings only if membership/identity is independent of them. Configuration source/precedence, validated values, fingerprint identity and observable missing-context outcomes are documented and tested.
- [ ] Freeze the supported constraint subset before coding membership: platform suffix selection and boolean go:build expressions over declared/known target and user-tag facts. Derived facts have a documented table; unrecognized language-version/experiment/legacy constraints are explicit unknowns, not false defaults. cgo-dependent authority is unsupported. Mutually exclusive source variants cannot be merged into one package.
- [ ] Find relevant typed constant/iota groups through bounded active-package discovery, since a type declaration has no outgoing reference to its constants. Retain the exact original group needed for iota ordinal/implicit-expression meaning, including necessary predecessors; if that group exceeds the budget, record missing evidence. Do not extract an isolated enumerator and invent its value or imply constants exhaust a scalar's runtime values.
- [ ] Constant-only edits do not silently trigger review of an unchanged type. Record them as a follow-up demand gap; mixed type/constant edits select only actually attributed type roots. No method/function review input is introduced.
- [ ] All discovery/capture/metadata work has an explicit bounded policy inside existing ceilings and exclusions. Large directories are not automatically read or transmitted in full; incomplete membership/identity yields an honest omission.
- [ ] Freshness checks include the limited package membership/alternative identities establishing uniqueness, not just hashes of already-read declarations. New/deleted/renamed sibling files, changed constraints, configuration and restored source invalidate or safely reject stale binding/results.
- [ ] There is a concrete shipped-rule/evidence matrix for applicable model families, beginning with `meaningless_combinations`, `absence_confusion` and `bare_domain_value` where justified. Preserve declared type-closure requirements; unknown external fields do not become fake complete evidence, and actual eligible roots/rules can proceed independently.
- [ ] Positive split-package/typed-constant/header/field cases and ambiguous/inactive/excluded/budget/constant-only negatives exercise observation→capture→provider input→controlled result/advice in the existing seam, with no system/cache/vendor/source-generation traversal.
- [ ] Adopt exactly pinned grammar/runtime and existing native loading/packaging ownership. Known syntax gaps are explicit or addressed by a reviewed compatible fix. Existing required package/platform checks and a bounded installed package-model edit witness qualify their actual tested scope.
- [ ] Shared representations/contracts are extended consistently in place at version one, existing language consumers remain valid, and a precise partial Go profile plus evidence/limitations is recorded for the parent/coverage handoff.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

Coordinate shared artifact/rule/native owner edits with the first Python slice; no mandatory language-order edge or standalone infrastructure/refactor ticket is introduced.

title: Explore returning a validated partial ReviewUnit when graph preparation reaches its deadline
body:
Graph preparation currently has a 5-second time budget. When it expires, Hapsland returns no ReviewUnit, even if preparation has already assembled useful content.

On master at `47fdf0f0afffc6eca9f613813eee7e533808e082`, `graphIteration` emits `deadlineReached` and returns `unit: undefined`; `partialGraphUnit` explicitly excludes the `Deadline` reason. The full Bend resolver in the migration worktree also returns `NoReviewUnit` on deadline.

We should investigate whether returning the already assembled, validated portion would be more useful than discarding all preparation work. This issue requests a design decision, not an immediate change to timeout behavior.

Questions to resolve:

- What is a valid returnable checkpoint? Distinguish committed graph content from a tentative child whose measured contribution has not yet been admitted.
- Can unfinished references be represented honestly as omissions, without dangling links or a claim of complete exploration? What if the root itself has not finished preparation?
- How do we preserve source, tree, file, depth and work limits, permission checks, and the ReviewUnit structural guarantees?
- Can final validation and encoding remain bounded after the deadline, or must we retain an already validated checkpoint? Returning partial content must not introduce unbounded work after timeout.
- Would partial context improve review usefulness, or create misleading findings? Consider both a small accepted root and a larger graph interrupted during import expansion.
- Keep deadline behavior distinct from cancellation, provider failures and protocol violations; decide their semantics separately.

Expected outcome:

- Record a decision in the maintained owner of graph-preparation behavior, with the trade-offs and eligibility rules, or explain why discarding the result should remain the policy.
- If partial return is accepted, define concrete cases for expiry before root completion, after an accepted checkpoint, during a tentative child, and at final measurement; specify bounded finalization and an explicit incomplete reason.
- Identify the corresponding TypeScript and Bend implementation changes and parity checks before implementation.

Relevant code:

- [Current time budget](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/47fdf0f0afffc6eca9f613813eee7e533808e082/packages/source-analysis/src/direct-event/graph-resolver.ts#L60)
- [Partial-result eligibility and deadline handling](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/47fdf0f0afffc6eca9f613813eee7e533808e082/packages/source-analysis/src/direct-event/graph-resolver.ts#L365)
- [Graph iteration deadline](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/blob/47fdf0f0afffc6eca9f613813eee7e533808e082/packages/source-analysis/src/direct-event/graph-resolver.ts#L714)
