title: Specify batch reviews through the Hapsland CLI
body:
## Destination

Agree on an implementation-ready specification for batch reviews through the Hapsland CLI: auditing selected files (the priority) and reviewing declarations selected by Git changes. The map is complete when behavior, interface, and acceptance criteria are settled; implementation follows separately.

## Notes

Use wayfinder for planning and grilling plus domain-modeling for decisions with the owner. Do not reopen agreed starting constraints without a new contradiction. This map concerns explicit CLI invocation, not automatic checkpoint catch-up: [Decide checkpoint reconciliation coverage and mechanism](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/38) remains a separate map.

Starting constraints agreed with the owner before this map was created:

- Both workflows are required; auditing selected files is the priority. The review unit remains a declaration with permitted related context.
- Explicit CLI includes replace configured includes for that invocation only; ordinary exclusions remain effective by default.
- Add an explicit option to disable ordinary global exclusions. It does not override privacyExcludes, protected paths, Git-ignore, or rule restrictions. Context inheritance details and flag names remain to be decided.
- Auditing requires explicitly configured includes or CLI includes. There is no implicit whole-repository selection and no requirement to repeat CLI includes when configuration already supplies them.
- Git selections can be combined as a union without duplicate declarations. Review current working-tree declarations and current related definitions, not historical versions.
- Working changes, staged changes, a single commit, and a commit range are candidate selectors. Their exact meanings, default, and syntax are not yet settled. Repeated flags and comma-separated syntax are alternatives, not decisions.
- No new total-work limit is required now. Existing safety and provider limits remain in effect.
- Progress shows counts of files, declarations, and requests only, without file lists or current filenames. Distinguish estimated request counts from a known plan. Ctrl+C must stop new requests, attempt cancellation of active requests, and report an honest partial result; the provider may still process requests already sent.
- Declare parameters through Effect CLI. Derive help, Markdown, precedence rules, and examples from shared declarations or logic where possible; avoid separately maintained copies of facts.

Verified starting point: `rules check --path --line` uses Effect CLI and the shared review pipeline. `rules/cli-definition.ts` owns declarations; `scripts/generate-configuration.ts` currently emits commands, descriptions, and examples, but not a complete flag table. `scripts/documentation-facts.ts` already obtains facts and plans from runtime owners. `docs/adr/0002-accumulate-file-exclusions.md` prohibits re-inclusion across configuration layers: the new explicit CLI override needs a precise decision and a subsequent amendment to its contract owner. `docs/configuration.md` distinguishes root, context, and privacy selection. Select checks through CHECKS.md and the testing matrix; this map claims no runtime validation.

Work the first open, unblocked, unassigned child ticket; assign it to the developer driving the map before starting. Record the answer in that ticket's resolution comment, close it, and add only a gist and link below. Native sub-issues and blocking relationships define the frontier; do not duplicate the open-ticket list in this body.

## Decisions so far

- [Define file and context selection for batch audits](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/276): repository-root CLI patterns, effective-policy context inheritance, explicit audit scope, and optional narrowing of Git selections.

- [Define Git selection unions and selection of current declarations](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/277): repeatable Git-source unions select current declarations; conservative mapping reports ambiguity, while confirmed deletions are not applicable.

- [Define progress, partial results, and cancellation for batch reviews](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/278): count-only stderr progress, final text/JSON results, distinct completion statuses, scoped error handling, and reuse of existing freshness checks.

- [Define the Effect CLI interface and shared source for generated documentation](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/279): rules audit/check-changes, typed repeatable Git selectors, explicit batch exit codes, and shared Effect CLI/documentation generation.

- [Agree on the final batch CLI contract and acceptance criteria](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/280): consolidated specification published as [Batch declaration reviews through the Hapsland CLI](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/282), including required Effect Service/Layer composition and offline acceptance boundaries.

## Not yet specified

No unresolved planning questions remain. The consolidated specification is ready for implementation-ticket decomposition. Surface newly discovered product requirements explicitly rather than hiding decisions in implementation.

## Out of scope

- Production implementation within this map; an MCP endpoint.
- Automatic checkpoint catch-up or changes to triggers and hooks.
- Reviewing historical source versions, a new total-work or cost limit, and filenames in progress output.
- Comparative quality or speed claims and paid provider runs to settle planning decisions.

Decide the base for paths and globs when invoked from a subdirectory, repeated includes, empty lists, and zero matches. Determine whether CLI overrides preserve the original contextIncludes/contextExcludes inheritance or make context follow the new root selection. How should working changes, staged changes, a single commit, and a commit range select current declarations for review?

Already agreed: union without duplicates; review current declarations and related definitions, not historical versions. Decide defaults; staged, unstaged, and untracked behavior; single-commit and merge-parent semantics; endpoint diff versus merge-base; deleted and renamed files; and mapping historical changed ranges onto current code. Do not silently substitute auditing every declaration in a changed file for selecting affected declarations.

Consider repeated selectors versus comma-separated syntax and ambiguous refs. Flag names remain proposals. Define errors instead of silently broadening scope, and how Git selection interacts with includes. The outcome is selection and declaration examples with unsupported cases explicitly identified.

title: Define progress, partial results, and cancellation for batch reviews
body:
## Question

What should the CLI report to humans and automation on success, findings, skips, errors, and Ctrl+C?

Already agreed: counts only, without filenames; files, declarations, and requests; estimates distinct from a known plan; stop new requests and attempt cancellation of active requests; a partial result is not a complete clean review. Do not introduce a new total-work limit.

Decide counter meanings under concurrency and retries, stdout/stderr and TTY/non-TTY/JSON behavior, the partial-result schema, continuation after individual errors, and exit codes. Clarify snapshots and freshness when files change during a long run, and distinguish zero declarations, zero applicable rules, and zero findings. The current single-declaration rules check returns 0 even with findings and 6 for unavailable/skipped; do not silently transfer these semantics to batch results. Its JSON contains source: define public batch output explicitly.

The outcome is a table of observable results and testable examples, without live provider calls.

HITL: resolve with the owner using grilling and domain-modeling.

title: Batch declaration reviews through the Hapsland CLI
body:
## Problem Statement

**Purpose:** Specify explicit batch review of current source through the Hapsland CLI.
**Audience:** End users, coding agents, rule authors, contributors, and evaluation reviewers.
**Status:** Implementation specification synthesized from owner-approved planning decisions; implementation and validation pending.
**Authority:** Product specification consolidating the linked owner-approved planning decisions and the requested Effect Layer test boundary. It is not implementation or validation evidence.
**Expected use:** Use this specification as the source for implementation ticket decomposition and acceptance.
**Lifecycle:** Maintain this issue through explicit specification amendments. Update maintained rule/configuration guidance during implementation; record implementation evidence separately from the contract.

Users and coding agents can review one declaration at a file and line, but cannot explicitly audit a selected collection of files or review current declarations selected by several Git change sources in one invocation. Repeating the one-declaration command requires callers to perform Hapsland's selection and aggregation themselves. Hooks serve event-driven work and do not replace these explicit workflows.

## Solution

Add two commands under the existing rules capability:

- `hapsland rules audit`: review all eligible current declarations in explicitly selected files. Auditing is the primary workflow.
- `hapsland rules check-changes`: review eligible current declarations affected by selected Git changes, without duplicate declaration reviews.

Both use existing configuration, evidence admission, provider integration, and supported analyzer profiles. Review one declaration and its permitted related definitions per review unit; do not substitute fixed text chunks or blanket whole-file audits for affected-declaration selection.

Keep the existing single-declaration check behavior. Hooks remain independent. No MCP endpoint is required.

## User Stories

1. As an end user, I want one invocation to audit selected files, so that I do not have to discover every declaration myself.
2. As a coding agent, I want explicit batch review through a shell command, so that I can review work without a separate MCP integration.
3. As an end user, I want audits to require explicit includes, so that an omitted setting cannot unexpectedly send an entire repository to the classifier.
4. As an end user, I want configured includes to work without repeating them on every invocation, so that ordinary audits are convenient.
5. As an end user, I want CLI includes to replace configured includes for one invocation, so that I can intentionally audit another area.
6. As an end user, I want repeated includes to form a union, so that I can select several areas together.
7. As an end user, I want CLI patterns relative to the repository root, so that selection is stable from subdirectories.
8. As an end user, I want ordinary exclusions preserved by default, so that my normal selection remains effective.
9. As an end user, I want an explicit ordinary-exclusion override, so that I can inspect an otherwise excluded area intentionally.
10. As an end user, I want privacy restrictions to remain effective under that override, so that changing audit scope cannot bypass protected reads.
11. As a rule author, I want explicit related-context selection preserved and inherited context to follow effective root policy, so that source access is understandable.
12. As an end user, I want empty selection reported distinctly, so that a typo or empty scope cannot look like a clean review.
13. As an end user, I want all uncommitted changes selected by default in change mode, so that staged, unstaged, and new files are included.
14. As an end user, I want staged, unstaged, and untracked sources individually selectable, so that I can narrow a review.
15. As an end user, I want a commit or explicit endpoint comparison to select affected declarations, so that I can inspect work associated with a revision.
16. As an end user, I want an explicit merge-base comparison against a supplied ref, so that I can review committed branch work.
17. As an end user, I want several Git sources combined without duplicate reviews, so that overlapping selections do not repeat work.
18. As an end user, I want selected declarations evaluated in their current working-tree state, so that findings concern code I can act on now.
19. As an end user, I want ambiguous historical-to-current mapping reported as incomplete, so that uncertain selection cannot silently widen or disappear.
20. As an end user, I want confirmed deleted targets counted as not applicable, so that current-code review does not pretend to evaluate missing code.
21. As an end user, I want file, declaration, and request counts without filename lists in progress, so that parallel work remains readable.
22. As an end user, I want estimated requests distinguished from a known plan, so that I understand what the displayed total means.
23. As an end user, I want Ctrl+C to stop new requests and retain completed results, so that I can stop work and still use its partial outcome.
24. As an end user, I want independent checks to continue after isolated errors but stop after run-wide failures, so that failures have the correct scope.
25. As an end user, I want existing freshness checks reused, so that detected outdated inputs are not presented as current findings.
26. As a script author, I want one final JSON result without default source text, so that I can consume outcomes safely and reliably.
27. As a script author, I want distinct complete, findings, incomplete, no-work, and interrupted exits, so that I can automate follow-up correctly.
28. As a rule author, I want to select one enabled rule or all eligible enabled rules, so that I can focus checks without changing configuration.
29. As an end user, I want help and Markdown to describe the same flags, defaults, and precedence, so that documented commands behave as shown.
30. As a contributor, I want generated selection examples evaluated through the real policy, so that documentation does not maintain a second behavioral definition.

## Implementation Decisions

### Selection and policy

- Audits require explicit includes from configuration or CLI. Missing includes are an actionable invocation/configuration error. Explicit empty selection produces no-work. No implicit whole-repository audit.
- Repeatable CLI `--include PATTERN` forms a union and replaces configured root includes for this invocation. CLI patterns are repository-root relative. This does not redefine the existing single-declaration path base.
- Ordinary global exclusions remain effective unless `--ignore-excludes` is supplied. The override does not remove privacy exclusions, protected paths, containment, Git-ignore, file-kind/size bounds, provider limits, or rule restrictions.
- Explicit context includes/excludes remain effective. Omitted context selection follows effective root policy after CLI overrides, including exclusion override. Do not silently admit related files outside that scope.
- Git sources provide candidates; configured or CLI includes, when present, narrow them. Git mode does not require additional includes.
- No selected files, eligible declarations, or applicable rules produces no-work with an explicit reason and no classifier requests. If some include patterns match and others do not, continue with a warning; no matches never broaden scope.
- Audit every eligible declaration, including multiple declarations on the same source line. Reuse shared declaration preparation/evaluation; do not implement audit by repeatedly calling the line-selection command, whose ambiguity rules serve a different purpose.
- Run audits only within the currently supported analyzer and rule-input profiles. Unsupported source or missing required evidence remains visible through selection/result reasons, without extending language support implicitly.

### CLI and Git sources

Both batch commands accept repeatable `--include PATTERN`, optional single `--id ID`, single boolean `--ignore-excludes` (default false), and single boolean `--json` (default false). Omitted id selects all eligible enabled rules; unknown or disabled ids fail.

Only check-changes accepts these repeatable source flags:

| Flag | Selection |
| --- | --- |
| `--changes working` | Union of staged, unstaged, and untracked work. |
| `--changes staged` | HEAD-to-index changes. |
| `--changes unstaged` | Index-to-working-tree changes in tracked files. |
| `--changes untracked` | New untracked files subject to normal policy. |
| `--commit REF` | Changes introduced by a non-merge commit relative to its parent. |
| `--range FROM..TO` | Net difference between explicit endpoints, excluding intermediate changes reverted by TO. |
| `--merge-base REF` | Common-ancestor-to-HEAD difference against the explicit ref; add working to include uncommitted work. |

- If every source flag group is omitted, default to working. Otherwise use exactly the explicit union. Do not split comma lists or infer main/master/upstream.
- Resolve refs once per invocation. Require explicit range endpoints; reject malformed, triple-dot, unresolved, and ambiguous selectors before classifier dispatch.
- Initially reject single merge commits and root commits with actionable unsupported-selector errors; explicit endpoint comparisons are available. Do not infer a merge parent or silently widen selection.
- Deduplicate current review declarations across sources. Use the simplest conservative unambiguous mapping to current declarations. Ambiguous mappings are reported as skips and make the result incomplete; no heuristic rename/split recovery or whole-file fallback is required.
- Deleting lines inside a surviving selected declaration selects its current definition. A confirmed fully deleted declaration/file is not applicable and alone does not make the result incomplete. Uncertain mapping is distinct from confirmed deletion.
- Reject Git flags on audit, and path/line/scope flags on both batch commands. Reject unknown flags, blank/missing values, and repeated singleton flags through the actual Effect parser and domain validation.


### Effect dependency composition

The owner explicitly requires idiomatic Effect dependency composition in the affected CLI and review path. Where dependencies are still created imperatively inside workflows or threaded through ad hoc optional arguments in a way that prevents normal composition, refactor them into the existing or appropriately scoped Effect Services and Layers. This work is required even if current behavior can be tested through a shortcut. Keep dependency ownership with the relevant capability, reuse existing Effect services, and avoid introducing a wrapper service for every pure function.

The production composition supplies live Layers; tests supply controlled Layers to the same workflow. Do not build a separate test workflow, hide configuration in process-global mutations, or add product transport flags solely to facilitate testing. Preserve real parser, selection, source analysis, evidence admission, provider adaptation, and aggregation in integrated tests. This scope covers dependencies touched by batch CLI execution, not a repository-wide Effect migration.

This dependency requirement is distinct from the earlier bounded freshness decision: reuse existing freshness logic, with its explicitly stated timing boundary, without importing resident delivery machinery. Required dependency cleanup must not be skipped under the freshness cost allowance.

### Execution, progress, and results

- Reuse existing source preparation, rule/evidence admission, credential lookup, provider execution, and freshness checks through the explicit-review capability. Do not create an advicee, hook session, or resident delivery authority for a batch invocation.
- Continue independent work after declaration-specific failure. Stop new dispatch on run-wide configuration, credential, or backend failures. Add no batch retry loop; do not promise that existing transport layers never retry.
- Show only counters for files, declarations, and requests on stderr. Request states distinguish planned/estimated, active, successful, and failed work; file/declaration counts distinguish processed and skipped work. Use monotonic completed counts under parallelism; request accounting must not count an estimate as a dispatched request. Count logical classifier dispatches at the existing execution observation boundary; do not label these as HTTP wire attempts or billed requests. Provider retries may produce different transport counts.
- Use updating progress in a terminal and infrequent plain lines without animation for redirected output. Findings and final results go to stdout. Findings identify their file and declaration; the filename restriction applies to progress only.
- With --json, write one final structured result, including partial results, to stdout. Exclude source code by default. Preserve reasons, counters, findings, and completion status.
- Ctrl+C stops new requests, attempts cancellation of active requests, and retains completed results. Already dispatched requests may still be processed by the provider. Do not add a new total-work cap.
- Reuse per-declaration freshness validation before dispatch and after evaluation. Recheck retained inputs during final report preparation if a modest extraction of shared logic permits it. If that would require substantial architectural rewriting, retain completion-time validation and state its timing boundary. No atomic batch snapshot or automatic re-review is promised. Detected stale results make the result incomplete.

| Outcome | Exit |
| --- | ---: |
| Complete, no findings | 0 |
| Complete, findings present | 1 |
| Incomplete or unavailable | 6 |
| No work | 7 |
| Interrupted | 130 |

Status precedence is interrupted, then incomplete, then no-work, then complete with or without findings. An ambiguous target with zero evaluations is incomplete, not no-work. Normal policy exclusions, ordinary rule ineligibility, and confirmed deletions alone do not make a review incomplete. Classify reasons rather than mechanically copying internal preparation status names. Retain findings even when another status determines the exit. Existing parser/local failures retain their established failure path, currently 6. Invalid syntax emits diagnostics without a batch report; failures after valid batch dispatch produce its incomplete result. Do not accidentally inherit the generic partial-status exit 5. Existing single-declaration exits remain unchanged.

### Ownership and generated documentation

- Keep orchestration and command declarations in the existing rules capability; use existing source-analysis/review-execution interfaces. Keep selection policy with its domain owner. No new package or command framework solely for batch documentation.
- Extend the existing shared Effect CLI declarations and generated reference with flag types/choices, cardinality, requiredness, defaults, examples, valid combinations, and exits. Public structured help may supply metadata; narrow shared declaration inputs must drive both parsing and generation where help lacks necessary facts. Do not rely on Effect internals or metadata that merely repeats behavior without controlling it.
- Generate precedence examples by executing the actual selection policy. Independently assert expected examples in tests so a wrong resolver cannot silently redefine correctness through regeneration.
- Extend existing documentation update/drift-check entrypoints and generated sections. Store example argument vectors alongside shell rendering so quoted globs and paths are tested faithfully.
- Amend the exclusion contract/ADR with the explicit batch override while preserving ordinary configuration-layer rules. Update configuration, rules, and parent help to describe both batch commands and classifier calls. Keep format versions at 1; no compatibility shims or parallel policies.

## Testing Decisions

The primary acceptance boundary is the real Effect command parser and batch workflow composed with test Effect Layers. Keep real selection, Git operations on temporary repositories, source preparation, evidence admission, result aggregation, and serialization. Supply isolated configuration and a controlled HttpClient through Layers at the provider boundary, retaining the real provider adapter for wire-contract assertions. Use existing injection points where practical; a small composition change may expose required services rather than constructing live dependencies deep inside the workflow. Do not replace the whole batch workflow with a fake service or add an alternate parser.

Most acceptance scenarios execute in-process with deterministic Layer dependencies and synchronization. No loopback HTTP server is required for those tests. A direct DecisionModel test Layer is appropriate for narrowly testing scheduling or error classification; it does not establish provider serialization. Use the controlled HttpClient Layer for integrated CLI-to-provider assertions. Reuse existing test services and ConfigProvider rather than adding a parallel test framework or product endpoint option.

Retain a small subprocess boundary only for OS/process behavior that in-process Layers cannot establish: actual stdout/stderr, real SIGINT, final JSON flush, and exit 130. A test-only composition entrypoint may supply the same Layers in that process; no public product transport override is required. Generator checks use their existing real consumer. Test externally observable behavior; avoid testing internal function structure.
A separate existing documentation-generator consumer establishes rendered flags, examples, precedence, and read-only drift detection. It is necessary because runtime behavior alone cannot prove generated Markdown. No new lower-level seams are proposed.

Acceptance must cover:

1. Audit all eligible declarations in selected files; no implicit expansion from missing/empty scope or zero matches.
2. Repository-root CLI patterns from subdirectories; union and replacement; warnings for unmatched members.
3. Ordinary exclusions preserved and explicitly bypassed; explicit/inherited context selection; all protected boundaries retained before reads.
4. Default working sources; individual and combined sources; explicit selectors replace the default; include narrowing and deduplication.
5. Non-merge commit, endpoint, and merge-base comparisons; invalid/unsupported selectors; root-commit refusal; known deletion versus ambiguous mapping.
6. Current source and related definitions used regardless of source origin; no hidden whole-file fallback.
7. Per-item versus run-wide failures, no-work categories, findings/incomplete precedence, and exact exits.
8. Count-only progress under parallelism; stderr/stdout behavior; one final JSON without default source; actionable finding locations.
9. Ctrl+C stops dispatch, attempts cancellation, preserves completed results and exit 130; no claim that provider-side work was cancelled.
10. Existing per-unit freshness checks; final recheck when modest reuse allows; stale inputs and stated timing boundaries.
11. Actual Effect parser/help, requiredness, flag combinations, and faithful example argv handling.
12. Generator update/check behavior, independently expected precedence examples, and unchanged surrounding prose.

Select implementation checks under the repository checks policy and testing matrix: fast gate and relevant focused owner tests for TypeScript changes; explicit generated-document and documentation checks for affected output; representative offline subprocess checks for the CLI boundary. Broaden only for newly exposed impact. Required checks must pass on the final acceptance candidate. GitHub CI is not an extra completion gate, and no live paid provider calls are required for deterministic acceptance.

## Out of Scope

- Production implementation in the planning map itself; implementation ticket publication before its breakdown is approved.
- MCP integration, new runtime hooks, automatic checkpoint reconciliation, or resident lifetime changes.
- Reviewing historical source versions, reliable heuristic recovery of renamed/split declarations, and semantic review of confirmed deleted code.
- New total-work/cost caps, filename lists in progress, source-bearing JSON by default, batch retry loops, or an atomic repository snapshot guarantee.
- New language support, provider quality/cost comparisons, and broad release/platform support claims.

## Further Notes

Source decisions: [batch CLI planning map](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/275), [file and context selection](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/276), [Git selections](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/277), [results and cancellation](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/278), and [CLI and generated documentation](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/279).

The final contract/acceptance decision links this specification. Acceptance permits decomposition into independently verifiable implementation tickets; it does not establish implemented behavior, native runtime compatibility, or provider quality. All required tests above are planned, not executed evidence.

title: Audit configured file scope through the Hapsland CLI
body:
## Parent

[Batch declaration reviews through the Hapsland CLI](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/282)

## What to build

Provide rules audit for explicitly configured includes: discover every eligible current declaration, review it with permitted context, and return usable text or JSON results in one invocation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Actual Effect CLI exposes audit with optional enabled-rule selection and JSON; missing explicit configured includes fails before provider dispatch, while empty/no-match/no-eligible/no-applicable work is distinguished.
- [ ] Every eligible declaration is selectable, including multiple declarations on one line; preparation, evidence admission, current provider integration, and protected-read policies are reused without line-check ambiguity or resident attribution.
- [ ] Ordinary configuration exclusions and explicit/inherited context policy apply; declaration findings include actionable locations and default JSON omits source.
- [ ] Count-only progress and result accounting distinguish files, declarations, estimates, logical dispatches, and completed/failed work; estimates are not billed or HTTP-attempt counts.
- [ ] Complete clear/findings exits are 0/1, incomplete is 6, no-work is 7. Findings survive incompleteness; normal exclusions, rule ineligibility, and confirmed non-targets do not alone imply incompleteness.
- [ ] Independent item failures permit other work; run-wide failures stop new dispatch. Preserve existing freshness checks and document their timing boundary; no automatic re-review or new total-work cap.
- [ ] Real parser/workflow tests use controlled Layers and temporary repositories. Help, classifier-call descriptions, generated flags, exit reference, and user documentation describe the delivered audit scope.
- [ ] This finite configured-scope slice does not claim the entire parent feature is complete. Errors and interruption must never be reported as clean success; describe only implemented behavior until the lifecycle extension lands.

title: Report and stop long-running batch reviews reliably
body:
## Parent

[Batch declaration reviews through the Hapsland CLI](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/282)

## What to build

Make long-running audits understandable and interruptible through terminal/plain progress, stable machine output, scoped failures, and a retained partial result on real Ctrl+C.

- [ ] Terminal stderr shows updating count-only progress; redirected output uses infrequent plain lines without animation or filenames. Findings/final output stay on stdout.

- [ ] Result precedence is interrupted, incomplete, no-work, complete; stale/ambiguous failures remain incomplete even if zero evaluations finish.
- [ ] No new parallel execution requirement, retry loop, filename progress listing, or total-work cap is introduced. Reuse the batch lifecycle so future selection sources inherit the behavior.

title: Specify conversational rule authoring through Hapsland MCP
body:
## Destination

An agreed, implementation-ready specification for Hapsland’s runtime-neutral MCP interface and companion skill: turn operator corrections into deliberately saved review rules, and check relevant code afterward. Finish when product and architecture decisions are resolved; implementation is outside this map.

## Notes

- Operator direction (2026-11-21): use the inspected Traits workflow as the reference prism for every decision. Reuse it as the proposed baseline; ask the operator only about a concrete Hapsland-specific difference, explaining what necessitates it. Do not ask the operator to redesign reference behavior without such a difference. Reference evidence is advisory; recommendations still require operator confirmation.

- Scope agreed with the operator on 2026-11-21: rule discovery, complete proposals, approved persistence/activation, and focused code checks. Initial complete conversational validation targets Codex and Claude Code; the MCP contract remains runtime-neutral.
- Operator review can introduce or refine rules. Automatic agentic advice acts on existing rules and does not enter the rule-introduction flow. This is an explicit operator boundary, not an open design choice. Focused checks and reuse alongside automatic advice are resolved in the named decision below.
- Capture only preferences assessable through supported review inputs. Explain unsupported preferences rather than saving them as enforceable rules.
- Consult wayfinder, grilling, and domain-modeling for decision sessions; research for evidence tickets. Follow repository source organization, existing rule/configuration contracts, and administration interaction authority. Preserve version-one owned formats.
- Use “rule” for the Hapsland artifact; “Traits” names the reference tool, not a second Hapsland store. The D&D reference is Codex session 01a1fea2-cabd-7660-8832-00510e16e685 and its semantic-review experiment. It is inspiration, not an adopted contract.
- Existing production review transport remains hook clients plus resident IPC. Historical MCP-hook lifetime experiments do not establish the new conversational interface or authorize replacing production transport.
- This map records planning. Child resolutions hold decision detail; this issue only indexes them. No implementation readiness or runtime support is claimed by creating the map.

## Decisions so far

- [Define the operator rule-capture and revision conversation](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/291): reuse Traits capture/revision/approval practices with Hapsland evidence admission, project-scoped changes, observed validation before activation and bounded agent-led recovery; single operator thread, no mandated rollback subsystem.

- [Establish MCP conversation capabilities in Codex and Claude Code](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/292): researched native elicitation versus agent-question fallback, approval-policy and restart constraints; real-host workflow qualification remains open.

- [Define MCP rule proposal, approval, and application contracts](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/293#issuecomment-7065754217): accepted two tools for proposal/application and stored or unsaved checks; exact final approval, existing owners and safeguards, agent-led recovery without a durable proposal store or automatic rollback subsystem.

- [Define focused checks alongside automatic advice after rule changes](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/294#issuecomment-7065894496): accepted useful expected/observed unsaved-candidate validation before activation, bounded task checks and agent-led repair; preserve existing privacy/cost authority and report incomplete outcomes honestly.

- [Choose MCP packaging, registration, and companion-skill ownership](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/295#issuecomment-7066002094): accepted bundled stdio MCP and one companion skill, independently optional from hooks; selected user-profile registration with explicit repository targeting per call, existing onboarding lifecycle and thin rule-administration adapter; real-host qualification remains open.

- [Define specification completion and conversational acceptance evidence](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/296#issuecomment-7066483361): accepted concrete operation contract, six bounded scenario groups, preview-to-write correspondence and candidate equivalence; published [Implement conversational rule authoring through MCP and a companion skill](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/297) as the canonical implementation-ready handoff.

## Not yet specified

None within this planning destination. The accepted implementation specification owns the concrete scenarios and remaining deterministic, classifier and native-host evidence obligations. Execution and qualification remain open implementation work.

## Out of scope

- Production implementation, deployment, or release.
- Introducing/refining rules from automatic agentic advice.
- Expanding classifier inputs to documentation, full conversations, tasks, or other unsupported evidence.
- MCP access to credentials, setup, dashboard, or general administration. Registration needed to install this interface is in scope.
- Replacing existing hook/resident review transport or claiming support for additional agent runtimes.

title: Implement conversational rule authoring through MCP and a companion skill
body:
## Problem Statement

During operator review, useful corrections disappear into the conversation. The operator wants the coding agent to turn reusable feedback into Hapsland rules while the context is fresh, clarify only what changes the judgment, demonstrate useful behavior, and apply the approved rule. Manual rule scaffolding does not provide that complete conversation.

Hapsland also provides automatic advice. That mode uses existing rules. It must not introduce or refine rules from its own classifier output.

## Solution

Ship a Hapsland stdio MCP interface and one companion skill for Codex and Claude Code. Use Traits' inspected capture, revision, reconciliation, approval, and task-check practices where they fit Hapsland.

The operator conversation inspects existing rules, clarifies a reusable concern, drafts complete changes, evaluates an unsaved candidate, compares expected and observed judgments, obtains approval of the exact final content and effects, saves and activates the rule, and checks relevant task code. Failed or incomplete validation does not activate a candidate. The agent inspects and repairs failures, rejects the candidate, or asks the operator when judgment is needed.

Expose two tools, `derive_rule` and `check_rules`. Reuse Hapsland's current rule format, configuration, administration, evidence preparation, classifier execution, installation ownership, and automatic-advice mechanisms.

## User Stories

1. As an operator, I want reusable corrections captured before the agent finishes responding, so that I do not need to repeat them in later work.
2. As an operator, I want one-off corrections left as task feedback, so that the agent does not turn transient decisions into rules.
3. As an operator, I want the agent to inspect existing rules, so that it reuses a rule that already covers my concern.
4. As an operator, I want overlaps and conflicts explained using the actual existing requirements, so that reconciliation preserves meaningful exceptions and obligations.
5. As an operator, I want clarification only when it changes the judgment, so that the agent does not interview me about behavior already established by Traits or our decisions.
6. As an operator, I want complete final rule wording, so that I know what future reviews will assess.
7. As an operator, I want unsupported preferences explained, so that saving a rule does not imply Hapsland can evaluate unavailable evidence.
8. As an operator, I want missing context for one supported declaration distinguished from an unsupported rule, so that I can address the actual limitation.
9. As an operator, I want Project scope by default, so that a correction does not silently affect other projects.
10. As an operator, I want an explicit choice before changing Personal rules, so that cross-project effects are deliberate.
11. As an operator, I want a project-specific alternative to an inherited Personal rule to show its new identity and any local disabling, so that I can understand the complete effect.
12. As an operator, I want expected judgments stated before candidate evaluation, so that the agent cannot reinterpret unexpected output as success.
13. As an operator, I want an unsaved candidate checked while current rules stay unchanged, so that a failed candidate does not replace a working setup.
14. As an operator, I want revealing examples selected for the actual concern, so that validation demonstrates useful behavior without an arbitrary synthetic-example requirement.
15. As an operator, I want observed probabilities, thresholds, judgments, and missing evidence reported, so that I can inspect what the check established.
16. As an operator, I want mismatches, skips, stale results, and unavailable checks reported as incomplete, so that they cannot authorize activation.
17. As an operator, I want to revise, defer, or reject a candidate, so that failed validation has a clear next step.
18. As an operator, I want Save, Revise, and Skip choices for the exact final proposal, so that code-edit permission cannot be mistaken for permission to persist a rule.
19. As an operator, I want the preview to show content, destinations, scope, connections, and activation changes together, so that I approve the whole operation.
20. As an operator, I want a changed or lost preview reconstructed and approved again, so that stale conversational state does not authorize different writes.
21. As an operator, I want saved state, activation state, and check outcomes reported separately, so that a successful save is not presented as validated enforcement.
22. As an operator, I want partial changes inspected before retry or repair, so that a failed operation does not falsely claim restoration.
23. As an operator, I want confirmed task-code findings repaired and rechecked within the authorized scope, so that capturing a rule improves the current work.
24. As an operator, I want unchanged observations reused only when their effective inputs are demonstrably equivalent, so that reuse does not hide unverified changes.
25. As an operator, I want selected code, privacy exclusions, configured backend, and spending authority preserved, so that candidate validation cannot widen access or cost scope.
26. As an operator, I want every call and result to identify its repository, so that a user-profile MCP registration works predictably across projects.
27. As an operator, I want MCP and its skill installed independently of hooks, so that I can choose the integration I need.
28. As an operator, I want updates and removal to preserve unrelated settings and modified files, so that Hapsland manages only its owned integration artifacts.
29. As an operator, I want Codex and Claude Code approval fallbacks verified, so that an automatic host response is not mistaken for my approval.
30. As an operator, I want automatic advice to use enabled existing rules without initiating capture, so that the automatic mode cannot create requirements.
31. As a contributor, I want tool inputs derived from current rule and configuration owners, so that MCP does not introduce a parallel format or source of authority.
32. As a contributor, I want precise acceptance properties and observable tests at existing operation boundaries, so that implementation can proceed without a second speculative protocol or rollback system.

## Implementation Decisions

- Keep Hapsland-owned formats at version 1. Rule administration retains rule identity, configuration composition, authorized destinations, persistence, and activation. MCP does not create a second rules store.
- Each request supplies an explicit absolute `repository`. Resolve its physical Git working-tree root using current discovery. Do not infer the target from MCP startup directory or a mutable current-project value. Every result identifies the resolved repository. Declaration selectors are repository-relative positive one-based paths and lines.
- `derive_rule` provides `inspect`, `preview`, and `apply` operations. Inspection accepts an optional rule ID and otherwise returns inventory, including content, origin, activation, and effective selection. Inspection makes no writes or classifier calls.
- Preview accepts a nonempty collection of explicit creation or replacement changes with complete version-one content and exact configuration effects. Show final content, authorized destination, scope, affected existing rules, connection, selection, and activation changes. Preview mechanically validates without writing or calling the classifier.
- Administration resolves destination authority. Creation is limited to an authorized rule destination. Replacement must match the named existing authored file. Caller-supplied path and scope do not grant arbitrary writes.
- Apply takes the identical changes and preview digest. Recompute the plan under the existing mutation lock before writes. Bind repository, complete ordered changes, configuration effects, and relevant current snapshots. Reject stale, changed, or unauthorized plans without mutation. Reuse existing safeguards rather than adding a new concurrency subsystem.
- The skill obtains approval of the exact final proposal in the conversation. A digest establishes freshness, not human consent. A bare boolean, tool permission, or automatically supplied elicitation response does not replace the operator's choice. Do not generate replacement wording after approval. A changed proposal requires renewed validation and approval.
- Preview state can be process-local or reconstructed from supplied complete changes. Restart or loss of the proposal requires inspection, reconstruction, and fresh approval. No durable pending-proposal store is required.
- Application results distinguish saved content, effective activation, and failure. Report affected files and known completed or incomplete effects. If actual state is unknown, say so. The agent inspects before retry, repairs using ordinary operations, rejects the candidate, or asks the operator. Do not promise automatic restoration or a multi-file transaction.
- `check_rules` accepts a nonempty bounded collection of path-and-line targets. Stored mode accepts optional enabled rule IDs and otherwise checks eligible enabled rules. Candidate mode accepts complete previewed rule content and proposed owned rule bindings, activation, and selection changes, without writing them.
- Resolve source-read, evidence, privacy, credential, backend, and resource policy independently from current repository and user-profile configuration. Candidate fields cannot widen permitted access or substitute a backend. Denied target and supporting-source reads remain denied.
- Candidate checks represent the intended post-application effective definition, selection, threshold, and request settings. Check every materially changed candidate in a reconciled proposal. Current active rules and durable configuration stay unchanged.
- Results retain evaluated, skipped, and unavailable outcomes, actual reasons, selected declaration and supporting evidence, omissions, effective rule identity, request settings, probabilities, thresholds, judgments, and request counts. Stale or failed evaluation is incomplete. An empty selection, skip, or successful process exit is not a clear judgment.
- The skill states expected finding or clear judgments before dispatch. Expectations are operator-visible reasoning and are not additional classifier input. Choose the smallest examples that exercise the concern. A new violation detector needs a revealing expected finding; add a clear or boundary case when breadth or exceptions require it. Do not mandate a synthetic pair or alter production code solely to create fixtures.
- Before activation, compare expectations with actual observations. Mismatch, skip, unavailable, stale, failure, or otherwise inconclusive evidence blocks activation. Revise and revalidate, reject, or defer. Observed examples do not prove general classifier quality or formal totality.
- After approved application, inspect actual saved and active state. Check eligible declarations changed or directly involved in the task with affected stored rules. Triage findings in context, repair confirmed violations within authorization, and recheck. Do not weaken a rule to silence findings.
- Observation reuse is optional. Reuse only when effective rules, threshold, model and request settings, source, supporting evidence, and accompanying rules that affect the request are demonstrably equivalent. Otherwise perform a fresh bounded check. No reuse database is required.
- Project is the default scope. Personal changes require an explicit choice. A project-specific alternative to an inherited Personal rule uses a distinct rule ID, with any local disabling in the same preview.
- Only operator review introduces or refines rules. Automatic advice continues consuming existing configured rules and never initiates this capture flow from classifier advice.
- Bundle the stdio MCP server and one canonical companion skill in the existing retained Hapsland release. Register per selected user profile with explicit repository targeting per call. MCP plus skill is optional independently of hooks. The host owns the stdio subprocess; existing hook and resident transport stays unchanged.
- Existing onboarding and release owners manage registration, skill discovery, update, and removal. Preview effects, preserve unrelated configuration and owned-artifact conflicts, and report reconnect requirements. Verify actual host locations and flags against installed versions. Tool descriptions own executable contracts; the skill owns conversation and interpretation.
- Use native elicitation only when it presents the complete proposal and obtains the operator's choice. Otherwise use the host agent's question path. If no path can obtain actual operator approval, leave the proposal pending and do not apply. Cancellation and restart never imply approval.

## Testing Decisions

- Test externally observable behavior through the highest existing administration operations. Prefer real temporary repositories, real rule/configuration parsing, preparation and filesystem reads with deterministic reviewers. Add stdio subprocess tests for the new adapter and installed-host traces only for behavior that those boundaries uniquely establish.
- Extend the existing rules interaction reducer, preview/application owner, canonical Bend rule admission, and declaration-check preparation tests. Reuse current installation preservation and conflict fixtures. Do not introduce a second overall conversational model merely because the workflow has states.
- State two implementation acceptance properties. First, preview-to-write correspondence: writes start only when authorized destinations and the recomputed repository, ordered full rule content, configuration effects, and relevant snapshots match the approved preview. Inspect, preview, and mechanical rejection cause zero writes. Second, candidate equivalence: with the same source, evidence, and independently resolved policy, an unsaved check and the intended applied check prepare the same effective rule, selection, threshold, request settings, evidence, and admission decisions, while the unsaved check leaves active rules unchanged.
- Compare normalized preparation through candidate and applied paths using a deterministic reviewer. Do not require separate live probabilistic requests to return identical answers. Existing Bend decisions prove only decisions over their supplied facts; real preparation and filesystem tests must establish fact provenance, denied reads, request contents, and write outcomes.
- Verify capture, existing coverage and conflict handling, revision, Skip, and exact approval. Include a Personal-to-Project alternative with visible local disabling. Use the actual clarified totality concern or an equivalent task example rather than treating every throw as a violation.
- Verify unsupported documentation obligations are rejected as unenforceable. Separately verify missing required evidence for a supported declaration is an explained skip. Candidate selection changes must not read denied roots or supporting sources.
- Verify useful expected versus observed unsaved judgments before activation, including mismatch, skipped, unavailable, and stale outcomes. Verify revision requires fresh observations where effective candidate inputs change. A finding on a known violation is successful example validation, not a command failure.
- Verify exact content and configuration application, stale-plan rejection, out-of-scope writes, mismatched replacement identity, existing lock failure, restart reconstruction, and an actual partial write. Compare reported effects with disk state and exercise ordinary inspection, repair, and renewed preview before retry. No hypothetical competing-editor service or rollback engine is required.
- Verify saved-rule checks on relevant task declarations, contextual repair and recheck, truthful request counts and failure reasons, and automatic advice's existing-rule-only behavior. Test reuse only if implementation actually performs it.
- In Codex and Claude Code, verify bundled tool and skill discovery, explicit repositories A and B in requests and results, exact human approval despite automatic transport responses, cancellation, reconnect, independent hook selection, and preservation/conflicts during update and removal. Record actual versions, profiles, and limitations.
- Deterministic local tests establish mechanics. Bounded, separately authorized Jev observations establish behavior on selected examples. Installed native traces establish the recorded host/version/profile behavior. None establishes universal classifier correctness or untested platform support.
- Follow the repository's check-selection policy and testing matrix for each implementation acceptance candidate. Required local checks determine completion; report GitHub CI separately. Human intent, useful example selection, and real operator approval still require interaction evidence. There is no new Bend proof suite, Quint model, or conversation state machine required at this planning milestone.

## Out of Scope

- Production implementation, deployment, or release as part of this specification-publishing task.
- Introducing or refining rules from automatic advice.
- Expanding review inputs to documentation completeness, whole conversations, task obligations, runtime execution, or unsupported declaration kinds.
- General administration, credential management, dashboards, or setup through MCP. Registration needed for this feature remains in scope.
- Replacing existing hook clients or resident IPC, adding an HTTP service, or requiring Traits as a runtime dependency.
- A separate rules store, durable proposal store, new global lease, automatic rollback engine, mandatory synthetic example pair, calibration program, or whole-repository audit authority.
- Additional agent-runtime or platform support beyond the explicitly qualified evidence.

## Further Notes

This is the accepted implementation scope synthesized from the operator discussion and the [conversational rule-authoring map](https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/290). The map indexes the original decisions and their rationale; this issue is the implementation handoff, not another planning ticket.

Astra reviewed the validation flow and concrete contract. Its read/write authority findings were corrected before acceptance. A separate fresh Astra evaluation recommended the two acceptance properties above and reuse of existing formal owners, without a new whole-conversation formal model.

At publication, no MCP implementation, paid classifier validation, or native-host qualification has been performed. The documentation check passed for the concrete contract draft; that is documentation evidence only. Do not report the planned scenario matrix as executed tests.

title: Inspect and check enabled rules through the MCP stdio interface

## Parent

## What to build

Give an agent a useful read-only MCP workflow: inspect existing rule coverage and check selected declarations against enabled stored rules in an explicitly named repository. Adapt existing rule administration and production declaration preparation instead of creating another rule or review authority.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Expose derive_rule inspection and check_rules stored mode through a real stdio subprocess; discover exactly the two named tools and derive boundary rule/configuration shapes from their current owners.
- [ ] Require an explicit absolute repository on every request, resolve its physical Git working-tree root with existing discovery, and identify that root in results. Demonstrate repositories A and B through one server without startup-directory fallback.
- [ ] Inspect inventory or a named rule with complete content, identity, origin, activation and effective selection. Inspection performs zero writes and zero classifier calls.
- [ ] Accept a nonempty bounded collection of repository-relative positive one-based path/line targets. Stored checks select optional enabled IDs or eligible enabled rules and preserve existing source-read, privacy, credential, backend and resource policy.
- [ ] Return evaluated, skipped and unavailable outcomes with actual reasons, selected declaration and permitted evidence/omissions, effective rule identity/settings, probabilities, thresholds, judgments and actual request counts. Empty selection, failures and stale observations never become clear judgments.
- [ ] Verify administration behavior with real temporary repositories and deterministic reviewers, plus stdio subprocess tests for adapter-specific behavior. Run the required fast/focused checks and affected boundary consumers selected under CHECKS and the testing matrix; claim only executed evidence.

## What to build

Let an agent preview a complete new Project rule and observe its behavior on selected declarations without changing current rules or configuration. This is the first unsaved-candidate path; persistence and the approval conversation follow in a dependent ticket.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] derive_rule preview accepts complete version-one rule content and exact owned configuration effects, mechanically validates them, and shows final content, authorized destination, Project scope, connections, selection, activation and preview digest without writes or classifier calls.
- [ ] check_rules candidate mode evaluates the intended post-application effective definition and settings using existing preparation/evaluation and canonical rule-admission owners; current active rules and durable configuration remain unchanged.
- [ ] Resolve source-read, evidence, privacy, credentials, backend and resource policy independently from current repository/profile configuration. Candidate bindings/selection cannot widen denied roots or supporting-source access, replace the backend or expand spending authority.
- [ ] Establish candidate equivalence by comparing normalized real preparation for unsaved and intended applied states with the same source/evidence/policy and a deterministic reviewer: effective rule, selection, threshold, request settings, evidence and admission decisions match.
- [ ] Preserve missing-evidence skips, denied-read omissions, mismatch-relevant observations, unavailable/stale failures and truthful request counts. A skipped selection issues no classifier request and an inconclusive result is never clear.
- [ ] Exercise useful finding and, where warranted, boundary/clear fixtures without requiring a synthetic pair or changing production code to manufacture examples. Do not claim live classifier accuracy from deterministic tests.
- [ ] Run required fast/focused checks and affected stdio/preparation consumers under CHECKS and the testing matrix; extend current owners rather than introducing a parallel store, format or proof suite.
- [ ] A missing-evidence skip on a supported declaration issues zero classifier requests; distinguish it from an unsupported documentation-completeness obligation. Preserve source-bearing result privacy without creating a transcript or example archive.

title: Capture, approve and apply an exact Project rule in conversation
body:
## Parent

https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/297

## What to build

Ship the canonical companion skill and the complete single-Project-rule journey: clarify a reusable correction, inspect existing coverage, validate the unsaved proposal, obtain approval of its exact content and effects, create and apply it, inspect saved/active state, and check and repair relevant task code.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The skill captures reusable corrections before finishing, skips one-off feedback, reuses existing coverage and asks only for missing judgment. Project is the default; unsupported evidence obligations are explained separately from missing context for a supported declaration.
- [ ] Before candidate dispatch, state operator-visible expected judgments and reasons without adding them to classifier input. Compare expectations with observations; mismatch, skip, unavailable, stale or failed evidence blocks activation. Revised effective inputs require fresh observations unless full equivalence is demonstrable.
- [ ] Show complete final content/destinations/configuration/activation effects and Save, Revise and Skip. Code-edit permission, a boolean, tool permission or automatic transport response is not human approval. Changed content requires renewed validation and approval; cancellation never applies.
- [ ] Support exact complete-body creation of a new Project rule through the existing administration owner. Under its existing mutation lock, recompute and bind repository, ordered complete changes, configuration effects and relevant snapshots before writing. Inspection, preview and mechanical rejection perform zero writes.
- [ ] Reject stale plans and out-of-scope creation destinations before mutation. Test lock failure and an actual failure after content write but before configuration completion; report observed saved content and activation separately, completed/incomplete effects and unknown state honestly.
- [ ] After failure inspect disk state before ordinary repair/repreview/retry. After restart or lost proposal, inspect and reconstruct a preview and obtain fresh approval; no durable proposal store, rollback promise or new concurrency subsystem.
- [ ] After approved application inspect actual saved/active state, check affected stored rules on eligible declarations changed or directly involved in the task, repair confirmed violations within authorization and recheck. Preserve reasons/request counts and do not weaken rules to silence findings.
- [ ] Verify the clarified throwing-head concern or an equivalent task example, revision, Skip, exact approval, recovery and task repair using existing interaction/administration/preparation owners and real temporary files. Automatic advice continues consuming existing rules without initiating capture.
- [ ] Run required fast/focused and affected stdio/consumer checks under repository policy. The skill explains backend/scope/possible charges before paid checks and respects existing authorization; deterministic tests do not establish real human consent or live classifier usefulness.
- [ ] Keep source-bearing results private without an automatic transcript/example archive. Any optional observation reuse requires demonstrably equivalent effective rules, threshold, model/request settings, source, supporting evidence and accompanying request rules; otherwise rerun bounded checks, without a reuse subsystem.

title: Reconcile related rules and approve a Project alternative to a Personal rule
body:
## Parent

https://github.com/dearlordylord/hapsland/issues/297

## What to build

Let an operator resolve overlap or conflict as one explicit proposal involving several complete rule changes, including a distinct-ID Project alternative to an inherited Personal rule and any visible local disabling. Preserve meaningful existing exceptions and obligations.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Inspect actual existing requirements and explain coverage/overlap/conflict before drafting. Personal changes require explicit operator choice; Project alternatives use distinct rule identity and show inherited-rule local disabling in the same proposal.
- [ ] Preview a nonempty ordered collection of complete explicit creations/replacements and exact owned configuration changes, showing affected existing rules, authorized destinations, scope, connections, selection and activation together.
- [ ] Check every materially changed candidate under its intended effective configuration without saving. Compare expected and observed behavior before exact final approval; revision or changed effective inputs cannot reuse invalid observations.
- [ ] Apply the identical approved collection through existing administration and lock ownership. Extend preview-to-write correspondence and candidate-equivalence tests to reconciled proposals, preserving independent policy authority and rejecting changed/unauthorized plans without writes.
- [ ] Exercise a real partial application of a combined proposal, compare reported effects with disk state, inspect before repair and require renewed preview/approval for subsequent writes; do not claim multi-file transactions or automatic restoration.
- [ ] Verify exact saved and effective activation outcomes, relevant stored-rule task checks and preservation of unrelated requirements/exceptions using real parsing/filesystem/preparation with deterministic reviewers. Keep owned formats at version one and remove superseded paths in place.
- [ ] Run required fast/focused and affected consumer checks under CHECKS and the testing matrix. Reuse current interaction and canonical admission owners; no second overall conversation model, rules store or proof suite.
- [ ] Support exact complete-body replacement of an existing authored file and demonstrate a real Project rule replacement during reconciliation. Reject a replacement whose destination does not match the named existing authored rule before any write; changing path or scope cannot grant write authority.
